### Describe the bug

When using **Claude Code** (Anthropic's CLI tool) in Warp terminal, Thai tone marks (วรรณยุกต์) and upper vowels (สระบน) are not rendering properly. All diacritical marks above Thai consonants disappear.

This is related to #3584 which was closed as "not planned", but this issue significantly affects Thai language users who use Claude Code in Warp.

**Example:**
- Expected: ก่อนที่จะรายงาน (with tone marks)
- Actual: กอนทจะรายงาน (tone marks missing)

Characters affected:
- Tone marks: ่ ้ ๊ ๋
- Upper vowels: ิ ี ึ ื ั ็

### To reproduce

1. Open Warp terminal
2. Run Claude Code CLI (claude command)
3. Have Claude output any Thai text containing tone marks or upper vowels
4. Observe that all diacritical marks above consonants are missing

### Expected behavior

Thai text should display with all diacritical marks intact, including:
- Tone marks: ่ ้ ๊ ๋ (mai ek, mai tho, mai tri, mai chattawa)
- Upper vowels: ิ ี ึ ื ั ็ (sara i, sara ii, sara ue, sara uue, mai han-akat, mai tai khu)

Example: "สวัสดี" should show all characters, not "สวสด"

### Describe the bug

Tab completion for file/directory arguments doesn't work for commands that Warp doesn't recognize natively (e.g., zed, mate, code, subl), unless an explicit path prefix like ~/ is provided.

### To reproduce

Open Warp terminal
Navigate to any directory: cd ~/Documents
Type zed  (with space) and press TAB
Expected: List of files/directories in current directory appears
Actual: Nothing happens, or only recently used files are shown

Workaround that works:

zed ~/ + TAB → shows files (but starts from home, not current directory)
Open a zsh subshell (zsh command), then zed  + TAB → works correctly

What I've tried (none of these fixed it):

Added compdef _files zed mate code subl to .zshrc
Switched from Universal Input to Classic Input
Disabled Warp's intelligent autosuggestions
Modified keybindings.yaml
Various zstyle completion settings

### Expected behavior

Warp should either:

Pass TAB completion to the shell for unrecognized commands, OR
Default to file completion for any command it doesn't have specific completions for

title: Feature request: CLI/API to query Warp AI credit usage programmatically
body:
Title: Feature request: CLI/API to query Warp AI credit usage programmatically

Hi Warp team,

I'd love a way to **query my Warp AI credit usage programmatically**, similar to how cloud providers expose billing/usage APIs.

## Problem

Right now, the only way to see AI credit usage is via the Warp UI (e.g., Settings → Billing and usage, or per-turn credit chips). That works for manual inspection, but it doesn't help when:

- I want to track usage over time in my own dashboards
- I want alerts when I approach a certain usage threshold
- I want to correlate terminal/AI usage with other metrics (e.g., project activity, time of day, etc.)

## Proposed solution

Expose **either or both** of the following:

1. **CLI command** (ideal for scripting):
   - Example: `warp credits` or `warp usage`
   - Options for:
     - Current billing period usage (default)
     - Custom date range
     - Plan vs reload credit consumption
   - Machine-readable output: `--format json` / `--format yaml` flags

   Example:
   ```bash
   warp credits --period "current" --format json
   ```
   Output could include:
   - Total credits used this period
   - Remaining included credits
   - Remaining reload credits
   - Breakdown by feature / model (if available)

2. **HTTP API endpoint**
   - Authenticated with the same identity as the Warp account
   - Returns structured usage/billing data (JSON)
   - Suitable for automation/integration into monitoring systems

## Why this helps

- Enables **automated monitoring** and alerts
- Helps budget and forecast AI usage
- Makes it easier to justify Warp spend to teams/orgs
- Lets power users integrate Warp usage with their existing observability stack

Even a minimal first version (e.g. just "credits used this month" via CLI/JSON) would already be very useful.

Thanks for considering this!

title: Feature Request: Automatic Session Checkpoint & Recovery System for Agent Mode
body:
## Problem Statement

When Warp Agent Mode sessions crash or tabs disappear unexpectedly, all context is lost. There's no automatic recovery mechanism, requiring manual investigation through shell history, file timestamps, and logs. This makes long-running workflows fragile and frustrating, limiting Agent Mode's production readiness.

### Real-World Impact

**Recent incident (2026-01-10)**: During a 5-hour protocol reconciliation session processing 3,349 items:
- Session tab disappeared without warning at 62% completion (2,146 items processed)
- No crash detected in system logs
- No session state preserved
- Recovery required ~15 minutes of manual investigation:
  - Shell history analysis
  - File timestamp checking
  - Log file examination
  - Progress calculation from output files
  
**Result**: Lost productivity, unclear resume point, manual state reconstruction.

## Proposed Solution

Implement automatic session checkpointing with three integrated components:

### 1. Automatic Checkpoint Creation

Create `.warp-checkpoints/SESSION_CHECKPOINT_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.md` files automatically:

**Triggers**:
- Every 50 tool calls
- Before long-running operations (>60s expected)
- After major milestones (user-definable)
- On explicit user request ("checkpoint this session")

**Checkpoint Content** (Markdown format):
```markdown
# Session Checkpoint: <Task Name>
**Timestamp**: 2026-01-10 22:30:00 UTC
**Working Directory**: ~/project
**Agent**: Warp AI Agent

## Current Task
<One-line description>

## Progress
- Total: 2,146 of 3,349 complete (64%)
- Last item processed: "Item Name"
- Next item to process: "Item Name"

## Resume Command
```bash
cd ~/project
<exact-command-to-resume>
```

## Key Files Modified
- file1.ndjson (2,146 lines, 17:03:34)
- file2.json (3,355 lines, 16:53:52)

## Context
<Brief context about what we're doing and why>

## Recovery Commands
```bash
# Check status
<status-check-command>

# Resume work
<resume-command>
```
```

### 2. Recovery Prompt on Startup

When agent initializes in a directory:

```python
def on_agent_start():
    checkpoint_dir = Path.cwd() / ".warp-checkpoints"
    if checkpoint_dir.exists():
        recent = find_most_recent_checkpoint()
        if recent and age_minutes(recent) < 1440:  # 24 hours
            show_prompt(f"""
            📋 Found recent checkpoint: {recent.name}
            ⏱  Created: {age_minutes(recent)} minutes ago
            📊 Progress: {extract_progress(recent)}
            
            Would you like to review and resume?
            [View Checkpoint] [Ignore] [Delete]
            """)
```

**User Experience**:
- Non-intrusive notification
- One-click checkpoint review
- Easy resume with pre-filled command
- Option to ignore or clean up old checkpoints

### 3. Memory KB Integration

Add MCP write tool to `memory-fallback` server for system-wide checkpoint storage:

**New Tool**: `memory_fallback_add()`

```python
{
  "name": "memory_fallback_add",
  "description": "Add document to Warp memory knowledge base",
  "input_schema": {
    "document_name": "string (filename.md)",
    "content": "string (markdown content)",
    "auto_index": "boolean (queue for GraphRAG indexing)"
  }
}
```

**Workflow**:
1. Agent creates local checkpoint in `.warp-checkpoints/`
2. Optionally saves copy to `~/.unified-mcp-manager/memory/kb/`
3. Queues for GraphRAG indexing via existing idle indexer
4. Makes checkpoint searchable system-wide across all projects

**Benefit**: Future agents in *any* project can search: `memory_fallback_search("recent checkpoint protocol reconciliation")` and find recovery information.

## Benefits

### User Experience
- **Recovery Time**: 15 minutes → <2 minutes
- **Recovery Success Rate**: 95%+ of sessions recoverable
- **Peace of Mind**: Work is never lost
- **Multi-Project**: Search checkpoints across all projects via memory KB

### Production Readiness
- Makes Agent Mode reliable for:
  - Long-running data processing (hours)
  - Multi-day development workflows
  - Critical deployments
  - Batch operations

### Developer Experience
- Reduces agent confusion after crashes
- Provides continuity across sessions
- Enables "pick up where I left off" workflows
- Self-documenting progress

## Technical Implementation

### Phase 1: Local Checkpoints (Core Feature)

**Location**: `.warp-checkpoints/` directory (git-ignored by default)

**Agent Integration Point** (pseudo-code):
```python
class WarpAgent:
    def __init__(self):
        self.tool_call_count = 0
        self.checkpoint_dir = Path.cwd() / ".warp-checkpoints"
        self.checkpoint_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    
    def execute_tool(self, tool_call):
        result = super().execute_tool(tool_call)
        self.tool_call_count += 1
        
        if self.tool_call_count % 50 == 0:
            self.create_checkpoint()
        
        return result
    
    def create_checkpoint(self):
        timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
        checkpoint_file = self.checkpoint_dir / f"SESSION_CHECKPOINT_{timestamp}.md"
        
        content = self.build_checkpoint_content()
        checkpoint_file.write_text(content)
        
        # Optional: Save to memory KB
        if self.memory_kb_enabled:
            memory_fallback_add(
                document_name=f"CHECKPOINT_{timestamp}.md",
                content=content,
                auto_index=True
            )
```

### Phase 2: Recovery Prompt

**UI Integration**: Add check in agent startup sequence

**Storage**: Remember user's checkpoint preferences:
- Always show prompts
- Auto-resume from most recent
- Never show (disable feature)

### Phase 3: Memory KB Integration

**Requires**: Adding write tool to existing memory-fallback MCP server

**Implementation**: Extend server at `~/.unified-mcp-manager/memory/memory_mcp_server.py`:
```python
@server.call_tool()
async def handle_call_tool(name: str, arguments: dict) -> list[types.TextContent]:
    if name == "memory_fallback_add":
        doc_name = arguments["document_name"]
        content = arguments["content"]
        auto_index = arguments.get("auto_index", True)
        
        # Save to KB
        kb_path = KB_DIR / doc_name
        kb_path.write_text(content)
        
        # Queue for GraphRAG indexing
        if auto_index:
            add_to_graphrag_queue(doc_name)
        
        return [types.TextContent(type="text", text=f"Saved to memory KB: {doc_name}")]
```

## Related Issues & Discussions

This checkpoint system addresses needs mentioned in:
- #4679 - External scripting support (checkpoints enable external monitoring/recovery)
- #612 - Warp CLI + General Scriptability (checkpoints provide scriptable state)
- #8409 - Session hangs/crashes (recovery mechanism when Claude sessions fail)

## Current Workaround

Manual session handoff documents:
- Create `SESSION_HANDOFF_*.md` files manually
- Use `scripts/save-to-memory.sh` to copy to memory KB
- Manual investigation after crashes

**See full specification**: https://github.com/bryankaufman/two-tiered-ai-platform (reference SESSION_RECOVERY_PROTOCOL.md)

## Success Metrics

1. **Recovery Time**: <2 minutes to resume after crash

title: Help an upper limb amputee
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates

⸻

Team,

I'm writing to you with genuine respect and appreciation for what you've built with Warp. It is, without exaggeration, one of the best tools I've used across a 35-year career in programming, engineering, education, and systems design.

A little context, briefly and sincerely.

Earlier in my life, I followed my curiosity wherever it led. I became a commercial pilot (Captain), completed degrees in Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Software Engineering, and Microelectronic Engineering (sensor design), and worked in Higher Education before 2000 as the inaugural Online Learning Manager across five campuses of The University of Queensland. That role blended technology, pedagogy, and institutional strategy, and led to lecturing, publishing, and invitations to collaborate nationally and internationally.

Later, I worked in advanced analytics and predictive modelling (what we'd now comfortably call early AI) for Suncorp, one of Australia's largest insurers and banks. In 2013, a role was created for me: Solutions Advisor, Fraud and Intelligence, working alongside former law-enforcement specialists.

Life then took a very different turn.

In 2016, I survived a catastrophic medical event that left me in a five-week induced coma, followed by 19 surgeries, the loss of my upper limb (and part of my shoulder), and years of rehabilitation. I had to relearn how to stand, walk, and function again after losing nearly 50kg of muscle.

In the years that followed, I experienced further devastating losses within my family, including the deaths of two of my children. I share this not for sympathy, but to explain why accessibility is not theoretical for me - it is daily, practical, and absolute.

Despite this, my mind remains sharp and deeply engaged. I began programming as a teenager on a Dick Smith VZ-200 in the 1980s, taught myself electronics from my father's textbooks, and built robotics projects long before terms like "IoT" existed. That same curiosity and drive is what brought me back, decisively, to AI and cybersecurity in 2025-2026. I now spend 70-80 hours a week researching, building, and experimenting - typing one-handed.

Which brings me to Warp.

Warp is outstanding. Its design philosophy, speed, and ambition are exactly right. It has become my default environment.

However, there are specific accessibility barriers that currently stop me - and users like me - from fully using its power.

Example:
Workbook macros or command workflows that require combinations such as TAB + arrow keys are physically impossible for me to execute. Even with assistive settings enabled, reassigning these inputs does not reliably work.

This isn't a complaint - it's an opportunity.

I'm asking, respectfully, whether you would consider:
	•	Expanded key remapping flexibility beyond conventional modifier assumptions
	•	Alternative single-input or sequential input modes for core navigation
	•	Better support for users who cannot chord keys, even with large hand spans

If you're looking for inspiration, you might find SnippetsLab (https://www.renfei.org/snippets-lab/) interesting from an interaction-design perspective.

I'm currently on the free tier of Warp due to being on a health pension (and already maintaining a ChatGPT Plus subscription), but I would happily contribute ideas, feedback, or testing insight if it helps make Warp more accessible to people with permanent physical constraints.

I've built software, taught engineers, led teams, and lived through enough to know this:
Accessibility done well doesn't reduce power - it multiplies it.

Thank you for your time, and for building something genuinely special.

Warm regards,
Steve

Warp terminal on Windows cannot execute symbolic links via PowerShell, resulting in "No application is associated with the specified file for this operation" error. This completely breaks the Rust development workflow since all Rust toolchain commands (cargo, rustc, clippy, etc.) are symbolic links to rustup.exe. The same commands work correctly in Windows Terminal.

### To reproduce

title: Interactive UI for Agent Clarifying Questions
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

## Problem Statement

When Warp's AI agent needs clarification during planning or task execution, users must read text-based questions and type responses back into the chat interface. This creates friction and slows down the workflow compared to modern AI coding tools.

**Current experience:**
- Agent asks: "Which framework should we use?"
- User must type: "Option A" or similar
- Context-switching from reviewing to typing is slow and cumbersome

**Desired experience:**
- Agent asks question via interactive UI
- User clicks the desired option
- Agent immediately continues with selection

## Proposed Solution

Implement an interactive, mouse-clickable UI for agent clarifying questions, similar to Claude Code's AskUserQuestion tool and Cursor's Plan Mode.

**Visual Design:**
- Display questions as a focused card/panel in the terminal UI
- Render multiple-choice options as clickable selections
- Support both:
  - **Single-select**: Radio buttons (e.g., "Which framework?")
  - **Multi-select**: Checkboxes (e.g., "Which files should we refactor?")
- Highlight selected options visually
- Provide a "Continue" or "Confirm" button for submission
- Optional: "Skip" or "Auto-decide" button if user wants agent to proceed with default
- Include an "Enter text" option for custom responses not covered by pre-defined choices

**Input support:**
- Mouse clicks (primary interaction)
- Keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Space to select, Enter to confirm)
- Keybindings for quick selection (e.g., `1`, `2`, `3` for options)
- Text input field for custom responses

### Example UI Layout


```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Agent Question                              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                             │
│ Which framework should we use?              │
│                                             │
│  ◉ React (recommended)                      │
│  ○ Vue                                      │
│  ○ Svelte                                   │
│                                             │
│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐│
│ │         Continue (Enter) →               ││
│ └──────────────────────────────────────────┘│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Multi-Question Workflows

For agents that need to ask multiple clarifying questions:

- **Tabbed Interface**: Display questions as sequential tabs or a step indicator (e.g., "Question 1 of 3")
- **Progress Tracking**: Show which questions have been answered vs. pending
- **Batch Submission**: Collect all answers before sending back to agent in a single response
- **Navigation**: Allow users to move between questions (previous/next buttons) before final submission
- **Final Confirmation**: A "Submit All Answers" button sends the complete response set to the agent at once

### Example Multi-Tab Layout
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Agent Questions (1 of 3)                         │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ [✓ Framework] [Architecture] [Files]             │
│                                                  │
│ Which framework should we use?                   │
│                                                  │
│  ◉ React (recommended)                           │
│  ○ Vue                                           │
│  ○ Svelte                                        │
│  ○ Enter text...                                 │
│                                                  │
│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │ [Previous]            [Next →]               │ │
│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Benefits of batch submission:**
- Agents can see all answers together, reducing round-trips
- More context for intelligent follow-up
- Faster planning iteration when multiple clarifications needed
- Natural flow: answer all questions, then proceed

## Benefits

- **Faster planning**: No typing overhead for structured answers
- **Lower friction**: Click-based selection matches user expectations
- **Improved UX**: Aligns with Claude Code and Cursor
- **Accessibility**: Supports both mouse and keyboard input
- **Clear visual state**: Users always see what's selected before confirming
- **Natural for agentic workflows**: Agents can ask clarifying questions without blocking or requiring text input
- **Flexibility**: "Enter text" option handles unexpected scenarios

## Use Cases

1. **Planning phase**: "Which files should we modify?"
2. **Architecture decisions**: "Which pattern should we use?"
3. **Multi-step workflows**: "Proceed with X, Y, or Z?"
4. **Batch operations**: "Select items to process" (multi-select)
5. **Complex clarifications**: Agent asks 3+ questions before planning, user answers all at once

## Technical Notes

- Related to broader contextual UI work (see #8359), but focused specifically on agent-to-user question flow
- Could leverage existing Warp command block infrastructure
- Questions could be passed via SSE streaming or similar mechanism
- Support keyboard-only workflows (no mouse required)
- Multi-question workflows should batch answers in a single structured response to the agent

## Alternatives Considered

- ❌ Keep current text-based Q&A (slower, requires typing)
- ❌ Terminal-style arrow-key menus (feels outdated, slower)
- ❌ Slash commands (adds cognitive load, more typing)

title: Feature Request: Enhance 'Changes' panel with full Git staging, unstaging, and commit capabilities (VS Code-like Source Control UI)
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

## Summary

Enhance Warp's existing **Changes** panel to go beyond viewing diffs by adding full Git staging, unstaging, and commit functionality directly from the UI - similar to how VS Code's Source Control panel works.

## Current Behavior

Warp's **Changes** feature currently allows users to:
- View file-level diffs for modified, added, and deleted files in a Git repository.

However, to **stage**, **unstage**, or **commit** those changes, users must:
- Manually type `git add`, `git reset`, and `git commit` commands in the terminal, or
- Ask the integrated AI/LLM to run those commands on their behalf.

This creates an unnecessary context switch between a visual diff view and a CLI-based Git workflow.

## Proposed Solution

Upgrade the Changes panel to include interactive Git operations directly in the UI:

### 1. Staging & Unstaging
- **Stage individual files**: Add a `+` (stage) button next to each changed file, allowing users to run the equivalent of `git add <file>` with a single click.
- **Unstage individual files**: For files already staged, show a `-` (unstage) button to run the equivalent of `git reset HEAD <file>`.
- **Stage all / Unstage all**: Provide bulk action buttons (e.g., "Stage All Changes" / "Unstage All") at the top of the Changes panel.
- **Hunk-level staging** (stretch goal): Allow users to stage or discard individual diff hunks within a file, similar to VS Code's inline diff staging.

### 2. Commit from the UI
- **Commit message input**: Add a text field at the top of the Changes panel where users can type a commit message.
- **Commit button**: A dedicated "Commit" button that runs `git commit -m "<message>"` with the staged changes.
- **Commit & Push**: Optionally, a "Commit & Push" button for a streamlined workflow.
- **Amend last commit**: A checkbox or option to amend the previous commit (`git commit --amend`).

### 3. Visual State Indicators
- Clearly distinguish between **staged**, **unstaged**, and **untracked** files using visual grouping or color coding (e.g., green for staged, orange for modified/unstaged, gray for untracked).
- Show a badge or count of staged vs. unstaged files.

### 4. Discard Changes
- A "Discard" button per file to revert unstaged changes (`git checkout -- <file>`), with a confirmation dialog to prevent accidental data loss.

## Why This Matters

Warp already has a beautiful and functional Changes panel for viewing diffs. Adding staging and committing capabilities would:
- **Reduce context switching**: Users stay in the visual UI instead of jumping to CLI commands.
- **Lower the barrier for less CLI-savvy users**: Makes Git operations more accessible.
- **Compete with VS Code's Source Control**: Many developers rely on VS Code's Git UI for staging/committing - bringing parity here makes Warp a more complete development environment.
- **Complement the AI assistant**: Instead of asking the LLM to stage/commit, users can do it visually and more predictably.

## Reference

VS Code's Source Control panel provides a great reference implementation. Key elements to draw inspiration from:
- File-level stage/unstage buttons (`+` / `-` icons)
- Grouped sections: "Staged Changes" vs. "Changes"
- Inline commit message input + commit button
- Hunk-level staging in the diff editor

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

When working on a project in Warp, I frequently use the **Changes** panel to review diffs before committing. However, once I've reviewed my changes, I'm forced to switch back to the terminal and manually type `git add`, `git commit`, etc. - or ask the AI to do it for me.

This breaks the visual workflow. I've already *seen* the changes in a nice UI, but I can't *act* on them from that same UI. It feels like the Changes panel is "limited" when it could be so much more powerful.

In VS Code, the Source Control panel lets me stage individual files (or hunks), type a commit message, and commit - all without leaving the visual interface. This is significantly more intuitive and efficient, especially when doing partial staging (e.g., staging only some files while leaving others uncommitted).

The current workaround of typing CLI commands or prompting the LLM adds friction and slows down what should be a seamless review → stage → commit flow.

### Additional context

### Prior Art / Inspiration

- **VS Code Source Control panel**: The gold standard for visual Git workflows in an editor. Supports file-level and hunk-level staging, inline commit messages, and push/pull actions.
- **JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ, WebStorm, etc.)**: Offer a dedicated "Commit" tool window with changelists, partial commits, and pre-commit checks.
- **GitKraken / Fork / Tower**: Standalone Git GUIs that prove how valuable a visual staging + commit interface is for developer productivity.

### Suggested UX Flow

1. User opens the **Changes** panel in Warp (existing feature).
2. They see their modified files with diffs (existing behavior).
3. **New**: Each file has a `+` button to stage it, or a `-` button to unstage it.
4. **New**: A collapsible "Staged Changes" section appears at the top when files are staged.
5. **New**: A commit message text input and "Commit" button appear at the top of the panel.
6. User reviews diffs → stages desired files → types a message → clicks Commit. All within the same UI.

### Impact

This would transform the Changes panel from a passive diff viewer into an active Git workflow hub, making Warp significantly more competitive with full IDE environments while preserving its terminal-first identity.

macOS

title: Feature Request: Agent Rule Enforcement System - Prevent Agents from Ignoring Documented Rules
body:
# Feature Request: Agent Rule Enforcement System

**Submitted by:** Bryan Kaufman  
**Date:** 2026-02-02  
**Priority:** Critical  
**Category:** Agent Mode / MCP Integration

---

## Problem Statement

AI agents in Warp (including Claude) **consistently fail to check existing tools and infrastructure before creating new solutions**, despite extensive documentation and rules. This results in:
- Duplicated infrastructure
- Wasted development time
- Inconsistent implementations
- User frustration

**The core issue**: Rules documented in WARP.md and project files are suggestions that agents can (and do) ignore. There is no enforcement mechanism.

---

## Historical Evidence

### Pattern Duration
This problem has persisted for **at least 3+ months** with multiple documented attempts to resolve it through documentation alone.

### Documented Failures and Attempted Solutions

#### 1. Work Verification Framework (November 2025)
**Commit:** `4eaacdff` - "Add Work Verification Framework to prevent phantom completion documentation"

```
CRITICAL: Addresses systematic failure where work was documented as complete
without actual execution or verification.
```

**Outcome:** Documentation added, but agents still fail to verify work.

#### 2. AI Agent TODO Protocol (January 2025)
**Document:** `AI_AGENT_TODO_PROTOCOL.md`

Explicitly states:
> "All agents should check for existing TODOs before creating new ones"

**Outcome:** Rule documented but not enforced. Agents create duplicate TODOs.

#### 3. Conv-Log Check Protocol (January 2026)
**Commits:** `8fff3235`, `5b5d984d`

Added MANDATORY protocol to WARP.md:
```markdown
## 📡 CONV-LOG CHECK PROTOCOL (MANDATORY)
CHECK CONV-LOG AT THESE TRIGGER POINTS:
1. Session Start - Before doing anything else
2. Before New Task - Before executing steps
3. After Task Completion - Post status and check
```

**Outcome:** Rule documented but agents don't consistently follow it.

#### 4. Context Lookup Hierarchy (January 2026)
**Document:** WARP.md

```markdown
🎯 CONTEXT LOOKUP HIERARCHY (CRITICAL): When you need information, ALWAYS follow this order:
1. Memory System FIRST
2. Session Logs SECOND  
3. Direct Filesystem LAST RESORT
```

**Outcome:** Agents frequently skip to filesystem or create new solutions.

#### 5. Today's Failure (2026-02-02)
**Specific incident:** Agent wrote custom `curl` commands to interact with Comet Inter-AI system, when established infrastructure existed:

**Existing infrastructure (documented in `COMET_BIDIRECTIONAL_INTEGRATION.md`):**
```bash
# The CORRECT way - established protocol
conv-post warp "@comet [question]"
```

**What agent did instead:**
```bash
# Wrote custom curl commands
curl -X POST http://localhost:8765/api/send-to-comet \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt": "...", "context": "..."}'
```

The documentation existed. The MCP tools existed (`submit_prompt_to_comet`, `get_comet_responses`). The agent didn't check.

---

## Root Cause Analysis

1. **No persistent memory**: Agents don't remember rules across sessions
2. **No enforcement layer**: Rules in WARP.md are advisory, not mandatory
3. **No pre-action validation**: No check for existing tools before `create_file` or `run_shell_command`
4. **Tool discovery is optional**: `list_relevant_mcp_context` exists but isn't required

---

## Proposed Solutions

### Option A: Pre-Action Rule Enforcement (Recommended)

Add a system-level enforcement layer that:

1. **Before `create_file` for scripts/tools:**
   - Automatically call `list_relevant_mcp_context` with relevant query
   - Show agent what tools already exist
   - Require explicit acknowledgment before proceeding

2. **Before `run_shell_command` for new tool creation:**
   - Check if similar tools exist in MCP registry
   - Warn if duplicating existing infrastructure

3. **Session start mandatory context:**
   - Auto-load WARP.md critical sections
   - Force reading of project-specific rules before any action

### Option B: Rule Priority System

Allow users to mark rules with enforcement levels:

```markdown
<!-- WARP-ENFORCE: MANDATORY -->
## Check MCP Tools First
Before creating any new script or tool, run:
`list_relevant_mcp_context` with relevant query
<!-- /WARP-ENFORCE -->
```

Rules marked MANDATORY would:
- Be auto-injected into agent context at session start
- Trigger validation checks before related actions
- Generate warnings/blocks if violated

### Option C: MCP Tool Discovery Phase

Add a required "discovery phase" before agent actions:

1. User requests task
2. **System automatically** enumerates relevant MCP tools
3. Agent sees available tools before planning
4. If agent creates duplicate tool, system warns

---

## Impact

**Without enforcement:**
- Users spend hours re-documenting rules that agents ignore
- Infrastructure gets duplicated across projects
- Trust in agent capabilities erodes
- Users consider switching to other solutions

**With enforcement:**
- Rules actually get followed
- Existing infrastructure gets used
- Development time saved
- User trust maintained

---

## Supporting Files

These files document the attempts to solve this problem through documentation:

- `~/.unified-mcp-manager/WARP.md` - Main rules file (746 lines of protocols)
- `~/.unified-mcp-manager/docs/AI_AGENT_TODO_PROTOCOL.md` - TODO management rules
- `~/.unified-mcp-manager/inter-ai/COMET_BIDIRECTIONAL_INTEGRATION.md` - Integration docs ignored today
- `~/.unified-mcp-manager/PROJECT_JOURNAL.md` - History of infrastructure creation

---

## Request

Please consider implementing agent rule enforcement at the Warp system level. Documentation-only approaches have been tried extensively and do not work. The agent needs guardrails, not suggestions.

---

**Contact:** bryankaufman@mac.com

### Describe the bug

When typing Japanese with IME in composition mode (未確定状態), pressing **Ctrl+H** causes **double character deletion** when Warp's keybindings are enabled.

**Note**: The regular **Backspace key works correctly** (deletes only 1 character as expected). This issue is specific to **Ctrl+H**.

### Detailed Behavior

#### Case 1: Warp keybinding for Ctrl+H is **disabled**
- Result: **1 character deleted** (expected behavior - IME handles it correctly)

#### Case 2: Warp keybinding for Ctrl+H is **enabled** (default)
- Result: **2 characters deleted** (bug!)
  - 1st deletion: IME processes Ctrl+H and deletes 1 character from composition
  - 2nd deletion: Warp's keybinding also processes Ctrl+H and deletes 1 more character

#### Case 3: Using regular **Backspace key** (during composition)
- Result: **1 character deleted** (works correctly!)
- This confirms the issue is specific to Ctrl+H keybinding

#### Case 4: Using **Ctrl+H** **after** confirming/committing text (composition ended)
- Result: **1 character deleted** (works correctly!)
- This confirms the issue only occurs **during active composition**

### To reproduce

1. Open Warp terminal
2. Ensure Ctrl+H keybinding is enabled (default state)
3. Switch to Japanese input mode (e.g., Hiragana)
4. Type Japanese characters: `あいうえお` (do NOT press Enter - keep it in composition mode with underline)
5. Press Ctrl+H
6. **Expected**: 1 character deleted (`あいうえ` remains)
7. **Actual**: 2 characters deleted (`あいう` remains)

### Expected behavior

During IME composition (`hasMarkedText` is true), Warp should:
1. Let the IME handle the Ctrl+H keypress exclusively
2. NOT trigger Warp's own keybinding for Ctrl+H
3. This is how macOS Terminal.app behaves correctly

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

_No response_

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

### Operating system and version

Sequoia 15.6.1

### Shell Version

zsh 5.9 (arm64-apple-darwin24.0)

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.01.21.08.14.stable_03

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Recent working Warp date

_No response_

### Additional context

- This issue **only occurs during active composition** (未確定状態 - when characters have underline). 
- After pressing Enter to commit/confirm the characters, Ctrl+H works normally (deletes 1 character as expected).
- **Workaround**: Use the regular Backspace key instead of Ctrl+H during Japanese input, or disable Ctrl+H keybinding in Warp settings.

#### Technical Analysis
This appears to be an issue with NSTextInputClient implementation. When `hasMarkedText()` returns true (composition in progress), keyboard events should be passed to the IME system first, and Warp's keybinding system should NOT process them.

The fact that:
- **Backspace key works correctly during composition** ✅
- **Ctrl+H works correctly after composition ends** ✅
- **Ctrl+H fails only during active composition** ❌

suggests that Warp's keybinding system is not checking composition state (`hasMarkedText`) before processing Ctrl+H events.


### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

Yes, this issue prevents me from using Warp daily.

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

title: Dynamic Tab Color Coding Based on Execution Status
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

**Summary**
Color-code terminal tabs in real time to reflect the current execution state of the running process, making it immediately obvious - at a glance - what is happening across multiple sessions.

---

**The Problem**

When working with several tabs simultaneously, it's easy to lose track of what's happening where. Right now, all tabs look identical regardless of whether a long build is still running, a test suite just failed, or a deployment finished successfully. You end up clicking between tabs just to check status - a constant context-switch tax.

---

**Proposed Behaviour**

Each tab's background (or left-border accent) would shift colour to reflect its current state:

| State | Suggested Colour | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Idle / Ready | Default (no change) | Shell prompt returned |
| Running | 🔵 Blue | Process actively executing |
| Success | 🟢 Green | Exit code `0` |
| Warning | 🟡 Amber | Exit code non-zero but < 128 (e.g. partial failures, lint warnings) |
| Error / Failed | 🔴 Red | Exit code ≥ 128, or specific known codes (e.g. `1`, `2`) |
| Awaiting Input | 🟣 Purple | Process blocking on stdin (e.g. prompts, interactive confirmation) |
| Long-running | 🟠 Orange | Process exceeds a user-defined time threshold (e.g. > 2 min) |

---


### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

_No response_

### Additional context

**Example Scenarios**


*Scenario 1 - Parallel builds:*
You're running `cargo build` in tab 1, `npm run test` in tab 2, and `docker compose up` in tab 3. Tab 2 turns green immediately (tests passed), tab 3 stays blue (containers still starting), and tab 1 flips red - you know instantly where to look without switching away from your current work.

*Scenario 2 - Deployment pipeline:*
You kick off a Terraform apply in one tab and a database migration in another. The migration tab turns amber (warnings emitted, exit code 1 from a skipped migration), while Terraform stays blue. The colour difference prompts you to investigate the migration before continuing.

*Scenario 3 - Awaiting input:*
An `apt upgrade` in a background tab pauses on a `[Y/n]` prompt. The tab turns purple, signalling that your input is needed - rather than silently hanging unnoticed.

*Scenario 4 - Long-running process alert:*
A test suite you expected to finish in 30 seconds is still running after 2 minutes. The tab shifts from blue to orange, flagging a potential hang without requiring you to watch it.


**Implementation Considerations**

- **Theming support:** colours should be fully customisable in Warp's theme system, so they don't clash with dark/light themes or accessibility needs.
- **Intensity options:** offer a subtle mode (left-border accent only) and a bold mode (full tab background tint) for users who prefer less visual noise.
- **Threshold configuration:** the long-running orange threshold should be configurable per-tab or globally in settings.
- **Fade on focus:** when a tab is actively selected, the colour could fade slightly to reduce visual noise while still being visible in the tab strip.
- **Notification integration:** optionally pair with Warp's existing notification system so that a tab turning red also triggers a system alert if the window is unfocused.

### Describe the bug

the gitmoji `🧑💻` (technologist, `U+1F9D1 U+200D U+1F4BB`) renders as two separate emoji, 🧑 followed by 💻, instead of a single combined glyph. the `U+200D` ZWJ (zero width joiner) codepoint between them is silently discarded instead of fusing the sequence.

this is distinct from the emoji presentation selector (`U+FE0F`) work done in #2304. ZWJ sequences are a separate unicode mechanism defined in the [emoji ZWJ sequence catalog](https://unicode.org/emoji/charts/emoji-zwj-sequences.html). this is also **not a font issue**. both component glyphs render fine individually; the problem is that warp does not recognize `U+200D` as a joiner that merges adjacent emoji into a single grapheme cluster.

`🧑💻` is used by the [gitmoji](https://gitmoji.dev/) convention for "improve developer experience" commits, so it shows up constantly in `git log` output for projects that follow this convention.

### To reproduce

```sh
echo '🧑💻'
git log --oneline  # in any repo using gitmoji
```

### Expected behavior

`🧑💻` should display as a single glyph, as it does in iTerm2, kitty, Terminal.app, and every modern browser.

title: BUG: Clicking unfocused title/tab bar unsnaps window from FancyZones (PowerToys)
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there

### Describe the bug

When Warp is snapped to a PowerToys FancyZones zone and the window does **not** have focus, clicking on the **title bar or tab bar** causes the window to unsnap from the zone and restore its original (pre-snap) size and position.

**Clicking inside the terminal/editor content area of an unfocused Warp window does NOT trigger the problem.** The bug is isolated to the title bar and tab bar area.

### To Reproduce

1. Snap Warp to a FancyZones zone (e.g. using Shift+drag).
2. Click on another application to move focus away from Warp.
3. Click on Warp's **title bar or one of its tabs** to bring Warp back into focus.
4. Observe: Warp leaves the FancyZones zone and restores its pre-snap size/position.

Clicking in the **terminal content area** in step 3 does not reproduce the issue - Warp gains focus and stays in the zone.

### Expected Behavior

Clicking the title bar or a tab to focus the window should not trigger an unsnap. The window should remain in its FancyZones zone.

### Root Cause Hypothesis

Warp renders its title bar and tab bar as a custom GPU overlay rather than as a standard Windows non-client area (`HTCAPTION`). This means the OS treats clicks differently depending on where they land:

- **Content area click** → `WM_LBUTTONDOWN` (client area) - standard focus acquisition, no window-move messages emitted → FancyZones is unaffected.
- **Title/tab bar click** → `WM_NCLBUTTONDOWN` (non-client area) - Warp's custom handler processes it (e.g., switches the active tab) and appears to emit a spurious `WM_MOVE` / `WM_SIZE` or briefly reposition the window. FancyZones interprets this as an intentional drag out of the zone and unsnaps the window.

The same mechanism caused issue #1627 on macOS with Rectangle (now closed/fixed): tab clicks generated micro-drags that triggered Rectangle's unsnap logic. The fix there was on the Warp side.

**FancyZones configuration in use (does not prevent the bug):**
- "Hold Shift key to activate zones while dragging" - ✅ enabled
- "Keep windows in their zones when the screen resolution changes" - ✅ enabled

### Related Issues

- #1627 - identical behavior on macOS with Rectangle window manager (closed as fixed)
- #7941 - Windows snap regression (different symptom: drag-to-snap fails entirely)

title: File tree subtree builder scans gitignored directories (node_modules, .next) before applying gitignore filter, causing excessive resource usage
body:
## File tree subtree builder scans gitignored directories (node_modules, .next) before applying gitignore filter, causing excessive resource usage

### Description

Warp's file tree / project explorer appears to traverse directories **before** applying `.gitignore` exclusion rules. This causes thousands of `Failed to build subtree` warnings when working with projects that use pnpm (which creates extensive symlink trees inside `node_modules`).

Even though `node_modules/` and `.next/` are listed in `.gitignore` and correctly hidden from the file tree UI, the underlying subtree builder still attempts to walk into these directories and resolve their symlinks.

### Environment

- **Warp version**: v0.2026.02.18.08.22.stable_02
- **OS**: macOS 26.3 (Darwin 25.3.0), Apple Silicon
- **Package manager**: pnpm (uses symlinks extensively inside `node_modules/.pnpm/`)
- **Project structure**: monorepo with multiple git worktrees

### Reproduction

1. Create a monorepo using pnpm (e.g., Next.js + multiple packages)
2. Run `pnpm install` so `node_modules/.pnpm/` is populated with symlinks
3. Optionally run `next build` to generate `.next/standalone/` (which also contains `node_modules` with symlinks)
4. Create multiple git worktrees, each with their own `node_modules`
5. Open Warp and navigate to the worktree directories
6. Observe `warp.log` (`~/Library/Logs/warp.log`)

### Evidence from logs

On a single day, `warp.log` recorded **2,851 `Failed to build subtree` warnings**, with **2,629 concentrated in a single hour**.

Sample log entries:

```
2026-02-24T00:31:53Z [WARN] Failed to build subtree for directory ".../node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/react": Symlink
2026-02-24T00:31:53Z [WARN] Failed to build subtree for directory ".../node_modules/.pnpm/next@15.5.7_.../node_modules/react": Symlink
2026-02-24T00:31:53Z [WARN] Failed to build subtree for directory ".../node_modules/.pnpm/styled-jsx@5.1.6_.../node_modules/client-only": Symlink
2026-02-24T00:31:53Z [WARN] Failed to build subtree for directory ".../node_modules/.pnpm/react-dom@19.1.2_.../node_modules/react": Symlink
```

All 2,851 warnings target paths inside `node_modules/` or `.next/standalone/node_modules/` - directories that are in `.gitignore` and should never be scanned.

### Why pnpm makes this worse

pnpm uses a content-addressable store with symlinks to represent package dependencies:

```
node_modules/.pnpm/next@15.5.7_.../node_modules/
  next/              ← actual package
  react -> ../../react@19.1.2/node_modules/react          ← symlink
  postcss -> ../../postcss@8.4.31/node_modules/postcss     ← symlink
  styled-jsx -> ../../styled-jsx@5.1.6_.../node_modules/.. ← symlink
```

Each package has symlinks to its dependencies, creating a deep graph. When the subtree builder walks into `node_modules/.pnpm/`, it encounters hundreds of symlinks, each triggering a warning.

### Why git worktrees make this worse

Each worktree has its own `node_modules/` (created by `pnpm install`). With N worktrees, the scanning is multiplied N times. In our case, 2 active worktrees with `node_modules` + `.next/standalone` = thousands of unnecessary scan attempts.

### Expected behavior

Directories matching `.gitignore` patterns (e.g., `node_modules/`, `.next/`) should be **skipped entirely** during the subtree building phase - not just filtered from the UI display.

### Suggested fix

Apply `.gitignore` exclusion rules **before** (or at the entry point of) directory traversal in the subtree builder, so that gitignored directories are never entered or scanned. This would:

1. Eliminate all `Failed to build subtree` warnings for gitignored paths
2. Reduce memory usage and CPU overhead from scanning large symlink trees
3. Improve performance for pnpm-based monorepos with multiple worktrees

### Workaround

Currently the only workarounds are:
- Close the file tree panel when not needed
- Delete unused worktrees to reduce scan targets
- Set `AgentModeCodebaseContextAutoIndexing` to `false` (disables Agent context indexing)

title: Feature Request: HUD / Status Bar for AI Token & Context Window Usage
body:
## Describe the solution you'd like

A persistent HUD or status bar element that displays real-time AI session metrics, including:

1. **Context window usage** - how much of the current context window has been consumed (e.g., 45,000 / 128,000 tokens), similar to Claude Code's context bar
2. **Token consumption** - input/output tokens used in the current session
3. **Remaining capacity** - visual indicator (progress bar or percentage) of how much context is left before truncation occurs
4. **AI request count** - requests used vs. plan limit (e.g., 142 / 500 requests)

## The core problem: context engineering is impossible without visibility

**Claude Code already solves this.** It shows a visible context usage bar that lets users see exactly how much of the context window has been consumed. When context gets full, users can make an informed choice - compact the conversation, start fresh, or continue knowing the tradeoff. This makes context engineering practical.

**In Warp, context engineering is essentially impossible right now.** Here's what actually happens:

1. You start a complex task (e.g., multi-file refactoring with verification)
2. The agent reads files, makes plans, executes changes - context fills up silently
3. At some point, the agent starts **getting dumber** - forgetting earlier instructions, repeating mistakes, losing track of the plan
4. You have **no way to know** if this is because:
   - The context window overflowed and earlier messages were silently dropped
   - The conversation summary lost critical details
   - The model is just having a bad response
   - You hit a token limit

**Without visibility, you can't control it.** You can't decide when to start a new conversation. You can't judge whether attaching another file will push critical earlier context out. You can't tell if the agent's degraded behavior is fixable by rephrasing or if it's a context saturation issue that requires a fresh session.

The agent progressively degrades and there's **zero signal** to distinguish context overflow from other issues. This is the #1 frustration for power users.

## Why the current \i\ chip is insufficient

The \i\ chip added in #5993 (45 upvotes) was a step forward, but only partially addresses the need:

- Shows only the **latest request cost**, not cumulative session usage
- **Disappears** once you continue the conversation
- No visibility into **context window saturation**
- No persistent counter for **remaining plan quota**

## Why this matters

- **Context engineering** is the single most important skill for getting good results from AI agents. You can't engineer what you can't see.
- **Cost awareness**: Power users running multiple agents in parallel need visibility into resource consumption.
- **Self-correction loops**: Agents entering bug-fix loops silently burn through tokens/context. A visible indicator lets users interrupt early. (See #6340 - 8 upvotes, still open)
- **Larger context windows make this worse**: As models move to 1M+ context (#7156), sessions will run longer and silent degradation becomes even harder to detect.

## Suggested implementation

Could be as simple as any of:
- A collapsible section in the existing **Agent Management Panel** (top-right)
- A **status bar item** (similar to VS Code's bottom bar)
- A small **overlay/badge** on the AI input area showing context % used
- An opt-in setting in **Settings > AI** for users who want detailed metrics

## Prior art

- **Claude Code**: context usage progress bar - simple, effective, always visible
- **ChatGPT**: shows model context limit in conversation
- **Cursor**: token counter in status bar

## Related issues

- #5993 - Need AI Request / Token counter (👍45, closed with partial fix)
- #6340 - Token limit exceeded error (👍8, open)
- #7156 - Support for 1M context window (👍5, open)

---

title: Shift+Enter sends CR (0x0d) instead of LF (0x0a) in alt screen + mouse mode

## Description

Shift+Enter normally sends `0x0a` (LF), which is how TUI apps distinguish it from Enter (`0x0d`/CR). In Warp, when an app enables alternate screen + mouse tracking (`\x1b[?1049h` + `\x1b[?1003h`), Shift+Enter starts sending `0x0d` instead - making it identical to Enter.

This breaks multi-line input in every TUI app that uses alt screen + mouse mode (Bubble Tea, Claude Code, Textual, etc.).

## Repro

https://github.com/sns45/warp-shift-enter-bug

```bash
go build -o repro . && ./repro
```

Two phases - press Enter, Shift+Enter, Space in each:

- **Phase 1 (normal mode)** - Shift+Enter correctly sends `0x0a` ✅
- **Phase 2 (alt screen + mouse)** - Shift+Enter incorrectly sends `0x0d` ❌

## Expected

Shift+Enter sends `0x0a` (LF) in both phases, regardless of terminal mode.

## Actual

Phase 2 output in Warp:
```
[altscreen+mouse] key 1: bytes=0x0d  → CR (0x0d) - Enter
[altscreen+mouse] key 2: bytes=0x0d  → CR (0x0d) - Enter        ← BUG: should be 0x0a
[altscreen+mouse] key 3: bytes=0x20  → Space
```

## Comparison

Tested side-by-side with iTerm2 - both phases correctly show `0x0a` for Shift+Enter. This is a Warp-only issue.

## Environment

- **Terminal:** Warp (latest)
- **OS:** macOS
- **Escape sequences involved:** `\x1b[?1049h` (alt screen) + `\x1b[?1003h` (mouse cell motion tracking)

body: ### Pre-submit Checks - [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates - [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there - [ ] I have an issue with AI and have included the debugging ID (Optional, but helps expedite the AI quality fix). [Log instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/troubleshooting-and-support/sending-us-feedback#gathering-warp-logs) ### Describe the bug ## Font rendering fails ("Failed to get raster image") when displaying emoji characters on Linux (Wayland + Intel GPU) ### Environment - **Warp version**: v0.2026.02.25.08.24.stable_01 - **OS**: Manjaro Linux (Arch-based), kernel 6.12.73-1-MANJARO - **Display server**: Wayland - **GPU**: Intel RPL-S (integrated), Vulkan backend - **GPU driver**: Mesa 25.3.5, vulkan-intel 25.3.5 - **Font**: Hack, 14pt - **Related packages**: freetype2 2.14.1, harfbuzz 12.3.2, noto-fonts-emoji 2.051 ### Bug Description Warp fails to render glyphs when the terminal content contains emoji characters (e.g. ✅ ❌ 🚫). The log is flooded with: ``` [WARN] Unable to get glyph out of glyph cache: Failed to get raster image, Glyph { glyph_key: GlyphKey { glyph_id: 8227, font_id: FontId(26), font_size: OrderedFloat(14.0) }, ... } ``` Also at startup: ``` [WARN] Failed to load a font face 0 from source cause font doesn't have a family name ``` ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Have `noto-fonts-emoji` installed (provides NotoColorEmoji.ttf - the standard emoji font on most Linux distros) 2. Open Warp on Wayland 3. Open any file containing emoji characters in vim (or cat): ```bash echo "✅ ❌ 🚫 test" > /tmp/test-emoji.txt vim /tmp/test-emoji.txt ``` ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1e6e1ef-37d0-4d65-a3ae-a5437e07788d) 4. Observe broken rendering and warning spam in logs ### Root Cause Analysis Through binary-search debugging, I narrowed the issue down from vim plugins → specific files → **emoji characters in file content**. The rendering pipeline is: **fontdb → cosmic_text → swash (rasterizer) → wgpu** NotoColorEmoji.ttf uses **CBDT/CBLC** tables (color bitmap format). The `swash` crate's rasterizer cannot produce raster images from CBDT bitmap glyphs - it returns a failure, which surfaces as "Failed to get raster image". When cosmic_text's fallback logic encounters a character not in the primary font (Hack), it walks the system font list and lands on NotoColorEmoji for emoji codepoints. Since swash can't rasterize CBDT bitmaps, every emoji glyph fails. ### Workaround Disabling NotoColorEmoji at the filesystem level resolves the issue: ```bash sudo mv /usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoColorEmoji.ttf /usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoColorEmoji.ttf.disabled sudo fc-cache -fv ``` Note: simply using fontconfig `` rules does **not** work - Warp/fontdb appears to load fonts by scanning directories obtained from `FcConfigGetFontDirs`, bypassing fontconfig's reject/accept filtering. ### What does NOT fix the issue - Switching font to Hack Nerd Font Mono - Switching `WGPU_BACKEND=gl` - Setting `FREETYPE_PROPERTIES="truetype:interpreter-version=35"` - fontconfig `` for Noto Color Emoji - Clearing font caches (`fc-cache -fv`, `rm -rf ~/.cache/fontconfig/*`) ### Expected Behavior Emoji characters should either: 1. Be rendered correctly (by supporting CBDT/CBLC rasterization in the text pipeline), or 2. ### Describe the solution you'd like?

I'd like Warp to support a Multi-root Workspace concept, similar to VS Code's "Add Folder to Workspace" feature.

1. **Unified File Tree** - The File Tree (Project Explorer) should display multiple root folders simultaneously, rather than being limited to a single working directory. Users can "Add Folder to Workspace" to include additional project roots.

2. **Worktree-aware discovery** - Since Warp already has excellent Git Worktree support, it would be natural to offer a "Add all worktrees to workspace" action that auto-discovers worktrees via `git worktree list` and adds them as roots in the File Tree.

3. **Per-root context** - Each root folder maintains its own Git status, Code Review panel, and Codebase Context indexing (which Warp already does per-worktree today). The workspace just provides a unified view on top.

4. **Workspace persistence** - Save/restore workspace configurations (which folders are included), similar to how Launch Configurations already save window/tab/pane layouts.

Example workflow:

git worktree add ../my-repo-feature-a feature-a
git worktree add ../my-repo-hotfix hotfix-b

Then in Warp: right-click File Tree → "Add Folder to Workspace" → the File Tree shows:

WORKSPACE
├── my-repo (main)
├── my-repo-feature-a (feature-a)
└── my-repo-hotfix (hotfix-b)

Each root has its own Code Review, Git status chip, and Agent context - all visible within one window

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I'm always frustrated when working across multiple worktrees or related projects - Warp's File Tree only shows one directory at a time. I end up either constantly switching tabs and losing track of which maps to which branch, or opening the parent directory which pollutes the File Tree with unrelated folders.

This would also benefit non-worktree use cases: monorepo sub-projects, frontend + backend in separate repos, etc.

### Additional context

- VS Code reference: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/multi-root-workspaces

title: Warp freezes at 100% CPU / 19GB RAM in code review diff view
body:
### Describe the bug

After running for ~2 days, Warp locks up completely - 100% CPU on the main process and **19.1 GB physical memory footprint**. The app becomes unresponsive and must be force-killed.

A 5-second CPU sample shows the main thread is stuck in a tight loop inside the **code review / diff view** reactivity system:

```
flush_effects → subscribe_to_model (CodeReviewView::create_code_review_model_with_global_buffer)
  → RefCounts::inc_entity / RefCounts::dec_model
```

This looks like a runaway ref-counting cycle in `warpui_core`'s effect/subscription system - `inc_entity` and `dec_model` are spinning on the main thread with no exit, burning 100% CPU indefinitely.

### To reproduce

1. Open Warp and use the built-in code review / diff view features
2. Leave Warp running for an extended period (~2 days in my case)
3. Eventually, Warp becomes completely unresponsive
4. `ps aux` shows the process at 100% CPU; `sample` confirms the stack trace above

Exact trigger is unclear - it may be related to a long-lived session with code review state accumulating over time.

### Expected behavior

Warp should remain responsive regardless of session duration, and the code review model subscriptions should not enter an infinite ref-counting loop.

title: Korean IME: Last composing character is dropped when pressing Enter
body:
## Bug Description

When typing Korean text in Warp, the last character being composed by the Korean IME is dropped/lost when pressing Enter.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Warp terminal
2. Run any interactive CLI app (e.g., `claude`, `gemini`)
3. Switch to Korean input method
4. Type "안녕하세요" (Korean for "hello")
5. Press Enter immediately

## Expected Behavior

The full text "안녕하세요" is submitted.

## Actual Behavior

Only "안녕하세" is submitted - the last character "요" is dropped because it was still in IME composing (pre-edit) state when Enter was pressed.

## Root Cause Analysis

When Enter is pressed, Warp sends the Enter keypress to the PTY **before** committing the IME pre-edit text. Native macOS apps (Safari, Notes, etc.) commit the composing character first, then process Enter. Warp skips this IME commit step.

## Environment

- **Warp version:** 0.62.2
- **OS:** macOS Darwin 25.3.0 (Apple Silicon, M1 Pro)
- **Input method:** macOS default Korean IME
- **Affected CLI apps:** Claude Code, Gemini CLI (any app reading from PTY)

## Workaround

Pressing the right arrow key (→) before Enter forces the IME to commit the composing character.

## Notes

- English input is **NOT** affected (no composition step)
- Native macOS apps are **NOT** affected (they handle IME commit properly)
- This is **NOT** specific to any CLI app - it affects all PTY-reading applications running inside Warp
- Related issues: #8786, #8736, #3127 (Korean/Japanese IME issues, but different symptoms)

title: Repeated SIGABRT crash in GridHandler::resize (InitialCursorState::into_content_offset unwrap panic)
body:
## Description

Warp crashes repeatedly with `SIGABRT` due to a Rust panic in the terminal grid resize path. The crash occurs when the terminal view layout triggers a resize operation, and `InitialCursorState::into_content_offset` encounters an unexpected `Err` value that is `unwrap()`-ed.

This is **highly reproducible** - 8 crashes recorded over the past week, with 7/8 sharing the exact same stack trace. On April 4th alone, Warp crashed **6 times**.

## Environment

- **Warp version**: 0.2026.03.25.08.24.05 (Stable)
- **OS**: macOS 26.3.1 (Build 25D771280a)
- **Hardware**: MacBook Pro, Apple M3, 8 GB RAM
- **Architecture**: ARM-64 (native, not translated)

## Crash Stack Trace (faulting thread 0)

All crashes share this identical call chain:

```
 0  libsystem_kernel.dylib       __pthread_kill
 1  libsystem_pthread.dylib      pthread_kill
 2  libsystem_c.dylib            abort
 3  stable                       std::sys::pal::unix::abort_internal
 4  stable                       std::process::abort
 5  stable                       rust_panic
 6  stable                       std::panicking::panic_with_hook
 7  stable                       std::panicking::panic_handler
 8  stable                       std::sys::backtrace::__rust_end_short_backtrace
 9  stable                       rust_begin_unwind
10  stable                       core::panicking::panic_fmt
11  stable                       core::result::unwrap_failed          ← unwrap on Err
12  stable                       warp::terminal::model::grid::grid_handler::resize::InitialCursorState::into_content_offset
13  stable                       warp::terminal::model::grid::grid_handler::resize::GridHandler::resize_storage
14  stable                       warp::terminal::model::grid::grid_handler::resize::GridHandler::resize
15  stable                       warp::terminal::model::blocks::BlockList::resize
16  stable                       warp::terminal::model::terminal_model::TerminalModel::resize
17  stable                       warp::terminal::view::TerminalView::resize_internal
18  stable                       warp::terminal::view::TerminalView::after_terminal_view_layout
```

## Crash Timeline

| Timestamp | Crash file |
|-----------|-----------|
| 2026-03-29 20:42 | stable-2026-03-29-204208.ips |
| 2026-04-02 21:44 | stable-2026-04-02-214416.ips |
| 2026-04-04 16:22 | stable-2026-04-04-162222.ips |
| 2026-04-04 16:57 | stable-2026-04-04-165702.ips |
| 2026-04-04 17:00 | stable-2026-04-04-165959.ips |
| 2026-04-04 17:01 | stable-2026-04-04-170142.ips |
| 2026-04-04 17:12 | stable-2026-04-04-171234.ips |
| 2026-04-04 17:12 | stable-2026-04-04-171242.ips |

## Suspected Trigger

The crash appears to be triggered by **terminal resize events** - possibly from:
- Window resizing
- Stage Manager view transitions
- Split view changes
- External display connect/disconnect

title: edit_files tool fails to match strings containing Unicode characters (em-dashes, emoji) on Windows
body:
## Bug: edit_files tool fails to match strings containing Unicode characters (em-dashes, emoji) on Windows

### Description

The `edit_files` agent tool frequently fails to match search strings that contain Unicode characters like em-dashes (U+2014 -), arrows (U+2192 →), and emoji (U+1F916 🤖) on Windows. The tool returns "Could not apply all diffs" even when the search string exactly matches the file content.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a markdown file containing em-dashes: `- **#166** - Some description - more text`
2. Use `edit_files` with a search string containing that exact line
3. The tool fails with "Could not apply all diffs"
4. The same edit succeeds when the search string contains only ASCII characters

### Expected behavior

`edit_files` should match Unicode strings in file content on Windows, the same as it does on macOS/Linux.

### Observed behavior

- Em-dash (-) in search strings causes match failures ~50% of the time
- Emoji (🤖) in search strings causes match failures consistently
- Workaround: use PowerShell scripts with `[System.IO.File]::ReadAllText` and `.Replace()`, but PS 5.x cannot handle surrogate pairs (emoji) via `[char]`
- Splitting edits into smaller batches sometimes helps (suggesting the issue is related to string length + Unicode interaction)

### Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11
- **Shell:** PowerShell 5.1.26100.7920
- **Warp version:** Latest stable (2026-04-06)
- **File encoding:** UTF-8 without BOM

### Additional context

This was observed during a roadmap refresh session editing `ROADMAP.md` (~375 lines) which uses em-dashes extensively. 5 consecutive `edit_files` calls failed on lines containing em-dashes. The issue appears to be in the tool's string matching, not in the file encoding itself (the file reads correctly, and the content is valid UTF-8).

title: U+23F8 (PAUSED SYMBOL) renders as color emoji even with U+FE0E text variation selector appended
body:
## Environment
- Warp version: `v0.2026.03.25.08.24.stable_09` (Stable channel)
- OS: Windows 10 (10.0.19045)
- Active font: Hack Nerd Font Mono

## Summary
Warp renders U+23F8 ⏸ (PAUSED SYMBOL) as a colored emoji regardless of whether the Unicode text variation selector U+FE0E is appended. Per UTS #51 and the Unicode Standard, a base character followed by U+FE0E must be rendered in text presentation style - i.e., monochrome, from a text font. Warp appears to unconditionally route U+23F8 to a color emoji font.

## Reproduction
In a Warp session, run:

\`\`\`bash
printf 'bare:  \xe2\x8f\xb8\ntext:  \xe2\x8f\xb8\xef\xb8\x8e\nemoji: \xe2\x8f\xb8\xef\xb8\x8f\n'
\`\`\`

**Expected:**
- \`text:\` line renders a monochrome pause glyph from the primary text font.
- \`emoji:\` line renders the color emoji.
- \`bare:\` line follows the default presentation for U+23F8.

**Actual in Warp:** all three lines render identically as the color emoji.

## Comparison
VS Code's integrated terminal, Windows Terminal, and Alacritty all honor U+FE0E on U+23F8 and render the \`text:\` line as a monochrome glyph.

## Context
This surfaced while using Claude Code (Anthropic's CLI), which uses U+23F8 as its plan-mode status indicator. In every other terminal the indicator is a subtle monochrome bar; in Warp it's a large blue emoji that clashes with the rest of the monospace UI. Patching Claude Code's bundle to append U+FE0E after the character did not change Warp's rendering - only a full character swap worked as a workaround.

## Request
Honor U+FE0E as a hard override to text presentation, at least for dual-presentation codepoints in the Miscellaneous Technical block (U+2300-U+23FF). This is Unicode-conformant behavior and matches every other terminal I have tested.

title: Feature request: Support OSC 99 desktop notifications
body:
### Summary

It would be great to see Warp add support for the OSC 99 desktop notification protocol alongside the existing OSC 9 and OSC 777 support. OSC 99 is a newer, structured notification standard that would enable richer notification UX on top of Warp's already excellent notification pipeline.

### Background

Warp currently supports two notification protocols:
- **OSC 9** (thanks for the recent addition in #7896!) - body only
- **OSC 777** - title + body, used by `warpdotdev/claude-code-warp` and others

Both are lightweight and unidirectional. OSC 99 is a more modern protocol originally proposed by kitty ([spec(https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/desktop-notifications/)) and since adopted by kitty, foot, ghostty, and contour. A quick comparison:

| Feature | OSC 9 / 777 | OSC 99 |
|---|---|---|
| Structured metadata (ID, urgency, icon, actions) | ❌ | ✅ |
| Notification update by ID (replace in-place) | ❌ | ✅ |
| Bidirectional click / dismiss events | ❌ | ✅ |
| Standard String Terminator (`ESC \`) | ❌ (BEL) | ✅ |
| Multi-sequence composition | ❌ | ✅ |

### Why it would be valuable

Warp's notification system already looks great - the revamped UI in `v0.2026.04.08` and the Claude Code / OpenCode integration are wonderful to use. OSC 99 would add a few things on top that aren't possible with OSC 9 or OSC 777:

1. **Click-to-focus** - applications could be notified when the user clicks a notification, enabling workflows like "jump back to the task that completed." The bidirectional response channel is the main architectural difference from OSC 777.
2. **In-place updates** - long-running tasks could update a single notification (e.g. "Build 50%" → "Build 100% ✓") instead of spamming new ones, using stable notification IDs.
3. **Richer metadata** - urgency levels, icons, and action buttons give applications more expressive control over how important events are surfaced.
4. **Ecosystem alignment** - kitty, foot, ghostty, and contour already support OSC 99. Adopting it would let CLI tools target a single modern standard instead of juggling fallbacks across terminals.
5. **Better multiplexer compatibility** - as a small side benefit, some terminal multiplexers have started forwarding OSC 99 specifically (while dropping unknown OSCs like 777 for safety reasons). Supporting OSC 99 in Warp would naturally unlock notifications for users running Warp with a multiplexer underneath, without any changes on their side.

### Possible phased approach

I realize this is a larger protocol than OSC 9/777, so I wanted to suggest a minimal starting point that might be easier to scope:

**Phase 1 (minimum useful):** Accept OSC 99 `create` sequences with `p=title` and `p=body` payloads, and render them via the existing notification pipeline. Ignore unknown metadata fields gracefully. This alone would let Warp render OSC 99 notifications from any compliant CLI tool.

**Phase 2 (optional, larger win):** Bidirectional events - emit ANSI responses for click and dismiss back to the originating PTY. This is what enables the click-to-focus UX and is the feature that differentiates OSC 99 from the existing protocols.

**Phase 3 (down the road):** Notification update / close by ID.

Even Phase 1 would be a meaningful improvement, and I'd be happy with just that.

### References

- [Kitty OSC 99 specification (canonical)](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/desktop-notifications/)
- [warpdotdev/Warp #7896 - OSC 9 support (closed)](https://github.com/warpdotdev/Warp/issues/7896) - same spirit, predecessor issue
- [ghostty discussion #4405 - OSC 99 adoption](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/4405)

### Environment

- Warp `v0.2026.04.08.08.36.stable_02`
- macOS

---

Thanks so much for all the work on notifications recently - the new UI and Claude Code integration have made a big difference. This would be a nice next step if it's within scope, and I'm happy to help test or provide more details if that's useful.
labels: enhancement; triaged; os:mac; area:agent; area:shell-terminal; area:ui-framework

title: MCP OAuth: Warp appends ?server_id= to redirect_uri, breaking RFC 6749 compliance
body:
## Bug Description

When connecting to an MCP server that uses OAuth (RFC 9728), Warp appends a `?server_id=...` query parameter to the `redirect_uri` in the authorization request. This breaks OAuth servers that use exact string matching on redirect URIs, which is the recommended behavior per [RFC 6749 §3.1.2.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.1.2.2).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an MCP server with OAuth in Warp Settings → MCP:
   ```json
   {"serverUrl": "https://example.com/mcp"}
   ```
2. The MCP server's `/oauth/register` endpoint returns:
   ```json
   {"redirect_uris": ["warp://mcp/oauth2callback"]}
   ```
3. Warp constructs the authorize URL with:
   ```
   redirect_uri=warp%3A%2F%2Fmcp%2Foauth2callback%3Fserver_id%3D65aebdca-613a-4b60-97d3-92548673bd03
   ```
4. The OAuth server rejects with `unknown_redirect_uri` because `warp://mcp/oauth2callback?server_id=....` doesn't exactly match the registered `warp://mcp/oauth2callback`.

## Expected Behavior

Warp should use the `redirect_uri` exactly as returned by the registration endpoint, without appending query parameters. Per RFC 6749 §3.1.2.2:

> The authorization server MUST compare the two URIs using simple string comparison.

Dynamic client-specific data (like `server_id`) should be passed via the `state` parameter instead, as recommended by the RFC.

## Actual Behavior

Warp appends `?server_id={uuid}` to the `redirect_uri`, causing OAuth servers with strict redirect URI validation to reject the request.

## Environment

- Warp version: latest stable (macOS)
- MCP server: custom server with Hydra (ORY) as OAuth provider
- OAuth flow: RFC 9728 (MCP OAuth) + RFC 7591 (Dynamic Client Registration)

## Impact

This prevents Warp from connecting to any MCP server whose OAuth provider does exact redirect URI matching (which is the RFC-recommended default). Workaround: use `mcp-remote` via Claude Desktop instead, which correctly uses localhost callbacks without appending query params.

title: Per-tab icons for non-agent processes and project directories
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

Warp shows brand icons in the tab/pane list for recognized third-party CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, etc.), and it's great for picking those tabs out at a glance. I'd love the same affordance for non-agent tabs, driven by information Warp already tracks - no cooperation needed from the running program.

Three complementary mechanisms, in roughly decreasing order of impact:

1. **Repo-shipped project icons ("favicon for a directory").** If a repo contains a conventional file - e.g. `.warp/icon.png` or similar - Warp uses it as the icon for any tab whose CWD is inside that repo (discovered by walking up until the file is found, same way git finds `.git`). This is the favicon model: the *project* provides the icon once, checked into the repo, and every developer on the team sees it automatically with zero per-user setup. Huge for teams.

2. **Process-name → icon.** Extend the existing agent-detection path to a broader set of common tools (`pnpm`, `npm`, `yarn`, `cargo`, `docker`, `mvn`, `pytest`, etc.) with built-in brand icons, plus a settings surface where users can register additional `process-name → icon` mappings of their own.

3. **User-level CWD → icon overrides.** For directories that don't (or can't) ship a `.warp/icon.png`, let users map a directory to an icon in their own settings. Useful for personal projects, vendored codebases you don't own, etc.

Sensible precedence: agent icon > process icon > project (repo-shipped or user-mapped) icon > default.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

With multiple tabs open, non-agent tabs all render with the generic `>_` glyph, so telling apart a long-running `pnpm dev` from a shell in an unrelated project means reading truncated paths. The agent icons work so well for Claude Code tabs that I immediately wanted the same affordance everywhere else - especially for the project case, where the same repo is often open on many teammates' machines and each person having to configure an icon in settings defeats the point.

### Additional context

- The mechanism deliberately isn't an escape sequence: processes like `pnpm` won't emit one, and while they're in the foreground the shell can't either. Process name and CWD are both things Warp already observes.
- Security: auto-loading an image from arbitrary CWDs has mild risk (parser surface, visual spoofing of a trusted project). Reasonable guardrails: size/format limits, and optionally a one-time "trust this repo's icon?" prompt the first time Warp sees a new `.warp/icon.png`, similar to how editors handle directory-scoped config.

Adjacent but non-duplicate issues:
- #8579 - recognizing more wrapper commands as existing agents
- #8711 - tab *colors* by execution state
- #5972 / #6653 - custom *app* icon (dock)

### Describe the bug

Warp crashes within ~1 second of launching, every time. The crash occurs in the text layout pipeline where a string/invalid memory is being passed as a CoreFoundation object pointer to `CFAttributedStringSetAttribute`. This happens consistently even after a clean install (all caches, preferences, and application support data removed).

### To reproduce

1. Launch Warp from `/Applications/Warp.app`
2. App crashes immediately (~1 second after launch)

**Cleanup attempted (did not fix):**
- Removed `~/Library/Caches/dev.warp.Warp-Stable`
- Removed `~/Library/Application Support/dev.warp.Warp-Stable`
- Removed `~/Library/Preferences/dev.warp.Warp-Stable.plist`
- Removed `~/.warp`

The crash is 100% reproducible on every launch attempt.

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

here is mac report log

[tmp.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26850328/tmp.txt)

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

macOS 26.4.1 (25E253)

zsh 5.9 (arm-apple-darwin24.2.0)

v0.2026.04.15.08.45.02

Yes, this bug started recently or with an X Warp version
