today

### Additional context

here is ai analysis report：
## Crash Analysis

### Crash 1 - SIGSEGV at 0x8

```
Exception Type:    EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV)
Exception Subtype: KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000008
Termination Reason: Namespace SIGNAL, Code 11, Segmentation fault: 11
```

### Crash 2 - SIGBUS (Alignment Fault) at 0xe

```
Exception Type:    EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGBUS)
Exception Subtype: EXC_ARM_DA_ALIGN at 0x000000000000000e
Termination Reason: Namespace SIGNAL, Code 10, Bus error: 10
```

### Crash 3 - SIGSEGV at 0x0026002500240023

```
Exception Type:    EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV)
Exception Subtype: KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0026002500240023
Termination Reason: Namespace SIGNAL, Code 11, Segmentation fault: 11
```

> **Note**: The address `0x0026002500240023` decodes to UTF-16 characters `#$%&`, indicating that **string content is being misinterpreted as a CoreFoundation object pointer**.

### Common Crash Stack (all 3 crashes)

```
0  CoreFoundation    __CF_IS_OBJC / CFGetRetainCount
1  CoreFoundation    CFDictionaryGetValue
2  CoreFoundation    CFAttributedStringSetAttribute
3  stable            warpui::platform::mac::text_layout::create_attributed_string + 2932
4  stable            warpui::platform::mac::text_layout::layout_text
5  stable            warpui_core::text_layout::LayoutCache::layout_text
6  stable            warp_editor::render::layout::TextLayout::layout_text_with_options
7  stable            warp_editor::content::edit::LayoutTask::run
8  stable            warp_editor::content::edit::EditDelta::layout_delta
9+ stable            rayon parallel dispatch (bridge_producer_consumer / join_context)
```

The crash always happens on a **rayon worker thread** (Thread 48/50/52 across different runs) during parallel text layout processing at startup.

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The function `create_attributed_string` (at offset +2932) appears to pass an invalid/dangling pointer to `CFAttributedStringSetAttribute`. The varying crash addresses across runs (0x8, 0xe, 0x0026002500240023) suggest either:

1. A **use-after-free**: A CoreFoundation object (likely a font attribute dictionary) is freed by one rayon thread while another thread still holds a reference.
2. A **type confusion**: String buffer contents are being read as a CF object pointer due to an offset/casting error in the Rust FFI layer.

The fact that crash 3's address decodes to valid UTF-16 text (`#$%&`) strongly suggests scenario 2.

## Additional Context

- Thread 51/53 in the crash logs shows CoreText font fallback operations (`TFontCascade::CreateFallback`, `TDescriptorSource::CopyDefaultSubstitutionListForLanguages`) blocked on `_os_unfair_lock_lock_slow`, indicating concurrent text rendering contention.
- The main thread (Thread 0) is always in `rayon_core::latch::LockLatch::wait_and_reset`, waiting for the parallel layout tasks to complete.
- AppKit's `promptToIgnorePersistentStateWithCrashHistory` is visible in Thread 0's stack in earlier crashes, confirming the crash loop was detected by the system.

No

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

title: Vertical tabs don't update git branch when CWD changes via external tool
body:
### Describe the solution you'd like?

Warp should update its tab CWD/git-branch display whenever the shell's working directory changes - not only during the prompt rendering cycle. Ideally, Warp should respond to standard terminal escape sequences like OSC 7 (`\e]7;file://hostname/path\a`) for CWD updates, so tools can notify Warp of directory changes without waiting for the next prompt.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I use `wt switch <branch>` (from [worktrunk](https://github.com/jondot/worktrunk)) to jump between git worktrees. Each worktree is on a different branch in a different directory. The `wt` shell wrapper does a proper `cd` to the new worktree path.

When I run `wt switch` alone, the tab updates correctly - because the command finishes, fish redraws the prompt, and Warp picks up the new CWD during its prompt cycle.

But my workflow wraps `wt switch` in a function that immediately launches a long-running process (e.g. `claude`, `codex`) after switching. Since the prompt never redraws between the `cd` and the process launch, Warp's tab stays stuck on the old directory/branch for the entire session.

### What I've tried (none worked)

| Approach | Result |
|----------|--------|
| OSC 7 `\e]7;file://hostname/path\a` | Ignored - tab doesn't update |
| OSC 0 `\e]0;title\a` (same as fish_title) | Ignored |
| OSC 2 `\e]2;title\a` | Ignored |
| OSC 133 semantic prompt markers (fake command boundary) | Ignored |
| `commandline -f execute` from fish function | Doesn't fire - Warp manages input |
| `commandline -f execute` from `fish_prompt` handler | Fires but terminal input is broken (cursor position reports printed as text) |
| Running command directly from `fish_prompt` handler | Process is killed / Warp shows its own prompt over the running process |

### What does work (workarounds)

1. **Manual Enter press**: Return from the function (prompt renders, tab updates), pre-fill command in buffer via `commandline -r`, user presses Enter
2. **osascript hack**: Same as above but auto-press Enter via `osascript -e 'tell app "System Events" to key code 36'` after a 0.3s delay - fragile and requires accessibility permissions

### Warp already has the CWD data via its own plugin

The [claude-code-warp](https://github.com/warpdotdev/claude-code-warp) plugin sends the correct `cwd` in every OSC 777 notification payload (session_start, prompt_submit, stop, tool_complete, etc.). Warp receives the current working directory on every hook event but doesn't use it to update the tab's CWD/branch display. The data is already there - it just needs to be applied to the tab state.

### Root cause

Warp only reads the shell's CWD during its own prompt rendering cycle via `warp_precmd`. No escape sequence or programmatic approach can trigger a CWD re-read from within a running command or function. This affects any workflow that changes CWD and then immediately launches a long-running process without returning to the prompt:

- Git worktree managers (`wt switch` → launch editor/agent)
- `zoxide`/`autojump` in wrapper functions
- Project launchers that `cd` then start a dev server

### Proposed solution

Support OSC 7 (`\e]7;file://hostname/path\a`) as a CWD update signal, independent of the prompt cycle. This is a standard escape sequence supported by Terminal.app, iTerm2, VS Code terminal, and others. It would let any tool notify Warp of directory changes at any point - not only between commands.

Alternatively, use the `cwd` field already present in the OSC 777 `warp://cli-agent` payloads to update the tab when it changes.

### Additional context

- macOS, Warp v0.2026.04.15.08.45.stable_02
- Shell: fish
- The shell prompt and `git branch --show-current` both reflect the correct new branch after switching - only Warp's tab fails to update
- Related: #3108 (Add support for ANSI OSC) - OSC 7 is the specific sequence needed here

title: SSH Wrapper: interactive session immediately closes on Windows (MSYS2 bash) → Linux - pty-req/exec never dispatched after CHANNEL_OPEN
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABugs) and there are no duplicates (related: #6583, #4850 - but distinct: Windows client → Linux server with deep pty-req/exec analysis)
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there
- [x] I have included the logs (verbose SSH `-vvv` trace below)

### Describe the bug

When SSHing from **Warp on Windows (MSYS2 bash)** to a **Linux server (Ubuntu 24.04)**, the interactive session immediately closes with `Connection closed by remote host` after successful authentication. The SSH Wrapper opens a ControlMaster session channel (`CHANNEL_OPEN`) but **`pty-req` and `exec` are never dispatched** - the channel stays uninitialised and the server closes it.

**Diagnostic fingerprint:** in a working session the server sends the `authorized_keys` SSH debug message **twice** (once per channel request: pty-req + exec). In the failing Warp session it appears **only once**, then the connection drops with `Exit status -1`.

**Server-side auth.log** shows `Disconnected from user root` with no preceding `Received disconnect from ...:11` - confirming the server (sshd child) initiated the close, not the client.

All server-side causes have been ruled out: `PermitRootLogin yes`, no ForceCommand, no AllowUsers/DenyUsers, MaxStartups default (commented out), no SELinux, no /etc/nologin, standard ~/.bashrc, no ~/.ssh/rc.

### To reproduce

1. Open Warp Terminal on Windows (MSYS2 bash shell)
2. Run: `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa user@<linux-host>`
3. Authentication succeeds, then immediately: `Connection to <host> closed by remote host.`

Same command works from Windows Terminal / PowerShell / Git Bash.

### Expected behavior

An interactive SSH session is established on the remote Linux server.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

**Failing Warp trace (key section from `ssh -vvv`):**
```
Authenticated to <host> using publickey.
debug1: setting up multiplex master socket
debug1: channel 0: new mux listener [/c/Users/Tom/.ssh/17764971694137]
debug1: channel 1: new session [client-session]
debug3: ssh_session2_open: channel_new: 1 (tty)
debug2: channel 1: send open
debug3: send packet: type 90    <- CHANNEL_OPEN sent
debug1: Entering interactive session.
debug1: pledge: id
debug3: receive packet: type 80  <- GLOBAL_REQUEST (hostkeys)
debug3: receive packet: type 4   <- DEBUG authorized_keys message (ONCE only)
Connection to <host> closed by remote host.
debug1: Exit status -1
```

**Working plain SSH (no ControlMaster):**
```
Authenticated to <host> using publickey.
debug1: Remote: ...authorized_keys:1: key options: ...  <- appears TWICE (pty-req + exec)
debug1: Remote: ...authorized_keys:1: key options: ...
debug1: Sending command: id
uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
```

**Isolation tests:**

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| Plain SSH command (no ControlMaster, no PTY) | ✅ Works |
| SSH with `-t` + command, no ControlMaster | ✅ Works |
| ControlMaster=yes + /tmp socket + PTY + command | ✅ Works |
| ControlMaster=yes + ~/.ssh/ socket + PTY + command | ✅ Works |
| Warp init script (od/tr/printf OSC hook) run standalone | ✅ Works (SCRIPT_OK printed) |
| **Warp full combination (ControlMaster + PTY + Warp init script as interactive session)** | ❌ Fails |

Add a **sticky header for the user's prompt** at the top of the active Agent Mode conversation viewport. As the agent's response (skill content, tool calls, reasoning, diffs, streamed output) scrolls past, the original user prompt should pin to the top of the block/pane so it is always visible.

Proposed behavior:

- When a prompt's response exceeds the visible viewport height, the prompt row collapses into a compact, single-line sticky header anchored to the top of the conversation area. The header shows a truncated version of the prompt (with an ellipsis) plus a turn indicator (e.g. "You · 3m ago").
- Clicking the sticky header expands it to the full prompt inline (or scrolls back to the original prompt location).
- The sticky header should auto-release once the next prompt scrolls into view, so only the *currently referenced* prompt is ever pinned.
- A keyboard shortcut (e.g. `CMD-UP` / `CTRL-UP` within the agent pane) should jump the viewport back to the prompt that owns the current response.
- The header should include quick actions that today require finding the original prompt: **Edit & resubmit**, **Copy prompt**, and **Jump to end of response**.
- Works for both in-terminal agent blocks and the conversation-list view; in shared-session / ambient-agent views the same sticky header should show the prompt author as well.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

When an Agent Mode turn produces a long response - invoking a skill with verbose output, running multi-step tool calls, printing large diffs or streamed command output - the user's original prompt is pushed off-screen with no way to reference it without manually scrolling up. There is no pinned header, sticky label, or quick-jump affordance to bring the original prompt back into view, and for long turns the user loses track of what they originally asked. This makes it hard to verify the agent is still answering the right question, to copy/tweak the prompt for a follow-up, or to re-orient when switching tabs back to an in-flight conversation.

**Reproduction of the underlying pain point:**

1. Open an Agent Mode conversation in a Warp terminal.
2. Send a message that triggers a long agent response (e.g. invoke a skill with verbose output, or ask the agent to refactor a large file).
3. Wait for the full response to render.
4. Observe that the original prompt is no longer visible in the viewport and must be found by scrolling up.

Based on the report in warpdotdev/warp-external#856.

### Additional context

- The same pattern is well-established in Messages.app, Slack threads, Notion comments, and ChatGPT's web UI, so users already have a clear mental model for "sticky prompt at top of current turn".
- Non-goals for this issue: changing the underlying conversation data model, adding threading, or redesigning the full agent transcript. The ask is the minimal UI addition: pin the current turn's prompt while its response is in view.
- Related but distinct surfaces (keep separate): in-conversation search, conversation-list navigation, and block-level bookmarks - those should not be folded into this request.

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

3

body:
### Pre-submit Checks

### Describe the solution you'd like?

## Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have searched Warp feature requests and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have searched Warp docs and my feature is not there

## Describe the solution you'd like?

Please add **PHP** to the supported languages list in the built-in code editor:
https://docs.warp.dev/code/code-editor/language-server-protocol

**Files to support:** `*.php`, `*.phtml`, and ideally Blade templates (`*.blade.php`) for Laravel users.

**Suggested language server:** [Intelephense](https://intelephense.com/) by Ben Mewburn - the de-facto standard PHP LSP today. It's cross-platform, fast, distributed as a single npm package (`intelephense`), and is what Zed, VS Code, Neovim (coc / nvim-lspconfig), Helix, Emacs lsp-mode, and Sublime LSP all default to. A free tier covers the core intelligence features; a one-time license unlocks premium ones (rename, code actions, etc.).

Phpactor would be a reasonable open-source fallback, but shipping Intelephense by default would match what the rest of the ecosystem does and give the best out-of-the-box experience.

## Why this matters

**1. PHP is one of the largest dev populations still missing from Warp's LSP list.**
It consistently sits in the TIOBE / Stack Overflow / GitHub top 10 languages, powers a huge share of the web (WordPress alone runs ~40% of sites), and has a very active modern ecosystem - Laravel, Symfony, Filament, Livewire, Laravel Nova, Statamic. Right now `.php` files open with *"Language support is not available for this type of file"*, which sends a lot of us back to VS Code / PhpStorm / Zed just to edit.

**2. This directly affects Warp's agentic workflow story.**
I run `claude-code-cli` (and occasionally Codex / Oz) inside Warp every day for a Laravel codebase. The agent generates or modifies PHP code, and then I want to review / tweak it right there in Warp's editor - hover types, go-to-definition into `vendor/`, diagnostics. Without an LSP, I either accept agent output blind or bounce to another editor, which defeats one of the main reasons to use Warp in the first place. The "stay in one place" pitch from #8270 applies exactly the same way to PHP.

**3. Laravel + Warp is already a common combination.**
There are existing Warp issues from Laravel users around related UX gaps - artisan completions (#5620), JetBrains file-link open (#3332), double-click filename selection on `.php` paths (#1871). A working PHP LSP would be the natural next step for this audience.

**4. Integration should be straightforward.**
Intelephense is `npm install -g intelephense` and speaks standard LSP over stdio - the same shape as Warp's existing `pyright` / `rust-analyzer` / `gopls` integrations. No weird bootstrap (unlike, say, JDTLS for Java). Warp's auto-install flow for missing server binaries would work out of the box.

## Nice-to-haves (not blockers)

- Respect `~/intelephense/licence.txt` for Premium users - the same convention Zed, Sublime, and Neovim use.
- Blade highlighting / basic LSP routing for `*.blade.php` - Intelephense itself handles the PHP regions, and Laravel users would get huge value even from partial support.
- Once custom server configs are supported, let users swap Intelephense for Phpactor.

---

Happy to help test a preview build against a real Laravel / Filament / Livewire project.

Thanks! 🙏

title: Git diff chip flickers between tracked-only and all-files count when untracked files are present
body:
<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary
When running a terminal command in a repo that has both modified tracked files and untracked files, the git diff chip flickers between two values: the correct one that counts all changes (2 files | 8 edits) and an incorrect one that omits untracked files (1 file | 4 edits). The flicker is consistent and reproducible on every command run.

## Problem
The `GitDiffStats` chip has two update paths that compute the file/edit counts differently:

1. **`GitRepoStatusModel` (filesystem watcher)**: calls `DiffStateModel::diff_metadata_against_head()`, which runs `git status --untracked-files=all` and reads line counts from untracked files directly. **Includes untracked files.**
2. **`shell_git_line_changes()` (shell fallback)**: runs `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 git -c diff.autoRefreshIndex=false diff --shortstat HEAD`. **Excludes untracked files.**

When a command completes, the shell-command fallback fires and briefly overwrites the filesystem-watcher value with a count that omits untracked files. The filesystem watcher then fires again and restores the correct value, producing the visible flicker.

## Expected behavior
The chip consistently shows the correct count that includes both modified tracked files and untracked files (2 | 8 in this reproduction case).

## Actual behavior
Every time a command is run, the chip briefly flickers to the incorrect value (1 | 4), which excludes untracked files, before snapping back to the correct value (2 | 8).

## Reproduction steps
1. Open Warp in a local git repository.
2. Create at least one **modified tracked file** with a few edits (e.g., add 4 lines to any tracked file).
3. Create at least one **untracked file** in the same repo (e.g., `touch scripts/repro.sh` and add 4 lines).
4. Observe the git diff chip in the prompt - it should show both files/edits (e.g., `2 | 8`).
5. Run any terminal command (e.g., `echo hello`, `ls`, `git status`).
6. Watch the git diff chip: it briefly shows the lower, tracked-only value (e.g., `1 | 4`) then corrects to `2 | 8`.
7. The flicker repeats every time a command is run.

**Specific repo state used during reproduction:**
- Modified tracked file: `.mcp.json` (+4 lines, 0 deletions)
- Untracked file: `scripts/repro-mcp.sh` (4 lines)
- Correct chip value: `2 | 8`
- Incorrect (flickered) chip value: `1 | 4`

## Artifacts
Video with a repro: https://www.loom.com/share/b0f148fe1c004eb591ec82e4149fcace.

## Warp version
Unknown (please fill in from Warp → About Warp)

## Operating system
macOS

## Possible source references
- `app/src/context_chips/builtins.rs (162-180)`: `shell_git_line_changes()` runs `git diff --shortstat HEAD`, which only counts tracked file changes and excludes untracked files - this is the source of the incorrect lower value.
- `app/src/code_review/diff_state.rs (1624-1665)`: `diff_metadata_against_head()` uses `git status --untracked-files=all` and reads line counts from untracked files - this produces the correct higher value.
- `app/src/context_chips/current_prompt.rs (1428-1472)`: filesystem-watcher update path that calls `GitLineChanges::from_diff_stats(&metadata.stats_against_head)` - correct path, but races with the shell command path on block completion.
- `app/src/context_chips/current_prompt.rs (1480-1492)`: `is_updated_externally()` guard that should suppress the periodic 30-second timer when `GitRepoStatusModel` is live - but does not appear to suppress the block-completion shell command trigger.

title: Bug: IME (Input Method) never enabled on Linux/Wayland - set_ime_allowed(true) missing from Linux code path
body:
## Summary

On Linux/Wayland, Warp never activates the input method (fcitx5, ibus, etc.), making CJK and other IME-based input completely non-functional. Pressing the IME trigger key (e.g. `Ctrl+Space`) has no effect inside Warp.

## Root Cause

`winit::Window::set_ime_allowed(true)` is called **only inside a `#[cfg(windows)]` block** in `crates/warpui/src/windowing/winit/window.rs`:

```rust
// line 1363
#[cfg(windows)]
{
    // ...
    window.set_ime_allowed(true);  // ← only reached on Windows
    // ...
}
```

On Linux, this call is never made. Without it, winit never sends `zwp_text_input_v3.enable()` to the Wayland compositor, so the compositor never activates the IM session, and fcitx5/ibus never receives a keyboard grab for the window.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Warp on Linux with a Wayland compositor (tested: Hyprland 0.54.3)
2. Install fcitx5 with Rime or Pinyin input method
3. Focus the Warp terminal input
4. Press `Ctrl+Space` (or your configured IME trigger key)
5. Nothing happens - fcitx5 is not activated

`fcitx5-remote` confirms it stays inactive (`1`) while Warp is focused.

## Expected Behavior

Pressing the IME trigger key activates the input method, allowing preedit and CJK character composition (same as any other Wayland-native terminal).

## Environment

- OS: Arch Linux, kernel 6.19.14
- Compositor: Hyprland 0.54.3 (Wayland)
- Input method: fcitx5 5.x with `libwaylandim.so` (text-input-v3 support confirmed)
- Warp: built from source (OSS)

## Fix

Add a `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` block after window creation that calls `set_ime_allowed(true)`:

```rust
#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
if let Ok(window) = created_window.as_ref() {
    window.set_ime_allowed(true);
}
```

This causes winit's Wayland backend to call `zwp_text_input_v3.enable()`, which notifies the compositor to activate the IM session for the window. Verified fix: fcitx5 activates on `Ctrl+Space` and CJK input works correctly after the change.

Related: #6877

title: Tab config repo picker truncates long paths with no way to see, scroll, or alias them
body: ## Summary The repo picker used by tab config `type = "repo"` parameters truncates long entries with no way to see the rest of the path, scroll horizontally, hover for a tooltip, or attach a friendly nickname/alias. When several saved repos live deep inside paths like `~/Library/Mobile Documents/iCloud~md~obsidian/Documents/...` or `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-/...`, the visible portion of two different entries can be byte-for-byte identical, making it impossible to tell them apart at the moment of selection. ## Problem Tab configs make it easy to launch flows like "open Claude in a project" by declaring a `[params.] type = "repo"` parameter. On open, Warp shows a dropdown of saved repos so the user can pick which directory to launch in. Today that dropdown: - Renders each entry as the raw absolute path. - Has a fixed dropdown width with single-line entries. - Truncates the tail of long paths with an ellipsis. - Does not appear to expose hover/tooltip, horizontal scroll, mid-path elision, or any user-defined display name. In practice this means: - Two different repos that share a long common prefix (for example two projects under the same iCloud Documents folder) collapse into visually identical rows ending in `...`. The user cannot reliably pick the right one without trial and error. - The most distinctive part of a path (typically the trailing repo/project name) is exactly the part that gets cut off. - The search box at the top filters by the underlying path, but the user can't always remember the exact prefix to type, especially for cloud-sync paths with vendor-specific tokens like `iCloud~md~obsidian` or `GoogleDrive-`. This is mostly a UX issue for users who keep work in nested cloud-sync folders, monorepos, or any directory with a deep parent chain. ## Expected behavior A user opening a tab config that uses a `repo` parameter should always be able to identify the full path of each entry in the picker, and ideally label entries with a friendly name they choose. Reasonable ways to satisfy this (any one or a combination would help): 1. **Show the full path on demand** via a tooltip on hover, by widening the dropdown to the longest entry up to a sensible cap, or by allowing the dropdown to scroll horizontally. 2. **Smart elision in the middle** of the path instead of the end, so the trailing project/repo name is always visible (e.g. `/Users/brandon/Library/.../obsidian/Documents/`). macOS Finder and several IDE quick-open palettes use this pattern. 3. **User-defined nicknames / aliases** for saved repos, surfaced as the primary label in the picker, with the full path shown as secondary text underneath or on hover. This could be done either: - via a per-repo nickname stored alongside the saved repo entry in Warp's persisted workspace state, edited from a "rename" action in the picker, or - via an optional `display_name` / `alias` field declared per `[params.] type = "repo"` entry in the tab config TOML schema (less likely to scale because the schema doesn't own the saved-repo list). 4. **Two-line rows** showing the basename prominently and the full path as muted secondary text, similar to VS Code's "Open Recent" picker. Any of these would unblock the underlying need: "let me reliably distinguish saved repos at the moment of selection." ## Actual behavior Long paths are visually cut off with an ellipsis at a fixed dropdown width, and there is no hover, scroll, alias, or alternate display mode to recover the missing characters. Entries that share a long prefix become indistinguishable. ## Reproduction steps or desired workflow 1. title: Group sidebar tabs into collapsible Groups
body:
### Problem

When working with many open tabs in the sidebar, the list becomes long and hard to navigate. Tabs related to the same project, task, or context get visually mixed with unrelated ones, and there's no way to hide tabs you're not currently focused on without closing them.

### Proposal

Add the ability to organize sidebar tabs into named **Groups** that can be collapsed/expanded.

### Desired behavior

- Create a Group from the sidebar (e.g. right-click → "New group", or drag tabs onto each other)
- Drag tabs in/out of a Group, and reorder Groups themselves
- Click the Group header to fold/unfold; folded Groups show only the header + tab count
- Optional: name and color/icon per Group
- Groups persist across restarts and (ideally) sync with the rest of Warp's settings
- Keyboard shortcuts to fold/unfold the focused Group and to jump between Groups

### Why it helps

- Keeps long-running tabs (e.g. a server, a log tail) tucked away while you focus on a specific task
- Lets users keep more tabs open without the sidebar becoming unmanageable
- Mirrors a pattern users already know from browsers (Chrome/Arc/Firefox tab groups) and editors (VS Code editor groups)

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tabs can be grouped and ungrouped from the sidebar UI
- [ ] Groups can be collapsed and expanded
- [ ] Group state (membership, order, collapsed/expanded) survives restart
- [ ] Keyboard shortcut for collapse/expand

title: Linux bootstrap is missing libclang-dev and clang-format, breaking script/presubmit
body:
## Summary

Two packages required by `script/presubmit` on Linux are not installed by `script/linux/install_build_deps` (or any of its callers - `install_runtime_deps`, `install_test_deps`, `bootstrap`). A contributor running `script/linux/bootstrap` on a fresh Ubuntu/Debian machine and then running `script/presubmit` will hit two distinct failures.

## Problem 1: missing `libclang-dev` → `cargo nextest` fails to build `minimp4-sys`

`script/presubmit:56` runs `cargo nextest run --no-fail-fast --workspace`. That activates the `integration_tests` feature on `warpui_core` (`crates/warpui_core/Cargo.toml:12`), which pulls in `minimp4` → `minimp4-sys`. The `minimp4-sys` build script uses `bindgen` to parse C headers, and bindgen calls into `libclang` to do that.

Without `libclang-dev` installed, the build script fails:

```
error: failed to run custom build command for `minimp4-sys v0.1.1`
...
--- stderr
/usr/include/stdio.h:34:10: fatal error: 'stddef.h' file not found

thread 'main' (...) panicked at .../minimp4-sys-0.1.1/build.rs:14:10:
Unable to generate bindings: ClangDiagnostic("...'stddef.h' file not found\n")
```

The missing `stddef.h` lives in clang's resource directory (`/usr/lib/llvm-*/lib/clang/*/include/`). It's shipped by `libclang-common-*-dev`, which is pulled in transitively by `libclang-dev`:

```
libclang-dev → libclang-18-dev → libclang-common-18-dev   (the resource-dir headers)
                               → libclang1-18              (the .so bindgen loads)
```

Note: a plain `cargo build` does **not** trigger this - only test/integration builds do - which is why this hasn't shown up before for contributors who only build but don't run presubmit locally.

## Problem 2: missing `clang-format` → presubmit's clang-format check fails

`script/presubmit:32` calls `./script/run-clang-format.py -r --extensions 'c,h,cpp,m' ./crates/warpui/src/ ./app/src/`, which requires the `clang-format` binary on PATH.

`clang-format` is installed on macOS by `script/macos/bootstrap:44` via Homebrew, but is **never installed** by any of the Linux scripts. So presubmit fails for any Linux contributor who hasn't installed it manually.

## Reproduction

On a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 (or any Debian-derived) machine:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp
cd warp
script/linux/bootstrap
script/presubmit
```

Expected: presubmit passes.
Actual: fails on `clang-format` (step at line 32) or, after `clang-format` is installed manually, fails on `cargo nextest` building `minimp4-sys`.

## Suggested fix

Add both packages to the `PACKAGES=( ... )` array in `script/linux/install_build_deps` (lines 18-36):

```bash
# Needed by bindgen (used by minimp4-sys, pulled in by warpui_core's
# integration_tests feature) - pulls in libclang-common-*-dev which
# provides clang's resource-dir builtin headers.
libclang-dev
# Required by script/presubmit's clang-format check on C/C++/Obj-C sources.
clang-format
```

Both fit `install_build_deps` (compile-/build-time tooling) rather than `install_test_deps` (runtime tools the test suite spawns as subprocesses, e.g. zsh/fish/vim/gcloud). Precedent: `libasound2-dev` is in build_deps despite being only needed for the voice-input feature.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (noble)
- Pre-installed: `libclang1-18`, `llvm-18` (as transitive deps of other packages)
- Not pre-installed: `libclang-dev`, `clang-format`
labels: bug; triaged; repro:high; os:linux

title: warp-oss debug build crashes on launch: View menu adds flag-gated 'Toggle Conversation List View' item unconditionally
body:
## Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have searched Warp bugs and there are no duplicates.
- [x] I have searched Warp's known issues page and my issue is not there.

## Describe the bug

`warp-oss` (OSS channel, debug profile) panics during `applicationWillFinishLaunching`, before the main window finishes its first paint. The window flashes open and immediately disappears.

```
thread 'main' panicked at 'action should have a name: ToggleConversationListView',
app/src/app_menus.rs:103
```

In release builds the same code path doesn't crash (the failing assertion is `debug_assert!`), but the **View** menu silently renders the literal string `<NO DESCRIPTION>` for that item - so this is also a user-visible regression there.

## To reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp
cd warp
git lfs install
brew install protobuf      # see "Additional context"
cargo run --bin warp-oss --no-default-features --features=gui
```

The window appears for ~2-3 s, then the process exits with code 101.

## Expected behavior

The app launches successfully. The "Toggle Agent conversation list view" entry under **View** is either:

1. shown with its real label (`"Agent conversation list view"`, per `app/src/workspace/mod.rs:797-809`), or
2. omitted from the **View** menu while its feature flag is disabled.

## Root cause

`FeatureFlag::AgentViewConversationListView` (`crates/warp_features/src/lib.rs:623`) is **not present in `DOGFOOD_FLAGS`, `PREVIEW_FLAGS`, or `RELEASE_FLAGS`** (`crates/warp_features/src/lib.rs:868-952`), so it is off by default in every channel including OSS.

The two `EditableBinding`s that register this action's description and key bindings are both gated on that flag:

- `app/src/workspace/mod.rs:738-746` - custom-action binding, description `"Left Panel: Agent conversations"`.
- `app/src/workspace/mod.rs:797-809` - `cmd-shift-A` keystroke binding with the `MAC_MENUS_CONTEXT` override (`"Agent conversation list view"`).

Both carry `.with_enabled(|| FeatureFlag::AgentViewConversationListView.is_enabled())`, so when the flag is off they are filtered out by `Keymap::editable_bindings()` (`crates/warpui_core/src/keymap.rs:441-447`).

`make_new_view_menu` at **`app/src/app_menus.rs:384`** adds the menu item **unconditionally**:

```rust
updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::ToggleConversationListView, ctx),
```

The chain is then:

1. `default_name(action, ctx)` calls `ctx.description_for_custom_action(action.into(), MAC_MENUS_CONTEXT)`.
2. `default_binding_for_custom_action` finds no binding because both candidates were filtered out by `is_enabled()`.
3. `description_for_custom_action` returns `None`.
4. `unwrap_or_else { debug_assert!(false, "action should have a name: {action:?}") }` at `app/src/app_menus.rs:103` fires → panic.

This is a general class of bug: any flag-gated UI surface added unconditionally to the menu bar will reproduce it the next time a flag is shipped off-by-default.

## Proposed fix

Two changes; either alone works, both together is the right shape.

### 1. Gate the menu item on the same flag the bindings use (root cause)

```rust
// app/src/app_menus.rs::make_new_view_menu
let mut items = vec![
    updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::ToggleWarpDrive, ctx),
    MenuItem::Separator,
    updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::CommandPalette, ctx),
    updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::NavigationPalette, ctx),
    updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::LaunchConfigPalette, ctx),
    updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::FilesPalette, ctx),
];

if FeatureFlag::AgentViewConversationListView.is_enabled() {
    items.push(updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(
        CustomAction::ToggleConversationListView,
        ctx,
    ));
}

items.extend([
    updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::ToggleProjectExplorer, ctx),
    updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::ToggleGlobalSearch, ctx),
    MenuItem::Separator,
    // ... rest unchanged
]);
```

### 2. Make `default_name` not panic on a missing description (defense in depth)

```diff
--- a/app/src/app_menus.rs
+++ b/app/src/app_menus.rs
@@ -100,7 +100,7 @@ fn default_name(action: CustomAction, ctx: &AppContext) -> String {
     ctx.description_for_custom_action(action.into(), bindings::MAC_MENUS_CONTEXT)
         .unwrap_or_else(|| {
-            debug_assert!(false, "action should have a name: {action:?}");
+            log::warn!("custom menu action has no description: {action:?}");
             "<NO DESCRIPTION>".into()
         })
 }
```

The current `debug_assert!` turns this class of bug into a debug-only crash that doesn't show up until someone runs `cargo run` directly. Logging matches release behavior and leaves a discoverable signal in `~/Library/Logs/warp-oss.log`.

## Screenshots, videos, and logs

```
2026-04-30T02:32:43Z [INFO]  [warpui::platform::mac::window] Opening window with id 0
2026-04-30T02:32:43Z [INFO]  [warpui::platform::mac::window] Using discrete GPU for rendering new window.
2026-04-30T02:32:46Z [ERROR] [panic] thread 'main' panicked at 'action should have a name: ToggleConversationListView': app/src/app_menus.rs:103
   ...
   9: {closure#0}                              at app/src/app_menus.rs:103:13
  11: default_name                             at app/src/app_menus.rs:102:10
  12: updateable_custom_item_with_checkmark    at app/src/app_menus.rs:126:10
  13: updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark at app/src/app_menus.rs:136:5
  14: make_new_view_menu                       at app/src/app_menus.rs:384:9
  15: menu_bar                                 at app/src/app_menus.rs:68:9
  22: warp_app_will_finish_launching           at crates/warpui/src/platform/mac/app.rs:309:38
  23: -[WarpDelegate applicationWillFinishLaunching:]
                                                at crates/warpui/src/platform/mac/objc/app.m:217:22
```

Full log: `~/Library/Logs/warp-oss.log`.

## Operating system

macOS

## Operating system and version

macOS 15 (Darwin 24.6)

## Shell version

zsh 5.x

## Current Warp version

Built from `master` against the pinned `v0.2026.04.29.08.56.stable_00` release tag (cloned 2026-04-30).

## Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp (first OSS clone).

## Additional context

Two adjacent papercuts encountered while reproducing this on a clean macOS 15 / Xcode 16.4 box, both worth folding into `script/macos/bootstrap`:

1. **`protoc` is required but not installed by bootstrap.** `warp_multi_agent_api`'s `build.rs` invokes `protoc` and fails with `Could not find` `protoc` until `brew install protobuf` is run.
2. **OSS bundle icons are missing.** `app/Cargo.toml` references `channels/oss/icon/no-padding/{512x512.png, icon.ico}`; that directory is populated by `script/install_channel_config`, which depends on SSH access to the private `warp-channel-config` repo. OSS contributors can't fetch it. `cargo bundle --bin warp-oss` therefore fails until the icon paths are stubbed. A committed-in OSS placeholder icon (or making the icon entry optional in the bundle metadata) would let `./script/run` succeed end-to-end for OSS contributors.

## Does this block you from using Warp daily?

Yes, this issue prevents me from using Warp daily.

## Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

`FeatureFlag::AgentViewConversationListView` (`crates/warp_features/src/lib.rs:623`) is **not present in `DOGFOOD_FLAGS`, `PREVIEW_FLAGS`, or `RELEASE_FLAGS`** (`crates/warp_features/src/lib.rs:868-952`), so it is off by default in every channel including OSS.

The two `EditableBinding`s that register this action's description and key bindings are both gated on that flag:

- `app/src/workspace/mod.rs:738-746` - custom-action binding, description `"Left Panel: Agent conversations"`.
- `app/src/workspace/mod.rs:797-809` - `cmd-shift-A` keystroke binding with the `MAC_MENUS_CONTEXT` override (`"Agent conversation list view"`).

Both carry `.with_enabled(|| FeatureFlag::AgentViewConversationListView.is_enabled())`, so when the flag is off they are filtered out by `Keymap::editable_bindings()` (`crates/warpui_core/src/keymap.rs:441-447`).

`make_new_view_menu` at **`app/src/app_menus.rs:384`** adds the menu item **unconditionally**:

```rust
updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::ToggleConversationListView, ctx),
```

The chain is then:

1. `default_name(action, ctx)` calls `ctx.description_for_custom_action(action.into(), MAC_MENUS_CONTEXT)`.
2. `default_binding_for_custom_action` finds no binding because both candidates were filtered out by `is_enabled()`.
3. `description_for_custom_action` returns `None`.
4. `unwrap_or_else { debug_assert!(false, "action should have a name: {action:?}") }` at `app/src/app_menus.rs:103` fires → panic.

This is a general class of bug: any flag-gated UI surface added unconditionally to the menu bar will reproduce it the next time a flag is shipped off-by-default.

## Proposed fix

Two changes; either alone works, both together is the right shape.

### 1. Gate the menu item on the same flag the bindings use (root cause)

```rust
// app/src/app_menus.rs::make_new_view_menu
let mut items = vec![
    updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::ToggleWarpDrive, ctx),
    MenuItem::Separator,
    updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::CommandPalette, ctx),
    updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::NavigationPalette, ctx),
    updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::LaunchConfigPalette, ctx),
    updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::FilesPalette, ctx),
];

if FeatureFlag::AgentViewConversationListView.is_enabled() {
    items.push(updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(
        CustomAction::ToggleConversationListView,
        ctx,
    ));
}

items.extend([
    updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::ToggleProjectExplorer, ctx),
    updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark(CustomAction::ToggleGlobalSearch, ctx),
    MenuItem::Separator,
    // ... rest unchanged
]);
```

### 2. Make `default_name` not panic on a missing description (defense in depth)

```diff
--- a/app/src/app_menus.rs
+++ b/app/src/app_menus.rs
@@ -100,7 +100,7 @@ fn default_name(action: CustomAction, ctx: &AppContext) -> String {
     ctx.description_for_custom_action(action.into(), bindings::MAC_MENUS_CONTEXT)
         .unwrap_or_else(|| {
-            debug_assert!(false, "action should have a name: {action:?}");
+            log::warn!("custom menu action has no description: {action:?}");
             "<NO DESCRIPTION>".into()
         })
 }
```

The current `debug_assert!` turns this class of bug into a debug-only crash that doesn't show up until someone runs `cargo run` directly. Logging matches release behavior and leaves a discoverable signal in `~/Library/Logs/warp-oss.log`.

## Screenshots, videos, and logs

```

2026-04-30T02:32:43Z [INFO]  [warpui::platform::mac::window] Using discrete GPU for rendering new window.
2026-04-30T02:32:46Z [ERROR] [panic] thread 'main' panicked at 'action should have a name: ToggleConversationListView': app/src/app_menus.rs:103
   ...
   9: {closure#0}                              at app/src/app_menus.rs:103:13
  11: default_name                             at app/src/app_menus.rs:102:10
  12: updateable_custom_item_with_checkmark    at app/src/app_menus.rs:126:10
  13: updateable_custom_item_without_checkmark at app/src/app_menus.rs:136:5
  14: make_new_view_menu                       at app/src/app_menus.rs:384:9
  15: menu_bar                                 at app/src/app_menus.rs:68:9
  22: warp_app_will_finish_launching           at crates/warpui/src/platform/mac/app.rs:309:38
  23: -[WarpDelegate applicationWillFinishLaunching:]
                                                at crates/warpui/src/platform/mac/objc/app.m:217:22
```

Full log: `~/Library/Logs/warp-oss.log`.

## Operating system

macOS 15 (Darwin 24.6)

zsh 5.x

Built from `master` against the pinned `v0.2026.04.29.08.56.stable_00` release tag (cloned 2026-04-30).

## Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp (first OSS clone).

## Additional context

Two adjacent papercuts encountered while reproducing this on a clean macOS 15 / Xcode 16.4 box, both worth folding into `script/macos/bootstrap`:

1. **`protoc` is required but not installed by bootstrap.** `warp_multi_agent_api`'s `build.rs` invokes `protoc` and fails with `Could not find` `protoc` until `brew install protobuf` is run.
2. **OSS bundle icons are missing.** `app/Cargo.toml` references `channels/oss/icon/no-padding/{512x512.png, icon.ico}`; that directory is populated by `script/install_channel_config`, which depends on SSH access to the private `warp-channel-config` repo. OSS contributors can't fetch it. `cargo bundle --bin warp-oss` therefore fails until the icon paths are stubbed. A committed-in OSS placeholder icon (or making the icon entry optional in the bundle metadata) would let `./script/run` succeed end-to-end for OSS contributors.

title: Vertical tabs settings popup items (View as / Density) are unclickable
body:
## Summary

When the vertical tabs settings popup is open, clicking any option - **View as** (Panes / Tabs), **Density** (Compact / Expanded), **Pane title as**, and other toggle items - has no visible effect. The popup opens correctly but its interactive items do not respond to clicks.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable vertical tabs (`Settings → Features → Vertical Tabs`).
2. Click the settings (gear) button at the top of the vertical tabs panel.
3. The settings popup opens showing "View as", "Density", "Pane title as", etc.
4. Click any option - e.g. switch from "Panes" to "Tabs" under **View as**, or toggle **Compact** / **Expanded** under **Density**.

**Expected:** The selected option activates and the panel updates accordingly.
**Actual:** Nothing happens. Cursor shows a pointer on hover, but clicking produces no response.

## Root cause

`render_vertical_tabs_panel` renders the settings popup a **second time** as a panel-level overlay, in addition to the workspace-level rendering (wrapped in `Dismiss`) that already exists in the workspace view render function.

Both render calls pass the same `&VerticalTabsPanelState`, so every `Hoverable` button in the popup shares the **same `MouseStateHandle`** instance. `Hoverable` records a pending click on `LeftMouseDown` via `self.state().click_count = Some(n)`, then fires the handler on `LeftMouseUp` via `click_count.take()`.

Because warpui's `Stack` uses `EventDispatchMode::Broadcast` by default, **both overlay instances receive every mouse event**. The dispatch order is:

1. Panel-level copy (dispatched first): receives `LeftMouseUp`, calls `click_count.take()` - consumes the value - then bails because `is_mouse_over_element` returns `false` (covered by the higher-z-index workspace overlay). **No action dispatched.**
2. Workspace-level copy (inside `Dismiss`): receives `LeftMouseUp`, calls `click_count.take()` - finds `None` because step 1 already consumed it - skips the handler. **No action dispatched.**

Result: clicks are silently dropped and the popup items appear completely unresponsive.

## Fix

Remove the redundant panel-level popup render from `render_vertical_tabs_panel`. The workspace-level `Dismiss` rendering already handles positioning, click-outside-to-close, and z-ordering correctly.

## Environment

- OS: Arch Linux, Hyprland 0.54.3 (Wayland)
- Branch: `master` (reproduced from initial public release commit)

title: Find (cmd+f) selection jumps to a different match when new output streams in, instead of staying on the same text
body:
<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary
When using cmd+f to search a block whose output is still streaming (for example, logs from a long-running server), the currently selected match jumps to a different piece of text as new matches are appended, instead of staying anchored to the originally selected match.

## Problem
The find UI appears to identify the "currently selected" match by its index in an ordered list of matches rather than by a stable handle to the actual matched span. When new matches arrive earlier in the list (or the list is rebuilt to include the new output), the selection stays at the same numeric index (e.g. still "5 of N") and the highlighted text visibly changes, even though the user's selection should have shifted to a higher index to remain on the same text.

This makes find effectively unusable for inspecting a specific occurrence of a string in a block whose output is still being appended: the user keeps losing the location they navigated to whenever new matches arrive.

## Expected behavior
While the match list grows due to new live output, the selection should remain anchored to the same underlying matched text. If new matches appear before the current one, the index should update accordingly (e.g. "5 of 100" becomes "6 of 101"), but the highlighted text should not change.

## Actual behavior
The selection stays at the same numeric index as new matches stream in (e.g. "5 of 100" → "5 of 101") and visually jumps to whatever match now occupies that position. The text the user had navigated to is no longer highlighted, and they have to re-find it manually.

## Reproduction steps or desired workflow
1. Run a long-running command in a Warp block whose stdout/stderr produces lines containing some search term (for example, a server that periodically logs the word `request`).
2. While output is still streaming, press cmd+f and search for that term.
3. Use the find navigation to step to a specific match (e.g. result 5 of 100) and note which line is highlighted.
4. Wait for new output containing additional occurrences of the search term to be appended.
5. Observe that the highlighted match changes to a different line while the counter stays at "5 of N+k". The originally selected text is no longer the selected match.

title: Drag-and-drop image into CLI agent (Claude Code) inserts file path instead of attaching the image
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have searched Warp bugs and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have searched Warp known issues page and my issue is not there

### Describe the bug

When a CLI agent (e.g. Claude Code) is the active foreground process in a Warp tab, dragging an image file (e.g. a screenshot) onto the terminal inserts the file path as text into the agent's prompt, rather than attaching the image as image context.

Pasting the same image with Cmd+V (with the image bytes on the clipboard) attaches the image correctly. The two flows should converge for image files dropped while a CLI agent is active.

https://www.loom.com/share/32b03580946249389be828e15e5a7d8d

### To reproduce

1. Open a Warp tab and start a Claude Code session.
2. Take a screenshot (Cmd+Shift+4) so the screenshot file lands on the Desktop.
3. Drag the screenshot file onto the Warp window with the Claude Code session active. Reproduces both when dragging from Finder and when dragging the macOS screenshot preview thumbnail directly.
4. Observe: the file path is typed into Claude Code's prompt as plain text.
5. For comparison, copy the same screenshot to the clipboard (Preview → Edit → Copy, or Cmd+Shift+Ctrl+4 to copy directly), then Cmd+V into the same Claude Code session - the image is attached.

### Expected behavior

Drag-and-drop of an image file into a tab with an active CLI agent session should attach the image as image context (the same outcome as the Cmd+V flow), not insert the file path as text.

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

### Operating system and version

macOS 26.4.1 (25E253)

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.04.22.08.46.stable_03

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Additional context

Quick code trace from a read of the open-source repo:

- \`TerminalView::drag_and_drop_files\` (\`app/src/terminal/view.rs:23754\`) gates the image-attach branch on \`!is_in_long_running_command\` (line 23773). When a CLI agent like Claude Code is running, the active block is long-running, so the attach branch is skipped and the drop falls through to \`typed_characters_on_terminal\` (line 23830), which writes the path string into the PTY.
- \`Input::process_paste_event\` (\`app/src/terminal/input.rs:9849\`) takes a different path for clipboard image bytes - it calls \`handle_pasted_image_data\`, which does not consult the long-running-command gate. That's why Cmd+V works.
- The downstream \`can_attach_on_filepaths_paste_or_dragdrop\` (\`app/src/terminal/input.rs:9921\`) already has an explicit branch that returns \`true\` when \`CLIAgentSessionsModel::is_input_open(...)\` is true, so the gating helper is ready for this case - only the upstream long-running-command short-circuit blocks it.

This is **not** a request to revert #7032 (path-pasting in normal shell input). The proposed scope is narrowly: when a CLI agent session is active for the terminal, route image drops through the existing image-attach pipeline instead of typing the path into the PTY. Outside CLI-agent sessions, drag-drop behavior remains unchanged.

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

title: Add LSP-backed autocomplete with auto-import to the code editor
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

 While editing a source file in the Warp code editor, I want a VSCode-grade LSP autocomplete popup as I type:                                            
                                                                                                                                                          
  - After ~150ms of identifier typing, or immediately on a server-defined trigger character (`.`, `::`, `<`, etc), or on Cmd+./Ctrl+. (manual), a compact 
  popup anchors near the cursor with language-aware suggestions sourced from the file's LSP server.                                                       
  - The popup is passive by default - Enter still inserts a newline / fires auto-indent until I explicitly navigate with ↑/↓, at which point Enter accepts
   the highlighted item.                                                                                                                                  
  - Accepting an item that requires a new import (e.g. `useState` from `react`, `HashMap` from `std::collections`, `Path` from `pathlib`, an unimported
  package symbol in Go) inserts the symbol AND the `import` line in a single undoable action.                                                             
  - Snippet items (e.g. methods that ship parameter placeholders) expand to literal text with the first placeholder selected so I can immediately type to
  replace it.                                                                                                                                             
  - The popup auto-closes on Esc, on cursor movement out of the typed prefix, on focus loss, or when the prefix no longer matches any item.
                                                                                                                                                          
  Coverage in v1: TypeScript / JavaScript, Rust, Python, Go (the four languages that already have LSP servers configured under `crates/lsp/src/servers/`).
   Adding new languages later requires only registering a server - no UI work.                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                          
  Out of scope for v1 (tracked as v2):                                                                                                                    
  - Keyword templates (`for` → full for-loop expansion, `if` → if-else block) - these aren't part of LSP, they're VSCode-bundled `.code-snippets`.
  - Tab/Shift+Tab navigation between snippet stops; v1 selects only the first stop.                                                                       
  - AI / model-driven completion (separate flow).                                                                                                         
  - Multi-cursor editing concurrent with completion.                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                          
  Gated behind a `code_intelligence_completion` feature flag and a `code.editor.lsp_autocomplete_enabled` user setting; with the flag off, behavior is    
  identical to today.                                                                                                                                     
                                                

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

                                                                                            
  Yes. The Warp code editor (the surface opened via `workspace.open_file_with_target`) currently has LSP-backed hover, diagnostics, find references, and
  goto-definition wired end-to-end, but there's no `textDocument/completion` integration. While editing source files, users get no language-aware         
  suggestions while typing - only the symbols they remember by hand.
                                                                                                                                                          
  There's also no auto-import path: typing an unimported symbol leaves the user to add the `import` line manually. Concrete pain:                         
                                         
  - A TypeScript user typing `useState` in a `.tsx` has to switch to another window to remember the import path, then come back and add `import { useState
   } from 'react';` manually.                                                                
  - A Rust user typing `HashMap` doesn't get `use std::collections::HashMap;` added automatically.                                                        
  - Python and Go users see the same workflow break for any symbol that isn't already imported.                                                           
                                                                                                                                                          
  Without completion the code editor is unusable for anything beyond casual edits - users either copy-paste from another IDE or memorize APIs. The        
  plumbing (LSP servers, capability negotiation, telemetry) is already shipped; the only missing piece is `textDocument/completion` (and lazy             
  `completionItem/resolve`) on the wire and a popup driver in the code editor view.  

### Additional context

 Draft `product.md` (testable behavior invariants, edge cases, telemetry boundaries) and `tech.md` (capability declaration, service / model surface,
  popup driver, telemetry, feature-flag rollout) are ready to be moved into `specs/GH<this-issue-number>/` once the issue is labelled `ready-to-spec`.    
                                                                                             
  A working implementation also exists locally covering: LSP service / model wiring (`completion` + `completion_resolve`), `snippet_support` +            
  `resolve_support[additionalTextEdits]` capabilities, the `CodeIntelligenceCompletion` feature flag, `code.editor.lsp_autocomplete_enabled` setting,
  popup view with two-state key routing (visible / interactive), forward debounce + monotonic request sequence, client-side prefix filter, lazy           
  `completionItem/resolve`, auto-close on cursor-out-of-prefix, snippet first-stop selection, and privacy-conscious telemetry. Happy to break it into
  separate PRs once the spec lands.

title: Expose Editor State via IPC for External CLI Agents
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

## Problem Description
When using Warp with external CLI coding agents (like OpenCode, Claude Code, etc.), the agent has **no way to detect** what file is currently open in Warp's editor or what text is selected. This creates a significant UX gap compared to Neovim-based integrations.
### Current Situation
| Editor | Detects Active File | Detects Selection |
|--------|---------------------|-------------------|
| Neovim (via `opencode.nvim`) | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| VS Code (extension) | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| Warp | ❌ No | ❌ No |
## Proposed Solution
Expose Warp's internal editor state via a new IPC Service, similar to how Neovim exposes state via its msgpack-rpc API (accessible via `--listen` socket).
Warp already has a complete IPC infrastructure in `crates/ipc`:
- Unix Domain Sockets (Linux/macOS) or Named Pipes (Windows)
- Request/Response protocol with `Service` trait
- `ServerBuilder::with_service()` registration pattern
### Implementation Sketch
```rust
// New IPC service in Warp's main app
pub struct EditorStateService;
#[derive(Message, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct GetEditorStateRequest {
    pub include_content: bool,
}
#[derive(Message, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct EditorStateResponse {
    pub active_file: Option<String>,
    pub selections: Vec<Selection>,
    pub cursor: Cursor,
    pub buffer_content: Option<String>,
}
Environment Variable for Discovery
The socket path should be exposed via environment variable (similar to Neovim's $NVIM_LISTEN_ADDR):
// In main app initialization:
WARP_EDITOR_IPC_SOCKET=/tmp/warp-editor-{pid}.sock
Comparison with Neovim
Mechanism	Neovim	Warp (proposed)
Socket path	$NVIM_LISTEN_ADDR	$WARP_EDITOR_IPC_SOCKET
Protocol	msgpack-rpc	bincode (same as internal IPC)
Available data	File, buffer, selections, diagnostics	File, selections, cursor
## Alternatives Considered
1. **File-based approach**: Warp writes state to a temp file (`/tmp/warp-editor-state.json`). Agents poll the file.
   - Rejected: Less efficient, race conditions, no real-time updates
2. **Extend OSC 777**: Add new escape sequences for bidirectional communication.
   - Rejected: OSC is designed for one-way terminal output, not query/response
3. **Expose via MCP**: Use the Model Context Protocol which Warp already supports.
   - Potential future option: But requires MCP server embedded in Warp, more complex
This would enable the same level of context awareness that Neovim users get with `opencode.nvim`, making Warp + OpenCode a much more powerful combination.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I'm always frustrated when using OpenCode in Warp because there's no way for the agent to know what file I have open or what text I'm selecting. 
In Neovim, `opencode.nvim` can detect the active file and selection through Neovim's API. In VS Code, the extension can detect the active tab. But in Warp, the `opencode-warp` plugin can only send notifications TO Warp (via OSC 777), not query Warp FOR editor state.
Currently I must manually attach context using `Ctrl+Shift+L` or `@file` references, which breaks the flow of coding and requires extra manual steps that shouldn't be necessary.

### Additional context

- Warp's editor already has `Selection`, `Cursor`, `Buffer` data structures (see `app/src/editor/README.md`)
- The IPC infrastructure is battle-tested for plugin communication (see `app/src/plugin/`)
- `opencode-warp` plugin repo: https://github.com/warpdotdev/opencode-warp
- Neovim reference implementation: https://github.com/nickjvandyke/opencode.nvim

Windows

4

None

title: Feature request: support opening an external file at a specific line via URL Scheme and CLI
body:
## English

### Feature request
I'd like Warp to support **opening a local file from an external app and jumping to a specific line number** (and ideally column too).

This is the primary request.

Not just:
- opening Warp
- opening a directory
- creating a tab/window

But specifically:

- invoke Warp from an external app
- open a specific local file
- jump to a specific line (optionally column)

For example:
- open `/Users/name/project/src/index.ts`
- jump to line `120`, column `8`

### Proposed interfaces

#### 1) URL Scheme
For example:

```text
warp://action/open_file?path=/absolute/path/to/file&line=120&column=8
```

Any equivalent design would work, as long as it publicly supports:
- file path
- line number
- optional column number

#### 2) CLI
For example:

```bash
warp --goto /absolute/path/to/file:120:8
```

or:

```bash
warp --file /absolute/path/to/file --line 120 --column 8
```

### Why this matters
Warp already seems to have:
- a custom URL scheme / deep link system
- internal file search/open capabilities (such as `Cmd+P`)
- strong developer workflow primitives

But it appears to be missing a **stable public integration surface** for "open this file at this exact line".

This would be extremely useful for integrations such as:

- opening the current file from a JetBrains plugin
- jumping into Warp from external scripts / automation tools
- navigating from logs / stack traces / build output to source locations
- integrating browser / desktop tools with local source files
- tighter interoperability with terminal/editor workflows

### Important clarification
I understand Warp already has internal file-opening capabilities.

What I'm requesting is specifically:

**Please expose a public way to open a file from outside Warp and jump to a specific line number.**

That would make integration with IDE plugins, scripts, and third-party tools much more practical and reliable.

---

- 打开 `/Users/name/project/src/index.ts`
- 跳转到第 120 行，第 8 列

### 期望支持的方式

#### 1) URL Scheme
例如：

```text
warp://action/open_file?path=/absolute/path/to/file&line=120&column=8
```

或者任何你们认为更合适的设计，只要能稳定支持：
- 文件路径
- 行号
- 列号（可选）

#### 2) CLI
例如：

```bash
warp --goto /absolute/path/to/file:120:8
```

或者：

```bash
warp --file /absolute/path/to/file --line 120 --column 8
```

### 为什么这个功能很重要
Warp 现在已经有：
- 自定义 URL Scheme / deep link 能力
- 内部的文件搜索/打开能力（例如 `Cmd+P`）
- 很强的开发者工作流定位

但目前看，似乎还缺少一个**稳定的对外入口**，让其他应用或插件可以直接把"某个文件 + 某一行"交给 Warp。

这个能力对于工具集成非常有价值，例如：

- 从 JetBrains 插件打开当前文件到 Warp
- 从外部脚本 / automation 工具跳转到 Warp
- 从错误日志 / 构建输出 / stack trace 跳转到对应文件位置
- 从浏览器或其他桌面工具联动本地源码位置
- 与终端工作流、编辑器工作流更紧密集成

### 重点说明
我知道 Warp 内部已经有文件搜索/打开能力，但我希望的是：

**把"从外部打开指定文件并跳转到指定行号"作为公开能力开放出来。**

这才便于 IDE 插件、脚本、第三方工具做稳定集成。

### Describe the solution you'd like?


Add Mistral Vibe to Warp's list of recognized CLI agents so running `vibe` (interactive TUI) or `vibe-acp` (ACP-mode binary) in a Warp pane is detected as a known agent on par with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, etc.

Mistral Vibe is the open-source ACP-compatible CLI shipped by Mistral AI alongside Devstral 2 (Dec 2025). It is Apache 2.0 licensed, installable via `uv tool install mistral-vibe` or `pip install mistral-vibe`, and supports any OpenAI-compatible model endpoint - Mistral cloud (Devstral 2 / Devstral Small 2), vLLM, MLX, llama.cpp.

The change is purely additive and follows the existing pattern. Specifically, in `app/src/terminal/cli_agent.rs`:

- Add a `Vibe` variant to `enum CLIAgent` (around line 116).
- Complete the exhaustive matches that already enumerate the other agents:
    - `command_prefix` → `"vibe"` (the user-facing entry point; `vibe-acp` is an alternative the CLI also exposes).
    - `display_name` → `"Mistral Vibe"`.
    - `icon` → a new `Icon::MistralLogo` (or initially `None` for a draft PR).
    - `brand_color` → Mistral's orange (e.g. `#FA520F`).
    - `brand_icon_color` → white.
    - `supported_skill_providers` → `&[SkillProvider::Agents]` to start; `mistral-vibe` also has a native skill loader (`skill_paths` in `~/.vibe/config.toml`) which could become a dedicated `SkillProvider::Vibe` later.
    - `supports_bash_mode` → defaults to `false`; can be enabled in a follow-up.
- Add the brand color constant (e.g. `MISTRAL_ORANGE`) and the icon asset.
- Optionally: a minimal `vibe.rs` plugin manager in `app/src/terminal/cli_agent_sessions/plugin_manager/` returning `can_auto_install() = false` and providing manual install instructions (`uv tool install mistral-vibe`). This is *not* required for basic recognition - `is_installed()` defaults to `false` in the trait - but it makes the install footer behave like the other agents.

No new protocol or transport code is needed: `vibe-acp` already speaks ACP, and `vibe` itself is a regular interactive terminal process that Warp's blocks/editor already wrap.


### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Today, `vibe` runs fine in a Warp pane but Warp doesn't recognize it as a CLI agent, so users miss out on:

- The CLI agent toolbar.
- The brand-colored icon in the harness selector.
- Skill-provider integration.
- Agent-mode session telemetry / session sharing.

Mistral's Dec 2025 Devstral 2 release (123B, SWE-bench Verified 72.2%) and Devstral Small 2 (24B, 68.0%) are competitive open-weight coding models, and Mistral Vibe is the maintained open-source CLI for them. Adding it to the recognized list brings open-weight coding agents into parity with the closed-source agents Warp already supports, which fits Warp's stated multi-model / multi-harness direction.

- Devstral 2 model card: https://docs.mistral.ai/models/devstral-2-25-12

When selected, the agent runs the user's prompt through the locally-installed `claude` (Claude Code) or `codex` (OpenAI Codex CLI) binary on disk, using whatever auth those CLIs already have set up - i.e. the user's existing Claude / OpenAI subscription. **No Warp credits should be consumed for these turns.**

The conversation surface in Warp should look identical to the cloud-agent path:

- Tool calls (Bash, Read, Edit, Grep, Glob, Write) render as the same Warp ToolCall cards used by cloud agents
- Multi-turn context is preserved (prior turns visible to the CLI)
- The top-bar AI status pill shows the active local model + token usage (e.g. `Local Claude · 23.4k / 200k`)
- A bare `clear` in the terminal also resets the local-agent conversation so the CLI's context window matches what the user sees

This is opt-in per-conversation via the model picker; the existing cloud-agent flow is untouched when those options aren't selected.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I already pay for a Claude (Claude Code) subscription and an OpenAI (Codex) subscription. When I use Warp's `/agent` mode, every turn also burns Warp request credits - even though my own subscriptions could already cover the call. Today there's no way to tell `/agent` "for this conversation, use my local CLI instead of Warp's backend."

The closest existing options don't solve this:

- **BYO API key (#7422)** - uses raw API tokens metered by token, not the flat-rate subscription quota I'm already paying for. Doesn't help if I'm subscribed to Claude Pro / ChatGPT Plus.
- **Cloud agent with model selector** - still routes through Warp and counts against Warp credits.
- **Just running `claude` / `codex` directly in the terminal** - works, but loses Warp's UI affordances: tool-call cards, scrollable conversation history, terminal-block context auto-injection, attachments.

The user need is "give me Warp's `/agent` UX, but billed against my own existing subscription, not Warp's."

### Additional context

I have a working prototype on a feature branch (`ahmet/local-subscription-agent`) gated behind a `local_subscription_agent` cargo feature. Implementation sketch:

- New synthetic model ids `local-claude` / `local-codex` registered in `app/src/ai/llms.rs`
- Dispatch in `app/src/ai/agent/api/impl.rs` short-circuits `local-*` ids to a synthetic `ResponseStream` backed by a tokio task
- Task spawns the CLI as a subprocess (`claude -p -` / `codex exec --json -`), writes the prompt envelope to stdin, parses stream-json output line-by-line
- Each `tool_use` / `tool_result` content block (Claude) and `command_execution` item (Codex) is translated into the matching `RunShellCommand` / `ReadFiles` / `Grep` / `FileGlobV2` / `ApplyFileDiffs` proto so the UI is identical to cloud
- Stderr is drained in a background task to avoid the 64 KB pipe deadlock with `--verbose`
- Token usage per turn is recorded in a global `OnceLock<RwLock<Option<LocalUsageSnapshot>>>` slot read by the workspace top-bar

Happy to file a spec PR (`specs/GH<this-issue>/product.md` + `tech.md`) once the issue is triaged with `ready-to-spec` if maintainers want the full spec flow before reviewing the code.

title: macOS IME (超注音 / Yahoo Bopomofo): arrow key advances candidate selection by 2 instead of 1
body: ### Pre-submit Checks - [x] I have searched Warp bugs and there are no exact duplicates (related issues linked below) - [x] I have searched Warp known issues page and my issue is not there ### Describe the bug On macOS, when using **超注音 (Yahoo Bopomofo / 極限注音)** - a widely used third-party Traditional Chinese input method in Taiwan - pressing the **right** or **left** arrow key during candidate selection advances the highlighted candidate by **2 positions** instead of 1. This makes it impossible to land on even-indexed candidates (#2, #4, #6, ...) via arrow keys. The bug does **not** occur with macOS built-in 注音 (Apple Bopomofo) or Apple Pinyin. It does **not** reproduce in Terminal.app, iTerm2, Ghostty, or VS Code's integrated terminal - only in Warp. ### To reproduce 1. macOS, install 超注音 (Yahoo Bopomofo) - free third-party IM, https://tw.yahoo.com/超注音 2. In Warp, switch input source to 超注音 3. Type a Bopomofo combination with many candidates, e.g. `ㄅㄨˋ` (yields 不 / 把 / 被 / 補 / 版 / 堡 / ...) 4. Candidate window appears with `1不` highlighted 5. Press right arrow once 6. **Observed:** highlight jumps from `1不` to `3被` (skips `2把`) 7. Continue pressing right: `3被` → `5版` → `7表` → ... (always advances by 2) Number-key selection (`1`-`9`) works correctly as a workaround, but arrow-key navigation is broken. ### Expected behavior Right arrow advances candidate selection by 1 position, matching behavior in Terminal.app, iTerm2, Ghostty, and every other macOS app. ### Screenshots, videos, and logs Screen recording showing the candidate index jumping by 2 on each right-arrow press. Sequence: `1不` → `3被` (skipped `2把`) → `5版` (skipped `4補`). Candidate row layout: `1不 2把 3被 4補 5版 6堡 7表 8ㄅ 9並 ...` ### Operating system (OS) macOS ### Operating system and version macOS 26.4.1 (25E253) ### Shell Version zsh 5.9 ### Current Warp version 0.2026.04.27.15.32.03 ### Regression No, this bug has existed throughout my experience using Warp. ### Recent working Warp date N/A ### Additional context #### Suspected root cause The bug appears to originate in `keyDownImpl` in `crates/warpui/src/platform/mac/objc/host_view.m`, where every keyDown event is dispatched through **two parallel paths**: ```objc - (BOOL)keyDownImpl:(NSEvent *)event { BOOL wasComposing = [self hasMarkedText]; [textToInsert setString:@""]; interpretingKeyEvents = YES; [self interpretKeyEvents:[NSArray arrayWithObject:event]]; // path 1: AppKit IME (NSTextInputClient) interpretingKeyEvents = NO; BOOL handled = NO; if (self.readyForWarp) { handled = warp_handle_view_event(self, event, wasComposing || [self hasMarkedText]); // path 2: Rust / winit } ... } ``` Most macOS IMEs render their candidate UI through the standard `IMKCandidates` panel (a separate `NSPanel` owned by the input method server), so they only consume events arriving through **path 1**. 超注音 hooks deeper into the input context and observes key events through **path 2** as well - so the right-arrow event reaches its internal candidate index twice, advancing it by 2. This may also explain the long-standing #2335 (macOS Chinese candidate window misbehavior, open since 2022) and #9145 (Japanese IME popup misalignment in TUI apps): different surface symptoms (popup positioning vs. event double-counting) but plausibly the same root - inadequate isolation between the two key-event paths during IME composition on macOS. #### Suggested fix When `wasComposing || [self hasMarkedText]` is `YES` **and** the keycode corresponds to an arrow / page-navigation key, skip `warp_handle_view_event` (or have the Rust side early-return when the composing flag is set). This matches the contract Terminal.app and iTerm2 follow via standard NSTextInputClient delegation: while the IME is composing, the host should not act on navigation keys independently. #### Related issues - #2335 - macOS: candidate window doesn't follow cursor (open since 2022) - #9145 - macOS: Japanese IME conversion candidates popup misaligned (TUI-specific) - #9012 - Windows: pre-edit string not visible (Windows-specific, but same family of IME-path bugs) - #9357 - Tracking issue for Chinese support layers #### Willing to PR I'm willing to send a PR for this. Would appreciate maintainer confirmation of the suggested fix direction (early-return on path 2 during composition for navigation keys) before opening one. ### Does this block you from using Warp daily? No (number-key selection works as a workaround, but arrow-key navigation flow is broken) ### Is this an issue only in Warp? Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.
