title: Claude Code mailbox stays empty on WSL because plugin falls back to legacy OSC 777 notifications
body:
<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary
On WSL, the Claude Code plugin emits the legacy OSC 777 notification format instead of the structured `warp://cli-agent` format, so per-task entries never appear in Warp's notification mailbox in the top-right. Toasts and OS-level (Windows Action Center) notifications still render, which makes this look like a partial / silent failure.

## Problem
A Reddit user (`Aoshi_`) reports that on WSL, "Claude has completed a task" toasts show up and Windows Action Center receives notifications, but the mailbox dropdown in the top-right of Warp is always empty after Claude finishes a task. Reinstalling the plugin and updating both Warp and the plugin did not help. The same flow works on macOS/Linux/native-Windows, where mailbox entries appear as expected.

Original report: https://old.reddit.com/r/warpdotdev/comments/1snko27/

## Expected behavior
After Claude Code completes a task in a WSL pane, an entry should appear in Warp's notification mailbox (top-right) describing the completed task, just like on macOS, native Linux, and native Windows. Clicking the entry should navigate to the originating terminal.

## Actual behavior
- "Claude has completed a task" toast appears in Warp.
- Windows Action Center receives a notification.
- The notification mailbox in the top-right corner of Warp is always empty.

## Reproduction steps or desired workflow
1. Run Warp on Windows with a WSL distro configured.
2. Install the Claude Code plugin (`warpdotdev/claude-code-warp`).
3. Open a WSL tab and start a Claude Code session.
4. Submit a prompt and let Claude finish it.
5. Observe that a toast appears, but the mailbox icon in the top-right shows no new items / opening the mailbox shows it empty.
6. Repeat with multiple sessions/prompts; mailbox stays empty.

## Artifacts
None attached.

## Warp version
Unknown (reporter said they "updated Warp and the plugin today" at the time of the Reddit thread, ~late April 2026, but did not specify a build).

## Operating system
Warp on Windows host, with Claude Code running inside WSL (distro/version unspecified by reporter).

## Possible source references
- `app/src/terminal/local_tty/windows/environment.rs` (lines 103-120 set `WARP_CLIENT_VERSION` and, when `HOANotifications` is enabled, `WARP_CLI_AGENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION` on the Windows-side env block; lines 155-180 build `WSLENV` for the WSL starter, which forwards only `WARP_HONOR_PS1`, `WARP_USE_SSH_WRAPPER`, `WARP_SHELL_DEBUG_MODE`, `TERM_PROGRAM`, `WARP_IS_LOCAL_SHELL_SESSION`, `SSH_SOCKET_DIR`, and optionally `WARP_INITIAL_WORKING_DIR`). Neither `WARP_CLIENT_VERSION` nor `WARP_CLI_AGENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION` is added to `WSLENV`, so they don't cross the Windows → WSL boundary and don't reach the Linux shell where the Claude plugin runs.
- `claude-code-warp` plugin: `plugins/warp/scripts/should-use-structured.sh` (the `should_use_structured` function returns 1 when either `WARP_CLI_AGENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION` or `WARP_CLIENT_VERSION` is empty, causing `plugins/warp/scripts/on-stop.sh:9-12` to fall through to `plugins/warp/scripts/legacy/on-stop.sh`).
- `plugins/warp/scripts/legacy/on-stop.sh:48` - legacy fallback emits OSC 777 with title `Claude Code` instead of `warp://cli-agent`.
- `app/src/terminal/cli_agent_sessions/event/mod.rs:71-74` - `parse_event` early-returns `None` for any title that isn't the `warp://cli-agent` sentinel, so legacy-titled OSC 777 notifications are never lifted into `CLIAgentEvent`s and never reach `CLIAgentSessionsModel` / `AgentNotificationsModel` (which back the mailbox UI in `app/src/ai/agent_management/notifications/view.rs`).
- For comparison, the macOS/Linux PTY env path (`app/src/terminal/local_tty/unix.rs:276-288, 320-325`) sets both env vars directly on the child process, which is why mailbox entries work there.
- Likely fix surface: extend the WSL `WSLENV` builder in `windows/environment.rs` to also forward `WARP_CLIENT_VERSION` and (gated on `HOANotifications`) `WARP_CLI_AGENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION`.

### Describe the bug

On Windows 11, Warp is not registered as a notification app in the system, which means CLI agent notifications never appear even when everything else is configured correctly.

### To reproduce

1. Install Warp on Windows 11 (via .exe installer)
2. Install OpenCode and configure the @warp-dot-dev/opencode-warp plugin
3. Run opencode inside Warp terminal
4. Complete a task and observe - no notification appears

### Expected behavior

After a CLI agent (OpenCode/Claude Code/etc.) completes a task, a notification should appear in:

- Windows Action Center / System notifications

_No response_

Actual behavior:

- Warp does not appear in Settings → System → Notifications → Warp (it simply doesn't exist in the list of apps)
- Running Get-AppxPackage *warp* in PowerShell returns nothing - confirming Warp is installed as a Win32 app, not an AppxPackage
- The opencode-warp plugin loads correctly and logs "Warp plugin initialized"
- The environment variable WARP_CLI_AGENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION is set correctly (no warning about unsupported Warp version)
- However, no notifications ever reach Windows Notification Center

The Warp installer does not register the application as a Windows notification app (AppID/Toast Activator). Without proper registration in:

`HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Classes\AppUserModelId`
or proper AppxManifest, Windows silently drops notifications from the app.

No

title: Path detection: CJK / full-width punctuation not treated as word boundary, paths become un-clickable
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there
- [ ] I have an issue with AI and have included the debugging ID
- [ ] I have technical issue and have included the logs

### Describe the bug

Warp's clickable-path detection fails when a file path is immediately preceded by a CJK / full-width punctuation character with no ASCII whitespace in between. The same path with a leading ASCII space (or preceded by ASCII punctuation) is recognized correctly.

This is common when terminal output is generated by AI CLIs or Chinese/Japanese developer tooling that prints file paths inline in prose, e.g. `路径：<path>` or `出力先：<path>`. Today those paths are un-clickable in Warp, while iTerm2 (Cmd+Click) and VS Code's integrated terminal handle them fine.

Concrete example:

```
路径：/Users/me/project/plan.md          ← NOT clickable (fullwidth ：touching /)
路径: /Users/me/project/plan.md          ← clickable  (ASCII : + space)
/Users/me/project/plan.md                ← clickable  (bare)
```

The only difference between line 1 and line 2 is `：` (FULLWIDTH COLON, U+FF1A) directly touching `/`, vs `: ` (ASCII colon + space). The path itself is identical and exists on disk in all three cases.

### To reproduce

1. Create any file, e.g. `touch /tmp/warp-repro.md`
2. In Warp, run:
   ```sh
   printf '路径：/tmp/warp-repro.md\n路径: /tmp/warp-repro.md\n/tmp/warp-repro.md\n'
   ```
3. Hover each line and try Cmd+Click:
   - Line 1 (full-width `：` touching path): **not recognized**, no hover underline, Cmd+Click does nothing
   - Line 2 (ASCII `: ` + space): recognized, opens in configured editor
   - Line 3 (bare path): recognized, opens in configured editor

### Expected behavior

The path should be recognized in all three cases. The path-detection logic should treat Unicode punctuation and CJK characters as word boundaries, not just ASCII whitespace / punctuation.

The most common offenders are:

| Char | Codepoint | Name |
|---|---|---|
| `：` | U+FF1A | FULLWIDTH COLON |
| `，` | U+FF0C | FULLWIDTH COMMA |
| `。` | U+3002 | IDEOGRAPHIC FULL STOP |
| `「`/`」` | U+300C / U+300D | CJK corner brackets |
| `『`/`』` | U+300E / U+300F | CJK white corner brackets |
| `（`/`）` | U+FF08 / U+FF09 | FULLWIDTH PARENTHESES |

A pragmatic fix: in the left/right boundary check, accept **any character whose Unicode General Category is `P*` (punctuation / `Z*` separator / `Lo` CJK ideograph)** as a boundary, rather than only ASCII whitespace + specific ASCII punctuation.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

_No response_

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

### Operating system and version

26.4.1 (Tahoe)

### Shell Version

zsh 5.9

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.04.29.08.57.01

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Recent working Warp date

_No response_

### Additional context

Impact: LLM-backed CLIs (Claude Code, etc.) and Chinese/Japanese developer tooling routinely print file paths inline in CJK prose. Today every such path requires selecting + right-click → Open File, which defeats the purpose of Cmd+Click.

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes - iTerm2 Cmd+Click and VS Code integrated terminal both recognize the same paths.

title: Add option to disable per-line truecolor background painting (BCE-style flood) for diff-style ANSI output
body:
## Summary

Warp currently paints `\x1b[48;2;R;G;Bm` (truecolor background) ANSI codes edge-to-edge across the full block width for every emitting line. When a tool (e.g. Claude Code's diff renderer, `delta`, `git diff` with custom config) emits contiguous lines all carrying the same bg code, the visible viewport is filled with a solid wall of color - perceived as the entire screen being tinted.

Please add a setting to either:
1. **Clamp** truecolor bg painting to the printed text width (don't extend to end of line / block), OR
2. **Disable** Background Color Erase (BCE) / per-line bg painting globally, OR
3. **Dim or desaturate** truecolor bg fills past a configurable threshold.

## Repro

1. Run any tool that emits truecolor bg codes on entire `+`/`-` diff lines (e.g. Claude Code with `theme: "dark-daltonized"` viewing a large patch).
2. Open a hunk where the visible viewport is 100% `+` or `-` lines (no context).
3. Observe: the entire viewport is flooded teal (`+`) or red (`-`).
4. Compare against pure `git diff --color=always` (foreground-only codes - no flood).
5. Compare against the same content in iTerm2 / Ghostty / Alacritty - visible flood still occurs in all of them, but with structural chrome (sidebars, padding) the perception is less aggressive in some.

## Why this matters

- **Eye strain / accessibility** - sustained large-area saturated bg fills are uncomfortable and can be migraine-triggering. Users who rely on colorblind-accessible themes (e.g. teal/orange) face worse contrast trade-offs.
- **No current workaround at the Warp layer** - verified via:
  - `~/.warp/settings.toml` - no per-line bg / BCE / clamp keys
  - `dev.warp.Warp-Stable` plist - no relevant render keys
  - Custom themes (`~/.warp/themes/*.yaml`) - palette swap doesn't change painting behavior
  - Window opacity / blur - affects whole window, not just bg fills
  - Vertical tabs / sidebar - adds chrome but doesn't reduce the painted area
  - Hard `⌘Q` + reopen - no effect (not a render-state staleness issue)

## Proposed UX

```toml
[appearance.rendering]
truecolor_bg_clamp = "text_width"   # or "off" / "block" (current behavior, default)
truecolor_bg_max_saturation = 0.6   # optional 0.0-1.0 desaturation cap
```

Either a single binary toggle or the more granular options above would solve it.

## System info

- Warp Stable on macOS (Darwin 25.4.0)
- Reproduced across multiple themes (built-in Phenomenon, custom Cmux palette, dark-daltonized-equivalent)

Happy to provide a screen recording or specific repro stream if useful.
labels: enhancement; triaged; repro:high; accessibility; area:settings-keybindings; area:shell-terminal; warp:auto-triage-review

title: Show start timestamp on collapsed Agent thinking/reasoning phases
body:
<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary
Add a start timestamp to each collapsible "thinking" / reasoning phase in an Agent conversation, visible on the collapsed header so users can see when each phase began without expanding it.

## Problem
During an Agent conversation, reasoning/thinking phases compress to a single expandable line. The collapsed header shows no time information. For longer or multi-turn conversations - especially ones the user steps away from, leaves running with `Run until completion`, or wants to correlate against external events (CI, Slack, logs, cloud agent runs) - there is no way to tell at a glance:

- when the agent started thinking on a given turn
- how long ago a particular phase began relative to neighboring blocks
- which collapsed phase corresponds to a specific point in time the user remembers

Today the only way to recover any per-phase timing context is to expand the phase or cross-reference Command History / the cloud agent management view, neither of which surfaces per-thinking-phase start time inline in the conversation.

## Reproduction steps or desired workflow
Desired workflow:

1. Start any Agent conversation.
2. Send a prompt that triggers a thinking/reasoning phase.
3. The thinking phase collapses to a single expandable line.
4. The collapsed header displays the start time of that phase, for example `▸ Thinking... (started 11:42:07)` or a relative form like `▸ Thinking... (2m ago)`.
5. When expanded, the start time (and ideally the duration) is also shown at the top of the expanded view.

Nice-to-haves:

- A Settings toggle (e.g. under **Settings** > **Agents** or **Appearance**) to turn timestamps on/off and choose absolute vs. relative format.
- Match Warp's existing locale / 12h-24h conventions.
- Apply the same treatment to other collapsible agent sub-blocks (tool calls, plan steps) for consistency.

Out of scope:

- Per-token timing.
- Editing or reordering thinking phases.

title: remote-server SSH wrapper install fails on macOS due to bash-3.2 tilde expansion
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have searched Warp bugs and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have searched Warp known issues page and my issue is not there
- [x] I have included the logs

### Describe the bug

Warp's remote-server SSH wrapper (the new agent-based one, not the legacy `warpify`/tmux wrapper) fails to install its `oz` agent binary on any remote macOS host where `bash` resolves to Apple's stock `/bin/bash` (version 3.2.57 - i.e. every macOS host that hasn't put homebrew bash on PATH for non-login shells, which is the default).

User-visible symptom in `~/Library/Logs/warp.log`:

```
[INFO]  Checking for remote server binary at ~/.warp/remote-server/oz-v0.2026.04.29.08.57.stable_01
[INFO]  Installing remote server binary to ~/.warp/remote-server/oz-v0.2026.04.29.08.57.stable_01
[INFO]  Starting remote server connection for session SessionId(...)
[INFO]  [remote_server] zsh:1: no such file or directory: /Users/<user>/.warp/remote-server/oz-v0.2026.04.29.08.57.stable_01
[INFO]  Reader task: server disconnected (EOF)
[ERROR] Connection failed for session SessionId(...): initialize: Response channel closed before receiving a reply
[WARN]  Remote server connection failed for session SessionId(...); flushing bootstrap to unblock SSH session
```

Warp falls back to ControlMaster/legacy mode and the user sees `Initialize: Response channel closed before receiving a reply` - a misleading symptom (the protocol channel didn't close prematurely; the agent simply doesn't exist).

### Root cause

`crates/remote_server/src/install_remote_server.sh:30`:

```bash
install_dir="${install_dir/#\~/"$HOME"}"
```

`run_ssh_script` in `crates/remote_server/src/ssh.rs` invokes the install script with `ssh ... bash -s` and pipes the script body into stdin. On macOS the resolved `bash` is `/bin/bash` (3.2.57 - Apple has not shipped a newer bash since the GPLv3 transition).

In bash 3.2, the `"$HOME"` *inside the replacement* of `${var/pattern/replacement}` is treated as **6 literal characters including the double-quotes**, not expanded. Bash 4+ strips them. Empirical confirmation:

```
$ /bin/bash --version
GNU bash, version 3.2.57(1)-release (arm64-apple-darwin25)

$ HOME=/Users/me /bin/bash -c 'x=~/foo; echo "${x/#\~/"$HOME"}"'
"/Users/me"/foo                      # ← literal quotes

$ HOME=/Users/me /bin/bash -c 'x=~/foo; echo "${x/#\~/$HOME}"'
/Users/me/foo                        # ← correct
```

Downstream consequences in the install script:

- `mkdir -p '"/Users/<user>"/.warp/remote-server'` succeeds, creating a directory tree under `$HOME` whose first component is literally `"`.
- The 278 MB agent tarball downloads and extracts cleanly.
- `mv` lands the binary at `$HOME/"/Users/<user>"/.warp/remote-server/oz-v0...`.
- `install_binary()` returns `Ok(())`.
- `connect()` then asks zsh to exec `~/.warp/remote-server/oz-v0...` (the *correct* path), which doesn't exist → `zsh:1: no such file or directory`.

You can verify on any affected host: there will be a directory literally named `"` in the user's home folder containing a misplaced `oz-v0...` binary. On my Mac Studio that directory was dated to my very first connection attempt - the bug has been silent since the first install.

### To reproduce

1. From a Mac running Warp, `ssh` into another Mac (or any host where `bash -s` resolves to bash 3.2 - i.e. any macOS without `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash` shadowed via login shell config).
2. Wait for the remote-server bootstrap.
3. Observe the `initialize: Response channel closed before receiving a reply` error and the misplaced binary at `~/"/Users/<user>"/.warp/remote-server/oz-v0...` on the remote.

### Expected behavior

Install lands at `$HOME/.warp/remote-server/oz-v0...`; remote-server agent launches; full Warp UI works over SSH.

### Proposed fix

One character: drop the inner quotes around `$HOME` in the replacement. Bash 3.2 and 4+ both expand `${install_dir/#\~/$HOME}` correctly.

Happy to open the PR - I have it ready locally with two regression tests:

1. A live test that pipes the relevant snippet into `/bin/bash` and asserts the resolved path contains no literal `"` characters.
2. A static check over `INSTALL_SCRIPT_TEMPLATE` that grep-matches the buggy `/#\~/"$HOME"` pattern and explains why in the failure message.

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

### Operating system and version

macOS 26.2 (build 25C56), Darwin 25.2.0 arm64 (Mac Studio M2 Max). Reproduces against any Mac running default `/bin/bash` 3.2.57.

### Shell Version

Local: zsh 5.9. Remote `bash --version`: `GNU bash, version 3.2.57(1)-release (arm64-apple-darwin25)`.

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.04.29.08.57.stable_01

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Additional context

- The connection works fine when Warp falls back to the legacy ControlMaster path. The bug only affects the new remote-server wrapper.
- Workaround for affected users: pre-place the agent at the correct path so `binary_check_command` (`test -x ~/.warp/remote-server/oz-v0...`) returns 0 and the broken install step is skipped:
  ```
  ssh <host> 'mv "\"/$HOME\"/.warp/remote-server/oz-v0..." ~/.warp/remote-server/oz-v0...'
  ```
- The bug doesn't happen on Linux remotes because Linux bash is 4+ (Apple is the outlier - they freeze /bin/bash at 3.2 to avoid GPLv3).
- Diagnostic timeline I went through, in case useful for triage: shell-init noise from missing brew tools (red herring - `bash -s` doesn't source rc files); URL guessing against `releases.warp.dev` (wrong base - actual URL is `app.warp.dev/download/cli`, served from GCS); `fs_usage`-style polling watcher confirmed zero filesystem writes in `~/.warp/remote-server/` during failure (red herring - writes were going to `~/"/Users/.../"...`); reading `crates/remote_server/src/install_remote_server.sh` and `ssh.rs:run_ssh_script` made the bash-3.2 incompatibility obvious.

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.
labels: bug; triaged; repro:high; os:mac; area:ssh

title: Resizable panel drag lags behind cursor (especially on Wayland)
body:
## Description

When dragging a resizable panel edge (e.g. the right/left sidebar), the panel visually lags behind the cursor and can jump when reversing direction near the min/max size boundary. Most noticeable on **Wayland**.

## Root Cause

In `ResizableState::resize()` (`crates/warpui_core/src/elements/resizable.rs`), `last_position` was set to the **computed dragbar coordinate** (`origin ± new_size`) instead of the **actual cursor position**.

Each drag frame computed delta as:
```
delta = dragbar_position → cursor_now   // wrong
```
instead of:
```
delta = cursor_prev → cursor_now        // correct
```

This introduces systematic error that accumulates - especially when size hits min/max clamp, causing a visible jump on direction reversal.

`DragResizeElement` already does this correctly via `consume_delta()` which sets `last_y = y`.

## Fix

Set `last_position = new_position` (cursor position) in `resize()`. PR: leozeli/fix-resizable-drag-lag-wayland

title: Opt-in: bare left-drag selects in TUI without holding Shift on macOS
body:
## User pain point

On macOS, `Cmd+C` is intercepted by the terminal app and never reaches the running TUI as a stdin byte sequence. With Warp's current default, a bare left-button drag inside a full-screen TUI (Claude Code, vim, htop, tmux, etc.) is forwarded to the application via the mouse-reporting protocol. The application owns the selection, Warp itself has no native selection, and pressing `Cmd+C` appears to do nothing - Warp's clipboard handler has nothing to copy.

The existing workaround is `Shift`+drag, which bypasses mouse-reporting and routes the drag to Warp's native selection. But this is non-obvious: macOS users have decades of muscle memory expecting bare-drag to always select text. Discovering the `Shift` modifier requires reading docs or asking - which is why this question keeps coming up across community channels.

iTerm2 has solved this since forever: left-button drag is **always** a native selection gesture, and you hold `Option` to forward it to the TUI when needed. Other mouse events (right-click, scroll wheel, modifier+click) still follow mouse-reporting normally, so TUI features like scrolling, context menus, and click-to-position keep working.

## Proposed solution

Add an opt-in setting `terminal.native_left_drag_select_enabled` in the AltScreenReporting group, default `false` (no behavior change for existing users). When the setting is enabled:

- Left-button events (down, up, drag) are intercepted by Warp's native selection logic - same effect as if `Shift` was held.
- Bare left-drag in a TUI selects text natively in Warp; `Cmd+C` copies the resulting selection.
- All other mouse events (right-click, scroll, middle-click, modifier+click) continue to follow mouse-reporting, so TUI mouse functionality is preserved.

UI surface mirrors the existing `mouse_reporting_enabled` / `scroll_reporting_enabled` / `focus_reporting_enabled` toggles:

- Settings → Features → Terminal → "Native Left-Drag Selection" switch
- Command palette: `native left drag select` toggle action
- Context flag for keybinding integration

## Why opt-in (not default-on)

Some users / TUI workflows rely on bare-drag being forwarded to the application (e.g., custom drag-to-resize panes in tmux). Making this default-on would break their setup. Opt-in is safer and lets each user decide whether to follow Warp's literal-protocol default or iTerm2's selection-first default.

## Working code

The implementation is already done and verified in a fork - happy to open it as a code PR after this issue gets `ready-to-implement` (or `ready-to-spec` if a spec is preferred first):

- Branch: https://github.com/spalagu/warp/tree/feat/left-drag-select-default
- Diff: https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/compare/master...spalagu:warp:feat/left-drag-select-default
- ~120 lines of changes:
  - New setting in `app/src/terminal/alt_screen_reporting.rs`
  - `should_intercept_mouse()` extended with `is_left_button` parameter in `app/src/terminal/alt_screen/mod.rs`
  - 7 callsites updated (3 in `block_list_element.rs`, 4 in `alt_screen/alt_screen_element.rs`)
  - UI exposure in `app/src/settings_view/features_page.rs` (toggle widget + telemetry + dispatch)
  - `app/src/settings_view/mod.rs` (context flag)
  - Existing test in `view_test.rs` updated for new signature

`cargo check -p warp --bin warp-oss --features gui` passes cleanly. Manually validated on a `cargo bundle --release` build of the fork: `Cmd+C` now copies a bare-drag selection in Claude Code, vim, etc., when the toggle is on.

## Related issues / discussions

- #3280 (mouse selection in TUI requires Shift, non-obvious for macOS users)
- #2990 (similar request - native selection in TUI)
- #8462 (open feature request: send raw bytes via keybindings - adjacent but different angle)

## Notes

- Same default-`false` choice mirrors iTerm2's choice of having the *opposite* default available (Option to override). Either default works, opt-in is more conservative.
- Win/Linux mouse semantics on macOS are slightly different - this setting is platform-agnostic in code but the macOS pain point is the dominant one (Cmd+C interception).

title: Adopt DAP↔MCP as a first-class agent capability (working POC: glasspane)
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

Adopt **Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP) ↔ Model Context Protocol (MCP)** as a first-class agent capability - i.e. document the pattern in Warp's MCP guide and treat DAP-MCP servers as a supported integration shape, the same way `tools/list`, `resources/list`, and `prompts/list` are.

A DAP-MCP server exposes a debugger's operations (set breakpoint, step, evaluate-in-scope, get stack trace, inspect variables) as MCP tools. Any MCP-aware agent - including Warp's Oz, Claude Code, Cursor - can then drive a real debugger inside a sandboxed program, instead of `print`-statement-and-rerun debugging.

I built a working POC that already runs against today's Warp stack via the existing MCP integration:

→ **https://github.com/david-engelmann/glasspane**

It's a small Python (FastMCP) server that:

- spawns `debugpy` and connects as a DAP client,
- exposes 13 tools (`debug_launch`, `set_breakpoint`, `continue`, `step_over` / `_in` / `_out`, `pause`, `evaluate`, `stack_trace`, `scopes`, `variables`, `threads`, `list_breakpoints`, `terminate`),
- exposes 4 live resources (`debug://session-state`, `debug://breakpoints`, `debug://output/stdout`, `debug://output/stderr`),
- ships a real-debugpy integration test that drives the full handshake → breakpoint → evaluate → continue cycle against an example buggy program (`tests/test_debugpy_integration.py`).

```
$ pytest -v
============================== 15 passed in 0.67s ==============================
```

Architecture (for reference):

```
┌────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────┐         ┌──────────────┐
│  Warp Agent    │  MCP    │  glasspane       │   DAP   │  debugpy     │
│  (or any MCP   │◄───────►│  (FastMCP        │◄───────►│  (Python)    │
│   client)      │         │   server)        │         │              │
└────────────────┘         └──────────────────┘         └──────────────┘
```

The bridge is language-agnostic at the architecture layer. v1 ships `DebugpyAdapter`; later adapters target `lldb-dap` (C/C++/Rust), `vscode-js-debug` (JS/TS), `delve` (Go), JDB. Each is a `~80-line` file in `adapters/` and doesn't touch the rest of the surface.

To register it with Warp today:

```json
{
  "glasspane": {
    "command": "/Users/david/personal/glasspane/.venv/bin/python",
    "args": ["-m", "glasspane.server"]
  }
}
```

What I'm specifically asking for:

1. **Documentation** - add a "DAP-MCP" section to Warp's MCP guide showing this as a supported pattern, so users know it's possible.
2. **Optional discovery** - if a user has `debugpy` (or `lldb-dap`, etc.) on PATH, suggest a one-click setup of a glasspane-style server during agent onboarding.
3. **Optional UX** - surface "debugger paused at line X" as a distinct block state in the agent UI when MCP tool results come back with that signal. Lower priority; the data is already available, it's just rendering.

(1) is the headline ask and the smallest lift on Warp's side - basically just acknowledging the integration shape exists.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Today's coding agents debug by adding `print` statements, running, reading output, repeating. This is slow, low-fidelity, and loses information at every step. The agent has no way to ask "what is `total` actually equal to at line 42?" without modifying the source.

Adding DAP-via-MCP gives agents:

- **Granular state inspection** without edits - `debug_evaluate("filtered")` instead of `print(filtered); rerun`
- **Per-frame variable access** - agents can step backward up the call stack and inspect any caller's locals
- **Conditional breakpoints** - `condition="user.id == 42"` skips noise and pauses on the case that matters
- **Multi-language** via the adapter pattern - Python today, C/C++/Rust/JS/TS/Go later, same MCP surface

Concrete example. Given a failing test where `total == 0` but should be 250:

| Without DAP | With DAP-MCP |
|---|---|
| Add `print(orders)` before filter | `debug_set_breakpoint(file, line=27)` |
| Add `print(filtered)` after filter | `debug_continue()` (hits breakpoint) |
| Run the test | `debug_evaluate("filtered")` → `[]` |
| Read output | `debug_evaluate("orders")` → `[{value: 100}, ...]` |
| Notice `[]` | Notice the `>` vs `>=` mismatch on line 25 |
| Edit, rerun, edit, rerun | Done in 4 tool calls |

That's exactly the round-trip captured in `tests/test_debugpy_integration.py` against `examples/buggy_aggregation.py` in the linked repo.

### Additional context

The adapter pattern in `glasspane/adapters/` is intentionally minimal so contributors can add a language in <100 lines:

- `lldb-dap` adapter → C / C++ / Rust / Swift
- `vscode-js-debug` adapter → Node / browser
- `delve` adapter → Go
- `jdb` adapter → Java

Each just provides "spawn DAP server + return connected streams"; the session machinery, MCP surface, and event handling are language-agnostic.

This pitch composes cleanly with the existing roadmap items:

- **#7326 (ACP support)** - orthogonal. ACP-attached harnesses can use MCP servers, so a Warp-as-ACP-client setup can wire glasspane in without changes.
- **Local-model harness work (#9619)** - orthogonal. A local-model agent can call DAP tools just as well as a cloud-model one, since MCP is the abstraction.
- **MCP completeness (#9436 tools/resources, #9456 prompts/list)** - same code path. Once `prompts/list` lands, glasspane can expose pre-built debugging prompts (`/debug.find-bug`, `/debug.understand-flow`).

Happy to drive any of (1)/(2)/(3) above as follow-up PRs if there's interest. Repo is ready to read; the integration test gives reviewers a 1-second "yes this works" signal.

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

### How important is this feature to you?

4

Ignore

title: Custom terminal:copy / terminal:paste keybindings don't apply inside the New Worktree / New Session dialog input fields
body:
## Describe the bug

I have remapped copy/paste in `~/.config/warp-terminal/keybindings.yaml`:

```yaml
---
"terminal:paste": ctrl-v
"terminal:copy": ctrl-c
"terminal:cancel_command": ctrl-shift-C
"editor_view:insert_autosuggestion": shift-right
```

Inside terminal blocks these work perfectly - `Ctrl-C` copies, `Ctrl-V` pastes, `Ctrl-Shift-C` cancels.

However, the modal dialogs for **New Worktree** and **New Session** (the picker that lets you choose branch / base / directory etc., the same dialog tracked in #10269) ignore these remaps. In those input fields:

- `Ctrl-C` does not behave as the user-bound `terminal:copy`; behavior reverts to the OS/Electron defaults.
- `Ctrl-V` does not paste; you have to use `Ctrl-Shift-V` to paste a branch name or path.

This makes the dialog jarring to use because the keybinding contract that holds everywhere else in the app silently changes for these inputs.

Likely cause from the outside: the keybinding action namespace is `terminal:*`, and these dialog text inputs don't run inside a terminal context, so the user-mapped action never fires and the built-in default takes over. If that's the case, either the dialog inputs should also respect `terminal:copy`/`terminal:paste` (or have analogous `editor:*`/`dialog:*` actions that the same key binds to by default), or there should be a generic `app:copy` / `app:paste` mapping that wins in any focusable text input.

## To reproduce

1. Set the keybindings above in `~/.config/warp-terminal/keybindings.yaml` and restart Warp.
2. In the terminal: select text → `Ctrl-C` copies; `Ctrl-V` pastes. ✅
3. Open **Command Palette → New Worktree** (or **New Session**).
4. Click into the branch / directory text input.
5. Try `Ctrl-V` to paste a copied branch name → nothing happens; only `Ctrl-Shift-V` works.
6. Try `Ctrl-C` while text is selected → does not behave as the user-bound `terminal:copy`.

## Expected behavior

Custom copy/paste keybindings should apply consistently across the app, including the New Worktree / New Session / branch picker dialogs. If a user has bound `Ctrl-V` to paste, it should paste in any focusable text input, not just inside terminal blocks.

## Screenshots, videos, and logs

N/A - pure keybinding behavior, easy to reproduce from the config above.

v0.2026.04.27.15.32.stable.03

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp.

### Describe the bug
In Warp's built-in code editor on Windows, `Ctrl+Shift+End` and `Ctrl+Shift+Home` do not extend the text selection to the end / start of the file.

The actions **"Select and Move to the Bottom"** and **"Select and Move to the Top"** appear in `Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts` with `Ctrl+Shift+End` and `Ctrl+Shift+Home` listed as their bindings (no orange conflict border). The presentation suggests they're correctly bound - but pressing those key combos while focused in a code-editor file pane does nothing. Cursor doesn't move and no selection is created.

`Ctrl+End` and `Ctrl+Home` (no shift, navigation only) **do** work, so the navigate-to-extreme action is wired. The issue is specifically that the *selection-extending* variants are not dispatched in the code-editor surface.

### To reproduce
1. Open Warp on Windows.
2. Open a file in the built-in code editor (e.g., a `.js` file via the file tree).
3. Click to place the cursor somewhere in the middle of the file.
4. Press `Ctrl+Shift+End`.

**Expected:** Selection extends from the cursor to the end of the file.
**Actual:** Nothing happens. No selection, no cursor movement.

Same result with `Ctrl+Shift+Home` (expected: select to start; actual: nothing).

Windows

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.22631

Unsure - first time I've noticed this; can't confirm whether it ever worked in an earlier Warp build on Windows.

The bindings shown for "Select and Move to the Bottom" / "Select and Move to the Top" in Settings should fire in the code editor file pane. The actions exist in the action catalog and the Settings panel does not flag them as conflicting, so the wiring appears to be the gap.

title: Optional command replay on session restoration (per-tab/per-config flag)
body:
## Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have searched Warp feature requests and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have searched Warp docs and my feature is not there

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add an opt-in `replay_on_restore` flag (default `false`) that controls whether Session Restoration re-executes a tab/pane's startup command when the tab is restored. The flag should be settable in two places:

1. **Tab Config TOML** (`~/.warp/tab_configs/*.toml`) - a top-level or per-pane key, so configs can declare the intent up front:

   ```toml
   name = "geekom: main"
   replay_on_restore = true   # or per-pane below

   [[panes]]
   type = "terminal"
   commands = ["ssh -t geekom 'tmux attach -t main || tmux new -s main'"]
   replay_on_restore = true
   ```

2. **Restored ad-hoc tabs** - a per-tab toggle (right-click → "Replay command on restore") persisted in the session SQLite DB alongside the existing tab metadata.

On Warp launch with Session Restoration enabled, tabs/panes whose `replay_on_restore = true` get their original startup command re-run after the shell is ready. Tabs without the flag behave exactly as today (restored layout, idle prompt).

## Why this is useful

A common pattern is for a tab to be a long-lived bridge to remote state rather than a local shell - e.g.:

- `ssh host -t tmux attach -t name` (the canonical case)
- `kubectl exec -it pod -- bash`
- `docker compose exec service bash`
- `mosh host -- tmux attach`
- A long-running REPL or watcher

Session Restoration currently brings these tabs back as empty prompts (docs explicitly note "processes that were running will not be automatically restarted"). The user's only options are (a) manually re-run the command in each tab, or (b) bind the workflow to a Tab Config and click each one in the `+` menu. Both are friction in a workflow whose whole point was "pick up exactly where I left off."

Tab Configs already support startup commands, so `replay_on_restore` for restored Tab Config-launched tabs is essentially "the config's commands run again." The conceptual model is consistent.

## Why opt-in / why default false

Auto-replay of arbitrary commands is unsafe. Counterexamples to "always replay":

- Destructive ops (`rm -rf`, `terraform apply`, `kubectl delete`)
- One-shot commands that already completed (running `make build` again on every launch)
- Commands requiring fresh credentials/MFA - replaying triggers password prompts on every Warp restart
- Parallel-replay thundering herds (5 tabs all `ssh`-ing on launch, each prompting for keychain unlock)

Defaulting to `false` preserves today's safe behavior. Power users opt in per tab/config where they know the command is idempotent and replay-safe (typically attach-style commands).

## Related issues

- **#8508** - *Session restoration restores panes/tabs but not per-session environment variables set via `export`*. Same shape of problem (layout restored, runtime state not). Currently closed as `needs-info` (auto-closed after 3 business days with no reporter follow-up), not rejected on merit. A unified "what gets restored" settings surface might benefit both.
- **#2722** - *persist bookmarked Blocks on session restoration*. Also "session restored, but secondary state lost."

## Optional companion feature

A "Re-run" affordance on tabs whose process has exited (independent of restore). One-click manual replay of the last startup command. Together with `replay_on_restore`, these cover both unattended restore and ad-hoc reconnection. Could be a separate issue if preferred.

title: Warp sends whole-number floats (5.0) to MCP tools instead of integers (5), violating tool input schemas
body: ### Pre-submit Checks - [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates - [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there - [ ] I have an issue with AI and have included the debugging ID (Optional, but helps expedite the AI quality fix). [Debugging ID instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/agent/ai-faqs#gathering-ai-debugging-id) - [ ] I have technical issue and have included the logs (optional, but helps expedite the bug fix). [Log instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/troubleshooting-and-support/sending-us-feedback#gathering-warp-logs) ### Describe the bug similar to https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues/6945 which was solved, but with nested integers. When the agent calls an MCP tool with a numeric argument that the tool's `inputSchema` declares as `"type": "integer"`, Warp sends a JSON float (e.g. `5.0`, `1730419200000.0`) instead of a JSON integer (e.g. `5`, `1730419200000`). Many OpenAPI-backed servers like Cortex/Snyk-style auditors) reject these calls with `HTTP 500` or `Bad Request`, because their schema validation distinguishes integers from floats. There **is** existing coercion code for exactly this - `coerce_integer_args` in `app/src/ai/blocklist/action_model/execute/call_mcp_tool.rs` - but it only handles the simplest case: a top-level property whose schema is literally `{"type": "integer"}`. Every other common JSON Schema shape silently leaks the float through. ### To reproduce 1. Configure an MCP tool whose `inputSchema` declares an integer field nested inside an object, an array item, a `oneOf` branch, a `$ref`, or as a nullable `["integer", "null"]`. Minimal repro schema (matches a real PANW mcp server tool): ```yaml AuditManagementLogRequest: type: object properties: request_data: type: object properties: search_from: { type: integer } search_to: { type: integer } filters: type: array items: oneOf: - { properties: { value: { type: array, items: { type: string } } } } - { properties: { value: { type: integer } } } # ← timestamp ms ``` 2. Ask the agent to call the tool with values like `search_from: 0`, `search_to: 100`, and a timestamp filter `value: 1730419200000`. 3. Observe (server logs / network capture) that Warp sends: ```json { "request_data": { "search_from": 0.0, "search_to": 100.0, "filters": [{ "field": "timestamp", "operator": "gte", "value": 1730419200000.0 }] } } ``` The server rejects the call. ### Expected behavior Warp should send: ```json { "request_data": { "search_from": 0, "search_to": 100, "filters": [{ "field": "timestamp", "operator": "gte", "value": 1730419200000 }] } } ``` ### Screenshots, videos, and logs ### Operating system (OS) macOS ### Operating system and version macOS 26.4.1 (build 25E253), Apple Silicon (arm64) ### Shell Version zsh 5.9 ### Current Warp version v0.2026.05.06.15.42.03.stable_03 ### Regression No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp ### Recent working Warp date _No response_ ### Additional context MCP tool arguments round-trip through `google.protobuf.Struct` between the agent backend and the Warp client. `structpb.NumberValue` stores **all** numbers as `f64`, erasing the integer/float distinction. By the time the args land in the client as a `serde_json::Value`, an integer `5` has become `5.0`, and serde_json (via ryu) serializes it back out as `"5.0"` - which strict MCP servers reject for integer-typed fields. The mitigation lives in `app/src/ai/blocklist/action_model/execute/call_mcp_tool.rs`: ```rust pub(crate) fn coerce_integer_args( args: &mut serde_json::Map, input_schema: &serde_json::Map, ) { let Some(properties) = input_schema.get("properties").and_then(|p| p.as_object()) else { return; }; for (key, prop_def) in properties { let is_integer = prop_def.get("type").and_then(|t| t.as_str()) == Some("integer"); if !is_integer { continue; } // ...coerce f64 -> i64 } } ``` It walks **only depth-1 properties** and **only** schemas whose `type` is the exact string `"integer"`. It does not recurse ### Does this block you from using Warp daily? Yes, this issue prevents me from using Warp daily. ### Is this an issue only in Warp? Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals. ### Warp Internal (ignore): linear-label:b9d78064-c89e-4973-b153-5178a31ee54e None
labels: bug; triaged; ready-to-implement; repro:high; os:mac; area:agent; area:mcp

title: Sidebar-driven cmux-style workspaces (per-window tab groups)
body:
### Pre-submit checks
- [x] I have searched Warp feature requests and there are no duplicates.
- [x] I have searched Warp docs and this feature is not there.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Sidebar-driven concept where a single Warp window holds **N independent groups of tabs** ("Workspaces"), each scoped to a project, branch, or task. Internally typed as `TabGroup` to avoid colliding with the three existing `Workspace`s in the codebase (`workspace::view::Workspace`, `workspaces::Workspace` SaaS, `persistence::Workspace`); surfaced as **"Workspace"** in the UI.

Key behaviors:
- Left sidebar lists every workspace in the active window.
- Horizontal tab bar filters to the **active** workspace's tabs.
- `+` button at the sidebar header creates a new workspace; activating an empty workspace auto-spawns a default tab.
- Right-click on a row opens a popover with **Rename / Color / Delete**; hover reveals a `×` close button; double-click renames inline.
- Per-workspace color stripe inherits from the active tab's color (or can be overridden explicitly via the right-click swatches).
- Keybindings: `Cmd+Shift+T` new workspace, `Cmd+Shift+1..8` activate, `Cmd+Shift+R` rename active, `Cmd+Shift+B` toggle sidebar (preserves `Cmd+1..9` for tab switching).
- Persisted in SQLite alongside existing window/tab state.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

Today a `Window` owns a flat `Vec<TabSnapshot>` and the workspace view renders that single list. There's no level between OS window and tab bar, so a user juggling two projects has to either:
- Open a second Warp window → loses single-window focus, doubles chrome, breaks per-window state.
- Pile every tab into one bar → visual context collapses, color coding stops scaling past ~10 tabs.

Tools like cmux solve this with sidebar workspace entries. Warp has tracked related requests before (worktree-per-tab grouping, project grouping) but no general primitive landed because the name "Workspace" is already taken three times in the codebase. Introducing `TabGroup` as the internal name resolves the naming collision while preserving the user-facing word.

### Additional context

I've built a working proof-of-concept on a fork branch. Coverage:
- Diesel migration + \`tab_groups\` table + \`tabs.tab_group_id\`.
- \`WindowSnapshot.tab_groups\` + \`TabSnapshot.tab_group_index\` round-trip through SQLite.
- \`FeatureFlag::CmuxStyleWorkspaces\` registered in \`DOGFOOD_FLAGS\`.
- Sidebar renderer with hover/active states, color stripes, inline rename, hover-`×`, right-click \`Menu<WorkspaceAction>\` popover (rename / 6 ANSI swatches / delete), \`+\` header button.
- Tab-bar filter via \`tab_in_active_group()\` (legacy windows unchanged: empty \`tab_groups\` = single implicit default group).
- Closing a workspace closes its member tabs via existing \`close_tabs\`; closing the only workspace dispatches \`CloseWindow\`.
- Sidebar open/close state (\`cmux_sidebar_open\` column) decoupled from the legacy vertical-tabs panel state.

13 commits, ~1,800 LOC, \`cargo check --tests\` clean.

- Branch: https://github.com/ericknavarro97/warp/tree/claude/cmux-style-workspaces
- Fork PR (tracking): https://github.com/ericknavarro97/warp/pull/1
- Existing specs: https://github.com/ericknavarro97/warp/tree/claude/cmux-style-workspaces/specs/cmux-workspaces (will reformat to \`specs/GH<this-issue>/product.md\` + \`tech.md\` per \`CONTRIBUTING.md\` conventions once an issue number exists.)

Happy to open the spec PR once this is labeled \`ready-to-spec\`.

### Operating system (OS)
macOS

4

title: CJK characters become invisible at AI panel's right column boundary (revealed by selection)
body: ### Pre-submit Checks - [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates - [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there - [ ] I have an issue with AI and have included the debugging ID (Optional, but helps expedite the AI quality fix). [Debugging ID instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/agent/ai-faqs#gathering-ai-debugging-id) - [ ] I have technical issue and have included the logs (optional, but helps expedite the bug fix). [Log instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/troubleshooting-and-support/sending-us-feedback#gathering-warp-logs) ### Describe the bug After applying the well-known CJK font fix (installing `Sarasa Mono TC` via `font-sarasa-gothic`, setting both `font_name` and `ai_font_name`), some CJK characters in the **Warp AI response panel** still render as nearly transparent - they are not visible until the region is dragged-selected. The distinguishing observation: **the invisible characters always cluster at the same x-column range**, not on random characters. Example from one AI response (font_size 20.0, Darcula theme): | Line | Invisible char | Cell column | |---|---|---| | 你問：「我們公司 Q3 銷售如何**？**」 | `？` | 29-30 | | 1. ... 從「向**量**資料庫」 | `量` | 28-29 | | 2. ... 把片段**塞**進 prompt | `塞` | 28-29 | | 回答：「... 比**上**季成長 ...」 | `上` | 29-30 | All invisible chars fall in columns 28-30 (CJK chars are 2 cells wide). This corresponds to the **right edge of the AI response panel** in my window width. **Why this is not a font fallback / glyph-missing issue**: - `fc-match "Sarasa Mono TC:charset=4e0a"` (charset for 上) resolves correctly to `Sarasa Mono TC` Regular - Other CJK characters on the same line (and even adjacent characters within the same word) render normally - Selecting the region reveals the characters at full opacity - system selection's foreground-color override bypasses the broken alpha rendering Looks like a wide-character clipping / alpha bug specifically at the AI panel's right boundary. ### To reproduce 1. Install a CJK-capable monospace font: `brew install --cask font-sarasa-gothic` 2. Edit `~/.warp/settings.toml`: ```toml [appearance.text] font_name = "Sarasa Mono TC" ai_font_name = "Sarasa Mono TC" font_size = 20.0 match_ai_font = true ``` 3. Use a dark theme (e.g. Darcula) 4. `Cmd+Q` to fully restart Warp 5. Open a Warp AI conversation 6. Ask any question that produces a CJK response long enough for some CJK characters to land at the right edge of the AI panel 7. Observe specific CJK characters at the panel's right-edge column become nearly invisible 8. Drag-select that vertical column → the previously-invisible characters appear at full opacity Reliably triggered when a 2-cell-wide CJK character would naturally span the panel's right boundary. Quick verification that this is the column-boundary bug (and not generic CJK rendering): - Resize the Warp window wider → the invisible characters move along with the panel's new right edge - Reduce `font_size` → invisible characters shift to whatever column lands on the new right edge ### Expected behavior All CJK characters in the AI panel should render with full foreground opacity regardless of column position. Wide (2-cell) characters approaching the panel's right edge should either: - render normally with full alpha, OR - wrap to the next line cleanly before the boundary ### Screenshots, videos, and logs Sequence of 5 screenshots showing the same Warp AI response, progressively drag-selecting different regions. As each region is selected, a previously-invisible CJK character (`？`, `量`, `塞`, `上` respectively) becomes visible. All four invisible characters fall on the same vertical column range (cells 28-30), corresponding to the AI panel's right edge. ### Operating system (OS) macOS ### Operating system and version macOS 15.x (Sequoia, Darwin 25.3.0) ### Shell Version zsh 5.9 ### Current Warp version v0.2026.05.06.15.42.stable_03 ### Regression No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp ### Recent working Warp date _No response_ ### Additional context **Environment** - Warp Stable - Font: `Sarasa Mono TC` Regular (installed via `brew install --cask font-sarasa-gothic`) - `font_size`: 20.0 - Theme: Darcula - `match_ai_font = true`, `ai_font_name = "Sarasa Mono TC"`, `font_name = "Sarasa Mono TC"` **Why this is reported as a new issue** (vs. existing #2902 / #1823) Existing CJK-rendering issues report "some Chinese text disappears" generically, often in vim/IME-input contexts. This report is narrower and adds a specific signal: **invisible characters always cluster at the same x-column boundary, not random characters**, which strongly suggests a wide-character clipping/alpha bug at the AI panel boundary rather than a general font/encoding issue. The official CJK workaround in Warp known-issues docs (`export LC_ALL=zh_CN.UTF-8` / `LANG=zh_CN.UTF-8`) does **not** fix this - that workaround is for locale/encoding issues, not GPU-rendering alpha at panel boundaries. `fc-match` confirms all affected characters (`？` `量` `塞` `上`) resolve to `Sarasa Mono TC` Regular, so the font has the glyphs. The bug is in how Warp renders 2-cell-wide characters that span the AI panel's right edge. ### Does this block you from using Warp daily? No ### Is this an issue only in Warp? Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals. ### Warp Internal (ignore): linear-label:b9d78064-c89e-4973-b153-5178a31ee54e None

title: [Windows] warp.exe crashes on window focus loss with Intel Iris Xe + DX12 backend
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there
- [x] I have technical issue and have included the logs (optional, but helps expedite the bug fix). [Log instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/troubleshooting-and-support/sending-us-feedback#gathering-warp-logs)

### Describe the bug

Warp crashes every time the window loses focus (Alt+Tab, clicking another app, etc.). The crash is silent - no error dialog, the process just terminates. This happened **9 times in 2 days**, generating 9 crash dumps under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps\warp.exe.*.dmp`.

Additionally, on every subsequent startup, the SQLite database requires WAL recovery, confirming each prior session ended as a crash rather than a clean shutdown.

**The crash is 100% reproducible on focus loss.** The last three log entries before every crash dump are always:

```
[INFO] active window changed: None
[INFO] dispatching global action for root_view:update_quake_mode_state
[INFO] dispatching global action for workspace:save_app
← process terminates here (log ends abruptly)
```

**Environment:**
- GPU: Intel Iris Xe Graphics (integrated), DX12 backend selected by Warp, driver `32.0.101.7077`
- Warp uses `wgpu` with the following adapters available:
  ```
  IntegratedGpu: Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics - DX12 (selected by default)
  IntegratedGpu: Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics - Vulkan
  IntegratedGpu: Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics - OpenGL
  Cpu: Microsoft Basic Render Driver
  ```

**Workaround found:** Switching the graphics backend from DX12 to **Vulkan** under `Settings → Features → System → Preferred graphics backend` stops the crashes. After switching, also delete `warp.sqlite-wal` and `warp.sqlite-shm` (with Warp closed) to clear the corrupted WAL state left by previous crashes.

Global Hotkey / Quake Mode is **disabled**, but `update_quake_mode_state` is still dispatched on every focus change event regardless, which appears to be what triggers the crash path when running on DX12 + Intel Iris Xe.

### To reproduce

1. Open Warp on Windows with an Intel Iris Xe GPU (default DX12 backend)
2. Open a terminal session
3. Alt+Tab to any other application (or click outside of Warp)
4. Warp silently closes

### Expected behavior

Warp should remain open and stable when losing window focus.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

**Startup log showing SQLite WAL recovery (every session after a crash):**
```
[WARN] SQLite error 283 (A WAL mode database file was recovered): recovered 249 frames from WAL file C:\Users\...\warp.sqlite-wal
[ERROR] Failed to read API keys from secure storage: File I/O error
```

**GPU adapter selection at startup:**
```
[INFO] Using DXC for DirectX shader compilation
[INFO] Enabled wgpu backends: Backends(NOOP | VULKAN | GL | METAL | DX12 | BROWSER_WEBGPU)
[INFO] Verifying adapter "Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics" is valid...
[INFO] Using Dx12 IntegratedGpu (Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics) for rendering new window.
```

**Last log entries before crash (consistent across all 9 crash dumps):**
```
[INFO] active window changed: None
[INFO] dispatching global action for root_view:update_quake_mode_state
[INFO] dispatching global action for workspace:save_app
← process terminates here (log ends abruptly, no ERROR/PANIC logged)
```

Crash dumps location: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps\warp.exe.*.dmp` (9 files, ~44-62 MB each)

### Operating system (OS)

Windows

### Operating system and version

Windows 11, WSL2 (Ubuntu), kernel `6.6.114.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2`

### Shell Version

bash 5.2.21 (WSL2)

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.05.06.15.42.stable_04

### Regression

Yes, this bug started recently or with an X Warp version

### Recent working Warp date

Prior to v0.2026.05.06.15.42.stable_04 (installer for stable_03 still present in `%TEMP%`)

### Additional context

- Global Hotkey is **disabled** in settings, yet `update_quake_mode_state` is dispatched on every focus change, suggesting this is an unconditional code path that may behave differently on DX12 vs Vulkan
- The `Failed to read API keys from secure storage: File I/O error` ERROR appears on every startup and may indicate a Windows Credential Manager issue that interacts with the `workspace:save_app` crash path
- **Switching to Vulkan backend fully resolves the crashes** - no crashes observed after the switch

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

Yes, this issue prevents me from using Warp daily.

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

title: MCP prompts capability: query, discovery, and slash-command dispatch in Warp
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

Surface MCP servers' **prompt templates** as first-class agent UX in Warp: query them at server startup, expose them through the slash-command menu, and prompt for arguments when the user invokes one. This is the "third leg" of MCP capability support alongside the already-shipped `tools/list` and `resources/list` paths (#6798 → #9436).

This issue is the **tracking parent** for a multi-PR rollout. Filing it in response to a process note on #10441 (the first sub-PR): the maintainer team wants a top-level scope before a partial implementation merges, so dead code doesn't accumulate.

### Scope and PR breakdown

| Sub-issue | Scope | PR | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **#9456** | Query `prompts/list` per advertised capability, store on `TemplatableMCPServerInfo` (data-only). | #10441 | Open, Oz-approved on prior SHA, awaits `ready-to-implement` |
| (to file after this issue is accepted) | Surface MCP prompts in the slash-command menu - make them discoverable + invocable inline. | - | Not started |
| (to file after this issue is accepted) | Argument-prompts UI for prompts that declare parameters (`PromptArgument`) - render input fields, validate required args, send back through `prompts/get`. | - | Not started |

The sub-issues are PR-sized; each can be reviewed independently. Sub-issue A is data-only on purpose - the field/getter it adds are `#[allow(dead_code)]` until sub-issue B's UI consumer lands.

### Volunteering

I'm volunteering to drive all three sub-PRs. Sub-issue A is already in flight via #10441; B and C I'll file once this top-level scope is accepted.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Today Warp queries MCP servers for `tools/list` (always) and `resources/list` (gated on the capability), but never `prompts/list`. Servers whose primary surface is prompt templates - e.g. prompts-only FastMCP servers, community prompt collections, [the github MCP server's prompts](https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server#prompts), [the Atlassian one](https://github.com/sooperset/mcp-atlassian) - are therefore invisible to Warp users even when properly registered and connected. The MCP server appears in Settings → MCP Servers as "connected, no tools available," with no indication that prompts exist.

Per the [MCP 2025-03-26 capability negotiation spec](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/lifecycle#capability-negotiation), a client must invoke a list method when (and only when) the corresponding capability is advertised during `initialize`. Warp partially implements this - it lists tools and resources - but skips prompts. The asymmetry is the bug.

### Additional context

#### Mechanically - what each sub-issue costs

**Sub-issue A (already in PR #10441):**
- `should_query_prompts(capabilities)` predicate (mirror of `should_query_resources`)
- `query_prompts_for(...)` async helper, fail-soft on errors
- `prompts: Vec<Prompt>` field on `TemplatableMCPServerInfo` + `.prompts()` getter
- Wired into `spawn_server`'s post-init block
- 11 unit tests covering predicate independence (2³ sweep), helper happy path, fail-soft paths

**Sub-issue B (slash-command discovery):**
- Extend the slash-command data source (`app/src/terminal/input/slash_commands/data_source/...`) to read from `TemplatableMCPServerManager`'s active servers and surface their prompts as commands
- Naming convention (suggest: `/mcp.<server>.<prompt-name>` or `/<server>.<prompt-name>` - TBD in review)
- Filter on enabled-MCP setting; respect existing AI-disabled gate

**Sub-issue C (argument UI):**
- For prompts with non-empty `arguments`, render input fields per `PromptArgument` (required vs optional, description, defaults if defined)
- On submit: build a `prompts/get` request with the populated arguments, send to the server, receive the rendered prompt content, dispatch into the agent block
- Use the existing rich-input form pattern where it exists; otherwise a minimal modal

#### Why this is the right shape

- Matches the existing tools/resources control flow exactly - no new architectural concept
- Adds value at every sub-PR: A unblocks B (prompts in the data model), B unblocks C (argument UI on top of discoverable prompts)
- Each sub-PR is reviewable in <500 lines

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

3

title: Warpify does not work with podman exec -it <container> /bin/bash
body:

- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there

- [ ] I have technical issue and have included the logs (optional, but helps expedite the bug fix). [Log instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/troubleshooting-and-support/sending-us-feedback#gathering-warp-logs)

### Describe the bug

Warpify does not work with podman exec -it <container> /bin/bash. Three underlying issues prevent it:

 1. The subshell command regex allowlist only matches docker exec/run, not podman exec/run, so the warpify banner never appears.
 2. Even when manually triggered via the added_subshell_commands override, warpify hangs at "Starting shell ..." because the DCS escape sequences use the C1 ST byte (0x9c) as the string terminator. Podman's PTY proxy (conmon) mangles this byte since it falls in the UTF-8 continuation byte range (0x80-0xBF), so the DCS sequence never terminates and the VTE parser consumes all subsequent output.
 3. After fixing the DCS terminator, the full ~32KB bootstrap script is written to the PTY in a single burst. Podman's double-PTY architecture (host PTY → conmon → container PTY) drops data for writes larger than ~8-16KB, so the bootstrap never completes.

### To reproduce

 1. Start a container: podman run -dit --name test ubuntu:latest bash
 2. In Warp, run: podman exec -it test /bin/bash
 3. No warpify banner appears (podman not in the allowlist)
 4. If you add podman exec to Settings → Warpify → Added Subshell Commands, the banner appears but clicking "Warpify subshell" hangs at "Starting shell ..." indefinitely

### Expected behavior

 Warpify should work with podman exec the same way it works with docker exec - the warpify banner should appear and clicking it should bootstrap the subshell successfully.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

_No response_

### Operating system (OS)

Linux

### Operating system and version

Fedora 44 (Linux 7.0.4-200.fc44.x86_64)

### Shell Version

bash 5.2

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.05.06.15.42.stable_04

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Recent working Warp date

_No response_

### Additional context

Podman uses the same CLI interface as Docker but its container runtime monitor (conmon) proxies PTY I/O differently. The double-PTY architecture (host PTY → conmon → container PTY) has two characteristics that differ from Docker: (1) the 0x9c byte gets mangled in UTF-8 mode, and (2) large single writes (>8-16KB) overflow intermediate buffers. A fix is submitted in PR #9831.

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

Yes, this issue prevents me from using Warp daily.

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

title: Add a setting to opt out of automatic model fallback when the selected model is unavailable
body:
<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary
Add a user-facing setting to opt out of Warp's automatic model fallback so an unavailable selected model surfaces an error instead of being silently swapped for a different provider's model.

## Problem
Warp's [model fallback system](https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/warp-agents/model-choice#model-fallback) silently swaps the selected model for a different one (potentially from a different provider) when the primary is temporarily unavailable. There is currently no way to opt out - the docs describe the behavior as automatic with no setting referenced.

For users who picked a specific model deliberately (e.g. Claude Opus 4.7 for code quality, prompt-style compatibility, reasoning behavior, or cost/credit reasons), being routed to a very different model (e.g. GPT-5.4) without consent is disruptive: the agent's tone, tool-use behavior, diff style, and credit consumption all change mid-session. The user reporting this prefers to see an error and retry/wait rather than continue on a substitute model.

## Reproduction steps or desired workflow
Current behavior:
1. Open **Settings** > **Agents** > **Profiles** and set the base model to `Claude Opus 4.7` (any variant).
2. Start an agent conversation while the Anthropic Opus 4.7 endpoint is unavailable (e.g. during a provider outage or capacity-throttled period).
3. Observe that Warp transparently switches the active model to a fallback such as `GPT-5.4` and continues the conversation.

Desired workflow:
1. Same setup as above.
2. In **Settings** > **Agents** (or **Settings** > **Agents** > **Profiles** as part of the base-model picker), expose a toggle such as "Automatically fall back to another model when my selected model is unavailable", defaulting to on to preserve current behavior.
3. With the toggle off, when the selected model is unavailable, Warp surfaces a clear inline error (e.g. "Claude Opus 4.7 is currently unavailable - retry or pick another model") and does not proceed on a different model. The user can then retry, wait, or manually pick an alternative from the model picker.

## Artifacts
None attached.

## Warp version
Unknown.

## Operating system
Unknown (report submitted from a Linux/Ubuntu host, but the reporting machine is not necessarily where the issue was experienced).

## Possible source references
- Docs: `agent-platform/warp-agents/model-choice` § "Model fallback" - describes current automatic behavior; this is the user-facing surface that would need to mention the new opt-out.
- Settings surface: `Settings` > `Agents` > `Profiles` (base-model picker) - natural location for a per-profile fallback toggle, alongside the existing base/planning model selection described in `agent-platform/warp-agents/agent-profiles-permissions` § "Agent Profiles".

title: Windows: OpenConsole.exe ACCESS_VIOLATION crash when PTY pipe breaks, causing pwsh.exe FailFast - Unknown Hard Error
body:
## Environment
- **Warp version**: v0.2026.05.06.15.42.stable_05
- **OS**: Windows 11
- **Shell**: PowerShell 7.6.1 (pwsh.exe), PSReadLine 2.4.5
- **Repro**: Reliably - every time Ctrl+C is pressed on a foreground process that uses the PTY (e.g., OpenCode CLI)

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open Warp with pwsh.exe as default shell
2. Run any foreground TUI/CLI app that uses PTY pipes (e.g., OpenCode `oc`, `nvim`, or a long-running script)
3. Press Ctrl+C to terminate the foreground process

## Expected Behavior
The foreground process terminates cleanly. Warp remains responsive. No error dialogs.

## Actual Behavior
1. `OpenConsole.exe` (bundled in `C:\Users\...\AppData\Local\Programs\Warp\x64\OpenConsole.exe`) crashes with **ACCESS VIOLATION (0xc0000005)** - recorded as Windows Application Event ID 1000
2. `pwsh.exe` then fails with **Environment.FailFast** - recorded as Windows Application Event ID 1025
3. A modal dialog appears titled "pwsh.exe - Advertencia del sistema" with message "Unknown Hard Error"
4. Clicking "Aceptar" (OK) closes Warp entirely

## Windows Event Log Evidence

### Event ID 1000 - OpenConsole.exe crash
```
Nombre de aplicación con errores: OpenConsole.exe, versión: 0.0.0.0
Nombre del módulo con errores: OpenConsole.exe, versión: 0.0.0.0
Código de excepción: 0xc0000005
Desplazamiento con errores: 0x000000000006287a
Ruta: C:\Users\[user]\AppData\Local\Programs\Warp\x64\OpenConsole.exe
```

### Event ID 1025 - pwsh.exe FailFast
```
Application: pwsh.exe
CoreCLR Version: 10.0.526.15411
.NET Version: 10.0.5
Description: The application requested process termination through System.Environment.FailFast.
Message: The Win32 internal error "No hay ningún proceso en el otro extremo de la canalización." 
         0xE9 occurred while getting console output buffer information.

Stack trace:
  at Microsoft.PowerShell.ConsoleControl.GetConsoleScreenBufferInfo(SafeFileHandle consoleHandle)
  at Microsoft.PowerShell.ConsoleHostRawUserInterface.get_CursorPosition()
  at Microsoft.PowerShell.ConsoleHost.InputLoop.Run(Boolean inputLoopIsNested)
  at Microsoft.PowerShell.ConsoleHost.EnterNestedPrompt()
  ...
  at System.Environment.FailFast(...)
```

## Analysis
The crash chain is:
1. Ctrl+C terminates the foreground process (e.g., OpenCode)
2. The PTY pipe between Warp → OpenConsole.exe → pwsh.exe breaks
3. `OpenConsole.exe` attempts to access an already-closed pipe → ACCESS VIOLATION (0xc0000005)
4. `pwsh.exe` calls `GetConsoleScreenBufferInfo()` which fails with Win32 error 0xE9 - "No process at the other end of the pipe"
5. `pwsh.exe` triggers `Environment.FailFast` → "Unknown Hard Error" dialog

The issue persists even after reinstalling Warp completely. It also occurs independently of the `@warp-dot-dev/opencode-warp` plugin (repros without it).

The root cause appears to be in how OpenConsole.exe handles abrupt pipe disconnection, combined with pwsh.exe's `ConsoleHost` failing fast when it can't reach the console buffer.

## Notes
- This happens with ANY foreground process terminated via Ctrl+C, not just OpenCode
- The `pwsh.ps1` bootstrap script's runspace pools may exacerbate the issue (multiple threads accessing the PTY concurrently), but the crash is reproducible even when the pools don't have active work

title: Size-based rotation for warp.log within a session (currently startup-only)
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

`warp_logging::rotate_log_files()` rotates `warp.log` and its telemetry siblings once at app startup: the previous session's log becomes `.old.0`, older ones shift up to `.old.N`, and the oldest gets discarded. That model works well for users who restart Warp frequently - each session gets its own log file.

For long-running sessions (developers who keep Warp open for days or weeks), the active `warp.log` grows unboundedly during a single session, with no checkpoints in between. The startup rotation never fires until the next restart.

Proposal: add an in-session size-based rotation mode to `warp_logging`, complementing the existing startup rotation. When the active `warp.log` exceeds a configured size threshold mid-session, it's rotated to an in-session sibling (e.g. `warp.log.in_session.N`) and a fresh active file is opened. The startup `.old.N` semantics that log-bundle uploads and other UX depend on stay untouched.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Two related reports for *other* log files exist:

- #7723 / #10874 - MCP server logs not rotated (`simple_logger`)
- #10877 - LSP server logs not rotated (`simple_logger`)

Both of those operate on a different rotation engine than `warp.log`, but the underlying user complaint is the same: Warp's diagnostic data grows without bound during long sessions. Capping `warp.log` at e.g. 50 MiB × 5 rotated copies would bound it at ~300 MiB even across multi-day sessions, while preserving the per-session file boundary at startup that today's UX (e.g. log-bundle uploads) relies on.

### Additional context

This complements (does not replace) the MCP/LSP rotation work. Different file, different rotation engine, but the same principle: cap on-disk footprint during long sessions while preserving the current per-session semantics.

Sketch of the implementation surface:

- Extend `LogConfig` with optional `max_file_size_bytes` (or equivalent threshold)
- Plumb that to the log writer (e.g. tracing-appender's rolling appender, or a manual periodic size check)
- Rotation pattern: e.g. `warp.log.in_session.N` to distinguish from the existing startup `.old.N` files

title: Optional LLM-driven summarization on log rotation (knowledge retention across discards)
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

When a log file rotates past the configured retention cap, its contents are discarded forever. For verbose servers (MCP, LSP) where rotation can fire multiple times per day, this discards potentially-useful debugging signal - error patterns, slow queries, transport hiccups - that the user could have referenced later.

Proposal: an **optional**, **opt-in** summarization layer that runs at rotation time. Before the oldest rotation file is unlinked, its contents are handed to a configurable summarizer (typically a model call) that extracts findings into a structured record. Records are appended to a sidecar file next to the logs, so the user retains a long-term view of what was happening even after the raw bytes are gone.

Two layers, separable:

**Layer A - Rotation event log (no model dep)**

A `<path>.rotations.jsonl` sidecar captures *when* rotations happened, *what* was rotated, and basic stats. Always on; no model required.

Example record:

```jsonl
{"timestamp":"2026-05-14T18:32:09Z","active_log":".../server.log","bytes_rotated":10485760,"discarded_path":".../server.log.5"}
```

**Layer B - Optional summarization pipeline (model-backed)**

A `RotationSummarizer` async trait threaded through `SimpleLogger::new_with_summarizer` as `Option<Arc<dyn RotationSummarizer>>`. Implementations may:

- Call a local model (Ollama, LM Studio) - preferred default
- Call a remote BYOK endpoint
- Use a deterministic mock (testing)
- Chain multiple calls (extract events → classify → summarize)

Summaries appended to `<path>.summaries.jsonl`.

Example record:

```jsonl
{
  "timestamp": "2026-05-14T18:32:14Z",
  "source_path": ".../server.log.5",
  "bytes_summarized": 10485760,
  "model": "qwen2.5-coder:7b@ollama-local",
  "pipeline": [
    {"step": "extract_events", "duration_ms": 412},
    {"step": "classify", "duration_ms": 287},
    {"step": "summarize", "duration_ms": 893}
  ],
  "summary": "Server emitted 142 warnings about cache misses on /api/products; one transport disconnect at 16:42 followed by automatic reconnect.",
  "findings": [
    "Cache miss rate spiked from baseline 3% to 41% between 16:30 and 16:50",
    "Single transport disconnect at 16:42 (recovered)",
    "No errors above WARN level"
  ]
}
```

**Hard contract - Layer B is fully optional:**

- Off by default
- No build-time model dependency
- No runtime model call unless the user explicitly opts in
- Summarizer failure (model unavailable, network down) returns `Ok(None)` (or surfaces an error that's logged + swallowed) and rotation proceeds without a summary - never blocks rotation

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Current rotation work (#10874 for MCP; companion #10877 for LSP and #10879 for `warp.log`) caps disk usage but loses long-term diagnostic context. For users running into intermittent issues that surface across hours or days, the "log was rotated out before I noticed" pattern is real.

Composability with the local-model work in #9619: a local Qwen / Devstral / Llama via Ollama runs summarization without any network egress, fitting the same privacy-strict use case the local-model harness work is designed for.

### Additional context

**POC PR: #10882 (draft).** Adds the two sidecars, the `RotationSummarizer` trait, a deterministic `MockSummarizer` reference impl, end-to-end tests, and sample synthetic log + sample rotation/summary records under `examples/advanced_log_rotation/`. The PR is intentionally scoped to architecture + plumbing + mock - a real local-model integration is the obvious follow-up but stays out of the POC.

The trait surface is namespace-agnostic - it works equally well for MCP logs (`simple_logger`'s `mcp` namespace), LSP logs (`lsp` namespace, see #10877), and any future `simple_logger` consumer. Each namespace can configure its own pipeline or share a global default.

Out of scope for the first iteration:

- Real LLM integration (the POC ships only the deterministic `MockSummarizer`; a real Ollama/BYOK impl would be a follow-up PR)
- Model selection UX
- Summary indexing / retrieval ("show me all rotations that mentioned `cache miss`")
- Automatic anomaly alerting based on findings
- Streaming summarization (currently batch only)

These are good follow-ups once the data shape stabilizes.

macOS
