title: OpenAI Responses requests should sanitize cross-provider tool_call_id values server-side (follow-up to #10837)
body:
### Pre-submit checks

- Originating PR (closed): #10837 - *fix(agent): sanitize overlong tool call IDs before OpenAI Responses requests*
- Originating issue: #8997
- Triage conversation: `406ae4eb-feb5-4aa3-800d-dd0f59a552a0`

### Summary

When an agent conversation involves a non-OpenAI BYOK backend (GLM, Kimi, etc. via OpenAI-compatible endpoints) and that same conversation later issues a `POST /v1/responses` call against real OpenAI - most commonly via the OpenAI-fallback path - the non-OpenAI provider's `tool_call_id` values are carried into the OpenAI request body unchanged. Those IDs routinely exceed OpenAI's 64-character limit, producing an unrecoverable 400:

```
OpenAI API error: POST "https://api.openai.com/v1/responses": 400 Bad Request {
    "message": "Invalid 'input[24].call_id': string too long. Expected a string
                with maximum length 64, but got a string with length 210 instead.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": "input[24].call_id",
    "code": "string_above_max_length"
}
```

PR #10837 proposed a client-side defense (hash overlong IDs at the request-building boundary). On review (@szgupta), the team decided this belongs in the server harness instead - `tool_call_id` is used as a reference key in multiple places in the data model, so any sanitization needs to be applied consistently across every consumer of the ID, not just the wire boundary.

This issue tracks the server-side fix.

### Reproduction (client-observable)

1. Configure a BYOK provider that emits long `tool_call_id` values (verified with GLM-5 and Kimi).
2. Start an agent conversation, drive it long enough that a fallback or follow-up call lands on OpenAI's `/v1/responses` endpoint with the prior turn's tool call results in the request body.
3. Request fails 400 with `Invalid 'input[N].call_id': string too long`.

Conversation ID with this exact failure: `406ae4eb-feb5-4aa3-800d-dd0f59a552a0`.

### Expected behavior

When the agent harness emits a `/v1/responses` request whose history contains `tool_call_id` values from a non-OpenAI provider, those IDs should be sanitized to satisfy OpenAI's 64-char limit. The sanitization must be deterministic (same upstream ID → same client-side ID) and applied uniformly everywhere the harness uses the ID as a reference key - request body, internal lookup tables, replay/serialization paths.

PR #10837 used `call_<sha256-hex truncated to 64 chars>` as the sanitization scheme. Whether the server fix adopts that exact scheme or something else is up to the team, but the deterministic-mapping property is load-bearing for preserving the tool-call ↔ result pairing across turns.

### Out of scope (handled separately)

The "why does a non-OpenAI provider's tool-call result reach OpenAI in the first place" question. Per @szgupta this is the fallback path doing what it's designed to do; users who want to disable it can use the Models settings toggle (screenshot in #10837 conversation). This issue is strictly about the harness sanitizing IDs before they leave for OpenAI.

### Operating system (OS)

Any (server-side issue; client is OS-agnostic).

### How important is this feature to you?

3 - users on GLM/Kimi via BYOK hit this whenever the OpenAI fallback engages on a conversation that includes a non-OpenAI tool call. It's unrecoverable per-conversation until the entry is purged.

title: Linux Wayland (NVIDIA nouveau): typing crashes on Plasma, launch crash + lost terminal tabs on Hyprland, past Agent conversations won't open
body:
<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary
On Linux/Wayland (NVIDIA nouveau), Warp exhibits three related problems: (1) opening past Agent conversations from the history list does nothing or errors, (2) on KDE Plasma Wayland the app crashes when typing into either the Agent chat input or a regular terminal prompt, and (3) on Hyprland the app crashes on launch on first attempt, and on the second launch opens but does not restore the previous window's terminal tabs/panes.

## Problem
After switching the user's display server from X11 to Wayland on KDE Plasma, Warp began crashing as soon as the user typed into a chat window - both the Agent/AI input and the normal shell prompt. Hoping for better behavior, the user switched to Hyprland; Warp then crashed on first launch, and on a second launch opened successfully but the previous session's terminal tabs/panes were gone. Independently, when trying to resume uncompleted work, the user clicks past conversations in the Agent history list and nothing happens (or it errors), so prior work cannot be reopened. Net effect: the user cannot reliably use Warp on this Wayland setup and has lost access to in-progress work.

## Expected behavior
- Typing in either the Agent chat input or a terminal prompt should not crash Warp on KDE Plasma Wayland.
- Warp should launch reliably on Hyprland on first attempt.
- Restarting Warp should restore the previous window's tabs/panes.
- Clicking a past conversation in the Agent history list should open that conversation.

## Actual behavior
- KDE Plasma Wayland: Warp crashes when typing into the Agent chat input and when typing at a regular shell prompt.
- Hyprland: Warp crashes immediately on first launch. On a second launch it opens, but the previously open terminal tabs/panes are not restored.
- Past Agent conversations are visible in the history list, but clicking them does nothing or errors; the conversation does not open.

## Reproduction steps or desired workflow
1. On Arch-based Linux (EndeavourOS) with NVIDIA nouveau drivers, run a Wayland session (KDE Plasma).
2. Launch Warp and start typing in either the Agent chat input or a regular terminal prompt → Warp crashes.
3. Switch the session to Hyprland and launch Warp → crashes on first launch.
4. Launch Warp again on Hyprland → window opens, but previous terminal tabs/panes are missing.
5. Open the Agent panel and click a past conversation from the history list → nothing happens or an error occurs; the conversation does not open.

## Artifacts
None attached. Logs under `~/.local/state/warp-terminal/warp.log*` are present and can be uploaded on request; no panic/crash/wgpu/wayland error strings were visible in the immediate tail of the most recent rotated log on inspection.

## Warp version
v0.2026.05.13.09.15.stable_01

## Operating system
EndeavourOS (Arch-based), kernel 7.0.7-arch1-1. GPU: NVIDIA on the nouveau (open) driver. Display servers tried: KDE Plasma Wayland and Hyprland.

## Possible source references
- Linux Wayland + NVIDIA crash on launch class of bugs (e.g. wgpu/Vulkan adapter selection): see related report `warpdotdev/warp#11003` ("Linux/Wayland + NVIDIA dGPU: wgpu Device lost on launch, all adapters report 'Can present: false', no fallback") for context on Wayland+NVIDIA launch failures, though that report is specific to the proprietary driver while this user is on nouveau.
- Wayland-related rendering/IME path: see existing reports `warpdotdev/warp#4462` (Wayland Plasma flicker), `warpdotdev/warp#5606` / `warpdotdev/warp#6877` (Wayland text-input/IME) - typing-triggered crash on Wayland may share input-handling surface area.
- Session/tab restoration code path: see `warpdotdev/warp#10833` and `warpdotdev/warp#8508` for prior tab/session restore regressions; lost-tabs-after-crash-restart may reuse the same restore logic.

title: Allow disabling automatic updates from the Settings UI (or at least via `settings.toml`)
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

Add a user-facing setting in **Settings → About / General** to disable Warp's automatic update behavior, with three states (or two toggles):

- **Automatically check for updates** (toggle, default **On**)
- **Automatically download updates in the background** (toggle, default **On**, dependent on the above)

Behavior when both are **Off**:

- No periodic poll to `/client_version` or `/client_version/daily` (currently every 10 minutes - see `AUTOUPDATE_POLL` in `app/src/autoupdate/mod.rs`).
- No background download of new builds.
- The **"Check for updates"** button in Settings still works for an on-demand manual check.
- If a new version is found via a manual check, the existing "Update available / Relaunch Warp" UI still appears - the user can opt in per-update.
- No "Update available" banner/badge is shown (#1991) unless the user manually checked.


### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Right now, there is **no runtime way at all** to stop Warp from polling for and downloading updates. The `autoupdate` behavior is gated only by a compile-time cargo feature and `AppExecutionMode::can_autoupdate()`. End users can't turn it off without rebuilding Warp from source or blackholing the update endpoint at the firewall - and even firewalling doesn't stop the 10-minute polling loop from running and failing.

That's a problem in many real situations:

1. **Reproducibility and version pinning.** Power users, SREs, anyone writing tutorials/screencasts, regulated environments (finance, healthcare, gov), and CI/dev VMs all need to stay on a known-good version. Today, the next launch can silently install a queued update.

2. **Metered, tethered, or flaky networks.** Polling every 10 minutes plus background-downloading multi-hundred-MB builds is unfriendly on cellular tethering, conference Wi-Fi, satellite, hotel networks, etc. Users should be able to opt out.

3. **Privacy.** Every poll is a [phone-home](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues/9717) with `update_id`, channel, and version. Users who don't want a periodic heartbeat to Warp's servers currently have no opt-out short of pulling the network.

4. **Package-manager-installed Warp on Linux.** Users on apt/dnf/AUR/Homebrew/nix get updates from their package manager. Warp's in-app updater duplicates and conflicts with that - the code already has an "apt repository disabled due to version update" path (`is_apt_repository_disabled_due_to_version_update` in `app/src/autoupdate/linux.rs`), which suggests this collision is already painful enough to warrant special-casing. A simple "off switch" would be cleaner.

5. **Corporate / MDM-managed fleets.** IT departments need a way to centrally pin Warp's version. Today the only option is to deploy a custom build without the `autoupdate` cargo feature, which most orgs won't do.

6. **Air-gapped / offline environments.** Research labs, secure terminals, customer-site engineering laptops. Today they see perpetual failed-update warnings (`AutoupdateStage::UnableToUpdateToNewVersion`) with no way to silence them.

Several of these are already filed informally in community channels; consolidating them under one "let me turn it off" toggle is the minimum-viable fix.


### Additional context

Claude suggested where to wire this in:

- `AutoupdateState::start_polling` (`app/src/autoupdate/mod.rs#L141-161`) already short-circuits on `FeatureFlag::Autoupdate.is_enabled() && AppExecutionMode::as_ref(ctx).can_autoupdate()`. Adding a runtime preference check at the same call site (and re-evaluating it when the setting changes via `ctx.observe`) is the natural place.
- The daily check kicked off in `AuthManager::on_user_fetched` (`app/src/auth/auth_manager.rs#L437-442`) should consult the same preference.
- `RequestType::ManualCheck` should continue to be honored regardless of the preference, so the "Check for updates" button still works on demand.
- The UI surface fits naturally in `MainSettingsPageView::render_version_info` (`app/src/settings_view/main_page.rs#L835-902`), right next to the existing update status and "Check for updates" call-to-action.

**Prior art:** This is a standard, expected control for a desktop app.
- VS Code (`update.mode`),
- Zed (`"auto_update": false,`),
- JetBrains IDEs (Settings → Appearance & Behavior → System Settings → Updates),
- iTerm2 (Preferences → General → "Check for updates automatically"),
- Sublime Text, Slack desktop, Discord etc.

### Operating system (OS)

Cross-platform

### How important is this feature to you?

4

title: feat: LaTeX PDF preview pane using tectonic (no TeX Live required)
body:
## Pre-submit Checks
- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

## Describe the solution you'd like?

Add a live PDF preview pane for `.tex` files in Warp. When editing a LaTeX document, a split pane shows the compiled PDF output and updates on every save - no external TeX Live installation required.

The entire stack can be implemented using existing Rust crates:

- **[`tectonic`](https://github.com/tectonic-typesetting/tectonic)** - self-contained LaTeX engine written in Rust. Bundles its own TeX distribution, compiles `.tex` → `.pdf` with a single crate dependency. No `pdflatex` or TeX Live needed on the user's machine.
- **[`pdfium-render`](https://github.com/ajrcarey/pdfium-render)** - Rust bindings to Google's PDFium library. Converts PDF pages to pixel buffers that can be rendered via Warp's existing `wgpu` pipeline.

**Proposed behaviour:**
- Opening a `.tex` file automatically shows a preview pane (dismissible)
- Compiles in a background thread on every save - no UI blocking
- LaTeX compile errors displayed inline in the editor (line numbers, error messages)
- Zoom + scroll in the preview pane
- Works on macOS, Linux, and Windows - no system dependencies

**Proposed technical stack:**

```
User saves .tex file in Warp editor
        ↓
crates/latex_preview detects save via existing file watcher
        ↓
tectonic::latex_to_pdf() runs in background thread
        ↓
pdfium-render converts PDF page → wgpu-compatible pixel buffer
        ↓
New WarpUI preview pane renders the pixel buffer alongside the editor
```

## Is your feature request related to a problem?

LaTeX is the standard document format in academia, research, and technical writing. Currently, working on `.tex` files in Warp means constantly switching to an external app (Overleaf, TeXShop, VS Code + LaTeX Workshop) just to see what the compiled document looks like. There is no terminal today that offers native LaTeX preview - Warp would be the first.

## Additional context

The syntax highlighting foundation for LaTeX is already being added to Warp via arborium (see `bearcove/arborium#202`). This feature would be the next natural step - from "LaTeX source is coloured" to "LaTeX source is live-compiled and previewed."

**Relevant prior art:**
- VS Code LaTeX Workshop (most popular LaTeX extension, 10M+ installs)
- Overleaf (cloud-based, but sets the UX standard users expect)
- TeXShop (macOS native, shows what the split-pane UX should feel like)

Cross-platform

title: IME regression on macOS: duplicate characters, double-press Backspace, and Tab inserts literal \t with Boshiamy IME (broken between Stable 0.2026.04.29 and 0.2026.05.13)
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have searched Warp bugs and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have searched Warp known issues page and my issue is not there

### Describe the bug

Between Warp Stable `0.2026.04.29.08.57.01` and `0.2026.05.13.09.15.03`, IME handling on macOS regressed. With the Boshiamy (無蝦米) input method active, three distinct symptoms appear that did not exist in the prior Stable build:

1. **Duplicate characters** - committed characters appear twice (committed char + the raw latin keystrokes used during composition leak into the terminal).
2. **Backspace requires two presses** to delete a single character (first press is consumed by the IME composition buffer, second press reaches the shell).
3. **Tab inserts a literal `\t`** instead of triggering shell completion (Tab is sent as a raw character before the IME finishes committing).

All three symptoms are facets of the same underlying issue: IME composition keystrokes are leaking into the terminal instead of being fully consumed via `NSTextInputClient`, contrary to standard macOS `NSResponder` behavior.

### To reproduce

1. macOS with the Boshiamy (無蝦米) input method selected as the active input source.
2. Open Warp Stable `0.2026.05.13.09.15.03`.
3. Type any Chinese character via Boshiamy. Example: keys `v o r` → expected `項`.
4. **Observed**: `項項` or `項vor` appears in the prompt instead of just `項`.
5. Press Backspace once → nothing visibly deleted. Press a second time → one character is deleted.
6. Press Tab during or immediately after composition → a literal `\t` is inserted; shell completion is not triggered.

Reproduces 100% of the time on the affected build. Does not reproduce at all on Warp Stable `0.2026.04.29.08.57.01` on a second Mac with the same OS family and the same Boshiamy install.

### Expected behavior

- IME composition keystrokes should be fully consumed by the input method during composition. Only the committed text should reach the terminal.
- Backspace during/after composition should behave atomically - one press deletes one character.
- Tab should trigger shell completion, not insert a literal tab character, regardless of whether an IME is active.
- Behavior should match `0.2026.04.29.08.57.01`, Terminal.app, and iTerm2.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

Screenshot of the duplicate-character symptom available on request (will attach via web UI in a follow-up comment). Happy to also capture a screen recording and attach Warp logs if it would help narrow down the offending build.

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

### Operating system and version

macOS 26.5 (build 25F71), Apple Silicon (arm64)

### Shell Version

zsh 5.9

### Current Warp version

`v0.2026.05.13.09.15.03` (Stable channel, bundle ID `dev.warp.Warp-Stable`)

### Regression

Yes, this bug started recently or with an X Warp version

### Recent working Warp date

2026-04-29 - confirmed working on Warp Stable `v0.2026.04.29.08.57.01` on a second Mac (same macOS family, same Boshiamy install, same shell, same locale). Regression window: **2026-04-29 → 2026-05-13 on the Stable channel**.

### Additional context

**Bisect evidence**

| Machine | Warp version | Bundle ID | Channel | Symptoms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Broken (this report) | `0.2026.05.13.09.15.03` | `dev.warp.Warp-Stable` | Stable | All 3 symptoms |
| Working (second Mac) | `0.2026.04.29.08.57.01` | `dev.warp.Warp-Stable` | Stable | None |

Only the Warp version differs between the two machines.

**Cross-terminal verification (same machine as the broken Warp)**

A/B tested Boshiamy on this same Mac in:

- Terminal.app - all 3 symptoms absent, Boshiamy works correctly.
- iTerm2 - all 3 symptoms absent, Boshiamy works correctly.

So the issue is specific to Warp `0.2026.05.13.09.15.03` on this machine; it is not a system-level IME or Boshiamy install issue.

**Workarounds attempted (none resolved the issue)**

- Switched `Settings → Appearance → Input` to `Shell (PS1)` (Classic Input). Symptoms unchanged - Classic Input only changes prompt rendering, not the IME handling layer.
- Verified `LC_ALL` / `LANG` are `zh_TW.UTF-8`.

**Suspected cause**

The `NSTextInputClient` implementation in the input layer appears to have changed between `0.2026.04.29` and `0.2026.05.13`. Composition keystrokes are no longer being fully consumed by the IME, so they leak through as raw key events to the terminal. Boshiamy is particularly affected because its radical alphabet is `a-z`, which 100% overlaps with valid shell input - every leak is visible. IMEs whose composition uses non-ASCII radicals (e.g., Zhuyin's ㄅㄆㄇ) may hide the same leak.

**Related issues**

- #341 (IME-related keybinding issues - still open)
- #6891 (general IME support - closed as duplicate of #341)
- #2335 (Chinese input following issue)

This appears to be a fresh regression on top of the longer-standing IME limitations, not a pre-existing issue, so a revert of the input-layer change between 04-29 and 05-13 may be a quick fix candidate.

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

title: macOS dock icon badge counting terminals that rang the bell
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

When a terminal rings the bell (`\a`), Warp bounces the macOS dock icon. The bounce is useful but **transient** (it stops) and **carries no count** - with several terminals belling across tabs/windows, one bell looks the same as five.

I'd like a **numeric badge on the dock icon** showing how many terminals have rung the bell and haven't been viewed yet. It's a persistent, glanceable complement to the bounce - driven by the *same* event (the terminal bell), so it never disagrees with the bounce users already know.

Behavior: a terminal is counted when it bells while you're not looking at it; cleared when you view it (focus the tab, or re-activate Warp on it) or its shell exits. Zero ⇒ no badge.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I run several terminals in parallel (often concurrent agent sessions). When I step away, the bounce doesn't persist, and when I return I can't tell how many terminals need attention without clicking through every tab.

### Additional context

- **Scope:** this is a count of *terminal bells* - exactly what bounces the   dock. It is deliberately **not** a semantic "agent needs input" badge (the   bell doesn't carry that distinction), and not a badge for every long-running   command (only ones that bell). macOS-only for now; other platforms no-op.

title: AI agent path helpers emit unquoted paths to `test -f` / `git -C` / `grep` / `find`, breaking paths with shell metacharacters
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there
- [ ] I have an issue with AI and have included the debugging ID (Optional, but helps expedite the AI quality fix). [Debugging ID instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/agent/ai-faqs#gathering-ai-debugging-id)
- [ ] I have technical issue and have included the logs (optional, but helps expedite the bug fix). [Log instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/troubleshooting-and-support/sending-us-feedback#gathering-warp-logs)

### Describe the bug

  When the AI agent invokes its `grep` or `file_glob` tools, several internal helpers in `app/src/ai/blocklist/action_model/execute/`
  build shell commands by interpolating an agent-supplied path directly into a double-quoted string and handing the result to
  `Session::execute_command`:
  
  ```rust
  // execute.rs
  format!("test -f \"{path}\"")                                  // is_file_path (POSIX)
  format!("if (Test-Path -PathType Leaf \"{path}\") ...")        // is_file_path (PowerShell)
  format!("git -C \"{absolute_path}\" rev-parse")                // is_git_repository

  // grep.rs
  grep_command.push_str(format!(" \"{target_path}\"").as_str()); // git grep / grep
  "Get-ChildItem -Path \"{}\" ... | Select-String ..."           // Select-String

  // file_glob.rs
  format!("find \"{target_path}\" -type f {pattern_args}")       // find
  format!("Get-ChildItem ... -Path \"{target_path}\" ...")       // PowerShell Get-ChildItem

  Inside POSIX "...", the shell still expands $VAR, `...`, and $(...). Inside PowerShell "...", the shell still expands $x (including
  $env:USERPROFILE) and treats ` specially. POSIX filesystems permit all of these bytes in a path component and PowerShell accepts them
  in -Path arguments, so a path containing shell metacharacters is split, expanded, or substituted by the shell before the underlying
  tool (test, git, grep, find, Get-ChildItem, Test-Path, Select-String) ever sees it.

  is_file_path and is_git_repository are particularly exposed because they are called as side-effects of the grep and file_glob tools
  (run_grep → is_file_path + is_git_repository, run_file_glob → is_git_repository) before the user sees the user-facing command, so even
   path values the user never typed flow into the shell verbatim.

  The repo already exposes the correct primitive: warp_util::path::ShellFamily::shell_escape covers both POSIX (backslash) and
  PowerShell (backtick) families, and From<ShellType> for ShellFamily makes the dispatch one line. The sister helpers
  format_change_directory_command (display_chip.rs) and the recently-fixed open_repo_folder / NeedsCd flows already do the right thing;
  the agent-side helpers were missed.

  This can lead to:
  - Probing the wrong path silently (e.g. is_file_path("/tmp/$HOME/x") resolves $HOME and probes a path the user never named - dangerous
   behavior)
  - Shell parsing errors when the path contains (, ), ;, &, |, etc.
  - Unexpected command execution behavior when the path contains $(...) or backtick command substitution

### To reproduce

  **To reproduce**
  1. Create a directory whose name contains a shell metacharacter:

  mkdir -p "/tmp/innocent\$(touch ~/PROBE_RAN)"
  2. Ask the agent to grep or glob inside it, for example:
  
  Search "TODO" in /tmp/innocent$(touch ~/PROBE_RAN)
  3. Observe that the agent emits, e.g.:

  test -f "/tmp/innocent$(touch ~/PROBE_RAN)"
  3. to the user's shell. The shell evaluates $(touch ~/PROBE_RAN) before test -f runs, creating ~/PROBE_RAN.
  4. ls ~/PROBE_RAN confirms the substitution ran as a side-effect of the agent's existence check.

### Expected behavior

  **Expected behavior**
  Every path the agent helpers interpolate into a shell command should be passed as a single, literal shell word - i.e. properly
  shell-escaped for the session's shell family - so that the underlying tool always receives the exact path the agent asked about,
  regardless of any special characters it contains.

  For example, when probing the path:

  /tmp/innocent$(touch ~/PROBE_RAN)
  is_file_path should emit:
  
  test -f /tmp/innocent\$\(touch\ ~/PROBE_RAN\)
  This ensures the shell does not expand or interpret any metacharacters before passing the argument to test, and the probe simply
  reports that the (admittedly oddly-named) path does not exist.
  
  The same treatment should apply to is_git_repository, run_git_grep_command, run_grep_command, run_select_string_command,
  run_find_command, and run_powershell_get_childitem_command.

title: New Worktree Config fails with spaces in the path
body:
## Description

The New Worktree Config generated a shell command that interpolated a filesystem path containing spaces **without quoting it**. The shell split the path on whitespace, which caused `git worktree add` to receive the wrong number of positional arguments and print its `usage:` help instead of creating the worktree.

The current workspace is `/Users/luizv/Developer/2026-05 Site da Jô` - the space in "Site da Jô" is what breaks the command.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new Worktree Config selecting one repo whose absolute path contains a space (e.g. `~/Developer/My Project`).
2. Observe the command it generates.

## Actual behavior

The Agent ran:

```sh
git worktree add -b turquoise-palo-verde /Users/luizv/.warp/worktrees/2026-05 Site da Jô/turquoise-palo-verde && cd /Users/luizv/.warp/worktrees/2026-05 Site da Jô/turquoise-palo-verde
```

The shell tokenizes `/Users/luizv/.warp/worktrees/2026-05 Site da Jô/turquoise-palo-verde` into 4 separate arguments. `git worktree add` receives too many positional args and prints its usage help. No worktree is created, but the failure mode is non-obvious because the command appears to "complete" - there is no explicit error message saying the path was misquoted.

## Expected behavior

It should quote (or escape) paths that may contain spaces or other shell-significant characters when composing commands. Either:

```sh
git worktree add -b turquoise-palo-verde "/Users/luizv/.warp/worktrees/2026-05 Site da Jô/turquoise-palo-verde" && cd "/Users/luizv/.warp/worktrees/2026-05 Site da Jô/turquoise-palo-verde"
```

or equivalent escaping. This is a general shell-safety issue - the command string should be quoted by default, since we cannot assume the user's workspace path is whitespace-free.

## Environment

- Warp version: v25.1.0
- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.3.0)
- Shell: zsh

title: Expose Terminal Accessibility Tree for macOS Assistive Apps
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

Requested Accessibility Surface

Below is the minimal AX surface that would fully unblock compatibility.

1. Window Enumeration

Windows should appear under:

AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)
→ kAXWindowsAttribute

Each window should expose:

Stable kAXTitleAttribute

Standard NSWindow accessibility behavior

This largely appears to work today.



2.  Tab Enumeration
Tabs should be discoverable inside each window through either:

Option A - Standard Tab Group

AXTabGroup
└── kAXTabsAttribute

Returning tab elements.

Option B - Radio/Button Style Tabs

Expose tab children as:

AXRadioButton

AXTab

With:

kAXTitleAttribute → tab display title

kAXValueAttribute → selected state (1 / 0)

This matches what Terminal.app and iTerm2 already expose.



3. Per-Tab Visible Buffer Text

Each tab/window should expose an:

AXTextArea

(or equivalent text-role accessibility element)

whose:

kAXValueAttribute

returns the currently visible terminal buffer as plain text.

Minimum Requirement

Visible viewport buffer

Nice-to-Have

Scrollback buffer access

The visible buffer alone is sufficient to fully support Echo.



4. Accessibility Notifications

The following AX notifications would enable efficient real-time updates:

kAXFocusedWindowChangedNotification

kAXValueChangedNotification on the text area

kAXUIElementDestroyedNotification

These are important for:

tab lifecycle tracking

window lifecycle tracking

incremental buffer updates

active-session detection



5. Selected Tab Signal

The active tab should be identifiable via either:

kAXValueAttribute == 1 on the selected tab element

kAXFocusedAttribute

equivalent focused-state signaling

Polling is acceptable if notifications are unavailable.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Echo is a macOS companion app that observes terminal activity across multiple terminal emulators (Terminal.app, iTerm2, etc.) to power voice and agent workflows.

Our detection layer is intentionally adapter-free and universal:

We walk each terminal application's Accessibility (AX) tree via:

AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)

kAXWindowsAttribute

We enumerate tabs under:

AXTabGroup

kAXTabsAttribute

AXRadioButton children

We read the visible terminal buffer through:

kAXValueAttribute on the AXTextArea child

This architecture currently works across every major macOS terminal except Warp.

Warp appears to render its UI through a custom GPU surface that exposes little to no meaningful Accessibility tree information:

No AXTabGroup

No AXRadioButton / AXTab hierarchy

No AXTextArea

No accessible visible buffer text

As a result, Warp becomes a special-case / tier-2 terminal in our compatibility matrix, which is the opposite of what we want - Warp users are exactly the developer cohort we'd most like to support first-class.

### Additional context

This would not only unblock Echo, but also improve interoperability with the broader macOS accessibility ecosystem:

VoiceOver

screen readers

dictation tools

accessibility automation

terminal-aware AI agents

developer productivity tooling

Terminal.app and iTerm2 already expose this AX structure successfully, so the precedent on macOS is well-established.

Even a minimal opt-in setting such as:

Settings → Privacy → Expose accessibility tree to assistive apps

would immediately unlock support for a large category of accessibility and automation tooling.

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

### How important is this feature to you?

5 (Can't work without it!)

title: macOS bootstrap: install Corepack and Metal Toolchain so the workspace builds on Xcode 16+ and Node 25+
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

`script/macos/bootstrap` should install two dependencies that recent macOS environments no longer provide out of the box, so a fresh checkout builds without contributors needing to discover the missing pieces by trial and error:

1. **Corepack** - needed by `crates/command-signatures-v2/build.rs`, which shells out to `yarn build`. Homebrew's `node` formula stopped bundling Corepack starting with Node 25, so it has to be installed as a separate Homebrew formula and then activated with `corepack enable`.
2. **Metal Toolchain** - needed by `crates/warpui/build.rs`, which invokes `xcrun metal` to compile `.metal` shaders. Starting with Xcode 16, Apple ships the toolchain as an optional download (`xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain`, ~700 MB) that is not installed by default.

As a secondary improvement, `crates/warpui/build.rs `should surface an actionable hint when the Metal Toolchain is missing - currently it just propagates Apple's raw stderr.


### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Following the README's `./script/bootstrap + cargo run` flow on a fresh macOS workstation with Xcode 26.5 and Node 26 (current Homebrew defaults), `cargo` sync fails twice in a row:

1. `crates/command-signatures-v2/build.rs` panics with `Failed to build command signatures JS: No such file or directory (os error 2)` because `yarn` is not in `$PATH`. The panic message helpfully points at `corepack enable`, but Corepack itself is also missing.
2. After resolving №1, `crates/warpui/build.rs` panics with `error compiling metal shaders to .air; error: error: cannot execute tool 'metal' due to missing Metal Toolchain; use: xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain.`

Neither dependency is mentioned in `script/macos/bootstrap`, so new contributors hit these errors after the bootstrap script reports success. Both are easy to fix once you know what's missing, but the discovery cost is real, especially since `xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch` (which `bootstrap` already calls) is almost, but not quite, the right place to expect the Metal Toolchain to land.

### Additional context

Reproducer environment: macOS 26.x, Xcode 26.5 (Build 17F42), `Homebrew node 26.0.0`, Apple Silicon.

Proposed implementation: add two idempotent blocks to `script/macos/bootstrap` (Metal Toolchain after `xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch`; Node + Corepack alongside the existing `brew install` calls), and refactor the two `assert!(...)` blocks in `crates/warpui/build.rs` into a helper that appends an actionable hint when Apple's stderr contains `missing Metal Toolchain`.

Happy to open a PR - local branch is ready, ~50 lines net, no behavior change for users whose dependencies are already present.

macOS

title: SECRETS_REGEX silently empty at startup despite persisted custom_secret_regex_list - local MCP-save redaction check never fires
body:
## Summary

The custom secret regex set (`SECRETS_REGEX`) read by `find_secrets_in_text` can be empty at runtime even when:

- `~/.warp-oss/settings.toml` has `[privacy.secret_redaction] enabled = true`
- The same TOML has `custom_secret_regex_list = [...20 default patterns...]`
- The Settings → Privacy UI correctly shows the toggle ON and lists all 20 default patterns

As a result, the local redaction check that PR #10839 fixes (`should_block_save_for_secrets(safe_mode, enterprise, contains_secrets)`) returns `contains_secrets=false` regardless of payload, because `find_secrets_in_text` runs against an empty `SECRETS_REGEX`. Saves go through, cloud sync receives the secret, and the *server* rejects with `Secrets detected while creating generic string object` - the cloud catches what the local check should have caught.

## Why it happens

`app/src/terminal/secret_regex_updater.rs:14` carries the comment `Initialize with current custom regexes (will be empty until safe mode is enabled)`. The intended flow:

1. App starts with `safe_mode=false`, `user_secret_regex_list=[]`
2. User toggles safe mode ON
3. `initialize_default_regexes_once` pushes the 20 defaults into `user_secret_regex_list`
4. That mutation fires `PrivacySettingsChangedEvent::CustomSecretRegexList`
5. The updater subscribes to that event (`secret_regex_updater.rs:18-22`) and recompiles `SECRETS_REGEX`

The flow assumes a transition from empty list → populated list. It does NOT handle the case where TOML already has the defaults persisted from a prior session: `PrivacySettings::new` loads the list, but no `CustomSecretRegexList` change event fires, so `SECRETS_REGEX` remains the initial empty `Regex::new_many(&[])` from `app/src/terminal/model/secrets.rs:39-42`.

The updater's startup call to `update_custom_secret_regex_list` at `secret_regex_updater.rs:15` either runs before `PrivacySettings` exposes the populated list, or runs after but is racing some other init step - needs confirmation during the fix.

The empty-regex condition also persists across a user toggling safe mode OFF→ON at runtime, because the updater only subscribes to `CustomSecretRegexList` changes, not `SafeModeEnabled` changes.

## Repro (verified 2026-05-19)

1. Quit warp-oss
2. Ensure `~/.warp-oss/settings.toml` has:
   ```toml
   [privacy.secret_redaction]
   enabled = true
   ```
   and a populated `custom_secret_regex_list` (the 20 defaults)
3. Launch warp-oss
4. Open Settings → Privacy. Confirm the toggle is ON and the regex list shows all 20 entries. (UI proves the data is loaded.)
5. Settings → MCP Servers → + Add. Paste a config where the secret is in a non-templatized field, e.g.:
   ```json
   {
     "demo-redact-8761": {
       "command": "/usr/bin/true",
       "args": ["--api-key=sk-FAKE0000000000FAKEdemoWARP8761"]
     }
   }
   ```
6. Click Save.

**Expected:** "This MCP server contains secrets. Visit Settings > Privacy to modify your secret redaction settings." toast; save blocked.

**Actual:** save succeeds (local), then sync fails server-side with `Failed to create mcp server` toast (cloud rejection on `Secrets detected while creating generic string object`). Confirmed via grep of `~/Library/Logs/warp-oss.log`:
```
[WARN] [warp::server::sync_queue] Failed to create GenericStringObject(Json(TemplatableMCPServer)) ... Secrets detected: Secrets detected while creating generic string object
```

Separately verified that the regex set, when compiled standalone with the same 20 patterns via `regex_automata::meta::Regex::new_many`, *does* match `sk-FAKE0000000000FAKEdemoWARP8761` (pattern_id=17, Generic SK). So the patterns and runtime engine are fine - the in-memory `SECRETS_REGEX` simply does not contain them.

## Proposed fix (small)

Add a subscription to `SafeModeSettingsChangedEvent::SafeModeEnabled` in `CustomSecretRegexUpdater::new` so the updater recompiles `SECRETS_REGEX` whenever the user flips safe mode:

```rust
let safe_mode_settings = SafeModeSettings::handle(ctx);
ctx.subscribe_to_model(&safe_mode_settings, |me, evt, ctx| {
    if let SafeModeSettingsChangedEvent::SafeModeEnabled { .. } = evt {
        me.update_custom_secret_regex_list(ctx);
    }
});
```

That covers the runtime-toggle path. The TOML-loaded-at-startup path likely needs an additional initial recompile after `PrivacySettings` finishes loading (e.g. on `initial_load_complete` or by replaying the value in the updater after a tick).

## Related

- Discovered while producing evidence for #10839 (which fixes the inverse bug - saves were being incorrectly blocked when safe mode is OFF). The predicate in #10839 is correct; this issue is upstream of the predicate, on the `contains_secrets` input.
- Companion issue: secrets pasted into `env` / `headers` get templatized to placeholders before the redaction scan runs (filing separately).

title: feat(uri-scheme): add focus_tab action to navigate to an existing session by ID
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

  Problem

  Warp's URI scheme currently supports opening new windows and tabs (warp://action/new_window,
  warp://action/new_tab), but there is no way to focus an existing tab or session by identifier.

  This becomes a real limitation when desktop notifications are used to signal that a specific session needs
  attention - for example, Claude Code (Anthropic's CLI) sends a push notification when it's waiting for user
  input. Clicking that notification can bring Warp to focus, but has no way to jump to the specific tab that Claude
   Code is running in. The user has to hunt for it manually.

  Proposed Solution

  Add a focus_tab action to the URI scheme:

  warp://action/focus_tab?id=<session_id>

  Where <session_id> is an identifier (e.g. the tab/session UUID) that tools running inside Warp can read from an
  environment variable (similar to WARP_SESSION_ID or TERM_SESSION_ID on macOS).

  The full flow for a tool like Claude Code would be:
  1. On startup, read the session ID from the environment.
  2. When sending a desktop notification, embed warp://action/focus_tab?id=<id> as the notification's click action.
  3. User clicks notification → Warp comes to front at exactly the right tab.
  
  Why this matters

  AI-assisted terminal workflows are becoming the norm. Tools like Claude Code, Aider, and similar agents
  frequently run long background tasks and notify when they need a response. Without tab-level deep linking, the
  notification UX is incomplete - you get the ping but still have to navigate manually.

title: Windows bootstrap missing libclang and protoc; cargo build fails
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have searched Warp bugs and there are no duplicates. An existing PR (#10911) implements the same fix, but no backing issue exists for it to link to.
- [x] I have searched Warp known issues page and my issue is not there.

### Describe the bug

`script/windows/bootstrap.ps1` advertises that it installs all required build dependencies, but two hard build dependencies are missing on Windows:

1. **`protoc`** (the Protocol Buffers compiler) - required by `prost-build`, used by the `warp_multi_agent_api` crate (a git-dep of `warpdotdev/warp-proto-apis`). This is the first failure a contributor hits.
2. **`libclang`** - required by `bindgen`-style build scripts elsewhere in the workspace. This is the same gap that was fixed on Linux in #9527 (which resolved #9526); the Windows side of the same gap has never been closed.

After a fresh bootstrap, `cargo build --release` fails on `protoc` first. Once `protoc` is installed manually, the build proceeds further but is expected to fail again on `libclang` for the same structural reason.

### To reproduce

On a Windows 11 machine with no prior Rust toolchain:

1. Clone `warpdotdev/warp` (master at `b376889`).
2. Run `.\script\windows\bootstrap.ps1` - completes without error.
3. Open a fresh PowerShell so PATH is refreshed.
4. Run `cargo build --release` from the repo root.
5. Build progresses through the dependency graph, then fails compiling `warp_multi_agent_api`.

Exact error:

```
error: failed to run custom build command for `warp_multi_agent_api v0.0.0 (https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp-proto-apis.git?rev=9a2d2425c5d1eb40fb547956e659511906e03f9e#9a2d2425)`

Caused by:
  process didn't exit successfully: `...\target\release\build\warp_multi_agent_api-...\build-script-build` (exit code: 1)
  --- stderr
  Error: Custom { kind: NotFound, error: "Could not find `protoc`. If `protoc` is installed, try setting the `PROTOC` environment variable to the path of the `protoc` binary. Try installing `protobuf-compiler` or `protobuf` using your package manager. It is also available at https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases" }
```

### Expected behavior

After `.\script\windows\bootstrap.ps1` completes, a fresh `cargo build --release` should succeed without any additional manual setup. Both `protoc` and `libclang` are hard build dependencies for any contributor on Windows, so the bootstrap script should install them alongside the existing Visual Studio Build Tools / CMake / InnoSetup / jq steps. This is the Windows analogue of the Linux gap fixed in #9527.

### Workaround

For `protoc`:

```powershell
winget install protobuf
```

For `libclang`, the standard approach is installing LLVM:

```powershell
winget install LLVM.LLVM
```

After both, open a fresh shell so PATH refreshes and re-run `cargo build --release`. Cargo resumes from the failed crate.

### Operating system (OS)

Windows

### Operating system and version

Windows 11 Pro, 10.0.26200 (build 26200)

### Current Warp version

N/A - building from source. Repository state: `b376889` on `master`.

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp. This is the first time I've attempted a local build. The `protoc` gap likely dates to whenever `warp_multi_agent_api` was added to default workspace members; the `libclang` gap has the same shape as the Linux issue fixed by #9527.

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No - this affects local development and contribution, not daily use of the shipped Warp binary.

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes - this is specific to Warp's `script/windows/bootstrap.ps1` not installing a required build tool.

### Additional context

A candidate fix is already proposed in **PR #10911** ("Install libclang and protoc in Windows bootstrap" by @AndreKalberer, opened 2026-05-14). That PR's scope matches this issue exactly - both deps. It is currently blocked partly because Oz flagged that it has no linked `ready-to-implement` issue to back it under Warp's contribution model (per `CONTRIBUTING.md`). Filing this issue should unblock that linkage.

Related precedents (Linux side of the same gap):
- #9526 - Linux bootstrap missing `libclang-dev` and `clang-format`
- #9527 - fix that closed #9526
- #9230 - earlier protoc-related Windows CI fix (different surface; mentioned in PR #10911 for context)

title: cargo build --release panics on Windows when CARGO_FULL_PROFILE is unset
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have searched Warp bugs and there are no duplicates.
- [x] I have searched Warp known issues page and my issue is not there.

### Describe the bug

`cargo build --release` panics on Windows because `app/build.rs` reads a custom `CARGO_FULL_PROFILE` env var and defaults to `"debug"` when unset. With only a release build done, `target/debug/` doesn't exist, and the build script's Windows-asset copy step panics trying to write `conpty.dll` to a nonexistent directory.

The faulty fallback is at `app/build.rs:132`:

```rust
let cargo_full_profile = env::var("CARGO_FULL_PROFILE").unwrap_or(String::from("debug"));
let target_dir = app_target_dir(&cargo_full_profile).expect("Could not get app target directory");
copy_windows_assets(&target_dir);
```

This silently fails for any Windows contributor who follows the obvious path (`cargo build --release` after bootstrap). It accidentally works for `cargo run` because cargo's default profile is debug, so the hardcoded fallback happens to match.

`CARGO_FULL_PROFILE` is not set by `script/windows/bootstrap.ps1`, not mentioned in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and not in the `cargo run` snippet in `README.md`. A first-time Windows contributor has no signal that they need to set it.

### To reproduce

On a Windows 11 machine with all bootstrap deps installed (including the manual fixes from #11301):

1. `cargo build --release` from a fresh shell with `CARGO_FULL_PROFILE` unset.
2. Build progresses through every dependency crate.
3. When cargo reaches the `app` crate's build script, it panics:

```
error: failed to run custom build command for `warp v0.1.0 (...\app)`

Caused by:
  process didn't exit successfully: `...\target\release\build\warp-...\build-script-build` (exit code: 101)
  --- stderr
  thread 'main' (64820) panicked at app\build.rs:436:9:
  Could not copy conpty.dll from "assets\\windows\\x64" to "...\\target\\debug": The system cannot find the path specified. (os error 3)
```

### Expected behavior

`cargo build --release` should succeed without requiring any env var the user wasn't told about. The build script should derive the profile from cargo's standard `PROFILE` env var (which IS set for build scripts), falling back to `CARGO_FULL_PROFILE` only if a non-standard custom profile name is needed.

A minimal fix:

```rust
let cargo_full_profile = env::var("CARGO_FULL_PROFILE")
    .or_else(|_| env::var("PROFILE"))
    .unwrap_or_else(|_| "debug".to_string());
```

Alternatively, the `cargo build --release` invocation could be documented (in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and/or `README.md`) as requiring `CARGO_FULL_PROFILE=release`, but that puts the burden on every Windows contributor instead of fixing the script.

### Workaround

Set the env var explicitly before the cargo invocation:

```bash
export CARGO_FULL_PROFILE=release
cargo build --release
```

```powershell
$env:CARGO_FULL_PROFILE = "release"
cargo build --release
```

### Operating system (OS)

Windows

### Operating system and version

Windows 11 Pro, 10.0.26200 (build 26200)

### Current Warp version

N/A - building from source. Repository state: `b376889` on `master`.

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp. This is the first time I've attempted a `cargo build --release` locally. The `app/build.rs` fallback to `"debug"` has been there at least as far back as `b376889`.

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No - this affects local development and contribution, not daily use of the shipped Warp binary.

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes - this is a defect in Warp's own `app/build.rs`.

### Additional context

The same build-script comment block at `app/build.rs:119-131` already acknowledges the limitation of cargo's `PROFILE` env var:

> We need to pass this information manually through an environment variable. Of the built-in variables set by Cargo: `OUT_DIR` is only a temporary directory, and `PROFILE` can only be `debug` or `release`.

But "only `debug` or `release`" is fine for the common case - the script could fall through to `PROFILE` as a sensible default. The current `unwrap_or("debug")` is the wrong fallback because it gives the *opposite* of what the developer is asking for on a release build.

title: File tree view's recursive watcher re-walks large subtrees (e.g. AppData\Local\Temp) on every event → sustained high CPU on Windows
body:
## Summary

When the code-editor file tree view (sidebar) is open and rooted at a path containing a large subtree, Warp registers a `RecursiveMode::Recursive` filesystem watcher on that path via `index_lazy_loaded_path`. Background activity inside the watched tree fires events constantly, and `repo_metadata::entry::Entry::build_tree` re-walks the affected subtree from scratch on every event. With 32 background-executor threads running in parallel, this saturates CPU on an otherwise-idle machine.

The most visible case on Windows is a home-directory-rooted file tree view: `AppData\Local\Temp` underneath it gets continuous writes from Office autosave, browser caches, antivirus, build tooling, etc. But the same pattern applies to any path under the watched root with a large, churning subtree (`node_modules`, `target/`, OneDrive sync dirs, cache directories, etc.).

This appears to be one of the causes contributing to #7561 ("idle CPU on Windows" reporters).

> **Note on related work:** #8471 proposes debouncing in `repo_metadata/watcher.rs` - that fix is upstream of `compute_file_tree_mutations` and is complementary to (not a duplicate of) the fixes proposed here, which address the cost *per* `Entry::build_tree` invocation and the absence of a failed-walk short-circuit. #11350 tracks the third, larger design issue: in-flight walks are not cancellable, which is why the user-side workaround takes ~10s to take effect.

## Reproducer (confirmed)

1. On Windows 11, launch a locally-built `warp-oss.exe` (release).
2. Open the code-editor file tree view (sidebar) and have it rooted at `C:\Users\<user>` (or any directory containing a large, write-active subtree).
3. Leave idle for several minutes while normal Windows background activity touches `AppData\Local\Temp` or any other watched subtree.
4. Observe sustained ~100% CPU across `background-executor-*` threads, with corresponding disk activity.
5. **Close the file tree view** - the CPU spike disappears within ~10 seconds, coinciding with `ExceededMaxFileLimit` failure log messages for the offending subtree.
6. **Reopen the file tree view** - the spike resumes immediately as `Entry::build_tree` re-registers the watcher and re-walks the tree.

The ~10 second delay between closing the sidebar and the CPU subsiding is tracked separately (in-flight walks are not cancellable).

## Profile evidence (symbolicated samply, captured during a spike)

Captured against a locally-built `target/release/warp-oss.exe`, symbolicated via the local PDB:

- 32 `background-executor-*` threads all churning at ~1000 samples/sec
- **99% of background-executor CPU** is in two functions:
  - `repo_metadata::entry::Entry::build_tree` - **80.6%**
  - `dunce::canonicalize_win` - **18.4%**
- Leaf syscalls: `NtClose` 64.1%, `NtQueryDirectoryFileEx` 15.2%, `NtOpenFile` 5.0%
- Std-library callers: `lstat` 32.4%, `stat` 21.3%, `OwnedHandle::drop` 16.2%, `readdir` 11.5%, `ReadDir::next` 11.3%, `File::open_native` 4.1%

Per-entry cost inside `Entry::build_tree` (`crates/repo_metadata/src/entry.rs:152-205`):

| Operation | Source line | Syscalls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entry_path.is_symlink()` | line 171 | `lstat` |
| `entry_path.is_dir()` | line 172 | `stat` |
| `dunce::canonicalize(entry_path)` | line 178 | `NtCreateFile` + `NtDeviceIoControlFile` + `NtClose` |
| Recursive `build_tree` for subdirs | line 182 | (recursion) |
| `read_dir` enumerator | line 153 | `NtOpenFile` + N × `NtQueryDirectoryFileEx` |

The walker only bails on the `MAX_FILES_PER_REPO = 100_000` quota (`entry.rs:161`) - it does all the work first. There is **no cache of failed-walk paths**, so every subsequent watcher event re-runs the entire walk.

## Root cause (two interacting design choices)

### 1. `WatchFilter` has no system-directory excludes

`WatchFilter` setup at `crates/repo_metadata/src/local_model.rs:404-411` only filters out git-internal paths via `should_ignore_git_path`. There is no exclude list for OS system directories (`AppData\Local\Temp`, `AppData\LocalLow`, etc. on Windows; `~/Library/Caches`, `/var/folders/*` on macOS; `~/.cache`, `/tmp` on Linux) or for known-noisy build artifacts (`node_modules`, `target/`, `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`).

### 2. `compute_file_tree_mutations` re-walks on every event with no failed-walk cache

`compute_file_tree_mutations` (`local_model.rs:595-654`) invokes `Entry::build_tree` on every "added" event with no memoization of paths that previously blew the `MAX_FILES_PER_REPO` quota. So even after the walker has proven a path is too large to enumerate, the next watcher event for the same subtree starts the walk over from scratch.

## Proposed fix

Two layers, both small:

### A. Cache failed-walk paths in `LocalRepoMetadataModel`

Add `failed_walk_paths: HashSet<StandardizedPath>` to `LocalRepoMetadataModel`. When `Entry::build_tree` returns `Err(ExceededMaxFileLimit)` for a path, insert it. At the top of `compute_file_tree_mutations`, skip any `path_to_add` that descends from a cached failed path.

Minimum diff. Hides the symptom even for paths the exclude list misses.

### B. Extend `WatchFilter` with a platform-specific system-dir exclude list

In `local_model.rs:404-411`, alongside `should_ignore_git_path`, add an exclude list that's case-insensitive on Windows:

- **Windows**: `AppData\Local\Temp`, `AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows`, `AppData\LocalLow`
- **macOS**: `~/Library/Caches`, `/var/folders/*`
- **Linux**: `~/.cache`, `/tmp`
- **Universal**: `node_modules`, `target/`, `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, `.gradle/`, `.idea/`

Make the list extensible so cross-platform expansion stays clean.

## Workarounds (what works and what doesn't)

| Workaround | Effective? | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Close the offending terminal pane | ❌ | Terminal panes don't register the watcher (see "Why this isn't a terminal-pane bug" below) |
| Close the code-editor file tree view sidebar | ✅ (with ~10s delay) | Spike subsides once in-flight walks finish (see follow-up issue) |
| Open the file tree view rooted at a smaller directory | ✅ | Avoids registering a watcher over a noisy subtree |
| Restart `warp-oss.exe` | ✅ | Tears down the watcher and any in-flight walks immediately |

## Why this isn't a terminal-pane bug

An obvious user-side mitigation is "close the terminal pane in the noisy directory", but it doesn't help. Searching `app/src/terminal/**` and `app/src/util/repo_detection.rs`, terminal-pane CWD changes flow through `detect_possible_git_repo`, which only looks for a `.git` ancestor - it does not register a lazy-loaded path or a recursive watcher.

The recursive watcher is registered by the **file tree view** at `app/src/code/file_tree/view.rs:1559-1564`:

```rust
if self.is_active && !self.registered_lazy_loaded_paths.contains(path) {
    self.repository_metadata_model.update(ctx, |model, ctx| {
        model.index_lazy_loaded_path(path, ctx)
    });
}
```

...and unregistered at `view.rs:388-398` when the file tree view becomes inactive (drains all registered paths) or when a specific entry is collapsed (`remove_lazy_loaded_entry`, line 410). `remove_lazy_loaded_path` is refcount-gated, so the underlying watcher tears down only when the last subscriber drops.

## Tests to add

- Regression test: a watcher event for `AppData\Local\Temp\new-file.tmp` does **not** trigger `Entry::build_tree`.
- Cache test: a path that returned `ExceededMaxFileLimit` is short-circuited on the second invocation.

## Environment

- Windows 11
- Locally-built `target/release/warp-oss.exe` from upstream `master` at commit `b376889` ("Add orchestration create environment modal (#10857)")
- The binary I profiled actually had one unrelated `log::warn!` line added in `orchestration_event_streamer.rs` (an SSE-drain-timer diagnostic from an earlier hypothesis). It does not touch `repo_metadata` and the profile evidence above is unaffected.
- Profile captured with `samply record --pid <pid> --duration 20`, symbolicated via local PDB at `target/release/warp-oss.pdb`. Raw profile not attached; happy to share on request.

## Related

- #7561 - original "idle CPU on Windows" umbrella report; this is at least one of its causes (likely multi-cause)
- #8471 - proposes debouncing in `repo_metadata/watcher.rs` (complementary to this issue)
- #10207 - closed; UX of `ExceededMaxFileLimit` toast (same bail-out path)
- #11350 - follow-up: in-flight `Entry::build_tree` walks are not cancellable when their owning subscriber unregisters

---

title: Entry::build_tree walks are not cancellable - closing the file tree view leaves CPU spike running until in-flight walks finish
body:
## Summary

`repo_metadata::entry::Entry::build_tree` recursive walks are not cancellable. When the file tree view becomes inactive and drains its `registered_lazy_loaded_paths`, the unregistration tears down the watcher but does **not** interrupt walks already in flight on background-executor threads. Those walks continue to completion (or until they hit `MAX_FILES_PER_REPO`), wasting CPU on a tree no subscriber is listening to anymore.

This is a follow-up to #11349 (file-tree-view recursive-watcher CPU issue). The fixes there (failed-walk cache + system-dir exclude list) reduce how often `Entry::build_tree` is invoked. This issue is about making invocations that are already running cancellable.

## Observed behavior

After identifying the file tree view as the watcher registrant (sibling issue), the user-side workaround is "close the file tree view sidebar". Empirically confirmed on Windows 11 against a locally-built `warp-oss.exe` (upstream `master` at `b376889`, plus one unrelated `log::warn!` line in `orchestration_event_streamer.rs` that does not touch `repo_metadata`):

1. With the file tree view rooted at `C:\Users\<user>`, CPU spikes to ~100% across `background-executor-*` threads.
2. Closing the file tree view → CPU **does not drop immediately**. It takes ~10 seconds for the spike to subside.
3. The CPU drop coincides with `ExceededMaxFileLimit` failure log messages for the offending subtree, indicating that the in-flight walks ran to completion (hit the `MAX_FILES_PER_REPO` quota) before the executor threads went idle.

This is the smoking gun for a missing cancellation path.

## Root cause

`Entry::build_tree` (`crates/repo_metadata/src/entry.rs:130-227`) takes `&mut Option<u32>` for a file budget and otherwise runs to completion. It has no `CancellationToken`, no `AtomicBool` stop-flag, and no other mechanism to bail between directory entries.

The view-side teardown at `app/src/code/file_tree/view.rs:388-398`:

```rust
ctx.unsubscribe_to_model(&self.repository_metadata_model);
self.unsubscribe_from_active_file_model(ctx);
let repository_metadata_model = self.repository_metadata_model.clone();
let paths: Vec<_> = self.registered_lazy_loaded_paths.drain().collect();
repository_metadata_model.update(ctx, move |model: &mut RepoMetadataModel, ctx| {
    for path in &paths {
        model.remove_lazy_loaded_path(path, ctx);
    }
});
```

...calls `remove_lazy_loaded_path` for each drained path. That descends (via refcount) into `remove_repository` (`crates/repo_metadata/src/local_model.rs:428`) which calls `watcher.unregister_path`. The watcher stops emitting new events, but any `Entry::build_tree` task already enqueued or in flight on a background executor keeps walking.

For a home-directory-rooted view that has already kicked off a walk into `AppData\Local\Temp` (or any large subtree), this means up to `MAX_FILES_PER_REPO = 100_000` files of `lstat` + `stat` + `dunce::canonicalize` per-entry work has to finish before the executor thread frees up.

## Proposed fix

Plumb a cancellation token through `Entry::build_tree` so it can bail between directory entries when its owning subscriber goes away.

Sketch (subject to taste - `CancellationToken` from `tokio-util`, `Arc<AtomicBool>`, or whatever pattern matches `repo_metadata`'s existing async-task abstraction):

```rust
pub fn build_tree(
    root: &Path,
    files: &mut Vec<FileMetadata>,
    gitignores: &mut Vec<...>,
    file_budget: Option<&mut u32>,
    max_depth: usize,
    current_depth: usize,
    ignored: &IgnoredPathStrategy,
    cancel: &CancellationToken,  // <-- new
) -> Result<Entry, BuildTreeError> {
    if cancel.is_cancelled() {
        return Err(BuildTreeError::Cancelled);
    }
    // ... existing per-entry loop, with cancel check at the top of each iteration
}
```

At call sites in `compute_file_tree_mutations`, hand the task a `CancellationToken` cloned from a token owned by the `LocalRepoMetadataModel` entry for that path. When `remove_repository` runs (or when a refcount-driven `remove_lazy_loaded_path` reaches zero), `cancel()` the token **before** calling `unregister_path` so the executor thread observes cancellation on its next iteration.

This bounds the wasted work after teardown to "at most one directory's worth of `read_dir` + per-entry stats", not "the whole subtree up to `MAX_FILES_PER_REPO`".

## Why this is filed separately from A + B

The two fixes in the sibling issue (failed-walk cache + system-dir exclude list) are small, localized, and defensive - they reduce *how often* `Entry::build_tree` is invoked. Cancellation is a structural change to the walker's signature and to every call site, and the right shape depends on conventions the Warp team already uses elsewhere in `repo_metadata`. Splitting it out keeps the first PR landable while this discussion happens.

## Tests to add

- An in-flight `build_tree` walk observes cancellation and returns early when its owning subscriber unregisters.
- The total CPU spent by an executor thread after `remove_lazy_loaded_path` is bounded by a single directory's stat cost, not by the full subtree size.

## Related

- #11349 - sibling A+B issue (failed-walk cache + system-dir exclude list)
- #7561 - umbrella "idle CPU on Windows" report
- #8471 - debouncing in `repo_metadata/watcher.rs` (complementary)

### Describe the solution you'd like?

**Summary**
Warp's command input still behaves like a traditional single-line shell prompt. With Warp Agent and other AI features becoming a core part of the product, users now frequently type long, paragraph-style natural-language prompts in the same input that's also used for short shell commands. The current input feels less ergonomic than a standard chat-style box (ChatGPT, Slack, Claude, etc.), and editing long content is noticeably painful.
This issue groups together a few closely related UX gaps.

**Current Behavior**
The input is effectively single-line. Long AI prompts wrap awkwardly and are hard to read/edit as a block.
I cannot click in the middle of the typed text to move the cursor to that position - the cursor stays where it was, and I have to navigate with arrow keys.
I cannot click-and-drag (or shift+click) to select a range of characters inside the input.
Because selection doesn't work, I cannot delete or overwrite a middle chunk of the command/prompt in one step; I usually have to delete everything to the right of the edit point.

**Expected Behavior**
The input should behave like a modern multi-line text box (think: ChatGPT / Claude / Slack composer):
Multi-line, chat-style input
Auto-grows vertically as the user types or pastes long content.
Has a comfortable max height with internal scrolling.
Clear visual affordance that this is a rich input, not just a shell prompt line.
Configurable submit behavior (e.g. Enter to submit, Shift+Enter for newline - or the inverse, user's choice in Settings).
Click-to-position cursor
Clicking anywhere in the typed text places the cursor at that exact position.
Mouse selection
Click-and-drag and Shift+Click select a range of characters.
Double-click selects a word; triple-click selects a line/paragraph.
Delete / replace selection
Pressing Backspace / Delete or typing over a selection replaces it as a single unit.
Standard word-wise shortcuts (Option+←/→, Option+Backspace on macOS, Ctrl+←/→ etc. on Windows/Linux) continue to work.

**Why This Matters**
AI-era usage pattern: A growing share of input in Warp is no longer "one short command per line." Users write descriptive, multi-sentence prompts for Warp Agent, paste error logs, draft commit messages, etc. The single-line shell-style input is increasingly mismatched with this usage.
Editing friction: For long Docker / kubectl / ffmpeg / complex git commands, the lack of click-to-position and mouse selection makes Warp feel slower than even a basic web text box, which undercuts Warp's positioning as a modern, IDE-like terminal.
User expectations: Every modern editor and chat app supports these basics. New users assume they work and are surprised when they don't.

title: Quake Mode hotkey intermittently fails to register on startup (macOS)
body:
<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary
Quake Mode global hotkey (bound to Cmd+§) intermittently fails to register on Warp startup. When the failure happens, the hotkey produces no effect anywhere - including in apps with a single window where macOS would not intercept Cmd+` - so the event is simply not reaching Warp. After quitting and relaunching Warp manually (sometimes 2-3 times) the hotkey starts working reliably across all apps until the next restart.

## Problem
This looks like a race during keyboard-event-tap registration at launch (e.g. CGEventTapCreate succeeds but the tap is created in a disabled state, or registration happens before the input source / keymap is ready). Once the hotkey "wakes up" it works everywhere - so this is not the well-known Cmd+§ ↔ macOS "Move focus to next window in active application" collision, even though the chosen hotkey would normally invite that suspicion.

Side note: similar startup-only flakiness has occasionally been observed with in-app tab shortcuts (Cmd+something for tab manipulation). No firm repro, but worth checking whether the underlying init path is shared between global hotkeys and in-app keybindings.

## Expected behavior
The Quake Mode hotkey should bind reliably on every launch, without requiring multiple manual restarts.

## Actual behavior
On some launches the hotkey does nothing at all - pressing it produces no response regardless of focused app or window count. Quitting and relaunching Warp manually, repeated 2-3 times, eventually makes the hotkey start working, after which it remains reliable until the next restart.

## Reproduction steps or desired workflow
1. Bind Quake Mode hotkey to Cmd+§ on a macOS ISO keyboard.
2. Launch Warp (especially as a login item or shortly after an auto-update).
3. Press the hotkey from any focused app, including apps with a single window.
4. Observe that on some launches the hotkey does nothing - the event is not reaching Warp.
5. Quit and relaunch Warp manually, repeating 1-3 times until the hotkey starts working.
6. Once it works, it works reliably across all focused apps until the next restart.

## Related UX suggestion
The hotkey picker silently accepts combinations that collide with macOS-reserved shortcuts. Example: Cmd+§ (same physical key as Cmd+` on ISO keyboards) collides with the macOS default "Move focus to next window in active application". The UI gives no hint. It would help to:
- Warn inline when the chosen combination conflicts with a macOS system shortcut.
- Offer a one-click alternative that keeps the user's primary key and only swaps the modifier (e.g. propose Ctrl+§ instead of Cmd+§), so muscle memory is preserved.

## Possible mitigation
If technically feasible: after registration, verify with CGEventTapIsEnabled() on a short delay and recreate the tap if it is disabled; retry with backoff if the keymap is not ready yet. If a clean fix is not possible, at minimum exposing a "Re-register hotkey" button in settings would save users the quit-and-relaunch ritual.

## Environment
- ISO keyboard layout
- Quake Mode bound to Cmd+§
- Accessibility permission for Warp: granted
- No third-party global-hotkey managers running (no Raycast / Alfred / Karabiner / Rectangle / etc.)

title: Make inactive pane dimming intensity configurable
body:
### Problem / pain point

Warp can dim inactive panes via the `appearance.panes.should_dim_inactive_panes` setting, but the dimming **amount** is hard-coded (a ~10% foreground overlay, `fg_overlay_2`). Depending on the theme, monitor, and ambient light, that fixed value is either too subtle to tell the active pane apart from inactive ones, or stronger than some users want. There is no way to tune it.

### Current behavior

**Settings → Appearance → Panes** exposes only an on/off toggle ("Dim inactive panes"). The intensity is not adjustable.

### Desired behavior

A percentage control (slider) for the dimming intensity, shown when "Dim inactive panes" is enabled. The default should preserve today's appearance so nothing changes for existing users.

### Constraints / notes

- Backwards-compatible default (current look = 10%).
- Should sync like the existing pane-dimming toggle.
- Purely an appearance/config change; no impact on terminal behavior.

### Environment

- Warp version: local OSS build from `master`.

title: File-link parser captures trailing sentence period, breaking markdown viewer activation
body:
# File-link parser captures trailing sentence period, breaking markdown viewer activation

## Summary

When a `.md` file path appears at the end of a sentence in terminal output, Warp's file-link parser includes the trailing `.` (sentence period) as part of the captured filename. The resulting token ends in `.md.` rather than `.md`, so Warp does not recognize it as a markdown file: clicking "Open in Warp" opens the file in a generic text pane with **no Editor/Viewer toggle** in the pane overflow menu (`⋯`), and the file appears as raw source instead of rendered markdown.

The Editor/Viewer toggle's absence is the deterministic signal that Warp failed to classify the file as markdown.

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows
- **Warp channels:** reproduced on both Warp Preview and Warp stable
- **Session type:** Local (not SSH, not WSL)
- **Terminals tested:** multiple terminal instances (rules out per-tab/session state)

## Repro

### Setup

Create a trivial markdown file:

```powershell
"# Hello`n`nSome **bold** text" | Set-Content C:\Users\chris\warp-md-test.md
```

### Test cases

Run each line in Warp and click the file-path link it produces. Check the pane overflow menu (`⋯`) - does the **Editor ↔ Viewer toggle** appear?

| # | Command | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `echo "Drafted at C:/Users/chris/warp-md-test.md"` (no trailing punct) | Toggle present, markdown renders | ✅ Works |
| 2 | `echo "Drafted at C:/Users/chris/warp-md-test.md."` (trailing period) | Period excluded from link; toggle present; markdown renders | ❌ Link captures the trailing `.`; opens as raw text; no toggle |

Case 2 reliably reproduces across fresh Warp tabs, across sessions, and across **both Warp Preview and Warp stable**. The single-character difference (trailing `.`) toggles the bug.

## Impact

AI assistants, code-review tools, and natural-prose documentation commonly produce sentences like:

> Drafted at `.tmp/spec.md`. The plan is in `docs/plan.md`. See `notes/README.md`.

Every `.md` reference at the end of a sentence is unclickable-to-rendered for this reason. The user has to manually edit the path (strip the period) before clicking, or accept raw text.

## Suggested fix

Most terminal link parsers solve this by trimming a closing punctuation set - typically `.`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `!`, `?`, `)`, `]`, `}`, `>`, `"`, `'` - from the end of a captured path token before extension-classifying it. Trimming `.` specifically would fix the case here without affecting any legitimate filename (filenames don't end in `.` on Windows or POSIX).

## Related (but distinct) issues

- **#7584** - Markdown viewer design / Editor↔Viewer toggle (closed, shipped). Confirms the intended behavior is rendered markdown with a toggle in the overflow menu.
- **#7683** - Markdown pane hangs on first open. Different failure mode (pane opens as markdown but blank); this bug never engages markdown classification at all.
- **#9091** - `.md` links not clickable over SSH. Different surface (SSH); this bug is local.
- **#10245** - CJK/full-width punctuation not treated as word boundary. Same class (punctuation boundary), different character set; ASCII trailing-period not covered.

No existing issue matches.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Case 2 in the repro table renders correctly: the trailing `.` is excluded from the captured link, the markdown viewer engages, and the Editor/Viewer toggle is present in the pane overflow menu.
2. **Highlight-range parity on Windows:** when a captured terminal token ends in `.` and the NT kernel transparently normalizes it away during path resolution, the **visible link highlight** also excludes the trailing `.` - matching the POSIX behavior already produced by the `SUFFIXES_TO_REMOVE` fallback path. Required so the user-visible underline is consistent across operating systems, not just the underlying file classification.

---
