title: Stale subtree-walk mutations applied to re-armed RepositoryRoot on rapid sidebar close/reopen
body:
## Summary

When the file-tree sidebar is closed at a path and quickly re-opened, an in-flight subtree walk from before the close can complete and apply its mutations against the freshly-created `RepositoryRoot` from after the re-open. The post-completion callback has no per-walk identity check, so the old walk's stale results land on the new tree state.

## Diagnostic

`compute_file_tree_mutations` is spawned via `ctx.spawn` at `crates/repo_metadata/src/local_model.rs:320-329` in response to watcher events. The post-completion callback at `crates/repo_metadata/src/local_model.rs:329-349` does `model.repositories.get_mut(&repo_path)` and applies the produced mutations. The `repo_path` key matches across `RepositoryRoot` incarnations, so `get_mut` happily returns the new one after a close/reopen cycle.

Three scenarios for path `P`:

```
Scenario A - single walk, no reopen (no problem)
  T=0   add P    → spawn W1
  T=5   close P  → remove_lazy_loaded_path drops RepositoryRoot R1
  T=10  W1 finishes → model.repositories.get_mut(&P) returns None → mutations dropped → fine

Scenario B - close, reopen, then old walk lands (the race)
  T=0   add P    → spawn W1
  T=5   close P  → remove_lazy_loaded_path drops RepositoryRoot R1
  T=5.1 open P   → add_lazy_loaded_path builds RepositoryRoot R2, spawns W2
  T=6   W1 finishes Ok(subtree_from_T0_to_T6)
  T=6.1 W1 callback runs model.repositories.get_mut(&P) → returns R2 (the new one)
        → W1's stale mutations apply to R2
  T=10  W2 finishes Ok(subtree_from_T5.1_to_T10)
  T=10.1 W2 callback applies to R2
        → R2 now mixes W1's stale snapshot + W2's fresh snapshot
```

The model has no per-walk identity. The callback cannot tell whether the `RepositoryRoot` it's modifying is the same incarnation the walk started against.

## Concrete log evidence

A profile-instrumented `warp-oss.exe` was run with the file-tree sidebar rooted at `C:\Users\chris`. The sidebar was opened, allowed to populate, then closed via the hide-panel gesture (`WorkspaceAction::ToggleLeftPanel`). The `[PROFILE-11350]` tag corresponds to `info!` lines added at the `build_tree` call sites in `crates/repo_metadata/src/{local_model.rs,entry.rs}` and at the `remove_lazy_loaded_path` entry point.

```text
19:28:34.233 [INFO] dispatching typed action: WorkspaceAction::ToggleLeftPanel
19:28:34.233 [INFO] [PROFILE-11350] remove_lazy_loaded_path CALLED
                     path=C:\Users\chris - sidebar closed / tree unregistered
                                                                            (26.5 s gap)
19:29:00.732 [INFO] [PROFILE-11350] build_tree EXIT  caller=file_tree_mutations
                     path="C:\\Users\\chris\\AppData\\Local\\Temp"  elapsed_ms=32071  result_ok=false
19:29:00.732 [WARN] Failed to build subtree for directory
                     "C:\\Users\\chris\\AppData\\Local\\Temp": ExceededMaxFileLimit
19:29:00.732 [INFO] [PROFILE-11350] build_tree EXIT  ...Temp  elapsed_ms=29569  result_ok=false
19:29:00.732 [INFO] [PROFILE-11350] build_tree EXIT  ...Temp  elapsed_ms=32320  result_ok=false
19:29:00.735 [INFO] [PROFILE-11350] build_tree EXIT  ...Temp  elapsed_ms=29822  result_ok=false
```

What this shows, factually:

1. **`remove_lazy_loaded_path` fires once** - on the registered root `C:\Users\chris` only - when the user toggles the left panel off. No per-subwalk cancellation signal is emitted.
2. **Four `file_tree_mutations` walks on `...\AppData\Local\Temp` were in flight at the time of the toggle** and continued running for **26.5 seconds** after `remove_lazy_loaded_path CALLED`. They EXIT'd within a 3 ms window of each other (`19:29:00.732` through `19:29:00.735`) - i.e. they ran to their own natural termination (`ExceededMaxFileLimit` on the Temp subtree), not to a cancellation check.
3. **Each walk's elapsed time exceeded 29 seconds** (29569, 29822, 32071, 32320 ms). The cancellation signal arriving at t=0 had no effect on any of them.

This is the precondition for Scenario B above: a walk that finishes its work and reaches the post-completion callback **tens of seconds** after the `RepositoryRoot` it started against has been removed. The window during which the user can re-open the sidebar and re-arm a new `RepositoryRoot` at the same path is the same 26.5-second window - long enough for the gesture to fit inside it.

The log captures the cancellation-survival half of the precondition; it does not capture a close/reopen instance with a stale apply, because that end-to-end gesture was not exercised in this session. The mechanism for the stale apply itself is the post-completion callback path described in the Diagnostic section above.

## Why it's probably not been noticed

1. **The watcher self-heals.** After the corruption lands, subsequent filesystem events trigger fresh walks that overwrite the stale state. The wrong entries usually disappear within a watcher debounce interval.
2. **Walks are currently slow.** With `compute_file_tree_mutations` walks running 25-34 seconds on noisy `AppData\Local\Temp`-class subtrees (Windows), users naturally don't close-then-reopen within the race window. The triggering interaction pattern is uncommon in practice.
3. **The symptom is transient and visual.** Briefly-wrong entries in the sidebar, corrected within seconds. No crash, no error log, no telemetry signal, nothing for a user to file against.

## Reproduce

Race timing makes a deterministic reproducer hard without instrumentation. Conceptual reproducer:

1. Open the file-tree sidebar rooted at a noisy directory such as `%USERPROFILE%`
2. Wait long enough for a watcher event to spawn a `compute_file_tree_mutations` walk on a slow subtree such as `AppData\Local\Temp`
3. While the walk is in-flight, close the sidebar
4. Immediately re-open the sidebar at the same path
5. Observe the sidebar entries when the old walk's mutations land - stale or mixed entries briefly appear, then get corrected by the next watcher event

## Related

#11350 - `Entry::build_tree` walks are not cancellable. Touches the same code surface (`local_model.rs`, the `ctx.spawn` callback) but for a different concern: whether walks can be terminated, not whether their results are correctly identified. Adjacent context.

#9592 / #10141 / #10205 / #9018 - assorted file-tree consistency issues with different mechanisms (post-`git mv` stale entries, sidebar blink, no-refresh-on-external-mutation). Listed for triage signal in case any are surface manifestations of the same underlying identity problem; the mechanism here (callback applies to wrong `RepositoryRoot` incarnation) is distinct from each.

title: Auto-discover models from /v1/models when configuring a custom inference endpoint
body:
## Summary

[PR #10781](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/pull/10781) ("Custom inference endpoints for third-party API models") shipped the BYOK + arbitrary OpenAI-compatible endpoint capability promised in @zachlloyd's [Discussion #9619 update](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/discussions/9619#discussioncomment-13392720). Users add a name + URL + API key, then **manually type every model name** the endpoint exposes.

@compgeniuses asked on [#9619](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/discussions/9619) (2026-05-18):

> "Also add ability to fetch model, for /models endpoint, as well as context windows, and whether model has vision or not."

This issue is to wire that up. The minimal piece: a button next to "Add model" in the custom inference endpoint modal that calls `GET <endpoint-url>/models` and pre-populates the model list from the response.

## Why

- **Friction:** users currently retype every model name from the provider's docs. For a provider with 100+ models (OpenRouter), this is impractical.
- **Errors:** a single typo in the model name reaches the agent request layer as a 404 with a vague message. Auto-discovery eliminates an entire failure mode.
- **Standardized:** OpenAI's `/v1/models` endpoint is the de facto standard. Every OpenAI-compatible provider implements it (OpenRouter, Azure OpenAI, Together AI, Anyscale, vLLM, Ollama with `/v1/models`, llama-cpp's openai-compat server).

## Behavior

In the "Custom inference endpoint" modal (`app/src/settings_view/custom_inference_modal.rs`):

1. Add a **"Fetch models from endpoint"** action next to the existing "Add model" button. Disabled until both URL and API key fields are non-empty.
2. On click: spawn an async request to `<url>/models` with `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`.
3. Parse the OpenAI-compatible response (`{ "data": [{ "id": "...", ... }, ...] }`).
4. **Merge** the discovered model names into the existing `model_rows` (skip duplicates by name; don't overwrite user-typed aliases on existing rows).
5. Show inline status: "Fetching..." while in-flight, then "Found N models" or a concise error.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- **Capability introspection** (context window, vision support, tool-call support). Non-standard across providers - fields like `context_length` / `pricing` / `architecture.modality` only appear on OpenRouter; Azure OpenAI doesn't expose them at all. Worth a separate issue if/when there's a need.
- **Token-cost surfacing.** Same reasoning as above.
- **Polling / cache invalidation.** One-shot fetch on user click is enough for the first cut.

## Acceptance

- [ ] New "Fetch models" button in the modal, disabled until URL + API key are populated.
- [ ] Click → spawns request to `<url>/models`, populates model rows from `data[].id` on success.
- [ ] Dedup against existing rows: a model already in the list isn't added again, and its alias is preserved.
- [ ] Inline status string: in-flight, success ("Found N models"), 401, 404, network error, non-JSON response.
- [ ] Unit tests: happy-path JSON parse, extra fields ignored, 401 / 404 / network / non-JSON error paths.
- [ ] Manual validation against at least two real providers (suggest: OpenRouter + a local Ollama with `OLLAMA_HOST=...` and OpenAI compat endpoint enabled).

## Related

- [PR #10781](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/pull/10781) - shipped Custom Inference Endpoints (the surface this builds on)
- [Discussion #9619](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/discussions/9619) - local-and-arbitrary-model thread; @compgeniuses comment that prompted this
- [#9620](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues/9620) - older spec for OpenAI-compatible BYOK endpoints (largely satisfied by #10781)

On Windows, when using Korean IME (Input Method Editor), intermediate composition characters are not displayed in real-time. Instead, the fully composed character appears all at once after composition completes, making typing feel very slow and opaque.

- Each IME composition stage (e.g., ㅎ, 하, 한) should be visible in real-time as it is typed.
- Typing speed should feel responsive, comparable to other terminals and text editors.

## Actual behavior
- The screen remains blank during composition until the full syllable is completed.
- Input feels very slow and unresponsive.
- This occurs in both the terminal (shell) input and the AI agent chat input area.

## Reproduction steps
1. Open Warp on Windows.
2. Switch to Korean input mode (press 한/영 key).
3. Type "한" by pressing the keys for ㅎ → 하 → 한.
4. Observe that nothing appears on screen until the final "한" is fully composed.

title: CTRL-\ keypress not forwarded to TUI applications on macOS
body:
<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary
**Note:** This is a regression - CTRL-\\ was previously forwarded correctly to TUI applications in earlier Warp versions.
CTRL-\ keypress is consumed by Warp and not forwarded to running TUI applications. The same keypress works correctly in macOS Terminal.app.

## Problem
This is a regression. CTRL-\\ previously worked correctly in Warp and was forwarded to TUI applications as expected. At some point it stopped being passed through.

When a TUI application registers CTRL-\ as a hotkey, Warp intercepts the keypress at a layer below the configurable keyboard shortcuts. The keypress produces no visible Warp action and is not passed through to the running process. This prevents TUI apps that rely on CTRL-\ from functioning correctly in Warp.

CTRL-\ does not appear in the Keyboard Shortcuts settings UI - searching for `\` shows only `⌘\` (Open Left Panel). The keypress is silently swallowed with no feedback or action.

In a traditional terminal, CTRL-\ sends SIGQUIT (0x1C) to the foreground process group. Warp appears to intercept this at the input handling layer rather than forwarding it.

## Expected behavior
CTRL-\ should be forwarded to the running process, especially during full-screen or TUI commands, consistent with macOS Terminal.app behavior.

## Actual behavior
CTRL-\ is consumed by Warp with no visible effect. The running TUI application never receives the keypress.

## Reproduction steps
1. Open Warp on macOS.
2. Run any TUI application that uses CTRL-\ as a hotkey.
3. Press CTRL-\.
4. Observe that nothing happens - the TUI does not receive the keypress.
5. Repeat in macOS Terminal.app - the TUI receives the keypress and responds correctly.

title: Memory: Editor SumTree<BlockItem> grows unbounded - 12 GB footprint (WARP-CLIENT-BETA-STABLE-4TSK)
body:
## Sentry Alert

- **Issue**: [WARP-CLIENT-BETA-STABLE-4TSK](https://sentry.io/organizations/warpdotdev/issues/7259255054/)
- **Event ID**: 9d2682f2e57d43b4a99c8da88342f31b
- **First Seen**: 2026-02-11 (long-standing)
- **Last Seen**: 2026-05-22T13:24:44Z
- **Event Count**: 76 events, 66 users
- **Release**: v0.2026.05.18.05.32.stable_02
- **Device**: Mac15,11 (Apple M3 Max), macOS 26.3.1
- **Total footprint**: ~12 GB (compressed ~7 GB, resident ~5 GB)

## Summary

Heap profile analysis reveals three major allocation sites accounting for ~3.2 GB of in-use memory. The root cause is that the editor's `SumTree<BlockItem>` render model stores **all** laid-out content (including full glyph and caret position data) for every block in the document, with **no eviction of off-screen content** and **no file size limits** on buffer loading.

## Allocation Site #1: SumTree<BlockItem>::push - ~2.03 GB

**Call path**: `SumTree<BlockItem>::push` → `RenderState::layout_edit_delta` → `RenderState::handle_layout_action` → `spawn_stream_local(Receiver<LayoutAction>)`

**Root cause**: The `RenderState` stores a `RefCell<SumTree<BlockItem>>` (`content` field in `crates/editor/src/render/model/mod.rs:388`) that holds **every laid-out block item** for the entire document. Each `BlockItem` contains a `Paragraph` which stores an `Arc<TextFrame>`, and each `TextFrame` contains `Vec1<Line>` where every `Line` stores:
- `Vec<Run>` with `Vec<Glyph>` (position, glyph ID, width per glyph)
- `Vec<CaretPosition>` (one per grapheme/codepoint)

When `layout_edit_delta` (line 2457) is called, it calls `EditDelta::layout_delta` which runs `LayoutTask::run` in parallel via rayon (`into_par_iter()` in `edit.rs:539-563`). Each task computes a full `TextFrame` with all glyph/caret data. The results are pushed into a new `SumTree` in `layout_pending_edit` (line 2599), which replaces only the affected range but retains all other blocks.

**Key issue**: There is **no virtualization** - blocks far off-screen retain their full glyph/caret position data. The `LayoutCache` created in `layout_edit_delta` (line 2463) is a throwaway `LayoutCache::new()` that provides no cross-layout caching benefit. Each `BlockItem::Paragraph` stores its `Arc<TextFrame>` permanently.

**No eviction mechanism exists**: The `SumTree` has no capacity limit, no LRU eviction, and no mechanism to lazily re-layout off-screen blocks. The `ViewportState` only controls which items are *rendered*, not which items are *laid out in memory*.

## Allocation Site #2: Buffer::replace_all - ~510 MB

**Call path**: `SumTree<BufferText>::append_str` → `update_content_with_text_fragments` → `Buffer::replace_all` → `GlobalBufferModel::populate_buffer_with_read_content`

**Root cause**: `Buffer::replace_all` (`crates/editor/src/content/buffer.rs:4564`) loads the **entire file content** into a `SumTree<BufferText>` buffer. `GlobalBufferModel::populate_buffer_with_read_content` (`app/src/code/global_buffer_model.rs:484`) calls this for both initial load and auto-reload (fallback path).

**Key issue**: There is **no file size limit** for buffer loading. The only size guard in the codebase is `MAX_FILE_SIZE = 3MB` in `crates/repo_metadata/src/entry.rs:16`, but this only gates treesitter parsing - it does NOT prevent loading large files into the editor buffer. A user opening a multi-hundred-MB log file or generated file will have the entire content loaded into both the `Buffer` SumTree and the `RenderState` SumTree.

Additionally, `replace_all` constructs a `CoreEditorAction::Insert` that creates `FormattedText` from the entire file content, effectively doubling memory during the replacement.

## Allocation Site #3-5: Text Layout (Glyph + CaretPosition) - ~700 MB combined

**Call path**: `Vec<Glyph>::from_iter` / `Vec<CaretPosition>::from_iter` → `line_from_ct_line` → `LayoutCache::layout_text` → `TextLayout::layout_text_with_options` → `layout_text_block` → `LayoutTask::run` (rayon workers)

**Root cause**: `EditDelta::layout_delta` (`crates/editor/src/content/edit.rs:497`) runs layout tasks in parallel via `into_par_iter()`. Each `layout_text_block` call creates `Paragraph` objects containing `Arc<TextFrame>` with full `Vec<Glyph>` and `Vec<CaretPosition>` per line.

**Key issue**: The `LayoutCache` (`crates/warpui_core/src/text_layout.rs:108`) uses a two-frame `TextCache<T>` (prev_frame + curr_frame HashMaps). This is designed for frame-to-frame caching during rendering, but in the layout pipeline, a **throwaway** `LayoutCache::new()` is created each time `layout_edit_delta` runs (mod.rs:2463), so there is zero caching benefit. Every layout recomputes all glyphs from scratch.

The `Glyph` struct (24 bytes each: `GlyphId` + `Vector2F` + `usize` + `f32`) and `CaretPosition` struct (12 bytes each: `f32` + `usize` + `usize`) are allocated per-character for every block. For a document with millions of characters, this creates hundreds of MB of retained glyph data for off-screen content that will never be rendered.

## Proposed Fixes

### P0: Viewport-bounded layout (addresses #1 and #3-5, ~2.7 GB)
Implement **lazy layout** for off-screen blocks:
- Store lightweight "placeholder" `BlockItem` variants for blocks outside the viewport (keep only `content_length`, `height estimate`, `lines count`)
- Only compute full `TextFrame` with glyph/caret data for blocks within or near the viewport
- When scrolling brings new blocks into view, lay them out on demand
- When blocks leave the viewport, downgrade them back to placeholders

This is the highest-impact fix and would eliminate the majority of the memory usage.

### P1: File size guardrails (addresses #2, ~510 MB)
- Add a configurable `MAX_EDITOR_FILE_SIZE` limit (e.g., 50 MB) in `GlobalBufferModel::populate_buffer_with_read_content`
- For files exceeding the limit, either refuse to open them or open in a read-only "large file" mode with truncated/chunked loading
- Consider streaming content for very large files rather than loading everything into a single `Buffer::replace_all` call

### P2: Glyph data deduplication (addresses #3-5)
- For monospaced code blocks, most lines share identical glyph metrics - consider sharing glyph layout data for lines with the same font/size
- Investigate whether `CaretPosition` data can be lazily computed (only when the user interacts with that line) rather than eagerly stored for all lines

### P3: Layout cache optimization
- Instead of creating a throwaway `LayoutCache::new()` in each `layout_edit_delta` call, share a persistent `LayoutCache` across layout cycles to get cache hits for unchanged blocks
- This would reduce redundant text layout computation during incremental edits

## Reproduction Scenario

This issue is most likely triggered by:
1. Opening a very large file (hundreds of MB) in the code editor
2. Having multiple large files open simultaneously
3. Long-running sessions where AI agent output accumulates large rendered content (breadcrumbs mention tantivy indexing and AI workspace cleanup)

The event device is a Mac15,11 (M3 Max) with likely 36-96 GB RAM, meaning the 12 GB footprint went unnoticed for a while before triggering the alert.
labels: bug

title: Feature request: `paste_transform` - pipe clipboard through a shell command before insertion
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp issues](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there

---

### Feature request: `paste_transform` - pipe clipboard through a shell command before insertion

#### Summary

When pasting output from AI TUI tools (Kiro CLI, Claude Code, GSD, and similar) into Warp, the clipboard contains rendering artifacts that make pasted code syntactically broken. Warp should expose a config hook that pipes clipboard content through an arbitrary shell command before inserting it into the input block.

---

#### Problem

Modern AI coding assistants render responses in styled terminal panels. Their `/copy to clipboard` commands capture the rendered buffer rather than raw message text. Two artifact classes land in Warp on every paste:

**1. Box-padding bleed.** TUI code blocks indent content by a fixed amount (typically 2 spaces). Every interior line carries that prefix. Heredoc content and config file values arrive with leading whitespace that breaks syntax:

```
# What lands in Warp after Cmd+V from Kiro CLI:
cat > ~/.config/app/config << 'EOF'
  [settings]
  timeout = 30
EOF
```

The `[settings]` and `timeout` lines have 2-space indent - the heredoc writes a broken config file silently.

**2. Soft-wrap line splits.** Lines that exceed the TUI's render width split at the column boundary. A single-line Python expression:

```
session_valid = python3 -c "import os,time; exit(0 if time.time() < os.path.getmtime(os.path.expanduser('~/.cache/app/token')) + 7200 else 1)"
```

arrives in Warp as two lines:

```
  session_valid = python3 -c "import os,time; exit(0 if time.time() < os.path.getmtime(os.path.expanduser('~/.cache/app/token')) + 7200
  else 1)"
```

This is a `SyntaxError` if pasted into a shell.

---

#### Proposed solution

Add a `paste_transform` field to `[terminal.input]` in `~/.warp/settings.toml`:

```toml
[terminal.input]
paste_transform = "tui-clean -"  # https://github.com/rndjams/tui-clean
```

Semantics:

- Warp pipes clipboard content through the specified command (stdin → stdout) before inserting into the input block.
- On non-zero exit or empty stdout, fall back to the original clipboard content - never silently drop a paste.
- Unset by default; no behavior change for existing users.
- Command runs in a login shell so `PATH` and user environment are available.

This is a power-user escape hatch. The correct long-term fix is for TUI tools to emit clipboard content via OSC 52 (bypassing the render buffer entirely - see root cause note below), but that requires changes across multiple third-party tools. `paste_transform` gives users relief before those upstream fixes land.

---

#### Alternatives considered

**ZLE `bracketed-paste` override.** In iTerm2 and traditional terminals, zsh's ZLE widget can intercept and transform paste content before it reaches the shell. Warp's input block bypasses the bracketed-paste protocol entirely, so this approach does not apply here.

**Manual `fixclip` alias before each paste.** Running `pbpaste | tui-clean - | pbcopy` before pasting works but breaks the Cmd+C → Cmd+V flow.

---

#### Root cause note

The underlying issue is that Kiro CLI, Claude Code, GSD, and similar tools copy the *rendered terminal buffer* on `/copy to clipboard` rather than raw message text. The correct fix for each tool is to emit an **OSC 52** escape sequence with plain-text content, bypassing the render pipeline. Separate issues filed with upstream tools:
- Kiro CLI: kirodotdev/Kiro#8814
- GSD: open-gsd/gsd-pi#69

`paste_transform` bridges the gap while those land.

---

#### Impact

- **Affected:** any Warp user who pastes generated code from an AI TUI assistant
- **Severity:** high - pastes are silently syntactically broken, not visually obvious
- **Frequency:** every paste from Kiro CLI, Claude Code, GSD, or similar
- **Workaround cost:** manual extra step before every paste, or OS-level system permission grants

---

#### Platform

- macOS arm64 (Apple Silicon)
- Warp v0.2026.05.20.09.21.stable_03
- zsh 5.9

#### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No, but it breaks every AI-generated heredoc and multi-line expression paste.

#### Is this issue specific to Warp?

The artifact exists in all terminals. The ZLE workaround handles it transparently in iTerm2, Ghostty, and kitty. The Warp-specific gap is that Warp's input block does not participate in the bracketed-paste protocol, so the ZLE fix has no effect here.

title: URL soft-wrap: AI TUI output splits URLs across rows - CMD+click opens truncated fragment
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there

### Describe the bug

AI TUI tools (Kiro CLI, Claude Code, GSD, and similar) render responses inside column-constrained panels and soft-wrap lines at the render width. When those wrapped lines appear in Warp's block output, URLs that span the wrap boundary are split across two rows. Warp's link detector sees only the first fragment as a URL candidate - CMD+click opens the truncated URL, silently failing any auth flow or navigation that depends on it.

**Concrete example** - kiro-cli wraps at its panel width:

```
# Block output as Warp receives it:
Authenticate here: https://auth.example.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=myapp&sta
te=abc123&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fmyapp.example.com%2Fcallback
```

Hovering the first line highlights `https://auth.example.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=myapp&sta` as the URL. CMD+click opens that truncated address - the browser reports an invalid request or silently fails the auth flow. The second line (`te=abc123&redirect_uri=...`) is not recognized as a URL at all.

**Second manifestation - interactive Ctrl+y prompt:**

Kiro CLI also presents OAuth URLs via an in-TUI prompt (`Ctrl+y to copy URL`). The URL displayed there is similarly soft-wrapped; `Ctrl+y` copies only the visible fragment to clipboard. The destination URL is inaccessible.

### Root cause

This is a **tokenizer-layer** problem in block output link detection, distinct from but related to the resolution-layer bug in #9908.

Warp's `possible_file_paths_at_point` / `scan_for_file_path` pipeline in `link_detection.rs` processes rows of block output independently. When a URL has been soft-wrapped by an upstream TUI renderer, each row is a valid string - the first fragment passes as a (truncated) URL, the second looks like a bare word. There is no cross-row context to signal that they are halves of the same URL.

The upstream cause is that tools like Kiro CLI copy the rendered terminal buffer rather than raw message text, and do not emit URLs via **OSC 8** (terminal hyperlinks, `\x1b]8;;URI\x07display\x1b]8;;\x07`). If they did, the URI param in the OSC 8 sequence is never soft-wrapped and Warp's click handler could use it directly once #6541 lands. Until then, Warp sees only the wrapped display text.

### Relationship to other issues

This is in the same link-detection subsystem as several related issues - all share `link_detection.rs` / `grid_handler.rs` as the fix site, but address different stages:

| Issue | Stage | Problem | Status |
|-------|-------|---------|--------|
| **#9908** | Resolution | Correct token, wrong resolution root (`ls DIR/`) | PR #10579 in review |
| **#9909** / **#10004** | Tokenizer | Box-drawing chars not in `FILE_LINK_SEPARATORS` | ✅ Fixed in #10004 |
| **This issue** | Tokenizer | Soft-wrapped URL split across rows | Open |
| **#6541** | Renderer | OSC 8 hyperlinks not rendered as clickable | Open - upstream fix |

**This issue is complementary to, not a duplicate of, #11608** (paste_transform). That issue covers the *paste* path - cleaning up artifacts when content is Cmd+V'd into the input block. This issue covers the *click* path - what happens when a user hovers and CMD+clicks a URL in block output. Different code paths; both need fixing independently.

### Expected behavior

1. When a block output row ends with a URL that extends to the end of the line (`https?://\S+$`), and the immediately following row begins with a URL-safe fragment containing URL-specific characters (digits, `%`, `?`, `&`, `=`, `/` - distinguishing real URL tails from prose words), the two rows should be joined into a single URL candidate before link validation.
2. Joined URLs must be clickable and must open the full, reconstructed URL.
3. Behavior is additive - rows that don't match the URL-continuation heuristic are unaffected. Non-URL clickable detection (file paths, per #9908) is unaffected.
4. If #6541 (OSC 8 rendering) lands, OSC 8 URIs should take precedence over this heuristic - the URI param is authoritative and never wrapped.

### Proposed fix

In `possible_file_paths_at_point` or the row-scanning loop that feeds it, before emitting URL candidates, apply a URL-fragment join pass:

```
for each row i in block output:
    if row[i] matches `https?://\S+$`:          // URL reaches end-of-line
        if row[i+1] starts with a URL-continuation fragment:
            //   - no leading whitespace on the fragment
            //   - first token is all URL-safe chars (RFC 3986)
            //   - first token contains at least one of: digit, %, ?, &, =, /
            //     (distinguishes "6085010" from prose words like "for")
            join row[i] + row[i+1].first_token as single URL candidate
            emit remainder of row[i+1] as separate non-URL content
```

The `_is_url_continuation` logic in [tui-clean](https://github.com/rndjams/tui-clean) (MIT) has a tested Python reference implementation for the heuristic and edge cases, including false-positive guards.

**Known limitation:** The heuristic cannot perfectly distinguish a URL continuation from a lowercase prose word that happens to contain URL-safe characters. This is an inherent constraint of heuristic text analysis. The clean fix is OSC 8 (#6541): once kiro-cli and similar tools emit proper hyperlinks, Warp can use the URI param as the authoritative click target regardless of how the display text was wrapped.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# Simulate kiro-cli wrapped URL output (any AI TUI tool with long auth URLs)
# Start a kiro-cli chat session, trigger an OAuth authentication URL (e.g.
# connect a GitHub MCP server), observe the URL wraps at the panel width.
# Hover the URL in block output - only the first fragment highlights.
# CMD+click - browser opens the truncated URL (invalid request).
```

For a minimal synthetic test without kiro-cli:

```bash
printf 'Authenticate: https://auth.example.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=myapp&sta\nte=abc123&redirect_uri=https%%3A%%2F%%2Fmyapp.example.com%%2Fcallback\n'
```

Paste this into a Warp block (via `echo` or similar). Hover the first line - only the fragment is highlighted.

### Environment

- macOS 26.4.1 (Darwin 25.4.0, arm64)
- zsh 5.9
- Warp v0.2026.04.27.15.32.stable_03
- Reproducible with: Kiro CLI 2.4.x (default TUI mode), Claude Code, GSD

### Additional context

**Upstream tracking:** kiro-cli filed as [kirodotdev/Kiro#8814](https://github.com/kirodotdev/Kiro/issues/8814) - root cause is that `/copy to clipboard` and TUI rendering scrape the rendered buffer rather than using OSC 52 / OSC 8.

**Workaround (paste path only):** [tui-clean](https://github.com/rndjams/tui-clean) rejoins URL fragments when pasting via the ZLE bracketed-paste hook. Does not help with block-output clicks; that requires a Warp-side fix.

**Scope boundary:** This issue covers single-line URL wraps. Multi-line URLs (where the URL wraps more than once) are out of scope for V1 - they're rare and the fix is iterative.

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes - other terminals don't have clickable link detection in block output, so the problem manifests differently (no click at all vs. wrong click).

title: Feature: Built-in SSH remote execution tool/skill for Oz agents (Windows-to-Linux cross-platform safety)
body:
<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary

Oz agents orchestrating work across a Windows host and a remote Linux server face a class of SSH failures that are entirely avoidable with the right invocation patterns. The `run_shell_command` tool provides no SSH-specific handling, so agents must rediscover the correct patterns every session. A built-in `run_remote_command` tool or bundled SSH skill in `oz-skills` would make multi-machine agent workflows reliable by default.

## Problem

When an Oz agent on Windows uses `run_shell_command` to issue SSH commands to a remote Linux machine, several silent failure modes occur that the agent cannot recover from without explicit foreknowledge:

1. **Hanging SSH sessions** - `ssh HOST "cmd"` without `-n -T` inherits `run_shell_command`'s stdin pipe and blocks indefinitely. The agent appears frozen; the user must Ctrl+C. `-n` redirects stdin from `/dev/null`; `-T` disables PTY allocation. Neither is applied automatically.

2. **CRLF line-ending corruption** - Files written by Warp agent tools on Windows have `\r\n` endings. When these are transferred via SCP to Linux and executed as bash scripts, the `\r` causes unclosed-string hangs. Every `.sh` file must be patched with `sed -i 's/\r//'` after transfer, but there is no platform reminder or enforcement.

3. **Orphaned background processes retaining GPU VRAM** - `nohup cmd &` over SSH without `< /dev/null` keeps the background job's stdin attached to the SSH session. Killing the SSH PID kills only the bash wrapper; the Python child survives, retains all GPU VRAM (40+ GB in our case), and causes OOM on the next launch. The fix (`< /dev/null` + `pkill -f name`) is non-obvious and undocumented.

4. **Heredoc parsing failure from PowerShell** - SSH commands containing heredocs (`<< 'EOF'`) are parsed by PowerShell as its own syntax, producing errors. Scripts must be written locally, SCP'd, CRLF-stripped, and executed - a multi-step pattern that must be rediscovered every session.

These failures surfaced repeatedly during a 32-hour GRPO training run orchestrated by an Oz agent, wasting multiple hours of GPU time across four separate crash-and-restart cycles.

## Desired workflow

Instead of agents (and users) rediscovering the correct SSH patterns:

`
ssh -n -T HOST "cmd"
scp file HOST:path && ssh -n -T HOST "sed -i 's/\r//' path"
nohup bash -c 'cmd' < /dev/null > log 2>&1 &
pkill -f script_name
`

the platform should provide one or more of:

**Option A - Built-in `run_remote_command` tool** for Oz agents, analogous to `run_shell_command`, that automatically applies correct SSH flags, handles CRLF on file transfer, and manages background-job stdin. Should work regardless of the agent host OS.

**Option B - Bundled SSH skill in `warpdotdev/oz-skills`** that documents and enforces these patterns, discoverable by agents via the existing skill system.

**Option C - Cross-platform SSH safety in `run_shell_command`** - when Warp detects that an agent is on Windows and issuing SSH commands, warn or patch the invocation automatically.

## Reproduction steps or desired workflow

1. Start an Oz local agent on Windows (PowerShell 7).
2. Ask it to launch a long-running Python training job on a remote Linux GPU server via SSH.
3. Agent calls `run_shell_command` with `ssh layer1labs "nohup python train.py > log 2>&1 &"`.
4. SSH hangs - no `-n` flag, stdin pipe inherited. Agent is stuck.
5. Restarted agent adds `-n` but writes a bash helper to disk via Warp's file tool (Windows CRLF) and SCP's it without stripping line endings.
6. Remote bash script hangs on first string literal - `\r` in the token.
7. Agent kills the bash PID; Python child keeps running, holds 40 GB VRAM.
8. Next launch OOMs. Two hours of training lost.

## Artifacts

None attached.

## Warp version

Latest (Oz agent, Windows host, May 2026)

## Operating system

Windows 11 / PowerShell 7.5.5 (Oz agent host) → Ubuntu Linux (remote GPU server)

## Possible source references

- `run_shell_command` built-in agent tool - the gap is the absence of a remote-execution equivalent with SSH safety defaults
- `warpdotdev/oz-skills` - natural home for a bundled SSH safety skill

title: SIGABRT: panic_cannot_unwind in DispatchDelegate::run_on_main_thread with 10+ concurrent sessions

### Describe the bug

Warp crashes with **SIGABRT** (`panic_cannot_unwind`) when **10+ terminal sessions/tabs are open simultaneously**. The crash occurs on the **main thread** during `DispatchDelegate::run_on_main_thread` → `dispatch_main_queue_drain`, suggesting a panic inside a GCD-dispatched closure that crosses an FFI boundary where unwinding is not permitted.

**Crash signature:**
```

```

**Thread state at crash:** 75 active threads including 12 PTY readers, 5 Bulk Filesystem Watchers, 5 notify-rs debouncer loops, 4 notify-rs fsevents loops, 12 tokio workers, 12 rayon workers.

### To reproduce

1. Open Warp and create **10-12 terminal tabs/sessions**
2. Run concurrent workloads in each (dev servers, file watchers, build processes, log tailing, etc.)
3. Continue working normally for **1-2 hours**
4. Warp crashes with SIGABRT - no specific trigger action, happens during routine usage

**Key observation:** This does **NOT** happen with 1-3 sessions. The crash correlates with high session count and concurrent main-thread dispatch pressure.

### Expected behavior

Warp should remain stable regardless of how many terminal sessions are open.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

```

```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Thread / Resource Summary at Crash</summary>

| PTY reader threads | 12 (= 12 terminal sessions) |
| Bulk Filesystem Watcher | 5 |
| notify-rs debouncer loop | 5 |

### Analysis

A closure dispatched to the GCD main queue via `run_on_main_thread` panicked during execution. Because the closure crosses an FFI boundary (`extern "C"` or similar unwind-incompatible context), the panic escalated to `panic_cannot_unwind` → `abort()`.

With 12 sessions, each session spawns its own PTY reader + file watcher + debouncer threads, all of which periodically dispatch UI updates to the single main thread queue. This creates significant contention on `dispatch_main_queue_drain`, increasing the likelihood of a panic inside one of these closures (possibly due to stale state or a race condition).

- #8881 - SIGABRT during window drag-resize

All share the pattern of panics in main-thread UI operations, but this crash originates specifically in `work_execute_closure` / `run_on_main_thread`, which hasn't been reported before.

title: Agent Mode conversation hangs permanently (InProgress, has_active_stream=false) with custom OpenAI-compatible provider
body:
<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary
Agent Mode conversation permanently hangs in `InProgress` with `has_active_stream=false` when using a custom OpenAI-compatible provider. The SSE stream completes successfully (router returns 200 OK, all chunks including `[DONE]` are sent), but Warp's internal state machine never transitions the conversation to `Completed`. Stale conversations persist in `warp.sqlite` and are re-polled after Windows reboot.

## Problem
When using a custom OpenAI-compatible provider (self-hosted FastAPI router proxying Cloudflare Workers AI), Agent Mode conversations get stuck in a state where:
- The SSE stream has already completed (no active stream)
- The conversation status remains `InProgress`
- Warp continuously polls every ~10 seconds with `Pending events are not ready`
- The conversation never transitions to `Completed`
- The affected tab becomes unusable - the agent cannot send or receive messages

This happens both for regular conversations and for orchestrator conversations (those using `run_agents` with child agents). The orchestrator conversation `11ae9701` has been stuck across multiple Warp restarts and a full Windows reboot because it is persisted in `warp.sqlite`.

## Expected behavior
When the SSE stream from the provider completes (all chunks sent, `[DONE]` received, HTTP connection closed), the conversation should transition from `InProgress` to `Completed` and the agent should be able to process the next user message.

## Actual behavior
The conversation remains stuck in `InProgress` with `has_active_stream=false`. Warp logs repeat indefinitely:
```
Pending events are not ready: conversation_id=AIConversationId(adc0ea85-b562-4353-a50b-76c172b92f29) owns_conversation=true has_active_stream=false status=InProgress
```
The stuck state persists across tab creation, Warp restart, and Windows reboot because the stale conversation is loaded from `warp.sqlite` on startup.

## Reproduction steps or desired workflow
1. Configure Warp Agent Mode with a custom OpenAI-compatible provider (e.g., a self-hosted FastAPI router at a custom base URL)
2. Start a conversation in Agent Mode
3. Send a message that triggers a multi-turn exchange (especially with tool calls or orchestration via `run_agents`)
4. Observe that after the provider returns a complete response with valid SSE, the conversation hangs
5. Warp logs show `Pending events are not ready: has_active_stream=false status=InProgress` repeating every ~10 seconds
6. The conversation is permanently stuck; only creating a new tab works around the issue

## Artifacts
None attached

## Warp version
Oz v0.2026.05.20.09.21.stable_03

## Operating system
Windows 11 Pro (Build 26100.x)

## Additional context

### Provider details
- Self-hosted FastAPI router (round-kimi-router) proxying Cloudflare Workers AI (Kimi K2.6)
- Exposes standard OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint
- SSE format: standard `data: {...}\n\n` chunks followed by `data: [DONE]\n\n`
- Router returns HTTP 200 OK for all affected requests
- No errors in router logs - requests complete normally

### Network path
Client → ngrok HTTPS → nginx:4080 → router:4005 → Cloudflare API

### Two stuck conversations observed simultaneously
1. `adc0ea85-b562-4353-a50b-76c172b92f29` - started hanging at 19:31:19
2. `11ae9701-1a6b-4ebe-b887-552b1fa2d93c` - orchestrator conversation with 4 child agent run IDs, persisting across reboots from a previous session

```json
{"ok":true,"targets":263,"alive":136,"failed":0,"daily_limited":20,"busy":0}
```

### SQLite persistence
The stuck conversation state is stored in `warp.sqlite` and reloaded on every Warp startup, causing the hang to survive application restarts and even Windows reboots.

title: Warp's "Custom Inference" privacy claim is false - requests are proxied through warp.dev
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates

### Describe the bug

I've been testing Warp's "Custom Inference" feature, which lets users configure a custom LLM endpoint and API token. After inspecting the network behavior, it's clear that requests are not sent directly to the configured endpoint - they are proxied through Warp's own infrastructure (*warp.dev). There is no technical reason for this. The user explicitly configured a third-party endpoint; the client should call it directly.

More importantly, the "Custom Inference" documentation claims that API keys are stored locally and never synced to the cloud. That statement is false in practice. If every request is routed through your servers, then the API key is, by definition, transmitted to and handled by your infrastructure on every call - regardless of where the key is "stored" at rest. The distinction between "synced" and "transmitted on every request" is meaningless from a security and privacy standpoint.

This is a serious misrepresentation. Please either (1) change the implementation so custom endpoints are called directly from the client, or (2) update the documentation to accurately describe the data flow, including the fact that user credentials and prompts are routed through Warp-controlled servers. Until one of those happens, the current description is misleading users about what they're consenting to.

### To reproduce

Warp's "Custom Inference" feature claims that API keys are stored locally and never synced to the cloud. In practice, requests made to a user-configured custom endpoint are not sent directly from the client - they are proxied through Warp's own infrastructure (`*.warp.dev`). This contradicts the in-product description and has clear privacy/security implications: the API key and prompt content are transmitted to Warp servers on every request.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Warp → Settings → AI → **Custom Inference** (or equivalent).
2. Configure a custom LLM provider with:
   - A custom endpoint URL pointing to a host you control (e.g. `https://my-provider.example.com/v1`).
   - A custom API token.
3. Save the configuration and select this provider as the active one.
4. Start capturing outbound network traffic from the Warp process,

title: Agent-dispatched multi-line shell block can leave zsh stuck at dquote> (hang)
body:
## Summary

When the Warp agent dispatches a multi-line shell command block to zsh, the receiving shell can drop into a `dquote>` continuation prompt and consume every subsequent character as quoted text until aborted. The exact same command, when written to a file and executed, runs without issue. This makes the failure look like a paste/dispatch-quoting bug in the agent → terminal hand-off rather than a user error.

## Environment

- App: Warp (Stable) on macOS
- Shell: zsh 5.9
- Mode: Agent-driven command execution (multi-line block)

## Reproduction

1. Have an agent (or `/agent`) issue a single tool call containing a multi-line shell block with the following ingredients combined in one dispatch:
   - Several lines of variable assignments and a `mkdir -p`.
   - A heredoc-like comment line (e.g. `# Start 5 downloads in parallel, each as nohup background process`).
   - Multiple `nohup ... \` continuations, each followed by another `\`-continued line with `>` and `2>&1 &` redirections.
   - Inline `echo "string with hyphens and dollars $!"` lines between the backgrounded commands.
   - A final `ps -o pid,etime,command -p $(jobs -p) 2>/dev/null`.

Example minimal-ish block:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/dlogs
LOG=/tmp/dlogs

# kick off two background downloads
nohup curl -sSL https://example.com/a \
  -o /tmp/a.bin \
  > $LOG/a.log 2>&1 &
echo "A PID=$!"

nohup curl -sSL https://example.com/b \
  -o /tmp/b.bin \
  > $LOG/b.log 2>&1 &
echo "B PID=$!"

jobs -p > $LOG/pids.txt
echo "--- All download jobs ---"
ps -o pid,etime,command -p $(jobs -p) 2>/dev/null
```

2. Submit it from the agent (not pasted manually).

## Expected

The shell parses the block, backgrounds the two jobs, prints the PIDs, writes `pids.txt`, and prints the job table.

## Actual

zsh accepts the block up to (apparently) the `echo "--- All download jobs ---"` line and then drops into:

```
dquote>
```

...waiting for a closing `"`. No background jobs are started, no PIDs are captured, no output is produced. The block hangs indefinitely; the only escape is `Ctrl-C` (or typing `"` + Enter, then `Ctrl-C`).

## Workaround

Writing the same content into a script file and invoking it as `bash /path/to/script.sh` succeeds every time, so the issue is in the way the block is transmitted to the shell rather than in the commands themselves.

## Suspected cause

The dispatch path appears to lose or transform a `"` somewhere in the multi-line block - probably the opening or closing quote of the `echo "--- All download jobs ---"` line gets stripped or split across boundaries during the agent → terminal hand-off. From zsh's perspective, it sees an opening `"` with no matching close and enters dquote-continuation mode for everything that follows.

## Impact

Any agentic workflow that legitimately uses:

- backslash-continued multi-line commands,
- inline comments,
- `"..."` echoes,
- `&` backgrounding,

...can silently hang the user's terminal. The agent's tool call appears to "succeed" from its side (the shell consumed the input), but the block never executes. Recovering requires manual `Ctrl-C` in the stuck pane.

## Suggested fixes

- Validate or escape quoting boundaries before dispatch, or send the block via a temp script file under the hood when it crosses some complexity threshold.
- Alternatively, feed the block to the shell via `bash -c '...'` with proper single-quote escaping so zsh never sees an interactive `dquote>` state.
- Surface a UI hint when the shell is stuck in a `dquote>`/`quote>`/`heredoc>` state for more than N seconds, since the user otherwise sees the block apparently hang.

## Logs / screenshots

Screenshot showing the dispatched block ending at `ps -o pid,etime,command -p $(jobs -p) 2>/dev/null` and the shell sitting at `dquote>` is available on request.

title: Default profile base model selection resets back to "auto" instead of persisting
body:
<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary
Changing the Base model on the Default profile in Settings → AI → Profiles does not persist - the selection reverts to "auto (cost-efficient)" instead of saving the chosen model.

## Problem
In Settings → AI → Profiles, the Default profile exposes a Base model selector that should let the user pin a specific frontier model (e.g. a Claude or GPT model) as the profile-level default for Agent Mode. After picking a non-Auto model the UI is expected to display the chosen model's name. Instead, the displayed Base model snaps back to "auto (cost-efficient)" and the selected model is not honored.

## Expected behavior
After selecting a specific Base model from the dropdown on the Default profile, the Profiles panel continues to show that model's display name, and the profile uses that model going forward (including across app restarts).

## Actual behavior
The Default profile's Base model field shows the selected model briefly (if at all) and then reverts to "auto (cost-efficient)", which is the fallback label rendered when `profile.base_model` is `None` or resolves to an unknown id.

## Reproduction steps or desired workflow
1. Open Settings → AI → Profiles.
2. Locate the Default profile card. The Base model row shows `auto (cost-efficient)`.
3. Click Edit and use the Base model dropdown to select a specific non-Auto model.
4. Return to the Profiles list (or reopen Settings).
5. Observe the Base model on the Default profile is again `auto (cost-efficient)` instead of the selected model.

## Artifacts
**Screenshot 1:** Settings → AI → Profiles panel showing the Default profile card with Base model: auto (cost-efficient) after attempting to change it.
_Paste screenshot 1 here_

## Warp version
v0.2026.05.20.09.21.03

## Operating system
macOS 26.4.1

## Possible source references
- `app/src/settings_view/execution_profile_view.rs:103-113` - Base model display falls back to `llm_preferences.get_default_base_model().display_name` ("auto (cost-efficient)") whenever `profile.base_model` is `None` or the saved `LLMId` cannot be resolved via `get_llm_info`. A failed save or a sanitization pass that clears the field would manifest exactly as "resets to auto".
- `app/src/ai/execution_profiles/editor/mod.rs:1557-1568` - `SetBaseModel` handler calls `AIExecutionProfilesModel::set_base_model` and also resets the per-profile context window limit.
- `app/src/ai/execution_profiles/profiles.rs:490-517` (`set_base_model`) and `1234-1325` (`edit_profile_internal`) - first edit of the Default profile creates a cloud-backed object via `create_ai_execution_profile`; if `personal_drive` is unavailable the edit is persisted locally on the `Unsynced` state, which is a recent fallback and may be relevant.
- `app/src/ai/execution_profiles/profiles.rs:1399-1416` (`reconcile_with_cloud_state_after_initial_load`) - reconcile after `CloudModelEvent::InitialLoadCompleted` can transition `Unsynced` → `Synced` and overwrite local state if an edit races initial cloud load.
- `app/src/ai/llms.rs:851-912` (`sanitize_disabled_custom_model_preferences`) - explicitly calls `set_base_model(profile_id, None, ctx)` for any profile whose Base model is a custom-endpoint LLM when the `CustomInferenceEndpoints` feature flag or entitlement is off; this resets the field to None, which renders as "auto".

title: Feature Request: Session management improvements - bulk delete, age-based purge, and meaningful session names
body:
<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary
Session management in Warp lacks basic housekeeping capabilities. Users cannot bulk-delete old sessions, purge sessions by age, or assign meaningful names to sessions. The only options are deleting sessions one by one or nuking the entire SQLite database - there is no middle ground.

## Problem
As sessions accumulate over days and weeks, the session list becomes cluttered with auto-generated, cryptic names that are difficult to identify. Managing this list is tedious because:

1. **No bulk delete** - Sessions can only be deleted one at a time. For users with dozens of old sessions, this is impractical.
2. **No age-based purge** - There is no way to remove sessions older than a certain threshold (e.g., "delete sessions older than 3 days"). The only alternative is deleting the entire `warp.sqlite` database, which wipes all session data indiscriminately.
3. **No session rename** - Session names are auto-generated and cannot be renamed to something meaningful. This makes it hard to identify which session was used for what purpose.

The underlying session data lives in a single SQLite file buried deep in `~/Library/Group Containers/2BBY89MBSN.dev.warp/Library/Application Support/dev.warp.Warp-Stable/warp.sqlite`, which is not user-serviceable for selective cleanup.

## Reproduction steps or desired workflow
1. Open the session list in the sidebar.
2. Right-click a session → option to **Rename** the session.
3. Select multiple sessions → option to **Delete selected**.
4. Access a **Purge old sessions** option (e.g., "Delete sessions older than X days") via right-click menu or Settings.

- Add a **"Direct Connection"** toggle in Custom Endpoint settings

title: Win+Arrow keys (Aero Snap) don't pass through to OS when Warp has focus on Windows
body:
### Describe the bug

When the Warp window has focus on Windows, the OS-level Aero Snap shortcuts `Win+Up`, `Win+Down`, `Win+Left`, `Win+Right` do not work - Warp appears to capture/swallow these key combinations and they are not passed through to Windows.

Interestingly, **`Win+Z` (Snap Layouts) still works** while Warp has focus, which suggests this is specific to `Win+<arrow>` combinations rather than the Windows key being globally captured.

The symptoms were first noticed around **2026-05-27**. Warp on this machine was updated to `v0.2026.05.20.09.21.stable_02` on 2026-05-22 (~5 days before symptoms were noticed), so it may have been latent since the update and only surfaced once `Win+<arrow>` was used. I do not see any matching entry under Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts (no `Super` / `Meta` / `Win` + arrow binding shown).

### To reproduce

1. Open Warp on Windows.
2. Make sure the Warp window has focus.
3. Press `Win+Up` (or `Win+Down` / `Win+Left` / `Win+Right`).
4. Expected: window maximizes / minimizes / snaps to half of the screen.
5. Actual: nothing happens. The key combo is silently consumed.
6. Click any other app (Explorer, Notepad, browser) to give it focus and try the same combo → works as expected.
7. With Warp still running but unfocused, the combos work in other apps.

### Expected behavior

`Win+<arrow>` should be passed through to the OS (Windows Aero Snap) regardless of whether Warp has focus, since these are reserved OS-level shortcuts and Warp does not advertise any built-in binding on them.

### Operating system

Windows

### Operating system and version

Windows 11 25H2, Build 26200 (OsName: "Microsoft Windows 11 Business", OsVersion: 10.0.26200)

### Regression

Yes, this is a new bug that started recently

### Recent working Warp date

Symptoms first noticed around 2026-05-27. Warp on this machine was updated to the current version on 2026-05-22.

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No - `Win+Z` (Snap Layouts) can be used as a workaround, but it's a meaningful regression in muscle-memory window management.

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes. The same key combinations work normally when any other application has focus (verified with Explorer / Notepad / browser while Warp is still running in the background).

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.05.20.09.21.stable_02

### Additional context

- No relevant entry visible under Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts (no `Super+Up` / `Meta+Up` / `Win+Up` binding shown).
- `Win+Z` works normally, so this is not a global Windows-key capture - only the `Win+<arrow>` combinations are affected.
- No common key-remapping tools are running (PowerToys / AutoHotkey / Keypirinha / SharpKeys - none detected in process list).
- Could not find a matching entry in the Known Issues page or in recent GitHub issues.

title: [Linux X11] Chinese IME (ibus + RIME) input regression between 0.2026.04.27 and 0.2026.05.20
body:
## Summary

On Linux (X11 + ibus + RIME), typing Chinese in Warp **stopped working** somewhere between `0.2026.04.27.15.32.stable.03` and `0.2026.05.20.09.21.stable.03`. Reverting to `0.2026.04.27.15.32.stable.03` immediately restores IME input. Other GUI apps (gnome-terminal, browsers, editors) continue to accept ibus input normally throughout - system-level IME is healthy.

## Environment

- **OS**: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS
- **Session**: X11 (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11`)
- **Desktop**: GNOME
- **IME framework**: ibus 1.5.26, engine = `rime` (ibus-rime)
- **Locale**: `LANG=zh_CN.UTF-8` (verified `XSupportsLocale()==1`)
- **Env vars (in Warp process)**: `GTK_IM_MODULE=ibus`, `QT_IM_MODULE=ibus`, `XMODIFIERS=@im=ibus`

## Versions tested

| Warp version          | Result                            |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------------|
| `0.2026.04.27.15.32.stable.03` | ✅ Chinese input works (preedit popup, candidates, commit) |
| `0.2026.05.20.09.21.stable.03` | ❌ Keystrokes go straight through as Latin; no preedit popup |

## Diagnostic evidence

### 1. System-side XIM is healthy

A minimal Python script replicating winit/Xlib's IME init succeeds against the same ibus instance Warp connects to:

```
setlocale(LC_ALL,'')   -> zh_CN.UTF-8
XSupportsLocale()      -> 1
XSetLocaleModifiers    -> @im=ibus
XOpenDisplay()         -> ok
XOpenIM()              -> ok  (XIM server reachable)
```

`xprop -root XIM_SERVERS` returns `@server=ibus`, `ibus engine` returns `rime`.

### 2. Internal winit binding changed between the two versions

Extracted from `strings /opt/warpdotdev/warp-terminal/warp`:

```
4/27: winit-6b6d13ea8b42c599/7ef0185
5/20: winit-6b6d13ea8b42c599/a4e0ecb
```

Both binaries contain the winit X11 IME code paths (e.g. `src/platform_impl/linux/x11/ime/mod.rs`, error messages like `failed to create IME context with preedit support.`), so the regression is unlikely a missing-feature build flag - more likely a behavior change within the winit fork or in Warp's IME interaction with it.

## What I already ruled out

- ❌ Switching between `universal` and `classic` `input_box_type_setting` (no effect)
- ❌ `ibus restart` followed by a cold restart of Warp (no effect on 5/20)
- ❌ Re-checking env vars, locale, `~/.xinputrc`, GTK immodule cache - all correct
- ❌ Removed orphan `/etc/xdg/autostart/fcitx.desktop` left behind by a prior fcitx purge - no effect

## Reproduction

1. Fresh Ubuntu 22.04 / X11 session with ibus + ibus-rime, `LANG=zh_CN.UTF-8`.
2. Install `warp-terminal_0.2026.05.20.09.21.stable.03_amd64.deb`.
3. Open Warp from the application launcher.
4. Press `Super+Space` to activate RIME.
5. Type pinyin - no preedit popup appears, ASCII goes straight to the buffer.
6. Without changing anything else, `dpkg -i warp-terminal_0.2026.04.27.15.32.stable.03_amd64.deb` to downgrade.
7. Open Warp fresh - Chinese input works immediately.

## Workaround in use

Pinned to `0.2026.04.27.15.32.stable.03` via `apt-mark hold warp-terminal` and disabled the apt source. This blocks future upgrades until a fix lands.

## Request

Please review the X11 IME-related changes between the winit fork's `7ef0185` and `a4e0ecb`, or Warp-side changes to IME handling in that window. Happy to provide more diagnostic data, run targeted builds, or capture an `strace`/`ltrace` of the IME init sequence on the broken version if useful.

title: Bring Your Own Speech-to-Text Provider for Voice Input
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

## Summary

Please add support for configuring a custom speech-to-text provider for Warp Voice Input.

Warp already supports bringing your own API key and custom inference endpoints for LLM inference, but Voice Input currently appears to be tied to Warp's default transcription path powered by Wispr Flow. I would like the same level of user control for the voice transcription layer.

## Problem

I mainly want to use Warp's Voice Input feature, not necessarily Warp-hosted AI inference.

Right now, Voice Input depends on Warp's default transcription provider and usage limits. This creates a few practical issues:

1. Users cannot use their own speech-to-text billing account.
2. Users cannot choose a provider that works better for their language, accent, microphone setup, or latency needs.
3. Users cannot route transcription through a private, self-hosted, or company-approved endpoint.
4. Users who already use OpenAI, Azure Speech, Google Speech-to-Text, Deepgram, AssemblyAI, Whisper-compatible servers, or local transcription services cannot plug them into Warp.
5. BYOK/custom inference support exists for LLMs, but there is no equivalent configuration for the voice transcription layer.

## Desired solution

Add a Voice Input provider configuration section under:

Settings → Agents → Warp Agent → Voice

The configuration could support:

- Default Warp / Wispr Flow provider
- OpenAI transcription API
- OpenAI-compatible transcription endpoint
- Azure Speech
- Google Speech-to-Text
- Deepgram
- AssemblyAI
- Local/self-hosted Whisper-compatible endpoint

At minimum, a generic custom provider option would be useful:

- Provider name
- Base URL
- API key
- Model name
- Optional headers
- Language preference
- Timeout / retry settings

## Expected behavior

When a custom speech-to-text provider is configured, Warp Voice Input should:

1. Record audio using the existing Voice Input UI and hotkey.
2. Send the audio to the configured transcription provider.
3. Insert the returned text into the active Warp input field.
4. Avoid consuming Warp voice transcription usage limits when the user's own provider is selected.
5. Clearly show which provider is active.

## Actual behavior

Voice Input currently appears to use Warp's built-in transcription provider only. Users can configure their own LLM API keys and inference endpoints, but cannot configure their own speech-to-text provider for Voice Input.

## Why this matters

Voice Input is becoming a core developer workflow, especially for agentic coding and terminal automation. For many users, transcription quality, latency, privacy, and cost control matter as much as the LLM model itself.

Supporting custom transcription providers would make Warp Voice Input more flexible for:

- Power users who already pay for speech-to-text APIs
- Developers using local or self-hosted Whisper-compatible services
- Users with accents or multilingual workflows
- Enterprise teams with approved AI vendors
- Privacy-sensitive users who want control over where audio is processed
- Users who want to avoid Warp-side voice usage limits by paying their own provider directly

## Additional context

This is not a request for custom LLM inference, since Warp already supports BYOK/custom inference endpoints for that layer.

This request is specifically for the Voice Input transcription layer: converting recorded speech into text before it is inserted into the terminal, Agent input, or other Warp input fields.

## Importance

High. I want to use Warp primarily through voice, and provider control would make Voice Input much more practical for daily use.

title: Letter shortcuts (Cmd+C, Ctrl+C, ...) don't fire on non-Latin keyboard layouts
body:
## Problem

On a non-Latin keyboard layout (Russian, Greek, and others), Cmd+C / Ctrl+C and most
other letter shortcuts silently stop working. The physical C key reports its layout
character - "с" in Cyrillic - as the logical key, while the binding stores "c", so the
two never match. The only workaround today is to switch back to a Latin layout before
every shortcut, which is a constant interruption for anyone who types in two scripts.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Add a non-Latin layout (for example Russian) and switch to it.
2. Select some text in the terminal.
3. Press Cmd+C (macOS) or Ctrl+C (Windows/Linux).

Expected: the text is copied.
Actual: nothing happens - the shortcut does not fire, because the layout character does
not match the binding.

The same applies to most letter and digit shortcuts (paste, find, new tab, and so on).

## Proposed solution

Match shortcuts on the physical key when the user opts in, in two ways:

- a per-binding `Code(NAME)` form in keybindings.yaml, where NAME is a W3C UIEvents code
  (e.g. `editor:copy: cmd-Code(KeyC)`);
- a global "Smart layout-aware shortcuts" toggle that promotes single letter and digit
  bindings to physical-key matching.

Both default to off, so existing behavior is unchanged until opted in. Symbol shortcuts
(like Cmd+/) are left on logical matching, since symbols live on different physical keys
across layouts.

I have a working implementation ready in #11923.

### Describe the bug

  `StandardizedPath::strip_prefix` (`crates/warp_util/src/standardized_path.rs`) strips a raw **string** prefix instead of matching
  whole **path components**, so it disagrees with its own component-aware siblings `starts_with` / `ends_with`.
  
  Because of this, a base directory like `/repo` is treated as a prefix of the unrelated sibling path `/repository/foo.rs`, and the
  method returns a corrupted mid-component remainder `Some("sitory/foo.rs")` instead of `None`.
  
  This propagates into `LocalOrRemotePath::strip_repo_prefix`, whose doc comment promises it returns `None` "when `file` is not under
  this location": 
  
  - The **Local** arm uses the std component-aware `Path::strip_prefix`, so it correctly rejects sibling directories.
  - The **Remote** arm goes through the buggy `StandardizedPath::strip_prefix`, so for **remote / SSH sessions** a file living in a
  *sibling* directory whose name merely shares a string prefix with the repo root (e.g. `/repository/...` next to repo `/repo`) is
  mis-attributed to the repo and assigned a garbled repo-relative path. The same logical query returns different answers for local vs.
  remote files.
  
  Root cause was introduced in PR #10961 ("Migrate to use `LocalOrRemotePath`"), merged 2026-05-18.
  


### To reproduce

  To reproduce
  Deterministic, no UI needed - add to `crates/warp_util`:
  
  ```rust
  let base  = StandardizedPath::try_new("/repo").unwrap();
  let child = StandardizedPath::try_new("/repository/foo.rs").unwrap();
  
  assert_eq!(child.starts_with(&base), false);   // correct (component-aware)
  assert_eq!(child.strip_prefix(&base), None);   // FAILS: returns Some("sitory/foo.rs")

  End-to-end (strip_repo_prefix, Remote arm), repo /repo, file /repository/src/foo.rs, same host:

  repo.strip_repo_prefix(&file)  // returns Some("sitory/src/foo.rs"); should be None

  with it (/srv/repository/... next to repo /srv/repo). The file is wrongly associated with the repo and shown with an incorrect
  repo-relative path.

### Expected behavior

  **Expected behavior**
  ```markdown
  `strip_prefix` should match at the path-component level, exactly like `starts_with` and `ends_with`. `/repository/foo.rs` is **not**
  under `/repo`, so `strip_prefix` should return `None`, and `strip_repo_prefix` should return `None` for both local and remote files

title: Windows acrylic backdrop uses light tint with dark themes
body:
## Description

On Windows 11, when the acrylic backdrop (transparency/blur) effect is enabled in Warp, the blur uses an OS-default light gray underpaint. This creates a washed-out, frosted-white appearance that clashes with dark terminal themes.

Without acrylic enabled, transparency correctly blends the dark theme colors with the desktop behind the window. With acrylic enabled, the blur introduces its own light base color that looks wrong.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable dark theme in Warp
2. Enable the acrylic/transparency backdrop effect (Settings → Appearance → Window opacity)
3. Observe the light frosted tint behind the blur

## Expected Behavior

The acrylic blur should use a dark tint that matches the active dark theme, similar to how other Windows apps (Terminal, Firefox, etc.) handle acrylic in dark mode.

## Root Cause

Warp uses winit's `BackdropType::TransientWindow` (maps to `DWMSBT_TRANSIENTWINDOW`). This Windows 11 API does not expose a tint color parameter - it delegates to the OS default, which is a light underpaint.

## Suggested Fix

Use the `DWMWA_ACCENT_POLICY` API with `ACCENT_ENABLE_ACRYLICBLURBEHIND` and a dark `gradientColor` (e.g., `0xCC000000` in ABGR) instead of the modern backdrop type. This is the same approach used by Windows Terminal, Firefox, and Chrome for dark-mode acrylic.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)
- Warp for Windows (open-source build)
- Dark theme enabled

🤞 I have a PR ready with the fix: #11939

- [ ] I have technical issue and have included the logs (optional, but helps expedite the bug fix). [Log instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/troubleshooting-and-support/sending-us-feedback#gathering-warp-logs)

### Describe the bug

he wildcard glob matcher in `crates/fuzzy_match/src/lib.rs` matches the `?`
  wildcard (and literal characters) **per byte instead of per character**.

  `is_glob_match` delegates to `is_glob_match_recursive`, which operates on
  `&[u8]`. So `?` advances by one *byte* and a literal compares one *byte*,
  instead of a full Unicode scalar value (`char`). A single multi-byte
  character can therefore satisfy multiple pattern positions, yielding
  false-positive matches for any non-ASCII text that reaches the exact-glob
  fallback (e.g. fuzzy file search over paths containing accented Latin, CJK,
  or emoji characters).
  
  This contradicts the crate's own documented contract ("`?` matches exactly
  one character") and diverges from the sibling helper `is_glob_match_chars`,
  which already walks `char`s correctly.

### To reproduce

  Against the `fuzzy_match` crate's public API:
  
  ```rust
  use fuzzy_match::match_wildcard_pattern;

  // "é" is ONE character (two bytes). The pattern "??" requires TWO
  // characters, so this MUST return None.
  assert!(match_wildcard_pattern("é", "??").is_none());

  Actual: returns Some(FuzzyMatchResult { score: 1000, matched_indices: [0] }).
  The all-ASCII equivalent match_wildcard_pattern("a", "??") correctly
  returns None, which is why the defect is invisible for ASCII input - each
  ? consumes one byte of the two-byte é

### Expected behavior

  ```markdown
  `?` should match exactly one character, and literals should compare whole
  characters, regardless of UTF-8 byte width. `match_wildcard_pattern("é", "??")`
  should return `None`; `match_wildcard_pattern("é", "?")` should match.

### Describe the bug

### Title

Warp uses over 1 TB in `~/Library/Group Containers/2BBY89MBSN.dev.warp` in about 10 hours, even when idle

***

### Environment

- macOS: Tahoe 26.5
- Mac hardware: 4 TB internal SSD  
- Time Machine: external 6 TB disk, **manual** backups (recently switched from automatic to manual; one manual backup run this morning)  
- Warp version: v0.2026.05.27.15.44.stable_01

***

### Summary

Warp's group container `~/Library/Group Containers/2BBY89MBSN.dev.warp` is growing extremely fast and reaches **over 1 TB** within roughly **10 hours**, even when Warp is **idle and not used for any work**.  

This disk usage shows up under macOS as "System Data", and it grows so quickly that other apps start failing or crashing due to low disk space.

***

### Important clarification

On the day I collected these numbers, I **did not actively use Warp for any real work**:

- I launched Warp and left it open, but I had **no AI tokens/credits**, so I wasn't using any AI features or running heavy commands in it.  
- All my actual development work (builds, logs, Docker, etc.) was done in **other terminals/tools**, not in Warp.  
- Warp was essentially **idle in the background** for about 10 hours.  

Despite that, the folder `~/Library/Group Containers/2BBY89MBSN.dev.warp` still grew to around **1.2 TB**.  

So this looks like a **background leak or runaway process inside Warp itself**, not a result of me streaming huge logs or running long builds inside Warp.[1][2][3][4]

***

### Details and diagnostics

1. macOS Storage ("About This Mac" → Storage) showed **System Data** increasing very quickly.  
   Over about **10 hours**, System Data usage increased by around **1 TB**.[2][5]

2. I first checked Time Machine local snapshots to rule out snapshot-related issues:

   ```bash
   tmutil listlocalsnapshots /
   ```

   Output:

   ```bash
   Snapshots for disk /:
   com.apple.TimeMachine.2026-06-01-021727.local
   com.apple.TimeMachine.2026-06-01-123130.local
   ```

   - Only **two** local snapshots from today.  
   - No sign of a "local snapshot explosion", so Time Machine is **not** the main cause of the 1 TB growth.[6][7][8]

3. Next, I inspected disk usage inside `~/Library` and `~/Library/Caches`:

   ```bash
   cd ~/Library/Caches
   sudo du -h -d 1 | sort -h | tail -40
   ```

   ```bash
   cd ~/Library
   sudo du -h -d 2 | sort -h | tail -40
   ```

4. Relevant parts of the output (only the important lines):

   From `~/Library/Caches`:

   ```text
   25G    ./JetBrains
   12G    ./Yarn
   54G    .
   ```

   From `~/Library`:

   ```text
   85G    ./Containers/com.docker.docker
   31G    ./Application Support/JetBrains
   54G    ./Caches
   64G    ./Application Support/PremiumSoft CyberTech
   144G   ./Application Support
   1.2T   ./Group Containers
   1.2T   ./Group Containers/2BBY89MBSN.dev.warp
   1.6T   .
   ```

   Observations:

   - `~/Library/Group Containers` uses **1.2 TB** in total.  
   - That entire 1.2 TB is effectively in **`2BBY89MBSN.dev.warp`**, which I understand is used by Warp.  
   - Other tools (Docker, JetBrains, etc.) are large but in the **tens of GB** range, not enough to explain "+1 TB in ~10 hours".  

   So the TB-scale growth is clearly coming from Warp's group container folder and not from Time Machine, Docker, or IDE caches.[4][9][10]

5. While this was happening:

   - macOS Storage UI showed **System Data** increasing almost in real time.  
   - When free space got low, other apps started failing with "disk almost full" errors or crashing because they couldn't write to disk.[5][11][2]
   - After a reboot, some space slowly freed up, but `2BBY89MBSN.dev.warp` remained huge (TB-scale), so the situation can easily repeat.

***

### Approximate "steps to reproduce"

I don't yet have a strict minimal repro, but the pattern is:

1. Launch Warp and leave it **open/idle** for many hours.  
   - Do not run heavy logs or builds in Warp.  
   - In my case, I had **no AI tokens**, so I wasn't using AI features at all.  

2. Do normal development work using other terminals/tools (not Warp).  

3. Over ~10 hours, macOS System Data steadily increases, and:

   - `~/Library/Group Containers/2BBY89MBSN.dev.warp` grows to around **1.2 TB**.  
   - No significant increase in other big directories (Containers, Application Support, Caches, etc.) beyond their usual tens-of-GB usage.

This suggests some **background process in Warp** is continuously writing data into its group container even while Warp is idle and not actively used.[1][2][4]

***

### Expected behavior

- Warp should be able to store data under `~/Library/Group Containers/2BBY89MBSN.dev.warp`, but:

  - Disk usage should **not** grow into the TB range under normal or idle conditions.  
  - There should be clear **limits and retention policies** for logs, caches, and any other persisted data (e.g. session history, AI metadata, search index).  

- Even under heavy usage (long-running sessions, large logs, AI features), disk usage should remain within a **predictable upper bound** and not consume the majority of a multi-TB internal SSD.[3][10][4]

***

### Actual behavior

- With Warp simply **running in the background and mostly idle**,  
  - `~/Library/Group Containers/2BBY89MBSN.dev.warp` grows extremely fast and reaches about **1.2 TB** in ~10 hours.  
  - macOS counts this as System Data, which **fills the disk** enough to break other apps and workflows.

***

### Workaround

- Quit Warp completely.  
- Move or delete the folder:

  ```bash
  mv ~/Library/Group\ Containers/2BBY89MBSN.dev.warp ~/Warp-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
  # or delete it entirely if you're OK losing Warp data
  ```

- This immediately frees more than 1 TB of disk space.  
- However, this also resets Warp's local data (sessions/history/settings), so it's only a workaround, not a real fix.[9][4]

***

### Requests

1. Please investigate what is being stored under `~/Library/Group Containers/2BBY89MBSN.dev.warp` that can grow to **1+ TB** within hours, even while Warp is idle.

2. Identify which subfolders or file types are responsible for this growth:
   - session replay/history,

   - or something else.

3. Add or document:

4. If there are existing configuration options to:
   - limit how much data Warp stores on disk, or
