title: Double-click selection: CJK / full-width punctuation not treated as word boundary, selection over-extends
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have searched Warp bugs and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have searched Warp known issues page and my issue is not there
- [ ] I have an issue with AI and have included the debugging ID
- [ ] I have a technical issue and have included the logs

### Describe the bug

Double-clicking a word that is immediately followed (or preceded) by a CJK /
full-width punctuation character selects the punctuation too, instead of stopping
at it. For example, double-clicking `test` in `test，` selects `test，` (including
`，`, FULLWIDTH COMMA U+FF0C). The same text with an ASCII comma (`test,`) correctly
selects only `test`.

This looks like the same underlying cause as #10245 ("Path detection: CJK /
full-width punctuation not treated as word boundary"). That report was about
clickable file paths; double-click word selection appears to be a separate code
path, so it still shows the behavior.

### To reproduce

1. In Warp, run:
   ```sh
   printf 'test，next\ntest,next\n'
   ```
2. Double-click `test` on each line:
   - Line 1 (full-width `，` U+FF0C): the whole `test，next` gets selected - the comma
     fails to act as a word boundary (**wrong**)
   - Line 2 (ASCII `,`): only `test` is selected (correct)

Applies to CJK / full-width punctuation generally (`，。！？；：、「」『』（）《》` etc.),
none of which are currently treated as word boundaries.

### Expected behavior

Double-click should select only `test`, with full-width / CJK punctuation acting as a
word boundary the same way ASCII punctuation already does.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc2c69ee-4892-4324-a864-aad7ed5c7f76

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

macOS 26.3.1

### Shell Version

zsh 5.9

v0.2026.05.20.09.21.stable_03

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Recent working Warp date

_No response_

### Additional context

In case it helps (and happy to be corrected if I'm misreading the code): the
double-click path appears to reach `is_default_word_boundary` in
`crates/warpui_core/src/text/words.rs`, whose boundary set is ASCII punctuation
(plus `«` `»`) and whitespace - so non-ASCII punctuation like `，` (U+FF0C) isn't
treated as a boundary.

One thing that might be worth keeping in mind: ideally only non-ASCII *punctuation*
would become a boundary - CJK ideographs themselves should stay part of a word,
otherwise selecting CJK text like `你好世界` could break into single characters.

title: Add a Git Graph (commit DAG) panel with right-click git operations
body:
## Problem

Warp is a terminal, so users can run `git log --graph`, but ASCII graphs become unreadable with many branches and aren't interactive - you can't click a commit to inspect what it changed. The left tools panel has Project Explorer / Global Search / Warp Drive / Agent Conversations but no visual git entry point, so "looking at git history" - a high-frequency task - forces a context switch to the terminal or an external tool (tig, GitKraken, editor extensions). Common git actions (checkout, branch, merge, ...) likewise mean leaving for the terminal.

## Desired experience

A **Git Graph** tab in the left tools panel that:

- Renders the active repository's commit history as a colored DAG - branch lanes, nodes, merge/fork connectors, and HEAD / local-branch / remote-branch / tag badges - following the active pane's working directory.
- On selecting a commit, shows its details: message, author/committer, full hash, and changed-file list with insertion/deletion counts.
- Opens a **read-only diff** of a changed file in the main area when clicked.
- Supports branch filtering, pagination ("load more") for large histories, and a repository picker when a directory hosts multiple repos.
- Offers **right-click git operations** on commits / tags / branches - checkout, create/delete branch & tag, merge, rebase, reset, cherry-pick, revert, push/pull, archive - each behind an explicit prompt or confirmation, with a "working" overlay and inline error reporting.

Gating: the read-only browsing base and the write-operation layer sit behind separate feature flags (+ a `Settings → Git` visibility toggle), so the base can ship without the mutating layer.

## Notes

- Inspired by [vscode-git-graph](https://github.com/mhutchie/vscode-git-graph).
- Reuses Warp's existing code-review diff rendering for the file diff pane.
- Working implementation on a branch, contributed through the spec → code flow (`specs/GH12041/`).

title: Expose Agent token/credit usage programmatically (API/CLI/export) for per-task cost attribution
body:
<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary
Warp surfaces Agent token/credit usage interactively (the per-turn credit-count chip, the conversation usage footer, and Settings → Billing and usage), but there is no programmatic way to read or export it. Please expose per-turn / per-session / per-run token and credit usage through a stable surface (API, CLI, structured log, or export) so external tooling can capture it and attribute it to a unit of work.

## Problem
Teams building governed agentic workflows want the real cost of each unit of work (per task/ticket/branch) for capacity planning, budget reporting, and estimate-vs-actual calibration. Today that data exists only in Warp's UI:
- The credit-count chip / conversation usage footer shows per-turn credits, tool calls, context window, files changed - UI hover only.
- Settings → Billing and usage shows aggregate usage - UI only.
- BYOK exposes provider-side token usage, but it is not attributed to Warp sessions/tasks and is unavailable to non-BYOK users.

With no machine-readable surface, tooling cannot record actuals at completion time, and historical cost data cannot accrue for later analysis. Agent self-reporting is not a reliable substitute (models cannot accurately report their own token usage).

## Reproduction steps or desired workflow
Desired workflow:
1. An agent (local or cloud; interactive or `oz agent run`) completes work.
2. Tooling reads structured usage for that turn/session/run - at minimum input/output tokens (plus cache read/creation tokens where available), credits consumed, model used, and tool-call count - keyed by a stable conversation/session/run identifier.
3. Tooling attributes the usage to a unit of work and stores it for cost analysis.

Any one delivery mechanism would satisfy the need:
- A CLI/API to query usage for a conversation/session/run id (e.g., extend the `oz` CLI / Oz API to return per-run token + credit usage).
- A structured local event/log stream (OpenTelemetry-style metrics or a per-turn/run JSON usage record) that tooling can tail.
- An export of Billing-and-usage data at per-session granularity.

The existing `oz agent run` / Oz API surface and the AI debugging ID are natural anchor points for a stable per-run usage record.

## Artifacts
None attached.

## Warp version
Warp Preview channel on Windows; exact build unknown.

Windows.

title: [Windows] GPU driver auto-update at runtime → DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED (0x887A0005) → fatal wgpu panic instead of renderer recovery (AMD Radeon 780M, DX12)
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there
- [x] I have a technical issue and have included the logs

### Describe the bug

Warp was running in the foreground when AMD's updater auto-installed a new Radeon display driver (`amdkmdag.sys`; Adrenalin 26.5.2 -> 26.6.1, DX12 driver `32.0.31007.5012` -> `32.0.31019.2002`). About 29 seconds after the new driver registered, the DX12 device was reported lost (`DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED`, `0x887A0005`) and Warp **panicked and terminated** instead of recreating the renderer. The next launch required SQLite WAL recovery, confirming the prior session ended as a crash rather than a clean exit.

On Linux (#11003) the log at least shows `Recreating the renderer in an attempt to recover...`. On Windows/DX12 here it goes straight to `Handling wgpu errors as fatal by default` -> panic in `Surface::get_current_texture_view`, with no recovery attempt. A routine GPU driver update should not hard-crash the terminal.

### To reproduce

Environmental trigger (needs a live driver swap), but reliable when it happens:

1. Run Warp on Windows with the DX12 backend on an AMD iGPU.
2. While Warp is in the foreground, let AMD Adrenalin auto-update the display driver (or manually reinstall / roll the GPU driver) so the GPU device is removed and re-added.
3. Within seconds of the new driver registering, Warp panics and terminates. The next launch performs SQLite WAL recovery.

### Expected behavior

On a `Device lost` / `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED` event, Warp should recreate the wgpu device and surface and continue running (as it attempts on Linux in #11003), or at worst show a recoverable error -- not treat it as fatal and panic. A GPU driver update while the app is running is a routine, expected event on Windows.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

Warp log (UTC; trimmed to GPU-relevant lines):

```
2026-06-03T06:00:20Z [INFO]  window resized
2026-06-03T06:00:24Z [ERROR] Signal failed: The GPU device instance has been suspended.
                             Use GetDeviceRemovedReason to determine the appropriate action. (0x887A0005)
2026-06-03T06:00:24Z [WARN]  The current device is lost. Reason: Unknown. Message: Device is lost
2026-06-03T06:00:24Z [ERROR] Handling wgpu errors as fatal by default
2026-06-03T06:00:26Z [ERROR] thread 'main' panicked at 'wgpu error: Validation Error
Caused by:
  In Surface::get_current_texture_view
    Surface is not configured for presentation
': ...\\wgpu-29.0.1\\src\\backend\\wgpu_core.rs:3925
```

(`0x887A0005` appears localized in my OS; the text above is the official English wording of `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED`.)

Adapter in use: `Using Dx12 IntegratedGpu (AMD Radeon 780M Graphics) for rendering new window.`

Windows Event Log (System) -- the proven trigger, not just correlation:

```
08:59:21  SCM (7034): "AMD User Experience Program Data Uploader service terminated unexpectedly."
08:59:55  SCM (7045): "A service was installed... Service File Name:
          \\SystemRoot\\System32\\DriverStore\\FileRepository\\u0201164.inf_amd64_...\\amdkmdag.sys
          Service Type: kernel-mode driver"
09:00:24  (= 06:00:24 UTC) Warp: DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED -> panic
09:00:55  Kernel-PnP (225): GPU HD-Audio (HDAUDIO VEN_1002 = AMD) re-enumerated
```

Windows

Windows 11 (build 26100)

v0.2026.05.27.15.44.stable_01

No

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

title: Per-pane badge: an iTerm2-style background watermark to identify panes
body:
## Describe the solution you'd like?

Add a per-pane **badge** (borrowing iTerm2's term) - a short label rendered as **large, faded text in the pane's background**, so panes in a split are instantly distinguishable (e.g. `server`, `agent`, `logs`, `db`).

Key properties:

1. **Separate from the pane header title.** The badge is its own value and its own background element - not the small header label. (This is explicitly *not* the header-title rename in #10580.)
2. **Auto-populated by default** when enabled: from the running foreground command, else the working-directory name, else the shell. *(A deliberate enhancement over iTerm2, whose badge is manual-only.)*
3. **Character-limited.** Badge text is capped and truncated (with an ellipsis) so it stays legible as a background watermark - this applies to auto-generated values too.
4. **Optional manual override** per pane, which takes precedence over the auto value.
5. Controlled by **one global setting** (off by default) with a matching Command Palette entry; the badge persists across restarts.

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I'm always frustrated when I split a tab into multiple panes (dev server, coding agent, logs, DB shell) and can't tell them apart at a glance. Panes only show a small header title; there's no prominent, glanceable identifier, so in multi-pane / multi-agent workflows it's easy to act in the wrong pane. iTerm2 solves this with per-session badges, and Warp has no equivalent.

## Additional context

- Prior art: iTerm2 "badges" - large background text per session, manually configured.
- Distinct from #10580 (header *title* rename + color): a badge is a separate background element with its own value and character limit, and it auto-populates - not a header-title action.
- Adjacent: #9163, #11782 (titling / session-naming pain).
- Visual treatment (opacity, size, active vs. inactive pane, narrow-pane behavior, max length) would benefit from design mocks.

---

title: [Linux Wayland] zwp_text_input_v3.enable() never called - IME completely   non-functional
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there
- [x] I have an issue with AI and have included the debugging ID (Optional, but helps expedite the AI quality fix). [Debugging ID instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/agent/ai-faqs#gathering-ai-debugging-id)
- [x] I have technical issue and have included the logs (optional, but helps expedite the bug fix). [Log instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/troubleshooting-and-support/sending-us-feedback#gathering-warp-logs)

### Describe the bug

Environment:
  - OS: Debian GNU/Linux forky/sid
  - GNOME Shell 49.5 (Wayland)
  - IME: fcitx5 5.1.19 + rime (works in Ghostty, gtk3/4 apps)
  - Warp: v0.2026.06.03.09.49.stable_01
  - force_x11 = false (required for Wayland; default is true on non-WSL Linux)

  Summary:

  Warp correctly binds zwp_text_input_manager_v3 and creates a zwp_text_input_v3
  for the seat. Mutter sends enter(wl_surface) - but Warp never calls enable().
  Without enable(), the compositor doesn't know Warp wants IME, so it sends all
  keystrokes (including the IME toggle key Super+Space) as raw key events. Warp
  logs them as UnhandledModifierKey("cmd-space") and drops them. The IME never
  activates.

  Wayland protocol trace (WAYLAND_DEBUG=1):

   -> zwp_text_input_manager_v3#17.get_text_input(new id zwp_text_input_v3#21,
  wl_seat#10)
      zwp_text_input_v3#21.enter(wl_surface#34)
      // NOTE: enable() is NEVER called here
      zwp_text_input_v3#21.leave(wl_surface#34)
   -> zwp_text_input_v3#21.disable()
   -> zwp_text_input_v3#21.commit()

  Expected: enter → enable() + commit() → IME active. Actual: enter → silence →
  leave → disable().

  Warp log confirming IME toggle is intercepted (Super+Space to switch input
  method):

  18:16:21.437 EditorAction::UnhandledModifierKey("cmd-space")
  18:16:22.747 EditorAction::UnhandledModifierKey("cmd-space")

  Root cause analysis:

  Warp's winit fork (warpdotdev/winit@a4e0ecb) has an Enter handler at
  [text_input/mod.rs:57-73](https://github.com/warpdotdev/winit/blob/a4e0ecb5f9626ccac9445a73dc28354b52423abc/src/platform_impl/linux/wayland/seat/text_input/mod.rs#L57-L73):

  TextInputEvent::Enter { surface } => {
      let window_id = wayland::make_wid(&surface);
      let mut window = match windows.get(&window_id) {
          Some(window) => window.lock().unwrap(),
          None => return,                          // ← possible early return
      };
      if window.ime_allowed() {                     // ← returns false?
          text_input.enable();
          text_input.set_content_type_by_purpose(window.ime_purpose());
          text_input.commit();
          // push Ime::Enabled event
      }
      window.text_input_entered(text_input);        // ← always called
  }

  Warp calls window.set_ime_allowed(true) at window creation time
  (window.rs:1441), but at that point text_inputs is empty so the set_ime_allowed
  iteration is a no-op ([state.rs:513-527](https://github.com/warpdotdev/winit/blob/a4e0ecb5f9626ccac9445a73dc28354b52423abc/src/platform_impl/linux/wayland/window/state.rs#L513-L527)). Later when Enter fires, either:
  - windows.get(&window_id) returns None (surface/window ID mismatch), or
  - window.ime_allowed() returns false unexpectedly

  In either case, the result is that enable() is silently skipped and IME stays
  dead.

  Severity: All CJK and non-Latin input methods are completely non-functional on
  Linux Wayland. Users must use X11 (which has its own [IME regression ](https://github.com/warpdotdev/Warp/issues/11543)in recent
  winit fork) or switch to other terminals.

  Related: #11543 (X11 IME regression), #11822, #11992

1. open warp
2. switch input method

title: Active agent conversation lost after mid-session plan upgrade at credit exhaustion
body:
## Bug Description

A 16-hour active agent conversation (87 exchanges, 81.5M tokens, 5365 credits) disappeared from the Warp UI after upgrading my plan during the session. The conversation was never closed - I was actively committing code when I hit the credit limit, immediately purchased the max plan to avoid losing the session, and the conversation window vanished upon re-authentication.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a long agent conversation (this one was ~16 hours, 87 exchanges)
2. Hit the credit limit mid-session while actively working
3. Purchase a plan upgrade without closing the conversation
4. After the plan upgrade processes, the active conversation window disappears
5. The conversation is no longer accessible from the sidebar or via Ctrl-R → `a:` search

## Expected Behavior

The active conversation should persist through a plan upgrade. At minimum, it should be recoverable from the conversation panel after the upgrade completes.

## Actual Behavior

The conversation window disappears entirely. The conversation does not appear in the sidebar or search. The data IS still present in the local SQLite database (`ai_queries` table and `agent_conversations` table) but the UI has no reference to it.

## Evidence of Data Integrity

The conversation data was recovered manually by querying the local SQLite database:

```
sqlite3 "$HOME/Library/Group Containers/2BBY89MBSN.dev.warp/Library/Application Support/dev.warp.Warp-Stable/warp.sqlite"
```

- **Table:** `ai_queries` - all 87 user inputs present with timestamps
- **Table:** `agent_conversations` - metadata row present (1,785 bytes: usage stats, server_conversation_token, artifacts)
- **Conversation ID:** `4257be55-6ecc-46f6-84cc-27d2d8ef6454`
- **Server conversation token:** `81783d8a-b102-4e43-a50e-6b09821933bc`

The data exists both locally and (presumably) in the cloud via the server token, but the UI lost its handle on it.

## Impact

- 16 hours of work context lost from the UI
- $1,200 plan upgrade was the trigger that caused the loss
- Significant domain knowledge (compositing methodology, character refinement test results, pipeline architecture decisions) existed only in the conversation context
- Code changes survived (committed to git), but all discussion, reasoning, test findings, and methodology documentation had to be manually recovered from the SQLite database

## Session Details

- **Platform:** macOS (MacBook M2 Max 64GB)
- **Model:** Auto (Genius) → Claude Opus 4.6 (max)
- **Session duration:** ~16 hours (2026-06-05 14:02 → 2026-06-06 06:21 PST)
- **Tokens consumed:** 81,579,011 (Opus) + 2,809,233 (Haiku) + 52,810 (GPT-5 Nano)
- **Credits spent:** 5,365.39
- **Commands executed:** 155
- **Context window usage:** 48%

## Suggested Fix

Plan upgrades and re-authentication events should not disrupt active conversations. The conversation state should be preserved across account state changes, or at minimum, the conversation should be recoverable from the conversation panel after the transition completes.

JSON Schema Context: ◦ The schema defines pullRequestId as "type": "number" (not "integer") ◦ However, the Azure DevOps API expects an actual integer value 8650, not a float 8650.0 ◦ This is a common API design pattern where the schema uses "number" but the backend validates/rejects float representations 2. Impact Assessment: ◦ This affects any MCP tool where the schema uses "type": "number" but the backend API only accepts integer values ◦ Azure DevOps APIs are likely to have this issue, and other REST APIs may too ◦ Workaround: None currently available - users cannot force integer serialization 3. Specific MCP Tool Affected: ◦ MCP Server: ado (Azure DevOps MCP) ◦ Tool: repo_get_pull_request_by_id ◦ Parameter: pullRequestId ◦ API returns null when receiving 8650.0 instead of 8650 4. JSON Serialization Specifics: ◦ The issue occurs in Warp's tool invocation serialization layer ◦ Even when explicitly passing an integer (not a string), Warp converts it to float representation ◦ This happens before the parameter reaches the MCP layer 5. Reproduction Minimal Example: ``` Tool: repo_get_pull_request_by_id (azure-devops MCP) Input: {"pullRequestId": 8650, "repositoryId": "c41d4c16-cb9c-4cb3-9e39-df0e89f1fa45"} Expected MCP receives: {"pullRequestId": 8650, ...} Actually receives: {"pullRequestId": 8650.0, ...} Result: Azure DevOps API rejects the request and returns null ``` 6. Suggest a Fix: ◦ When serializing parameters, check if a number is a whole number (no decimal part) ◦ Serialize whole numbers as integers without .0 suffix ◦ Keep decimal numbers as floats ◦ Or: Add schema parsing to detect "type": "integer" and handle accordingly ### Does this block you from using Warp daily? title: Terminal pane does not refresh after closing split pane (regression v0.2026.06+)
body:
## Description

After closing a split pane (e.g., file editor pane), the terminal pane content does **not** automatically re-render to fill the newly available space. The terminal content remains visually cropped to the old split-pane size, leaving the bottom half blank or showing stale content.

This is a regression - version **v0.2026.05.06.15.42** works correctly.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Warp v0.2026.06.03.09.49.stable_01 (or newer)
2. Run a TUI application that relies on terminal dimensions (e.g., `htop`, `vim`, or any prompt_toolkit-based CLI like Hermes Agent)
3. Open a file in split pane (e.g., Cmd+P → select a file → it opens in a split pane)
4. Close the file pane (click X or use shortcut)
5. Observe: the terminal pane content stays cropped to the old smaller size

**Expected:** Terminal content should automatically re-render to fill the full pane after the split is closed.
**Actual:** Content remains visually cropped. Only manual triggers (Ctrl+L, resizing the Warp window, or changing terminal font size) force a re-render.

## Environment

- macOS (Intel Mac)
- Warp version: v0.2026.06.03.09.49.stable_01
- Working version: v0.2026.05.06.15.42

## Root Cause Analysis

It appears that Warp v0.2026.06+ no longer sends `SIGWINCH` (or equivalent terminal resize signal) to the child process when a split pane is closed. Additionally, the PTY window size (queried via `TIOCGWINSZ` ioctl / `shutil.get_terminal_size()`) remains unchanged throughout the split/unsplit cycle - the PTY stays at full-window size while only the visible viewport inside Warp changes.

TUI applications (like those built with prompt_toolkit, ncurses, etc.) rely on `SIGWINCH` to detect when they need to re-layout. Without this signal, they never know the visible area has changed.

In the working version (v0.2026.05.06), Warp presumably either:
- Updated the PTY size when a split changed the visible pane area, or
- Sent `SIGWINCH` or triggered a terminal refresh on pane close

## Workaround

Users must manually trigger a terminal refresh (Ctrl+L or resize the Warp window) after closing a split pane.

## Related

Possibly related to #12198 (Agent suggested prompts cut off when panes are split) which also involves split-pane rendering issues.

title: [Bug] Warp fails to open when GPU VRAM is nearly full - no software rendering fallback

## Problem

Warp terminal (OSS) crashes on launch when GPU VRAM is nearly exhausted (~97%+ usage). It tries to initialize a wgpu adapter, fails, and exits without falling back to software rendering.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Fill GPU VRAM to ~97%+ (in my case, running a local LLM via llama.cpp with )
2. Run `warp-terminal`
3. Warp exits immediately with no window

Same behavior with `WGPU_BACKEND=gl warp-terminal`.

## Expected Behavior

Warp should detect that GPU initialization failed and fall back to software rendering (or at least display a clear error message instead of silently exiting).

## Actual Behavior

- **Vulkan:** `Failed to create a logical device: Parent device is lost` → `Failed to open window: No usable wgpu adapter was found`
- **OpenGL:** `Can present: false` → `Failed to open window: No usable wgpu adapter was found`

- **OS:** Arch Linux (kernel 7.0.11)
- **GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (24 GB VRAM)
- **Driver:** NVIDIA 610.43.02
- **WGPU backends:** Vulkan, GL
- **Windowing:** X11
- **Warp version:** v0.2026.05.27.09.22.stable (OSS, AUR package `warp-terminal`)
- **VRAM at time of crash:** 23930 / 24576 MB (97.4%)

```

15:32:39.356 [INFO] Available wgpu adapters (in priority order):
15:32:39.356 [INFO] Other: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090/PCIe/SSE2

body:
## Summary

When viewing a `package.json` file in Warp, it would be great to have a **play button** (▶) next to each script defined under `"scripts"`, so you can run them directly from the file - just like JetBrains IDEs (WebStorm, IntelliJ IDEA, etc.) do.

## Current behavior

Opening `package.json` in Warp shows the file contents as plain text. To run a script, you have to manually type `npm run <script-name>` (or `yarn`, `pnpm`, etc.) in the terminal.

When Warp detects a `package.json` file is open or being viewed, it renders a small **▶ run** button inline next to each entry under `"scripts"`. Clicking it executes the script in the current terminal session using the appropriate package manager (detecting `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, etc. to pick the right runner).

## Why this matters

This is one of the most loved productivity features in JetBrains IDEs and significantly reduces context-switching. Since Warp already blends the editor and terminal experience, this feels like a natural fit and would make it a first-class tool for frontend/Node.js developers.

## Alternatives considered

- Using a separate npm scripts panel (VS Code style) - works, but inline is faster and more discoverable.
- Running scripts manually - current workaround, but adds friction.

## Additional context

- JetBrains reference: https://www.jetbrains.com/help/webstorm/npm-pnpm-and-yarn.html#ws_npm_run_scripts
- Would also be useful for other script files: `Makefile`, `Justfile`, etc. (though `package.json` is the highest-impact starting point).

title: Voice input: non-429 HTTP errors (e.g. 403 fair-use limit) are collapsed into TranscribeError::Transport and surface as a generic "Failed to transcribe voice input" toast
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there
- [ ] I have an issue with AI and have included the debugging ID (Optional, but helps expedite the AI quality fix). [Debugging ID instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/agent/ai-faqs#gathering-ai-debugging-id)
- [x] I have technical issue and have included the logs (optional, but helps expedite the bug fix). [Log instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/troubleshooting-and-support/sending-us-feedback#gathering-warp-logs)

### Describe the bug

When the transcription backend rejects a request with any HTTP status other than 429 - in my case **403 Forbidden**, presumably the documented [fair-use/anti-abuse limit](https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/agent/voice) - the client discards the status code, logs the failure as a *transport* error, and shows the generic toast **"Failed to transcribe voice input"**. The user gets no hint of the actual cause (temporary limit vs. mic problem vs. provider outage vs. account restriction), and even the log entry is misleading.

What happened to me: after a few hours of heavy (but legitimate) dictation into a CLI agent session, every dictation attempt suddenly started failing with the generic toast. Only `warp.log` revealed the cause - each attempt logged:

```
2026-06-09T18:28:38Z [WARN] Non-success status code received: 403 Forbidden
2026-06-09T18:28:38Z [ERROR] Failed to transcribe CLI voice input: Transport
```

(13 occurrences over ~1 hour, one per attempt; it then recovered on its own, consistent with a temporary fair-use limit.)

#### Root cause (master @ e367c9d)

1. **The status code is discarded in `transcribe()`.** Only 429 is classified (with `X-Warp-Error-Code: OUT_OF_CREDITS` → `QuotaLimit`, otherwise → `ServerOverloaded`); every other non-2xx response falls into an `else` that logs the warning above and returns the unit variant `TranscribeError::Transport`:
   https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/blob/e367c9de8b9629600885e40b029c10c8915f9ec8/app/src/server/server_api.rs#L1268-L1281
2. **`Transport` is a misnomer here** - genuine network errors return the same variant a few lines below, so an application-level 403 and a real connectivity failure are indistinguishable downstream and in the logs.
3. **Both toast call sites only match `QuotaLimit` and `_`**, so everything else becomes the generic message:
   - CLI agent input: https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/blob/e367c9de8b9629600885e40b029c10c8915f9ec8/app/src/ai/blocklist/agent_view/agent_input_footer/mod.rs#L1887-L1895
   - Editor: https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/blob/e367c9de8b9629600885e40b029c10c8915f9ec8/app/src/editor/view/voice.rs#L498-L506
4. **User-facing messages already exist but are never shown**: `TranscribeError::ServerOverloaded` carries "Warp is currently overloaded. Please try again later." via `thiserror`, yet no call site has an arm for it - it always lands in `_`:
   https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/blob/e367c9de8b9629600885e40b029c10c8915f9ec8/app/src/server/server_api.rs#L346-L362

#### Why this matters (real triage cost)

The same generic toast currently covers at least four very different root causes, each needing a different user action:

- **Fair-use limit (this report)**: 403, recovers on its own - the user should just wait.
- **Provider outage**: in #8960, staff confirmed a Wispr Flow outage as the cause of a wave of reports.
- **Account/plan restriction**: also in #8960, a reporter iterated with staff for weeks (mics, versions...) until logs revealed his account was locked out of AI features; in #6646 a commenter's failures turned out to be an anti-bot ban on signup.
- **Local mic problems**: the legitimately-generic case.

In both threads, staff could not reproduce and had to ask reporters for log files. Differentiated messages would have avoided most of that back-and-forth.

Related (not duplicates): #8960 ("voice doesn't work" - this issue asks that *when* it fails, the error says why), #12336 (spurious voice error toast, the inverse failure mode), #11839 (notes Voice is subject to the provider's usage limits).

### To reproduce

1. Use voice input heavily (long dictations into a CLI agent session) until the backend starts returning 403.
2. Dictate anything.
3. Observe the generic "Failed to transcribe voice input" toast; the 403 only appears in `warp.log`.

Version: v0.2026.06.03.09.49.stable_01 (latest stable at time of writing)
OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (kernel 6.5.0-1023-oem)

### Expected behavior

Map the failure cause to an actionable message, e.g.:

- 403 / fair-use or rate limit → "Voice input limit reached - try again in a while" (the 429 path already shows exactly this, but the fair-use 403 never reaches it)
- Provider outage / 5xx → "Voice service temporarily unavailable"
- Account/plan restriction → point the user at their plan/account
- At minimum, include the status code in the toast (e.g. "Failed to transcribe voice input (403)")

Suggested direction: add a status-preserving variant to `TranscribeError` (mirroring [`AIApiError::ErrorStatus(StatusCode, String)`](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/blob/e367c9de8b9629600885e40b029c10c8915f9ec8/app/src/server/server_api.rs#L175-L176), which the rest of the AI API already uses), classify 403 in `transcribe()` (and/or send `X-Warp-Error-Code` on fair-use 403s server-side), and extend the two match sites - wiring up the existing `ServerOverloaded` message along the way.

There is precedent for exactly this kind of improvement: #11248 ("Improved GitHub authentication error messages", merged, changelog 2026.05.27) and #12382 (maps a generic Transport error to a friendly message elsewhere in the app, recently merged).

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

Log excerpt above. Full logs available on request.

title: Crash: panic_bounds_check in RowIterator::next during grid rendering
body:
## Describe the bug

Warp crashed with a Rust `panic_bounds_check` in `RowIterator::next` during normal grid rendering. The terminal had been running for ~6.5 hours with no unusual activity - just standard terminal usage. No heavy output, no resize events that I'm aware of.

The crash was triggered during a normal paint frame: `warp_update_layer` → `build_scene` → `BlockGrid::draw` → `render_grid` → `GridHandler::row` → `RowIterator::next`, where the row iterator accessed an out-of-bounds index in the flat storage.

## To reproduce

I cannot reliably reproduce this. It happened once during a ~6.5 hour session with normal terminal usage (no heavy scrolling, no massive output). The crash occurred at 01:12 AM after Warp was launched at 18:38 PM the previous day.

## Expected behavior

Warp should not crash during normal usage.

## Environment

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **OS** | macOS 26.5.1 (25F80) |
| **Hardware** | Mac16,8 (MacBook Pro M4 Pro) |
| **Architecture** | ARM-64 (Native) |
| **Warp version** | v0.2026.06.03.09.49.02 (latest stable) |
| **Shell** | zsh |
| **Session uptime at crash** | ~6.5 hours |

## Crash report

Full crash log: https://gist.github.com/learnerLj/15e98a803108246f07f59f87c4b684a0

### Key stack frames

```

 6  stable                          std::panicking::panic_with_hook + 636
 7  stable                          std::panicking::panic_handler + 144
 ...
10  stable                          core::panicking::panic_fmt + 32
11  stable                          core::panicking::panic_bounds_check + 80  ← HERE
12  stable                          warp_terminal::model::grid::flat_storage::row_iterator::RowIterator::next + 3796
13  stable                          warp::terminal::model::grid::grid_handler::GridHandler::row + 68

- **Buffer management** issue in flat storage during long-running sessions

- This issue is specific to Warp (no equivalent crash in other terminals)

title: Synced inputs indicator is missing in the vertical tab layout sidebar
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have searched Warp bugs and there are no duplicates

### Describe the bug

When input synchronization is enabled (Edit → Synchronized Inputs, default keybinding Opt+Cmd+I), the classic horizontal tab bar marks every synced tab with a blue link icon. In the **vertical tab layout**, however, the sidebar gives no visual indication at all of which tabs have synced inputs enabled - there is no way to tell where your keystrokes will be broadcast without switching back to the horizontal tab bar.

This looks like an omission rather than a rendering bug. From reading the source:

- The horizontal tab bar queries the synced-input state when building each tab (`TabComponent::new`, `app/src/tab.rs:879-905`, via `SyncedInputState::should_sync_this_pane_group()`) and renders `Indicator::Synced` as `Icon::LinkHorizontal` tinted with `TAB_INDICATOR_SYNCED_COLOR` (`0x4A93FF`) in `render_indicator` (`app/src/tab.rs:1304-1308`).
- `app/src/workspace/view/vertical_tabs.rs` contains **zero references** to `SyncedInputState`. The only row-level indicators are the unread-activity accent dot (`render_title_indicator`) and badges, and the icon waterfall that picks each row's icon (`TerminalIconInputs`, `app/src/ui_components/agent_icon.rs:103`) does not take sync state as an input either.

So the sync state is simply never surfaced in the vertical tab layout.

### To reproduce

1. Enable the vertical tab layout (sidebar).
2. Open two or more tabs.
3. Toggle Edit → Synchronized Inputs → e.g. "Synchronize all panes in all tabs" (or the current-tab variant via Opt+Cmd+I).
4. Look at the sidebar: nothing marks the synced tabs.
5. Switch to the horizontal tab bar: the blue link icon appears on each synced tab as expected.

### Expected behavior

Tabs with synced inputs show the same (or an equivalent) synced-input indicator in the vertical tab layout sidebar, consistent with the horizontal tab bar - e.g. the blue `Icon::LinkHorizontal` on the row's title line.

Related: a commenter on #3437 also asked for a clearer indication of where input is broadcast; this issue covers the vertical-tab-layout half of that.

I'm happy to open a PR for this - the natural fix is to query `SyncedInputState::should_sync_this_pane_group()` in the sidebar's terminal row rendering (`render_terminal_row_content`, `app/src/workspace/view/vertical_tabs.rs:3995`) and append the same blue link indicator used by the horizontal tab bar.

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.05.27.15.44.stable_01

### Regression

No, this has existed since the vertical tab layout was introduced (the sidebar never read the synced-input state).

title: markdown_parser: long delimiter run (256+ `*`/`_`/`~`) overflows u8 counter, panicking/corrupting the parser
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there
- [ ] I have an issue with AI and have included the debugging ID (Optional, but helps expedite the AI quality fix). [Debugging ID instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/agent/ai-faqs#gathering-ai-debugging-id)
- [ ] I have technical issue and have included the logs (optional, but helps expedite the bug fix). [Log instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/troubleshooting-and-support/sending-us-feedback#gathering-warp-logs)

### Describe the bug

The inline Markdown parser in `crates/markdown_parser/src/markdown_parser.rs` counts a run of emphasis delimiters into a **`u8`** counter, so a run of **256 or more** identical delimiter characters (`*`, `_`, or `~`) overflows it.

`parse_delimiter_run` folds the run with `fold_many1(tag(kind.as_str()), || 0, |counter, _| counter + 1)`, and `counter` is inferred as `u8` because the result is stored in `InlineToken::Delimiter { count: u8 }` (`markdown_parser.rs:1653`, `:1677`). The 256th increment is `255 + 1`:

- **Debug builds** (which is how the crate's own tests run): panic - `attempt to add with overflow` at `markdown_parser.rs:1653`. `parse_markdown` / `parse_inline_markdown` panic instead of returning a value.
- **Release builds** (the workspace sets no `overflow-checks`): the `u8` wraps `256 → 0`, so the delimiter's `count` becomes `0` and the run is silently mis-rendered (the literal-text round-trip via `Delimiter::to_text` drops all the characters).

A second instance of the same class is at `markdown_parser.rs:1795`: `(self.original_count + other.original_count)` adds two `u8` run lengths and can also overflow when two large runs are paired.

`parse_markdown` / `parse_inline_markdown` are public entry points used to render arbitrary, possibly untrusted Markdown (agent/AI output, pasted content, table cells), so a long run of `*`, `_`, or `~` - easy to produce accidentally or maliciously - crashes or corrupts the parser.

### To reproduce

Against the `markdown_parser` crate's public API:

```rust
use markdown_parser::markdown_parser::parse_markdown;

// 255 delimiters: fine.
let _ = parse_markdown(&"*".repeat(255)).unwrap();

// 256 delimiters: panics in debug ("attempt to add with overflow"),
// wraps the count to 0 and silently mis-renders in release.
let _ = parse_markdown(&"*".repeat(256));
```

Observed in a debug build / `cargo test`:

```
thread '...' panicked at crates/markdown_parser/src/markdown_parser.rs:1653:59:
attempt to add with overflow
```

The same happens for `"_".repeat(256)` and `"~".repeat(256)`.

### Expected behavior

A long run of delimiter characters must not panic or corrupt output. Unmatched delimiters round-trip to literal text, so `parse_markdown(&"*".repeat(256))` should succeed and preserve all 256 `*` characters as plain text. The delimiter-run counter should be a width that cannot overflow for realistic input (e.g. `usize`).

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

_No response_

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

### Operating system and version

Mac OS 26.5

### Shell Version

zsh 5.9

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.05.27.15.44.stable_01

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Recent working Warp date

_No response_

### Additional context

Self-contained, crate-scoped bug in `crates/markdown_parser`. A proposed fix (widen the delimiter-run counter from `u8` to `usize`) with regression tests is in the accompanying PR.

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

title: warp_files: TextFileAccumulator::flush_range emits a reversed Range when the first in-range line exceeds the byte budget
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there
- [ ] I have an issue with AI and have included the debugging ID (Optional, but helps expedite the AI quality fix). [Debugging ID instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/agent/ai-faqs#gathering-ai-debugging-id)
- [ ] I have technical issue and have included the logs (optional, but helps expedite the bug fix). [Log instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/troubleshooting-and-support/sending-us-feedback#gathering-warp-logs)

### Describe the bug

`TextFileAccumulator::flush_range` in `crates/warp_files/src/text_file_reader.rs` can emit a **reversed `Range`** (`start > end`) for a truncated text-file segment.

The truncated line range is built as:

```rust
} else if self.truncated {
    Some(range.start..self.last_line)   // text_file_reader.rs:137
}
```

`self.last_line` is only assigned in `push_line` when a line is **successfully buffered** (it fit within the byte budget); it is initialized to `0` and reset to `0` at the end of every `flush_range`. If the **first line that falls inside the range already exceeds the remaining byte budget**, `push_line` sets `truncated = true` and returns *without* updating `last_line`. So `last_line` is still `0` and the emitted range becomes `range.start..0` - reversed.

This is reachable on the AI file-read path (`FileModel::read_text_file`). The byte budget is the *remaining* shared batch budget (`per_file_limit.min(batch_bytes_remaining)`), which shrinks as files are read; once it drops below the size of a file's first line, that file's segment gets a reversed `line_range`. Downstream, this `Range<usize>` produces an empty / nonsensical line span (`start > end`) surfaced to the model, and a reversed `Range` panics if it is ever used to slice.

### To reproduce

Using the accumulator directly (1-based line numbers; whole-file uses range `1..usize::MAX`):

```rust
// Whole-file read, budget smaller than the first line.
let mut acc = TextFileAccumulator::new("f.txt".into(), None, &[], 4);
acc.push_line("hello".into(), true); // 5 bytes > 4 → truncated, nothing buffered
acc.push_line("world".into(), true);
let (segments, _) = acc.finalize();

// Expected: a valid (empty) range, e.g. Some(1..1).
// Actual:   Some(1..0)  ← reversed (start > end).
assert_eq!(segments[0].line_range, Some(1..1));
```

The same happens for an explicit range whose first in-range line is too large (e.g. ranges `[2..6]`, budget `4`, first in-range line 5 bytes → `Some(2..0)`).

### Expected behavior

A truncated segment must never produce a reversed range. With no lines buffered, the range should be an empty `start..start` (e.g. `Some(1..1)` / `Some(2..2)`), consistent with the existing truncation contract in `whole_file_truncated_at_byte_limit` and `range_truncated_at_byte_limit`.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

_No response_

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

### Operating system and version

Mac OS 26.5

### Shell Version

zsh 5.9

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.05.27.15.44.stable_01

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Recent working Warp date

_No response_

### Additional context

Self-contained, crate-scoped bug in `crates/warp_files`. A proposed fix (clamp the truncated end to `range.start`) with regression tests is in the accompanying PR.

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No

title: Code review button & git diff chip show no lines changed when the repo contains a nested git worktree
body:
**Warp version:** v0.2026.06.03.09.49.04 (stable) - also reproduces on a current dev build
**OS:** macOS 26.3.1
**git:** 2.50.1 (Apple Git-155)

### Description

In a repo that contains a git worktree checked out *inside* the main checkout's working tree (e.g. `git worktree add ./my-feature -b my-feature`), the code review button (top right) and the git diff stats chip (bottom input bar) stop showing lines changed entirely - even though `git diff --shortstat HEAD` reports changes. Sibling worktrees of the same repo (checked out outside the main checkout) display lines changed correctly.

Confirmed live: removing the nested worktrees from the affected repo made the lines-changed counts reappear immediately; re-adding one makes them disappear again.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a repo with a commit and a tracked file:
   ```sh
   mkdir repro && cd repro && git init
   echo hello > file.txt && git add . && git commit -m init
   ```
2. Open this directory in Warp and modify the tracked file (`echo change >> file.txt`). The diff chip / code review button shows `+1` as expected.
3. Add a nested worktree inside the checkout:
   ```sh
   git worktree add ./nested -b nested
   ```
4. Touch the repo again (or wait for the refresh) - the diff chip and code review button no longer show any lines changed.
5. Remove the nested worktree (`git worktree remove ./nested`) - counts come back.

### Expected

Lines changed shown for the main checkout regardless of nested worktrees (the nested repo dir should be skipped, like git itself does).

### Actual

No lines changed shown anywhere (bottom chip and top-right code review button) for the main checkout.

### Likely root cause (from reading the code)

- `GitRepoStatusModel::load_metadata` → `diff_metadata_against_head` (`app/src/code_review/diff_state/local.rs`) runs `git status --untracked-files=all --porcelain=2 -z`. Git emits a nested worktree/repo as a single untracked *directory* entry (`? nested/`) and does not recurse into it.
- For every untracked entry, `num_lines_in_file_if_non_binary(repo_root.join(path)).await?` is called. `File::open` on a directory succeeds on macOS, but the first `read()` fails with `EISDIR` ("Is a directory").
- The `?` propagates the error out of `diff_metadata_against_head`, so the **entire** metadata computation fails; `GitRepoStatusModel` sets `metadata = None` ("metadata load failed") and the UI renders with no stats.

Suggested fix: skip directory entries (or tolerate per-file read errors with `unwrap_or(0)`) instead of failing the whole aggregation. The same pattern exists in `diff_metadata_against_base` (`local.rs`, the `?` at the untracked-file line-count call).

### Environment notes

- Affected repo: main checkout on `main` with nested worktrees; `git status --porcelain=v2` lists them as `? <worktree-dir>/` entries.
- `git diff --shortstat HEAD` in the same directory correctly reports changes (e.g. `1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)`).

## Summary

When a tab is renamed (via double-click or `WARP_DISABLE_AUTO_TITLE=true` with an OSC escape sequence), the agent running status is no longer reflected in the tab title. The tab title is locked to the custom name, so the dynamic agent state (working / blocked / completed / errored) that Warp normally surfaces in the title is suppressed.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a Warp tab and rename it (double-click the tab and enter a custom name, or set `WARP_DISABLE_AUTO_TITLE=true` + emit `\033]0;MyTitle\007` from your shell config).
2. Start an Oz agent task in that tab.
3. Observe the tab title - it shows only the custom name with no indication of agent state.

## Expected behavior

When a tab has a custom title, Warp should still surface the agent running status alongside it - for example:
- Append a status suffix: `MyProject - ⚙ running`
- Or show the status icon/badge on the tab while preserving the custom title text.

The tab status icon (working / blocked / completed / errored) and unread attention badge should continue to work regardless of whether the title is custom or auto-managed.

## Actual behavior

Tab status icon appears to update correctly (per docs), but the title text is fully locked. Users who rely on custom tab titles for project/directory context lose all title-based agent status visibility.

## Workaround

Remove the custom title and rely on Warp's auto-managed title, which does reflect agent state.

## Why this matters

Many users rename tabs to identify the project or working directory they are in (e.g. `frontend`, `api`, `infra`). Forcing a choice between a meaningful custom title and agent status visibility is a poor UX tradeoff, especially in multi-tab agent workflows.

title: Code Review diff flashes back to the loading skeleton on reload
body:
## Summary
Opening the Code Review / diff panel flashes the diff content back to the gray loading skeleton and then back to content (**"content → skeleton → content"**), most noticeable right after opening the panel.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Make some changes in a git repo.
2. Open the Code Review panel.
3. Observe: the diff renders, then briefly blinks to the skeleton placeholder before reappearing.

## Root cause
`render` gates the whole view on `all_editors_loaded()`. `invalidate_all` rebuilds every editor on each `DiffStateModelEvent::NewDiffsComputed`, resetting each `is_loaded` to `false`. On open, the metadata refresh (`should_reload_diffs = true`) emits a second, identical `NewDiffsComputed`, so the already-rendered diff blanks to the skeleton until the rebuilt editors reload. (Single-file updates already reuse editors in place, so only the full-reload path flashed.)

## Proposed fix
Reconcile and reuse existing per-file editors on full reload instead of tearing the whole view down, preserving their loaded state. Implemented in #12605.

## Environment
- Platform: macOS
- Area: code review / diff view

title: File viewer: no end-of-file feedback when content fits the window
body:
### Describe the solution you'd like?

In the file viewer (and markdown viewer), when a file fits entirely within the window there should be a default visual indicator that you've reached the end of the content - ideally by showing the existing scrollbar whenever content fills most of the viewport (e.g. ≥ ~75% of the window height), so it reads as "you're seeing everything." This should be default behavior, not an opt-in setting.

### Is your feature request related to a problem?

When a file fits exactly (or nearly) within the viewer window, there is no visual feedback that you've reached the end of the file. Scrolling is a silent no-op and no scrollbar is shown, so it's unclear whether there's more content below or the file has ended. When content overflows the viewport by even 1px, the scrollbar appears and behaves normally - the gap is only in the exact/near-fit case.

### Additional context

Alternatives worth considering: (a) rubber-band / elastic overscroll like native macOS (content bounces when scrolling past the edge), or (b) a static "end-of-file" indicator (subtle divider/gradient at the bottom of the content).

Related: #9808 (opposite concern - preventing overshoot in code diff).

---

**Operating system:** macOS
**Importance:** 2

title: `New File` action has no keyboard shortcut and isn't user-bindable
body:
# `New File` action has no keyboard shortcut and isn't user-bindable

<!--
Suggested labels for triage: enhancement, area:settings-keybindings, area:editor-notebooks
Repo: warpdotdev/warp
This is a feature request - per CONTRIBUTING.md it goes: file issue → maintainer applies readiness label → spec or code PR.
-->

## The problem

The **File → New File** menu item opens a blank, file-backed code editor - effectively a scratchpad you can type into and save to disk. It's genuinely useful for jotting things down with far more room than the agent's rich input affords.

But unlike its siblings, **New File can't be triggered from the keyboard at all** - it has no default shortcut *and* it's the only "New ..." item that doesn't appear in Settings → Keybindings, so you can't even assign one yourself:

| File menu item   | Default shortcut | Customizable in Settings? |
| ---------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------- |
| New Window       | ⌘N               | No                        |
| New Terminal Tab | ⌘T               | Yes                       |
| New Agent Tab    | -                | Yes                       |
| **New File**     | **-**            | **No**                    |

New Agent Tab shows the precedent: no default shortcut, but still user-bindable. New File is the only "New ..." action with neither - so the only way to open the scratchpad is mouse → menu, every time.

## Who experiences it

Anyone who uses New File as a quick scratchpad/notes buffer (more room than rich input, and savable to a file). 
Using the mouse on every invocation breaks an otherwise keyboard-driven workflow.

## Current behavior and why it falls short

- New File is wired as a fixed binding with no default keystroke (`CustomAction::NewFile => None` in `app/src/util/bindings.rs`), and it's registered only as a `FixedBinding` (`app/src/workspace/mod.rs`), so it never surfaces in the editable keybindings settings.
- Its siblings (New Window, New Terminal Tab) get default shortcuts via the same mechanism, so the gap looks like an oversight rather than an intentional exclusion.

## Desired behavior

Be able to open New File from the keyboard. **Preferred:** make it a **user-customizable keybinding** - show "New File" in Settings → Keybindings (unassigned by default) so each user can pick a combo that doesn't collide with their setup. A sensible built-in default would be a bonus but isn't required.

(Equally happy if the team prefers a fixed default shortcut instead - flagging the customizable route to avoid having to pick a default, but obviously not a requirement.)

## Constraints / notes

- ⌘N and ⌘T are already taken in the File menu; New File and New Agent Tab are the two without defaults, so any default needs an un-taken combo and cross-platform care (the codebase already has `cmd_or_ctrl_shift` / PTY-compliance helpers for this).
- Scope is small and self-contained: the action and its handler already exist; this is purely about exposing a trigger.
labels: enhancement; triaged; ready-to-implement; repro:high; area:editor-notebooks; area:settings-keybindings; warp:auto-triage-review

title: RTL text (Hebrew/Arabic) renders in reverse / incorrect visual order
body:
### Description

When output contains right-to-left script (Hebrew, Arabic), Warp renders the characters in the wrong visual order - the logical character order is shown left-to-right instead of being reordered for RTL display, so words appear reversed. This also corrupts mixed LTR/RTL lines (the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm doesn't appear to be applied to terminal output).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Print an RTL string to the terminal, e.g.:
   ```bash
   echo "שלום עולם"
   ```
   (Hebrew for "hello world")
2. Or with mixed content:
   ```bash
   echo "Permit מגרש 1234 approved"
   ```

### Expected behavior

RTL runs are reordered per the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (UAX #9) and displayed in correct reading order, the way Terminal.app, iTerm2, and most browsers handle it. Hebrew should read right-to-left.

### Actual behavior

Characters are displayed in logical (storage) order, so RTL words appear reversed. Mixed LTR/RTL lines are scrambled because no bidi reordering is applied.

### Environment

- Warp version: 0.2026.05.27.15.44.01
- OS: macOS 26.5 (Darwin 25.5.0)
- Architecture: Apple Silicon (arm64)
- Shell: zsh

### Impact

Any workflow that surfaces Hebrew/Arabic text (logs, API responses, file names, DB rows) is hard to read. I work with Israeli municipal data and Hebrew strings in tool output are unreadable, which forces transliteration as a workaround.

### Additional context

Happy to provide screenshots showing the reversed output if helpful.

title: Render command block output as Markdown (per-block toggle)
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

Add a per-block toggle to render a command block's output as Markdown instead of the raw terminal grid.

How it would work:
- A right-click context-menu entry on a block: "Render output as markdown" (and "Show raw output" to switch back).
- When enabled, the block's output is parsed as Markdown and rendered with proper formatting: headings, bullet/numbered lists, fenced code blocks, inline code, bold/italic, links, tables, etc.
- It's per-block and opt-in - default behavior is unchanged; existing blocks keep rendering as the normal terminal grid.
- Rendering respects the active Warp theme (monospace font, terminal text/background colors) so it stays visually consistent.

Why: CLI tools increasingly print Markdown to stdout. A common case is running an LLM in one-shot mode, e.g. `claude -p "summarize this error and suggest a fix"`. The model replies in Markdown, but in a normal block it shows up as raw source (`#`, `*`, backtick fences, `**bold**`), which is noisy and hard to read. Today only AI/Agent blocks render Markdown - there's no way to view Markdown output from plain commands rendered, even though Warp already has the rendering machinery internally.

This is a natural fit for Warp's architecture: it can reuse the Markdown rendering already used for AI responses (the `markdown_parser` crate + `FormattedTextElement`), and the existing variable-height rich-content layout system that AI blocks use (measure rendered height during layout, feed it back into the block-height SumTree so scrolling/positioning stays correct).

I've built a working prototype against the open-source repo - right-click a block → "Render output as markdown" re-renders the output cleanly and toggles back to raw. Block heights and scrolling stay correct because the Markdown height is fed back into the existing block-height system. Happy to open a PR if the team is interested.

title: Ctrl+Tab switcher previews ignore tab color-coding and bury the title behind the index
body:
### Pre-submit checks

- I searched the open issues and found no duplicate (closest is #6899, which is only about the subtitle path, not color/title).

### Describe the bug

Tabs can be **renamed** and **color-coded** in the tab bar/sidebar, and those customizations show up there. But the **Ctrl+Tab switcher** (the MRU palette shown when "Cycle most recent tabs/sessions" is bound to Ctrl+Tab) ignores the color entirely and de-emphasizes the title, so every entry looks nearly identical and is hard to scan quickly.

Two concrete problems with each switcher row:

1. **No color.** A tab's color-coding is never carried into the switcher, so colored tabs are visually indistinguishable from one another. The whole point of color-coding tabs is fast visual identification, which is exactly what a switcher should support.
2. **Title is buried.** Each row is rendered as `[Tab 3] my-title`. The leading `[Tab N]` index is read first; the (often custom) title - the thing you actually recognize - comes second.

### To reproduce

1. Settings → Keyboard → set Ctrl+Tab to "Cycle through most recently used tabs" (or sessions).
2. Open several tabs, rename a few, and assign each a different color in the tab bar.
3. Press and hold Ctrl, tap Tab to open the switcher.
4. Observe: rows are all the same color, and each row leads with `[Tab N]` rather than the title.

### Expected behavior

The switcher should reflect the same customizations as the tab bar:

- Each row shows a **color indicator** matching the tab's color-coding.
- The **title leads**, with the numeric index kept as a secondary disambiguation hint.

### Root cause (from reading the source)

- `TabNavigationData` (`app/src/session_management.rs`) - the per-row model for the switcher - has no `color` field, so color never reaches the renderer. (The title *is* already passed via `display_title()`, so custom names are present - just not shown first.)
- `Workspace::tab_navigation_data()` (`app/src/workspace/view.rs`) builds that struct but never reads `tab.color()`, even though `get_tab_color()` right below it shows the color is readily available.
- The row renderer `SearchItem::render_item` / `render_icon` (`app/src/search/command_palette/tabs/search_item.rs`) renders an untinted `Icon::Navigation` and formats the label as `format!("[Tab {}] {}", tab_index, title)`.

### Proposed fix

Small, self-contained change:

1. Add `color: Option<AnsiColorIdentifier>` to `TabNavigationData`.
2. Populate it from `tab.color()` in `tab_navigation_data()`.
3. In `render_icon`, tint the leading icon with the tab color (converted via the existing `AnsiColorIdentifier::to_ansi_color` + `ColorU` path, with contrast handled by the existing `render_search_item_icon`); fall back to the default fill when a tab has no color.
4. Reorder the label to lead with the title: `format!("{}  ·  Tab {}", title, tab_index)`.

I have a working patch for this (~19 lines across the 3 files) and am happy to open a PR once this is labeled `ready-to-implement`.

### Operating system

macOS (Darwin 25.5.0)

### Shell version

zsh 5.9

title: Warp hangs on startup after power loss while restoring a large session; second instance can't bind 127.0.0.1:9277 (Windows)
body:
<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary
On Windows, after an unclean shutdown (power loss) during a large multi-agent session, relaunching Warp produces a process that is alive and pumping the Windows message loop (so the OS reports it "responding") but is functionally frozen - the UI never progresses and agents never resume. A second Warp instance launched afterward cannot bind the single-instance local server port `127.0.0.1:9277` and runs as a second full instance alongside the stuck one.

## Problem
A hard power-off (brownout) during heavy multi-agent use repeatedly leaves Warp wedged on the next launch, causing lost work. The frozen instance pins ~8 GB RAM and holds the single-instance port, so re-opening Warp spawns a second full instance instead of focusing the existing window.

## Expected behavior
After an unclean shutdown, Warp should either recover the session and become fully interactive, or fail fast with an error. Re-launching should focus the existing instance rather than starting a second full instance, and the single-instance port should be reclaimed cleanly after an unclean exit.

## Actual behavior
- Relaunched instance is alive with `Responding = True` but ~0 CPU and stops emitting logs shortly after startup; UI is effectively frozen.
- A full user-mode dump shows all 123 threads parked idle: 78 in `ntdll!NtWaitForAlertByThreadId` (futex/parking-style waits), 31 in `NtWaitForSingleObject`, 8 message-pump threads in `win32u!NtUserMsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx`, 6 IOCP workers.
- No OS-level deadlock: `!locks` found 0 of 23 critical sections contended; 0 SRW/critical-section acquisition waits; 0 threads in synchronous file/socket I/O; no network-stack frames. Indicates a logical async-runtime stall (work never scheduled/woken), not a mutex deadlock or blocked syscall.
- `!analyze -v -hang` classifies it as `APPLICATION_HANG_cfffffff_win32u.dll!NtUserMsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx` (UI thread in the normal idle message wait).
- Two full `warp.exe` instances ran simultaneously (each with a `minidump-server` child); the second logged the 9277 bind failure.

Relevant `warp.log*` lines around the failed startup:
- `SQLite error 283 (A WAL mode database file was recovered): recovered 145 frames from WAL file ...\warp.sqlite-wal`
- `Failed to bind local HTTP server to 127.0.0.1:9277: Only one usage of each socket address ... (os error 10048)`
- `IPC server disconnected unexpectedly`
- `Received 'end_in_band_command_output' while not expecting to read in-band command output.`
- `Failed to read Grok tokens from secure storage: File I/O error`
- `GitRepoStatusModel: metadata load failed: Access is denied. (os error 5)`

Local state: `warp.sqlite` was 3.3 GB (`agent_tasks` ≈ 2.6 GB, `ai_queries` ≈ 467 MB, `blocks` ≈ 202 MB) with an 84 MB `-wal`. `PRAGMA quick_check` on a copy returned `ok` (no DB corruption). The frozen process held ~12 open connections to `warp.sqlite`.

## Reproduction steps or desired workflow
1. Use Warp on Windows with a large, long-running session involving multiple concurrent agents (DB grows large; here `agent_tasks` ≈ 2.6 GB, thousands of AI blocks).
2. While Warp is running, cause an unclean shutdown (power loss / forced power-off) so the app does not exit cleanly (WAL left dirty).
3. Power back on and launch Warp; on startup it performs SQLite WAL recovery.
4. Observe the relaunched instance hang: window is "responding" but never becomes interactive; agents do not resume; ~8 GB RAM pinned.
5. Open Warp again. A second full instance starts and logs `Failed to bind local HTTP server to 127.0.0.1:9277 (os error 10048)` because the stuck instance still owns the port.

Frequency: intermittent but recurring - after power loss and sometimes after ordinary reboots; appears correlated with large session/restore size.

## Artifacts
Captured locally (available on request; the memory dump is too large for a GitHub attachment):
- Full user-mode dump of the stuck process: `warp_38844.dmp` (~9.6 GB).
- cdb analysis log (thread stacks, `!analyze -v -hang`, `!locks`): `analysis.log` (~0.14 MB).
- Open-handle snapshot: `handles_38844.txt`.
- Consistent backup of `warp.sqlite` (+ `-wal`/`-shm`), `quick_check = ok`.
Log location: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\warp\Warp\data\logs\warp.log*`. (Analysis log and a validated recovery procedure will be added as a comment after recovery is confirmed.)

## Warp version
v0.2026.06.10.09.27.stable_01

## Operating system
Windows 11 Pro for Workstations, version 10.0.26200 (build 26200), 64-bit

### Describe the bug

On Windows, after an unclean shutdown (e.g., power loss) during a large, multi-agent session, relaunching Warp produces a process that is alive and pumping the Windows message loop (Task Manager shows Responding) but is functionally frozen - the UI never becomes interactive, agents never resume, the process pins ~8 GB RAM, and it cannot be closed cleanly (requires force-termination). Launching Warp again starts a second full instance that fails to bind the single-instance port 127.0.0.1:9277.

A full user-mode dump (cdb/WinDbg) shows all 123 threads parked idle - 78 in ntdll!NtWaitForAlertByThreadId, 31 in NtWaitForSingleObject, plus message-pump/IOCP threads - with no OS-level deadlock: !locks found 0 of 23 critical sections contended, no SRW/critical-section waits, no synchronous file/socket I/O, and no network-stack frames. !analyze -v -hang reports APPLICATION_HANG_..._win32u.dll!NtUserMsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx (UI thread in the normal idle message wait). This indicates a logical async-runtime stall (background work that never gets scheduled/woken), not a mutex deadlock or blocked syscall.

The pre-freeze log backtrace runs through onig_get_string_by_callout_args → git_index_checksum (Tree-sitter/Oniguruma + Git indexing), so this looks like the quiesced/stalled phase of the runaway Git-indexing/Tree-sitter executor in #8545 (same machine - #8545 was caught mid-runaway with unbounded memory/disk; this one caught after it stalled). The database is intact: PRAGMA quick_check on a copy of warp.sqlite returned ok.

### To reproduce

1. Use Warp on Windows with a large, long-running multi-agent session (the local DB grows large - here warp.sqlite ≈ 3.3 GB, agent_tasks ≈ 2.6 GB, thousands of AI blocks).
2. While Warp is running, trigger an unclean shutdown (power loss / forced power-off) so it does not exit cleanly (SQLite WAL left dirty).
3. Power back on and launch Warp. On startup it performs WAL recovery (SQLite error 283 ... recovered 145 frames from WAL).
4. The relaunched instance hangs: the window reports "Responding" but never becomes interactive, agents don't resume, ~8 GB RAM stays pinned, and it can't be closed cleanly.
5. Launch Warp again → a second instance starts and logs: Failed to bind local HTTP server to 127.0.0.1:9277 ... (os error 10048).

Frequency: intermittent but recurring - after power loss, and sometimes after ordinary reboots; correlates with large session/restore size.

### Expected behavior

After an unclean shutdown, Warp should either fully recover the session and become interactive, or fail fast with a clear error. Background workers (Git indexing / syntax parsing) should throttle or terminate and release memory, and Warp should exit cleanly even if they can't quiesce. Relaunching should focus the existing instance rather than starting a second one that can't bind 9277.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

Relevant warp.log* lines around the failed startup:
•  SQLite error 283 (A WAL mode database file was recovered): recovered 145 frames from WAL file ...\warp.sqlite-wal
•  Failed to bind local HTTP server to 127.0.0.1:9277: Only one usage of each socket address ... (os error 10048)
•  IPC server disconnected unexpectedly
•  Received 'end_in_band_command_output' while not expecting to read in-band command output.

Artifacts captured locally (available on request - the dump is too large to attach):
•  Full user-mode dump warp_38844.dmp (~9.6 GB)
•  cdb analysis.log (all 123 thread stacks, !analyze -v -hang, !locks)
•  Open-handle snapshot; verified warp.sqlite backup (quick_check = ok)

Full diagnostics (including the complete analysis.log) were also posted on the earlier report #12793. Log location: %LOCALAPPDATA%\warp\Warp\data\logs\warp.log*

Windows

10.0.26200

### Shell Version

PowerShell 7.5.5 (pwsh)

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.06.10.09.27.stable_01

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Recent working Warp date

_No response_

### Additional context

•  Same root cause as #8545 (bug, triaged, ready-to-implement) - this is the quiesced/stalled phase of that runaway Git-indexing/Tree-sitter executor, with a power-loss trigger and the dual-instance / port-9277 symptom.

title: Expose the Maximize/Minimize pane shortcut in the pane-header overflow menu
body:
### Problem

The **Maximize pane** / **Minimize pane** action (a single toggle, `pane_group:toggle_maximize_pane`) is already keyboard-bindable in **Settings → Keyboard shortcuts** and ships with a mac default of `cmd-shift-enter` (`⇧⌘↩`). That shortcut already shows next to the item in the terminal context menu, the env-vars pane menu, and the notebook context menu. However:

1. The **pane-header overflow (three-dot) menu** renders the "Maximize pane" / "Minimize pane" item with **no shortcut hint**, unlike the other menu, so a user who has bound a key gets no confirmation of it there.
2. The Settings entry is labeled "Toggle Maximize Active Pane", so searching "minimize" in Settings → Keyboard shortcuts surfaces nothing, hurting discoverability.

### Proposed change

- Surface the assigned shortcut next to the "Maximize pane" / "Minimize pane" item in the pane-header overflow menu, matching the existing pattern used elsewhere.
- Relabel the Settings entry to "Toggle Maximize / Minimize Active Pane" so it is searchable by both terms (bindings are saved by name, so this is backward-compatible).

This is a small discoverability improvement to an existing action - no new behavior. Closely related to #10580 (exposing other pane-header overflow actions).

### Notes

Implementation is ready in PR #12811.

title: Feature Request: Session navigation palette should match sessions by custom tab/pane name
body:
## User need

People who keep many sessions open rename their tabs/panes to meaningful labels (e.g. `deploy`, `meetings`, `frontend`) precisely so they can find them again. But the session navigation palette can't search by those names, so the names are decorative for navigation and you fall back to `Cmd+1/2/3` or scanning.

## Current behavior

The session navigation palette matches a session by its working directory, running/last command, and status only. The user-assigned tab name (rename-tab → `PaneGroup::custom_title`) and pane name (rename-pane → `PaneConfiguration::custom_vertical_tabs_title`) are **not** part of the searchable text, even though they're what the tab strip and vertical-tabs sidebar display. Typing a tab's name returns "No Results Found" when its directory/command don't also match.

## Desired behavior

1. Typing part of a session's custom **tab** name surfaces that session in the palette.
2. Typing part of a session's custom **pane** name surfaces that session.
3. The matched row shows the user-assigned name, so a result matched by name is recognizable next to its directory.
4. Sessions without a custom name behave exactly as today.

## Constraints / notes

- Both fuzzy and Tantivy full-text backends build their index from the same `searchable_session_string_and_ranges`, so a single source change covers both.
- Distinct from #9666, which is about the **sidebar** "Search tabs..." Panes-mode filter; this is the `Cmd+P` navigation palette.

I have a working implementation + test and will open a PR linking this issue.
labels: enhancement; triaged; repro:high; area:window-tabs-panes; area:search
