title: Feature/Bug: Custom LLM endpoints break on Ollama "thinking" models due to unexpected reasoning field
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there
- [x] I have an issue with AI and have included the debugging ID (Optional, but helps expedite the AI quality fix). [Debugging ID instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/agent/ai-faqs#gathering-ai-debugging-id)
- [x] I have technical issue and have included the logs (optional, but helps expedite the bug fix). [Log instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/troubleshooting-and-support/sending-us-feedback#gathering-warp-logs)

### Describe the bug

**Description**
When using a custom local endpoint in Warp to connect to Ollama (e.g., `http://localhost:11434/v1`), Warp breaks if the selected model is a "thinking/reasoning" model (like `gemma4:12b` or DeepSeek-r1).

The issue stems from a strictness mismatch between Ollama's OpenAI-compatibility endpoint and Warp's parser. Ollama injects a non-standard `reasoning` field directly into the `message` object of the response body. Warp appears to parse responses strictly against the official [[OpenAI Chat Completions API spec](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat/object)](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat/object) and fails to deserialize the payload when it encounters this unexpected key.

**Expected Behavior**
Warp should either gracefully ignore unexpected fields in the JSON response or provide a way for users to send specific request flags to custom endpoints to enforce strict compatibility.

**Actual Behavior**
Warp fails to parse the response from Ollama when the `reasoning` field is present.

*Example of Ollama's non-standard response:*

```json
{
  "choices": [{
    "index": 0,
    "message": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "Fideism is a philosophical position...",
      "reasoning": "Thinking process here..." // ← This breaks Warp
    },
    "finish_reason": "stop"
  }]
}

```

**Context & Investigation**
I initially opened an issue on the Ollama repository regarding this: [[ollama/ollama#16853](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/16853)](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/16853).

The Ollama team confirmed that this is isolated to "thinking" models. They also noted that they *do* have a built-in mechanism to suppress this non-standard field and enforce strict OpenAI compliance: if the client passes `"reasoning_effort": "none"` in the JSON request body, Ollama will omit the `reasoning` key entirely.

However, because Warp hardcodes the JSON payloads sent to custom endpoints, I have no way to inject `"reasoning_effort": "none"` into the request from Warp's UI to fix the compatibility.

**Proposed Solutions for Warp**
To fix this compatibility issue with local reasoning models, Warp could implement one of the following:

1. **Graceful parsing (Preferred):** Update Warp's JSON deserializer to gracefully ignore unknown/unexpected keys (like `reasoning`, `x_ollama_reasoning`, etc.) rather than failing.
2. **Custom Payload Configuration:** Allow users to define custom JSON key/value pairs to append to the request body when configuring a Custom LLM Endpoint in Warp.
3. **Automatic Fallback/Hardcode:** Automatically inject `"reasoning_effort": "none"` into requests sent to custom endpoints, or specifically those pointed at standard Ollama ports.

### To reproduce

1. Manually select a custom inference thinking model using exclusively an Ollama API endpoint.
2. Request a multi-step request that requires the model to perform changing actions in the terming safely in a given directory (e.g. Create a directory named `test`. Then create a python script in the `test` directory that prints ' Hello, world!' to the terminal.).
3. Monitor the 'Warping...' status for a failure mode notification to show something like: 'Failed:...' and subsequently defaults to a cloud model.
4. Manually change the agent to a cloud model, namely Sonnet or Opus to perform the following diagnostic steps

- Ask the Agent to test the custom inference endpoint to ensure it is working as expected per Warp custom inference configuration.
- Then ask the agent to check why local inference keeps failing with thinking models.

See my [issue](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/16853#issue-4712594313) posted on Ollama's Issues board where I show the feedback from having run the diagnostic steps.

### Expected behavior

One or all of the following:
- JSON deserializer should gracefully ignore unknown/unexpected keys (like `reasoning`, `x_ollama_reasoning`, etc.) rather than failing.
- Allow users to define custom JSON key/value pairs to append to the reqquest body when configuring a Custo LLM endpoint in Warp.
- Automatically inject `reasoning_effort": "none"` into requests sent to custom endpoints, or specifically those pointed at standard Ollama ports.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

[warp-logs-redacted.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29215940/warp-logs-redacted.zip)
---
Debugging ID: {"request_id":"46b1f4c5-ae36-4855-8fef-46dfeb7d08c5","conversation_id":"2a3caf7f-1f47-4c36-a322-0dfa3c68863a"}
---



```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║          DIAGNOSTIC REPORT: Ollama Thinking Models + Warp Compatibility      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

ENVIRONMENT
───────────
• Ollama endpoint: [REDACTED]/v1
• Test model: gemma4:31b (thinking/reasoning model)
• Ollama version: Latest (supports reasoning_effort parameter)

ISSUE CONFIRMED
───────────────
When Ollama serves a "thinking" model, it injects a non-standard "reasoning" 
field into the OpenAI-compatible response. This field:

1. Is NOT part of the OpenAI Chat Completions API spec
2. Contains the model's chain-of-thought reasoning
3. May contain special characters (newlines, markdown) that can cause 
   JSON parsing issues with strict deserializers

EVIDENCE
────────

Test 1: Request WITHOUT reasoning_effort parameter
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Request:
  POST /v1/chat/completions
  {"model": "gemma4:31b", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "2+2"}]}

Response (simplified):
  {
    "choices": [{
      "message": {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": "4",
        "reasoning": "The user is asking for the result..."  ← PROBLEM: Non-standard field
      }
    }]
  }

  ⚠ "reasoning" field present: True
  ⚠ reasoning length: 89 characters

Test 2: Request WITH reasoning_effort=none (Ollama's workaround)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Request:
  POST /v1/chat/completions
  {"model": "gemma4:31b", "messages": [...], "reasoning_effort": "none"}

Response (simplified):
  {
    "choices": [{
      "message": {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": "4"
      }
    }]
  }

  ✓ "reasoning" field present: False
  ✓ Response is OpenAI-spec compliant

CONCLUSION
──────────
The Ollama endpoint works correctly. The compatibility issue is:

1. Ollama injects "reasoning" field for thinking models (by design)
2. Warp's JSON parser rejects responses with unexpected fields
3. Ollama provides "reasoning_effort": "none" to suppress the field
4. Warp does not allow users to inject custom request parameters

RECOMMENDED FIX FOR WARP
────────────────────────
Option A (Best): Use lenient JSON parsing that ignores unknown fields
Option B: Allow users to configure custom request body parameters
Option C: Auto-inject "reasoning_effort": "none" for custom endpoints
```

### Describe the bug

On macOS, Warp's rich UI text rendering appears to misrender some shaped/symbol glyphs in rendered Markdown and context chips.

Observed examples:

- Rendered Markdown heading source: `# Daily Briefing Skill Implementation Plan`
- Actual rendered heading: `Daily Brieçng Skill Implementation Plan` (the `fi` in `Briefing` visually appears as `ç`)
- Git diff/status chip intended to show `1 • +4` visually shows the separator as `ǎ`, e.g. `1 ǎ +4`

This does not appear to be Markdown source-file corruption. The source file contains normal ASCII `f` + `i` bytes for `Briefing`, and does not contain `ç` or the Unicode `ﬁ` ligature character.

### To reproduce

1. On macOS, open a Markdown file in Warp's Markdown viewer / file notebook rendered mode.
2. Use this minimal Markdown content:

   ```md
   # Daily Briefing Skill Implementation Plan
   ```

3. Ensure the Markdown pane is in `Rendered`, not `Raw`, mode.
4. Observe the rendered heading.
5. Separately, in a repo with a git diff such as one changed file and additions, observe the diff/status context chip that should read like `1 • +4`.

### Expected behavior

- Rendered Markdown displays `Daily Briefing Skill Implementation Plan`.
- The diff/status chip displays `1 • +4` with a normal bullet separator.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

Screenshots are available from the local repro. The key visual symptoms are:

- `Briefing` appears as `Brieçng` in rendered Markdown.
- The git diff/status chip separator `•` appears as `ǎ`.

No Warp logs were attached because this appears to be a rendering/layout issue rather than a crash or shell integration failure.

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

### Operating system and version

macOS 26.5.1 (Build 25F80)

### Shell Version

zsh 5.9 (arm64-apple-darwin25.0)

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.06.17.09.49.stable_02 / CFBundleShortVersionString 0.2026.06.17.09.49.02

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Recent working Warp date

Unknown

### Additional context

I searched public Warp issues and Warp known-issues docs and did not find an obvious duplicate.

Investigation notes:

- Rendered Markdown/file notebook rich text styles use the UI font family, not the terminal font, in `app/src/notebooks/editor/mod.rs`.
- The default UI font on macOS is Warp's bundled Roboto family in `app/src/appearance.rs`.
- Header text is enlarged and assigned header weight in `crates/editor/src/render/model/mod.rs`.
- macOS rich text layout goes through CoreText in `crates/warpui/src/platform/mac/text_layout.rs`.
- The existing ligature setting is described as terminal-only in `app/src/terminal/ligature_settings.rs` and is applied to terminal rendering, not the rich UI/Markdown text path.

A small local CoreText probe using Warp's bundled Roboto fonts showed that CoreText shapes `Briefing` with a single `fi` ligature glyph by default, and setting `kCTLigatureAttributeName = 0` keeps `f` and `i` as separate glyphs. That suggests a likely mitigation for the Markdown heading symptom is to disable ligatures, or expose/respect a rich-text/UI ligature setting, when building the CoreText attributed string in the rich text layout path.

For the diff/status chip symptom, the source appears to intentionally render a bullet separator in `app/src/context_chips/display_chip.rs`, so that may be a related rich-text glyph shaping/fallback/rasterization issue rather than the same exact `fi` ligature issue.

No

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

title: Honor custom/OSC tab titles over cli_agent_title (or add a toggle to disable CLI-agent status in the tab)
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have searched Warp feature requests and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have searched Warp docs and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

When a CLI agent (e.g. Claude Code via the official `claude-code-warp` plugin) is running in a pane, its status **always** takes over the tab/pane title. I'd like a way to keep my own tab title - set via the agent's `/rename` or via an OSC escape (`\033]0;My Title\007`) - without it being overwritten by the agent status (e.g. `Wants to run AskUserQuestion`).

Any one of these would solve it:

1. **Honor an explicitly-set custom/OSC title over `cli_agent_title`.** If the user (or the running app) has set a custom tab title, prefer it, and surface the agent status as a badge/indicator rather than replacing the title text.
2. **A setting to disable CLI-agent status in the tab title** (e.g. `appearance.tabs.show_cli_agent_status_in_title = false`), independent of the agent notifications.
3. **Decouple the status indicator from the title text** - keep the status badge/dot, but leave the title as the conversation/custom title.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Tab/pane title resolution prioritizes `cli_agent_title` above everything else:

```
cli_agent_title  →  conversation_title  →  shell / OSC title
   (highest)                                  (lowest)
```

So when a CLI-agent plugin emits a `warp://cli-agent` status, Warp replaces the tab name with it. With the official Claude Code plugin, a `PermissionRequest` sends the summary `"Wants to run <tool>"`, which becomes the tab title. I use `/rename` to name each tab after its task; the chosen name shows fine until the agent needs attention, then the tab is renamed to the status and never reverts.

Things that do **not** solve it today:

- `WARP_DISABLE_AUTO_TITLE=true` - only gates the lowest-priority *shell* auto-title; `cli_agent_title` still overrides the custom/OSC title.
- `AgentTabTextPreference` (`ConversationTitle` / `LatestUserPrompt`) and `appearance.vertical_tabs.tab_item_mode` - neither falls back to a custom/OSC title nor disables the status text.
- Disabling the plugin works, but the tab status and the desktop notifications ride the **same** `warp://cli-agent` payload, so you lose the notifications too. There's no way to keep notifications but suppress the title takeover.

### Additional context

The agent status is genuinely useful as a *signal* (badge / dot / notification) - it just shouldn't clobber a title the user has deliberately set. Honoring an explicit custom/OSC title, or a simple toggle, would let users keep both the agent notifications and stable, self-named tabs.

**Operating system:** Cross-platform (app-level title-resolution behavior)

title: Update/restart button closes long-running terminal & CLI-agent (Claude Code) sessions without a warning modal
body:
> 🤖 Filed automatically by [@ozdotdev](https://x.com/ozdotdev) on behalf of [@advait_m](https://x.com/advait_m).
> Source: https://x.com/advait_m/status/2069964372118773854

## Summary
Clicking the in-app "Update now" / "Restart app and update now" button relaunches Warp and tears down running PTYs without first warning the user, even when long-running commands (e.g. Claude Code sessions) are active. Users have lost multiple active agent sessions across worktrees by clicking the update button. The other close paths (close tab, close window, quit app) already show a running-command confirmation, but the update/relaunch path does not.

## Reported behavior (from X thread)
- Clicking the update button accidentally closed ~10 Claude Code sessions running in 10 different worktrees, forcing the user to find and resume each session manually.
- A second user reports the same loss has happened repeatedly.
- Expectation: a warning modal should pop up when there are long-running commands running before the update relaunch proceeds.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Start one or more long-running commands / CLI-agent sessions (e.g. run `claude`) in Warp tabs/windows.
2. When an update is available, click the "Update now" / "Restart app and update now" banner button.
3. Warp relaunches and the running sessions/PTYs are terminated with no confirmation prompt.

## Likely root cause (code-grounded hypothesis)
The update banner button dispatches `WorkspaceAction::ApplyUpdate`, handled by `Workspace::apply_update` (`app/src/workspace/view.rs:18122`), which calls `autoupdate::initiate_relaunch_for_update` (`app/src/autoupdate/mod.rs:865`). That function requests a relaunch and immediately terminates the app, without going through the running-command confirmation that the other teardown paths use:
- close window: `UnsavedStateSummary::for_window` + `QuitWarningDialog` at `app/src/lib.rs:2402`
- close tabs: `UnsavedStateSummary::for_tabs` at `app/src/workspace/view.rs:11778`
- quit app: `UnsavedStateSummary::for_app` at `app/src/lib.rs:2468` (in `on_should_terminate_app`)

The shared warning machinery lives in `app/src/quit_warning/mod.rs` (`UnsavedStateSummary::should_display_warning` / `QuitWarningDialog`), and a running `claude` session is classified as `CommandContext::RunningCommand` via `TerminalView::session_command_context` (`app/src/terminal/view.rs:19081`) and counted by `RunningSessionSummary` (`app/src/session_management.rs:168`). The update/relaunch entry point does not call this check before relaunching, so the warning is not reliably surfaced for the update flow and long-running sessions are killed silently.

## Suggested fix direction
Make the update/relaunch path consistent with the existing teardown warnings: before calling `initiate_relaunch_for_update`, build an app-scoped `UnsavedStateSummary`, and if `should_display_warning` is true, show the `QuitWarningDialog` with confirm = proceed with the update relaunch and cancel = abort relaunch (`autoupdate::cancel_relaunch`). Ensure long-running CLI-agent sessions (Claude Code) are included in the count. Respect the existing `show_warning_before_quitting` setting and the "don't warn again" toggle.

## Related (not duplicates)
- #9416 requests keeping sessions alive across updates/relaunches (session persistence), which is a different, larger ask than adding a confirmation modal.

## Environment
- Reported on macOS (multiple worktrees, Claude Code sessions). Behavior should be fixed across platforms that support the in-app update relaunch.

### Describe the bug

Warp crashes (the whole app quits) when the terminal contains wide (full-width, cell-width 2) characters - e.g. a directory named in Korean (한글) shown in the shell prompt - and the terminal grid is resized (window/pane layout change, or prompt redraw while typing).

The crash is a Rust panic that aborts the process (SIGABRT / `abort() called`). From the macOS crash report, the panicking frame is:

```
warp::terminal::model::grid::resize::InitialCursorState::into_content_offset
  → core::result::unwrap_failed   (.expect("should have a content offset for point"))
```

Call chain:
`TerminalView::resize_internal` → `TerminalModel::resize` → `BlockList::resize` → `GridHandler::resize` → `resize_storage` → `InitialCursorState::into_content_offset` → **panic**

Root cause (preliminary): the cursor `point` computed against the live grid in `InitialCursorState::new` does not map to a valid content offset in `flat_storage` when the row contains wide characters; `content_offset_at_point(point)` returns `Err` (column exceeds content / wide-char spacer case) and the `.expect()` aborts instead of degrading gracefully. The `content_offset_at_point` doc comment itself lists `WIDE_CHAR_SPACER` / `LEADING_WIDE_CHAR_SPACER` cells as untested cases.

### To reproduce

1. Create a directory with a Korean name, e.g. `mkdir 한글폴더`
2. `cd 한글폴더` so the prompt shows the wide characters
3. Use the terminal / type a command / resize the window or split a pane (anything that triggers a grid resize)
4. Warp crashes and quits

(Only Korean was tested; any wide/CJK character is expected to trigger it.)

### Expected behavior

The terminal handles wide characters during resize without crashing; the cursor is placed at a reasonable position.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

`warp::terminal::model::grid::resize::InitialCursorState::into_content_offset + unwrap_failed`.

title: Link detection includes trailing fullwidth punctuation
body:
### Describe the bug

Warp link detection includes trailing fullwidth/CJK punctuation as part of clickable URLs and file paths.

This is common in CJK prose or AI/tool output where a sentence ends with a URL or file path followed by punctuation such as `，` or `。`. The punctuation should be treated as surrounding prose, not as part of the link target.

Examples:

```text
https://example.com，
/tmp/warp-repro.md，
```

Today the trailing punctuation can be included in the detected link/file path. The clickable range should stop before the punctuation.

### To reproduce

1. In Warp, output a URL followed by a fullwidth comma:
   ```sh
   printf 'https://example.com，\n'
   ```
2. Hover/click the detected URL.
3. Create a file and output its path followed by a fullwidth comma:
   ```sh
   touch /tmp/warp-repro.md
   printf '/tmp/warp-repro.md，\n'
   ```
4. Hover/click the detected file path.

### Expected behavior

- `https://example.com，` should detect `https://example.com` only.
- `/tmp/warp-repro.md，` should detect `/tmp/warp-repro.md` only.
- If a real filename actually ends in fullwidth punctuation, Warp should still be able to open that exact filename.

### Additional context

Related prior issues:
- #10245 handled CJK/full-width punctuation as path boundaries.
- #11477 handled trailing ASCII sentence period for file paths.

This issue covers trailing fullwidth/CJK punctuation, and applies to both URLs and file paths.

**Expected behavior**

If `GroupedTabs` is toggled off, existing tab-group data should be **preserved** (not deleted) so groups reappear when the feature is re-enabled. Ideally the feature shouldn't regress out of a preview that already had it.

### Describe the bug

## Summary

Warp crashes repeatedly (7 times in ~35 minutes) on Windows with exception code
0xc0000409 (STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN - the Windows code emitted by Rust's
panic-abort path). Every crash is at the identical fault offset, indicating a
deterministic, reproducible panic. The crashes began after Warp started logging
"File I/O error" when reading from Windows secure storage (Credential Manager)
on every startup.

## Problem

On every launch, Warp logs these errors before the UI is fully ready:

  [ERROR] Failed to read API keys from secure storage: File I/O error
  [ERROR] Failed to read Grok tokens from secure storage: File I/O error
  [WARN]  Failed to read MCP credentials from secure storage: File I/O error

Shortly after startup, warp.exe terminates abruptly. Windows Application Event
Log (Event ID 1000) records 7 identical crash entries over ~35 minutes.

Because Warp crashes without a clean shutdown, the SQLite WAL file is never
checkpointed. Every subsequent launch recovers frames from the WAL:

  [WARN] SQLite error 283: recovered 249 frames from WAL file
  [WARN] SQLite error 283: recovered 19 frames from WAL file

## Expected behavior

Warp should handle a "File I/O error" from Windows Credential Manager
gracefully - logging the failure and continuing without credentials - rather

title: Feature request: "Copy current path" command-palette action
body:
## Feature Request

Warp's built-in file viewer has a **"Copy file path"** option in its overflow and right-click menus (#8974, #13145), but there is no way to copy a path from the **command palette**, and no palette action to copy the current terminal session's working directory.

### Proposal

Add a **"Copy current path"** command-palette action that copies a path based on the currently focused pane:

- **File viewer focused** (rendered `FileNotebookView`) → copy the open file's path (works for local and remote/SSH files).
- **Terminal / block focused** → copy the current session's working directory (pwd).

This makes the action reachable by keyboard from anywhere - whether or not the file viewer is open - and extends the file-viewer "Copy file path" work (#8974 / #13145) to terminals.

### Why

Copying the current path is a common need: pasting it into a command, referencing it in a commit message, or sharing it with a teammate. Today you either right-click inside the file viewer or manually select the path from the header; there's no keyboard-driven, pane-aware way to do it.

title: Crash (panic) when pasting non-ASCII multi-byte Unicode (e.g. Telugu) into the editor input
body:
## Summary

Pasting or typing **multi-byte Unicode characters** (e.g. Telugu, Devanagari, CJK, emoji with variation selectors) into the Warp **editor input** (command line) causes an immediate crash (SIGABRT via Rust panic).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Warp (or a debug build)
2. In the editor input, paste any Telugu/Indic text - e.g. `క్ష`
3. Warp crashes immediately

## Root cause

In `app/src/editor/view/snapshot.rs`, `ViewSnapshot::layout_text_frames` builds `style_runs` using **char indices** instead of **byte offsets**:

```rust
// line ~518-524 in snapshot.rs
for (idx, stylized_char) in stylized_chars.into_iter().enumerate() {
    style_runs.push((
        idx..idx + 1,   // ← CHAR index, not byte offset
        StyleAndFont::new(family_id, properties, stylized_char.style()),
    ));
    line.push(stylized_char.char());
}
```

For ASCII, `char index == byte offset` (1 byte/char), so this works.
For multi-byte Unicode (Telugu `క` = 3 UTF-8 bytes), `idx=1` produces byte range `1..2` - which splits inside a multi-byte codepoint. `layout_text` (or the underlying Core Text binding) then tries to slice the UTF-8 string at a non-char boundary → **panic**.

## Fix

Track the running byte offset:

```rust
let mut byte_offset = 0usize;
for stylized_char in stylized_chars.into_iter() {
    let c = stylized_char.char();
    let char_len = c.len_utf8();
    style_runs.push((
        byte_offset..byte_offset + char_len,
        StyleAndFont::new(family_id, properties, stylized_char.style()),
    ));
    line.push(c);
    byte_offset += char_len;
}
```

## Crash trace

Crash type: `EXC_CRASH / SIGABRT` - Rust panic propagated from rayon worker via `resume_unwind`.

Faulting call chain (abbreviated):
```
rust_panic
  rayon_core::job::JobResult::into_return_value
    ViewSnapshot::layout_text_frames   ← rayon parallel closure panics here
      EditorElement::layout_text_frames
        warpui_core::presenter::LayoutContext::layout
          ... (full UI layout tree)
```

## Affected characters

Any Unicode codepoint > U+007F encoded in multi-byte UTF-8: Telugu, Devanagari, Kannada, Malayalam, Tamil, Bengali, CJK, Arabic, Hebrew, emoji, etc.

## Environment

- macOS 26.5.1 (25F80)
- Reproduced on debug build from source (commit post-open-source)

## Related

This is a separate issue from terminal *rendering* of Indic conjunct clusters (the grid renderer's `glyph_for_char` path). This crash is specifically in the **editor input** layout path.

title: Windows: repo watcher saturates the background thread pool re-indexing gitignored dirs (e.g. `target/`), starving other background work
body:
## Summary
On Windows, heavy churn in a large **gitignored** directory - e.g. a Rust `target/` during a `cargo build`, or while rust-analyzer is running - makes WarpDev's repository watcher repeatedly re-index that ignored subtree. Each re-walk is slow, blocking filesystem I/O, and the walks run directly on the background-executor's worker threads, so they **occupy the entire background thread pool**. While that happens, other background work is **starved**: most visibly, opening new terminal sessions bootstraps far more slowly because their startup tasks sit in the runtime's queue behind the walks. The pool stays saturated until the filesystem churn stops; restarting WarpDev clears it until the next build. Reproduced repeatedly and confirmed via process-dump symbolication.

> CPU caveat: in Task Manager this looks like only ~10-20% CPU, which *understates* the problem. The work is I/O-bound (threads spend most of their time blocked in filesystem syscalls), so a low CPU percentage hides the fact that every worker thread is tied up. The real symptom is pool saturation and starvation of other background tasks, not CPU burn.

## Environment
- OS: Windows (NTFS; Windows Defender real-time protection enabled)
- CPU: Intel Core Ultra 9 285H - 16 logical cores (so the background pool is 16 worker threads)
- Trigger context: a git repo indexed in Warp with an active `cargo build` and/or rust-analyzer writing into `target/`. In the original report, neovim (which starts rust-analyzer) and Warp sessions were both open in the same large Rust repo.

## Symptoms
- **New terminal sessions bootstrap much more slowly** while the churn is active - their background startup work is queued behind the subtree walks.
- More generally, anything scheduled on the shared background executor is delayed until a worker frees up; the pool does not drain until the churn stops.
- Sustained background disk I/O, and CPU sits around ~10-20% in Task Manager (low only because the work is I/O-bound - see caveat), never returning to idle.
- Closing neovim/rust-analyzer does not help while churn continues; it recurs on the next build. A restart returns things to idle until the next build.

## Root cause
The incremental repository-metadata watcher re-walked entire gitignored subtrees on every debounced filesystem event:

1. Git repos are registered with a single **recursive** OS watch plus a descend filter (`repo_watch_filter` / `should_watch_repo_directory` in `crates/repo_metadata/src/entry.rs`) that is meant to prune gitignored dirs like `target/`.
2. That descend filter is only honored by the **Linux/inotify** backend. On **macOS (FSEvents)** and **Windows (ReadDirectoryChangesW)** the OS does native recursive watching and ignores the per-directory descend predicate, so events for `target/**` are still delivered. (See the `cfg!(target_os = "linux")` branch and comment in `crates/repo_metadata/src/local_model.rs`.)
3. For each newly-created directory, `compute_file_tree_mutations` (`crates/repo_metadata/src/local_model.rs`) called `Entry::build_tree_with_standing_queries`. The gitignore check inside the builder (`evaluate_entry`) is **not ancestor-aware**, so a deep ignored path like `target/debug/.fingerprint` was not recognized as ignored and its entire subtree (tens of thousands of files) was walked - on every event.

## Dump analysis
We captured a process dump while WarpDev was busy and symbolicated it (PDB pulled from Sentry):
- The background-executor is a tokio runtime with **one worker thread per logical core** (`num_cpus`). On this 16-core machine that is 16 workers, and the dump showed **all 16** parked in `repo_metadata::entry::Entry::build_tree_with_force_included_paths_and_ancestor` - i.e. the **entire pool was saturated**, leaving no worker to service other background tasks. This is the direct cause of the slow session bootstrapping.
- Their leaf frames were synchronous Windows filesystem syscalls: `NtCreateFile`, `ZwQueryDirectoryFileEx`, `ZwClose`. Because the walks are synchronous, blocking I/O run directly on the async workers (not offloaded via `spawn_blocking`), a blocked worker cannot poll any other task - and the process still showed only ~10-20% CPU because those threads were mostly *waiting* on disk, not computing.
- The triggering call chain was `LocalRepoMetadataModel::handle_watcher_event` → `compute_file_tree_mutations` → `Entry::build_tree_with_standing_queries` → `Entry::build_tree_with_force_included_paths_and_ancestor`.
- A second dump captured while the app was **idle** showed all `background-executor` threads parked with **zero** `build_tree` frames, confirming the activity correlates with watcher work.
- Temporary diagnostic logging captured lines such as:
  `rebuilt subtree dir=...\target\debug\.fingerprint files=27245 elapsed_ms=53021`
  - ~53s of wall-clock for a single subtree walk (~27k files, mostly spent waiting on I/O), with walks queued back-to-back so the pool stayed continuously busy and the backlog grew.

## Why this is worse on Windows
The buggy logic is **not** Windows-specific - macOS receives the same `target/**` events and runs the same re-walks. The difference is **cost**, which is what turns wasted work into pool saturation:
- On **NTFS**, every open/enumerate traverses the I/O filter-driver stack, and **Windows Defender** intercepts file opens. A `target/` full of tiny files (`.fingerprint`, `deps`, `incremental`) is the worst case, so a single walk takes ~50-90s and ties up a worker that whole time.
- On **macOS/APFS** with a warm cache the same walk is ~1-3s and isn't AV-gated by default, so workers free up quickly and the pool never stays saturated (a brief blip you'd attribute to cargo/rust-analyzer).
- **Linux** is effectively immune: the inotify descend filter prevents watches on `target/` entirely (events never arrive unless the user explicitly expands the directory).

Note: the `target/` layout is identical across platforms and the gitignore-matching flaw is platform-independent. It is not the directory structure - it is the cost of walking it on NTFS+Defender, compounded by running rust-analyzer + Warp + live builds against the same large repo.

## Reproduction
1. Open a large Rust git repo in WarpDev on Windows (so it gets indexed/watched).
2. Keep Warp sessions in the repo; optionally run rust-analyzer (e.g. via neovim) in the same repo.
3. Trigger heavy `target/` churn, e.g. `cargo build` or `cargo clean && cargo build`.
4. Observe new sessions bootstrap slowly and background updates lag while the build runs, with elevated disk I/O, not returning to normal until the churn stops.

## Fix
PR #13151 makes the incremental watcher path represent newly-created gitignored directories as **unloaded placeholders** (matching the initial index's `IgnoredPathStrategy::IncludeLazy` behavior) instead of recursively walking them, using an ancestor-aware ignore check. Force-included paths (e.g. skill-provider directories) are still materialized. After the fix, a full `cargo build` churns thousands of `target/` paths with **zero** subtree rebuilds, so the worker pool stays free and other background work (including new-session bootstrapping) is no longer starved.

_Filed from a Warp Agent Mode investigation._

title: High GPU utilization on Linux (Intel Iris Xe / Wayland)
body:
## Disclosure

I used **Cursor** (AI-assisted IDE) with the **Opus 4.8 xhigh** model to help investigate this over ~**10 hours**. I am **not** a GPU/rendering expert - this write-up reflects my experience debugging a real-world laptop problem, not authoritative graphics architecture analysis. All measurements and conclusions below were validated with scripts and manual checks, but reviewers should treat numbers as **environment-specific** (see Measurement caveats).

## Why this matters (power & battery efficiency)

High GPU utilization on integrated graphics is not just a benchmark concern - it directly hurts **power efficiency and battery life** on laptops. When Warp keeps the GPU busy while I am only reading output (cursor blinking, no input), the machine runs hot and battery drains fast enough that I need **multiple recharges per day** as my primary terminal. Reducing unnecessary idle GPU work should help laptop users on Intel/integrated GPUs stay cooler and improve power efficiency.

## Problem summary

On **Linux (Wayland)**, **Intel Iris Xe** integrated graphics, **3840×2400** display, with **AI disabled** and terminal-only usage, Warp drives **sustained high GPU utilization** in two distinct situations:

1. **Idle (focused, cursor blinking)** - reading output, no typing or scrolling: **~12-16% GPU** continuously
2. **Active (typing / scrolling)** - full-viewport updates while working: **~50% GPU** on this display

This is **GPU utilization** (render engine busy %), **not** VRAM/memory usage (distinct from #2319).

### Impact on my machine

- GPU stays busy enough that the laptop runs **hot** ("melting into my lap")
- **Battery drains quickly** - I need **multiple recharges per day** with Warp as my primary terminal
- Unfocused or no Warp window: GPU drops to **~3%**
- Active workloads **feel responsive** on shipped stable release (release builds); debug dev builds stutter due to CPU starvation - a separate build-config artifact

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Arch Linux, GNOME, Wayland |
| GPU | Intel Iris Xe (i915) |
| Display | 3840×2400 |
| Stable channel | [`warp-terminal` (AUR)](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/warp-terminal) `v0.2026.06.24.09.19.stable_02` |
| Dev testing | `warp-oss` built from repo (release, Wayland) |

## Symptoms

### Idle (focused, no input)

1. Launch Warp, focus a terminal pane
2. Do **nothing** - no typing, no scrolling
3. Observe GPU in btop / Mission Center (render engine / i915 `rcs0`)
4. **Actual:** **~12-16%** sustained; drops to **~3%** when unfocused
5. With large scrollback scrolled into view, idle cost can **increase further** (full-window repaint on each cursor blink)

### Active (typing / scrolling)

1. Focus terminal, mash keys or scroll through output rapidly
2. **Actual:** **~50% GPU** on 3840×2400 integrated graphics
3. Feels smooth on [**AUR stable (release)**](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/warp-terminal); dev **debug** builds hang/stutter (CPU-bound, not comparable)

## Root causes (as understood)

### Idle - addressed by PR #13159

Editor **cursor blink** (500ms) calls `ctx.notify()` → full-window `build_scene` + full-viewport GPU rasterization + present every tick, even when nothing else changed.

### Active - open / follow-up

Full-viewport repaint every frame during genuine content change (typing, scroll). Cost is viewport-bound (~50% on this hardware) and does **not** appear to scale with total scrollback in release (block list already virtualizes). Further optimization (dirty regions, etc.) is **not** in the initial PR.

## Investigation notes

### Debug vs release builds matter

`cargo build` (**debug**) is CPU-starved under key-mash (~30-40% CPU vs ~4% [AUR stable](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/warp-terminal)), causing stutter that **does not reproduce** on release. **Always measure on release binaries.**

### What we ruled out (for idle fix)

- Redraw coalescing - already exists
- Scroll event coalescing - GPU build already capped at frame rate
- Scrollback culling at block level - already implemented (`ViewportIter`)
- Dirty-row paint for idle - blink partial repaint is the direct fix

## Measurement methodology

i915 PMU `*-busy` counters (btop-equivalent) via `script/gpu_idle_test/`. Same-commit **release** A/B: merge-base (base) vs branch (candidate).

See PR #13159 and `script/gpu_idle_test/README.md` for reproduction.

## Results

### Idle fix validation (PR #13159) - A/B comparison, not vs AUR stable

This table is a **before/after comparison of two release builds I compiled from the same git starting point** (the PR branch merge-base, commit `118c6a4e`):

| Build | What it is |
|-------|------------|
| **rel-base (control)** | Merge-base commit, **without** the blink partial-repaint fix |
| **rel-candidate (with fix)** | Same starting commit **plus** PR #13159's changes |

Only the fix differs - same machine, same Wayland setup, same `warp-oss` config. **Not** a comparison to the [AUR stable](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/warp-terminal) package (see below).

**Focused idle GPU (cursor blinking, no input):**

| How measured | rel-base (no fix) | rel-candidate (with fix) |
|---|---|---|
| Automated harness (i915 PMU, 25s sample) | ~12.4% avg | ~9.6% avg |
| Manual eyeball (Mission Center GPU graph) | ~6% | ~3% |

Idle dropped by about **3 percent** in manual testing (from 6% to 3%). Active typing/scrolling GPU unchanged (~52% harness avg).

### [AUR stable](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/warp-terminal) reference (not same-commit; config differs)

| | Idle GPU (approx) |
|---|---|
| AUR stable, logged in | ~11% |
| AUR stable, logged out | ~8% |
| rel-base (OSS, leaner config) | ~6% |

Do not compare absolute % across channels without matching config. The **attributable idle fix** is rel-base → rel-candidate on the same commit.

### Active (unchanged by PR #13159)

| | rel-base | rel-candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Harness ACTIVE avg | ~52% | ~53% |

## Tracking

| Symptom | Status | PR |
|---------|--------|-----|
| Idle GPU (cursor blink) | Fix proposed | #13159 |
| Active GPU (typing/scroll) | Open | - |

## Related

- GPU memory (different problem): #2319
- Possible related utilization reports: #7561, #6161, #10311 (not verified)

title: Collapsible named multi-pane tabs in the vertical tabs panel
body:
## Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AFEATURE) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

## Problem

In the vertical tabs panel with "Panes" display granularity, a tab with a custom name and multiple panes (splits) shows all individual pane rows at all times. When working with many split-pane tabs, the sidebar becomes long and hard to scan - there is no way to collapse a named tab's pane rows to reduce visual noise while keeping the tab accessible.

This differs from tab *group* collapsing (#9950), which folds a group of tabs. This is about collapsing the pane list within a single tab.

## Desired behavior

- **Collapse / expand** individual tabs in the vertical tabs panel when the tab has a custom name AND more than one visible pane.
  - A chevron toggle (▸ collapsed / ▾ expanded) appears in the hover action buttons belt, to the left of the existing kebab (⋯) and close (✕) buttons.
  - When collapsed, the tab shows its name header plus a horizontal icon row showing each pane's icon (with status indicators), grouped by type with same-type icons overlapping by 30%.
  - Clicking anywhere on a collapsed tab activates it (switches focus to the tab and its focused pane).
- **Collapsed state persists** across restarts via the existing tab snapshot / SQLite persistence layer.
- **Feature-flagged** behind `FeatureFlag::CollapsibleTabs` (dogfood-only initially).

## Scope

- Vertical tabs panel only, in "Panes" display granularity mode.
- Tabs without a custom name or with only one pane do not show the chevron.
- Tab group collapsing is unrelated and unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Horizontal tab bar changes.
- Keyboard shortcut for collapse/expand (can be added later).
- Collapsing tabs that are not named (no header to show when collapsed).

## Environment

- **OS:** Linux
- **Warp version:** built from master (commit 0b1e4ab4)

title: Feature Request: Option to exclude failed commands (non-zero exit code) from command history
body:
## Summary

Add a setting to prevent commands that exit with a non-zero exit code from being saved to Warp's command history.

## Problem

Warp currently records **every** executed command into its SQLite history database regardless of whether the command succeeded or failed. This means typos, mistyped commands, scripts that couldn't be found, and one-off failed attempts all accumulate in history and pollute `CTRL-R` search and `↑` navigation over time.

Since Warp already captures and stores `exit_code` per command in its database, it has all the data needed to filter these out - the feature just isn't exposed as a user option.

## Real-world examples

The following commands were found saved in a real Warp history database, all with 100% failure rate (never succeeded), cluttering search results:

| Command | Exit Code | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `claud` | 127 | Typo for `claude` |
| `agent` | 127 | Command not found |
| `github-cli` | 127 | Wrong name (should be `gh`) |
| `Z VERA/` | 127 | Capitalisation typo for `z` (zoxide) |
| `Run: npm -g uninstall @anthropic-ai/claude-code` | 127 | Pasted prose as a command by mistake |
| `python manage.py run` | 1 | Incomplete command (missing `server`) |
| `source ~/connect_claude_cli` | 127 | Wrong path, file doesn't exist |
| `/Users/gana/Downloads/aws-cli-login-python.py` | 126 | Script not executable |

All of these appeared in `CTRL-R` searches, mixed in with valid commands, making history much harder to navigate.

### Scale of the problem

Before manual cleanup, a real user's database contained:
- **1,181** total history entries
- **65** entries that had **never** succeeded (100% non-zero exit rate)
- **797** duplicate entries

The only current workaround is to manually query and delete rows from Warp's SQLite database - a process that requires knowing the database path, using `sqlite3`, and carries risk of corrupting the file.

## Proposed Solution

Add a toggle in **Settings → Features → History** (or equivalent):

> ☐ **Save failed commands to history**  
> When disabled, commands that exit with a non-zero exit code will not be saved to command history.

**Default:** enabled (preserve current behaviour, no breaking change).

### Optional enhancement

A more granular version could allow users to choose which exit codes to exclude, e.g.:
- Exit code **127** only (command not found - clear typos)
- Any non-zero exit code
- Specific exit codes (e.g. exclude 127 and 126 but keep 1)

## Why This Is Feasible

Warp's `commands` table already stores `exit_code` per row:

```sql
CREATE TABLE commands (
    id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    command TEXT NOT NULL,
    exit_code INTEGER,
    start_ts DATETIME,
    completed_ts DATETIME,
    pwd TEXT,
    shell TEXT,
    ...
);
```

The insert path already has the exit code available at the time of writing. This feature would simply require a conditional check before the insert, gated by a user preference.

## Impact

- Keeps `CTRL-R` and `↑` history clean and useful
- Eliminates noise from typos and mistyped commands
- No breaking change if opt-in (default: save all)
- Low implementation complexity - data is already available at write time

## Environment

- **OS:** macOS 15 (Sequoia)
- **Shell:** zsh 5.9
- **Warp version:** v0.2026.06.24.09.19.stable_03

## Related Issues

- #50 - Add the ability to delete a block (touches history deletion)
- #3570 - Command History UX issues

title: Feature request: option to warn/confirm before closing a window/tab with running processes
body:
### Current behavior

On macOS, pressing Cmd+W / Cmd+Q or clicking the tab/window close button immediately closes the Warp window without any confirmation. If there is a long-running task running in that window (e.g. a build, server, sync, remote session), it is killed with no chance to restore or reconnect.

### Expected behavior

Warp should offer a configurable confirmation when closing a window, tab, or pane that still has running processes, similar to iTerm2's " Warn before closing " preferences. Ideally it should be optional so users who prefer instant close can keep that behavior.

### Use case / impact

I usually work with 10+ Warp windows open. I frequently close a side-by-side Markdown preview window with Cmd+W or by clicking the tab close button, and accidentally close the CLI window instead. This kills the running process/session in that window, which is disruptive and sometimes costly (e.g. long-running builds, remote SSH sessions, server processes).

### Possible UX

1. Detect whether the current tab/pane has any running foreground or background processes (excluding the shell itself).
2. If so, prompt with a modal: "This window has a running process. Close anyway? / Keep open / Close all processes".
3. Add a checkbox: "Don't ask again for this session" or a setting under Preferences > Features > Windows/Tabs: "Warn before closing a tab with running processes".

### References / prior art

- iTerm2 Preferences → Profiles → Session → "Warn before closing" options.
- Terminal.app has a similar confirmation dialog for running processes.
- tmux solves this via persistent sessions, but that requires a different workflow.

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Window count: 10+ typical
- Trigger actions: Cmd+W, Cmd+Q, tab close button, red close button

title: Autonomous runs: slow commands self-cancel + retry loop (unresolved tool call)
body:
## Summary
In autonomous (cloud Oz / CLI) runs, a slow or network-bound shell command can end up reported as **cancelled** without the user cancelling it, and the agent then retries in a loop. This is a general issue for any slow/network command in an autonomous run; it was first surfaced via `/pr-comments` (see #13250, which hides that interactive-only skill from cloud agents as a targeted fix - but does not fix this underlying loop).

## Root cause (traced)
1. A slow command crosses the long-running threshold (`MAX_WAIT_DURATION`, 2s) in `app/src/ai/blocklist/action_model/execute/shell_command.rs` and becomes a long-running block. While it's running, the next requested command returns `RequestCommandOutputResult::CancelledBeforeExecution` (`shell_command.rs:234-242`).
2. `CancelledBeforeExecution` is converted to `ConvertToAPITypeError::Ignore` and **never sent to the server** (`crates/ai/src/agent/action_result/convert.rs:77-79`), so the tool call is left without a result.
3. On the next turn / resume, the result-less tool call is reconstructed/handled as a cancel:
   - client side: `create_cancelled_result_for_tool_call` → `CancelledBeforeExecution` (`app/src/ai/agent/api/convert_conversation.rs:1696-1699`), and/or
   - server side: `cancelledResultsForIncompleteToolCallsInLastResponse` / `collectCancelledResultsForIncompleteToolCalls` synthesize a Cancel result for any unresolved tool call so the LLM turn isn't corrupted (`warp-server/logic/ai/multi_agent/runtime/interceptors/input.go:638-751`).
4. The resumed agent sees "previous command was cancelled" and re-runs the command → cancel/retry loop.

The server-side synthesized Cancel is a correct safety net (`IsError()==false`); the real defect is the **client leaving an in-flight long-running command unresolved** in autonomous mode (dropping its result instead of returning a long-running snapshot or an error result).

## Suggested direction
In autonomous mode, surface an in-flight/long-running command as a still-running snapshot or an error result (so the tool call gets a real, paired result) rather than dropping it / letting it become a synthesized Cancel. Likely client-side in `shell_command.rs` + `convert.rs`, with the server reconciliation in `input.go` as context.

## Repro
Observed in a cloud Oz conversation invoking `/pr-comments` (slow `gh`/`fetch_github_review_comments.py` commands). Not reproducible in a plain local desktop build since it depends on autonomous (RemoteServerDaemon) execution + the server turn lifecycle.

_Filed by Oz (factory-client triage). Related PR: #13250._

title: macOS: Warp registers as the default app for Markdown (.md), overriding the user's chosen editor
body:
### Description

On macOS, Warp registers itself as the default application for Markdown (`.md`) files and reclaims that association after updates, overriding the user's chosen editor (e.g. VS Code). This is an OS-level Launch Services association - distinct from Warp's in-app "open file links" / Markdown viewer settings.

### Root cause

`script/update_plist` injects a `Markdown File` `CFBundleDocumentTypes` entry declaring Warp an **Editor** for the markdown UTIs (`net.daringfireball.markdown`, `com.unknown.md`, `net.ia.markdown`, `public.markdown`).

`.md` resolves to the UTI `net.daringfireball.markdown`. Most editors (e.g. VS Code) register markdown only by file **extension**, not by this UTI. macOS prefers a UTI-level handler over an extension-only one, so Warp wins the default-app resolution for `.md` **even at `LSHandlerRank Alternate`**, and re-wins on every auto-update's re-registration. Because it is an OS-level claim, disabling the in-app Markdown viewer (`prefer_markdown_viewer = false`) does not prevent it. (`com.unknown.md` also appears to be an invalid placeholder UTI.)

### Reproduction

1. Set VS Code as the default for `.md` (Finder → Get Info → Open With → VS Code → Change All).
2. Let Warp auto-update (or re-register its bundle).
3. `.md` reverts to opening in Warp. Confirm: `duti -d net.daringfireball.markdown` → `dev.warp.Warp-Stable`.

### Expected

A terminal should not take over the system default for Markdown files; the user's chosen editor should persist across updates.

### Suggested fix

Remove the `Markdown File` document type from `script/update_plist` (also dropping the invalid `com.unknown.md`). Leaves plain-text/source-code registrations untouched.

### Related
- #9076 - broader "stop hijacking file links"; the `.md` OS-level reclaim is reported in its comments.
- #5732 - closed "Why does Warp register itself for *.md files?".

### Environment
macOS 26.5; Warp v0.2026.06.24 (stable).

title: feat: auto-model selection - route to cheapest capable model based on task complexity
body:
## Summary

Warp's current `auto (open)` mode picks frontier open-weight models based on task complexity but the routing logic isn't exposed, configurable, or inspectable. There's no way to define explicit routing rules, set a budget cap, or tune the complexity thresholds that drive the selection.

## What's missing

| Gap | Impact |
|---|---|
| No complexity signal transparency | User can't tell *why* a request landed on a given model |
| No budget-aware routing | Can't say "never spend more than X credits/request" |
| No latency vs quality tradeoff presets | No "fast draft" vs "deep reasoning" mode that's separate from `auto` |
| No per-task-type overrides | Can't pin `coding` to a fast model while letting `reasoning` escalate |
| `auto` resets to default after session (#13136, #13137) | Even manual model choice isn't persisted |

## Proposed approach

Expose a routing config (in agent profile settings or `~/.warp/routing.json`) with the following levers:

```yaml
routing:
  budget_cap_credits_per_request: 10       # hard ceiling
  complexity_thresholds:
    simple:    [0, 30]    # route to cheapest capable model
    moderate:  [31, 65]   # mid-tier (e.g. Sonnet-class)
    complex:   [66, 100]  # top-tier (e.g. Opus/Gemini Ultra)
  task_type_overrides:
    coding: sonnet-class        # override for code tasks
    reasoning: opus-class       # override for deep reasoning
  presets:
    ship-fast:     { latency_weight: 0.7, quality_weight: 0.3 }
    quality-first: { latency_weight: 0.2, quality_weight: 0.8 }
```

**Complexity signals to expose** (can be shown in a tooltip or debug panel):
- Code complexity (AST-style heuristics on the prompt)
- Math / reasoning depth (formulas, multi-step logic)
- Context size (token count of conversation history)
- Tool-calling presence (agentic tasks floor at mid-tier)
- Domain specificity (narrow expert domains → escalate)

## Why this matters

Right now:
- Simple "what does this error mean" queries burn the same credits as a 500-line refactor
- There's no way to enforce a cost ceiling for batch/scripted use
- Power users can't tune routing to their workflow (latency-sensitive vs accuracy-sensitive)

## Prior art / inspiration

OmniRoute's auto-combo strategy ([source](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute)) uses 12 scoring factors (health, cost-inverse, latency-inverse, task fitness, stability, tier priority, tier affinity, specificity match, context affinity, quota, reset-window affinity, connection density) with per-mode-pack weight adjustments. The specificity detector fires on `codeComplexity`, `mathComplexity`, `reasoningDepth`, `contextSize`, `toolCalling`, and `domainSpecificity` signals - tool-using requests are floored at a "cheap" tier minimum to ensure function-calling reliability.

Warp could adopt a simplified version of this as first-class config, giving users full visibility and control over the routing decisions `auto` is already making.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `oz agent run` respects a `--routing-preset <fast|quality|balanced>` flag
- [ ] Routing decision is logged/visible per request (model chosen + reason)
- [ ] Budget cap config option (credits or USD) per agent profile
- [ ] Per-task-type model override in agent profile settings
- [ ] Model selection persists across sessions (#13136 / #13137 fix)

title: Workspaces in the vertical-tab drawer (Workspace → Group → Tab nesting)
body:
## Summary

Add named, color-coded **workspaces** to the vertical-tab drawer: a switcher
strip of pills (plus an always-present `ALL` view) that filters the tab list to
one workspace at a time, with a two-level hierarchy of **Workspace → Group →
Tab** so related terminal sessions stay organized under one project context.

## Problem

Power users keep many terminal tabs open across several projects. Today the
vertical-tab drawer is a single flat list; there's no first-class way to scope
it to "just this project's tabs." Tab *groups* help within a project, but there
is no higher-level container to switch between projects, and no way to hide the
tabs from other projects while working in one.

This is adjacent to #9382 (workspace-style tabs with multiple sessions) and
#9875 / #9950 (grouping vertical tabs by project + collapse/group background),
but approaches the need from the **drawer/organization** angle rather than an
in-tab session switcher: workspaces live in the left panel and filter which
tabs (and groups) are shown.

## Desired workflow

1. In the `ALL` view, create tabs and optionally group them (e.g. GROUP
   "avenger") - an ALL-level group.
2. Create a new WORKSPACE "dc" from the pill strip; inside it, create its own
   GROUP "dc" and a few tabs.
3. `ALL` shows every tab and both groups (a flat aggregate across all
   workspaces). Selecting WORKSPACE "dc" shows only GROUP "dc" and its tabs.
4. Switch workspaces via the horizontal pill strip (swipe/scroll when it
   overflows). Rename/recolor a workspace inline.
5. Move a tab or a whole group to another workspace via the right-click menu
   (moving a lone tab degroups it; moving a group relocates it with its members).
6. A tab inside a group inherits the group's color by default but can override
   it with its own color.
7. Everything persists across restart.

## Constraints / prior art

- Builds on the existing vertical-tabs drawer and tab-group model
  (`TabGroup`, `TabData`), extended with an `is_workspace` discriminator and a
  `workspace_id` back-reference; no new top-level data structures.
- Behind a feature flag (`FeatureFlag::GroupedTabs`, built with the
  `vertical_tabs` + `grouped_tabs` cargo features) so it's dark by default.
- Persistence adds three nullable columns (`tab_groups.is_workspace`,
  `tab_groups.workspace_id`, `tabs.workspace_id`) plus a
  `windows.active_tab_group_id` column for the active-pill restore.

## Note to maintainers

I have a complete, manually-tested implementation of this on a branch, with
unit tests and a screen recording, ready to open as a code PR once this issue
is triaged. Flagging for a readiness label (`ready-to-spec` if you'd like a
`specs/` doc first, or `ready-to-implement` if the design is acceptable as-is).
Happy to align the UX with #9382 / #9875 / #9950 if you'd prefer these
converge. @oss-maintainers

3. **Actual:** `new.log` appears normal (un-dimmed), right next to the dimmed `existing.log`.
4. **Expected:** `new.log` is dimmed, matching the initial index and `existing.log`.

### Root cause
The incremental watcher path (`compute_file_tree_mutations` → `LocalRepoMetadataModel::path_is_ignored` in `crates/repo_metadata/src/local_model.rs`) classifies newly-added paths using only the cached repo-root + global gitignores (`state.gitignores`). The initial index (`Entry::build_tree` → `evaluate_entry`) instead reads nested `.gitignore` files as it descends, so the two paths diverge. Files under a *root*-gitignored directory (e.g. `node_modules/`) are tagged correctly; the gap is specifically nested `.gitignore` files.

### Notes
Found during a Project Explorer bug bash (gitignore + lazy loading). This is one of two independent bugs from that bash. Bug-bash run: https://oz.staging.warp.dev/runs/019f200d-d5a2-7c0d-b7d7-1499a70f0f04

title: Project Explorer: file tree does not react to .gitignore edits
body:
### Summary
The Project Explorer (file tree) does not react to edits of `.gitignore`. Adding or removing ignore rules does not re-tag existing entries, and because the cached gitignore set is stale, newly-created files are also misclassified.

### Repro
1. Open a repo with an empty `.gitignore` and a normal `data.tmp`.
2. Run `echo '*.tmp' >> .gitignore`.
3. **Actual:** `data.tmp` stays normal (un-dimmed). `touch after.tmp` → `after.tmp` is also normal. `echo 'logs/' >> .gitignore` → the `logs/` folder stays expanded/normal rather than collapsing to a dimmed placeholder.
4. **Expected:** editing `.gitignore` re-tags the affected entries (matching a fresh index).

### Root cause
`state.gitignores` is captured once at index time (`gitignores_for_directory` in `index_directory`, `crates/repo_metadata/src/local_model.rs`) and is never reloaded when `.gitignore` changes. For contrast, code review's diff state (`app/src/code_review/diff_state/local.rs`) performs a full reload when `.gitignore` is modified; the file tree's `repo_metadata` model has no equivalent.

### Notes
Found during a Project Explorer bug bash (gitignore + lazy loading). This is the second of two independent bugs from that bash. Bug-bash run: https://oz.staging.warp.dev/runs/019f200d-d5a2-7c0d-b7d7-1499a70f0f04

title: macOS: Option-click on the green zoom button enters fullscreen instead of zooming the window
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there
- [ ] I have an issue with AI and have included the debugging ID (Optional, but helps expedite the AI quality fix). [Debugging ID instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/agent/ai-faqs#gathering-ai-debugging-id)
- [ ] I have technical issue and have included the logs (optional, but helps expedite the bug fix). [Log instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/troubleshooting-and-support/sending-us-feedback#gathering-warp-logs)

### Describe the bug

On macOS, Option-clicking the green traffic-light button is supposed to **zoom** the window (fill the visible screen area while staying a regular window, with the Dock and menu bar still visible) instead of entering native fullscreen. In Warp, Option-click behaves identically to a plain click: the window always enters native fullscreen. All other apps on the same machine honor Option-click correctly.

**Root cause (traced in the open-source repo):** this is a regression from #12557 (merged June 16, 2026, first shipped in builds cut after June 17). `WarpWindow`'s `sendEvent:` override now hit-tests left mouse-downs against the standard window buttons and, on a hit, delivers the event straight to the button via `[windowButton mouseDown:event]` (`crates/warpui/src/platform/mac/objc/window.m`). Delivering `mouseDown:` directly to the button bypasses AppKit's own event routing for window chrome, which is where the Option modifier is interpreted - so the zoom button always fires its default fullscreen action, even though the forwarded `NSEvent` still carries `NSEventModifierFlagOption`.

I verified this with a minimal standalone AppKit app containing four windows: a plain window styled like Warp's (transparent titlebar + full-size content view), one adding only the `sendEvent:` button-forwarding from #12557, one adding only Warp's host-view event swallowing, and one with both. Only the two windows with the `mouseDown:` forwarding exhibit the bug; the log confirms the forwarded event had the Option flag set and the window still entered fullscreen:

```
[A-control] >>> ZOOM (correct option-click behavior) <<<
[B-forward] forwarding mouseDown to button (option=524288)
[B-forward] >>> ENTERED NATIVE FULLSCREEN <<<
[C-swallow] >>> ZOOM (correct option-click behavior) <<<
[D-both] forwarding mouseDown to button (option=524288)
[D-both] >>> ENTERED NATIVE FULLSCREEN <<<
```

**Proposed fix (validated in the same harness):** keep the chrome hit-test from #12557 but use it only to latch event ownership (`_leftMouseDownStartedInNativeWindowChrome = YES`) and route the mouse-down through `[super sendEvent:event]`, exactly like the resize-edge path. AppKit then handles the button interaction natively - Option-click zooms, plain click enters fullscreen, close/minimize still work - and the latch keeps mouse-up/drag routed to AppKit on macOS 27 so the fix does not reintroduce #12389. Both the macOS 27-style routing (latched mouse-up to `super`) and the macOS ≤26 routing (mouse-up rerouted to the content view) were validated in the harness.

I have a fix ready and will link a PR to this issue.

### To reproduce

1. Open Warp on macOS as a regular (non-fullscreen) window.
2. Hold Option and click the green traffic-light button in the top-left corner.
3. The window enters native fullscreen (separate Space, Dock hidden).
4. Compare with any other app (Finder, Safari, iTerm2): Option-click on the green button resizes the window to fill the visible screen without entering fullscreen.

### Expected behavior

Option-clicking the green button should zoom the window (AppKit's `zoom:` behavior): the window fills the visible screen area but remains a normal window, with the Dock and menu bar still visible. A plain click should continue to enter native fullscreen.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

Harness log included above; the full standalone repro app source can be attached to the fix PR.

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

### Operating system and version

macOS 26.5 (25F71)

### Shell Version

zsh 5.9 (arm64-apple-darwin25.0)

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.06.24.09.19.stable_03

### Regression

Yes, this bug started recently or with an X Warp version

### Recent working Warp date

Builds prior to the merge of #12557 (June 16, 2026) route traffic-light clicks through AppKit and are unaffected.

### Additional context

The other half of Warp's chrome handling (host view swallowing `flagsChanged:`) was explicitly ruled out by the harness - it does not affect Option-click. Possibly related by symptom but distinct in mechanism: #8390 (the Window > Zoom menu shortcut being ignored).

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

title: File finder (⌘O): support recursive search outside git repositories
body:
## Summary
`⌘O`'s recursive "current directory **and subdirectories**" file search only works when the working directory is inside a detected **git repository**. Outside a git repo, `⌘O` falls back to a non-recursive listing of just the immediate directory (a plain `read_dir`), so users can't fuzzy-find files in subdirectories.

## Why it's git-only today
The recursive search is powered by Warp's repo-metadata index, which eagerly indexes a file tree per detected git root (`DetectedRepositories` / `RepoMetadataModel`). That index is what enables:
- fast fuzzy matching across the whole tree,
- `.gitignore`-based pruning,
- git-status-based ranking (changed files first),
- incremental freshness via repo-scoped file watchers.

Repo detection (`find_git_repo`) walks up from the pwd looking for a `.git` and stops at `$HOME`, so non-git directories never get an index and the recursive source returns nothing.

## Proposed direction
For non-git directories we likely don't want to eagerly index an unbounded tree (e.g. `~`, `/tmp`). Instead, do on-the-fly, `fzf`-style search: walk directories lazily as the user types, with sensible default ignores (dotfiles, common build/cache dirs) and depth/result caps to bound cost.

## Scope / notes
- Roughly a few days of eng work; needs a short spec (traversal strategy, default ignore set, perf/depth/result caps, ranking without git status).
- The non-recursive current-folder listing already works everywhere and can remain the zero-state.

## Context
Surfaced from user confusion about `⌘O` not showing subdirectory files when not inside a git repository.

title: Allow custom model names per connected provider (BYO / SuperGrok)
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

*(Note: #12832 covers the specific Composer case; this proposes a broader, provider-scoped mechanism.)*

### Describe the solution you'd like?

Add support for **custom model names on providers the user is already authenticated with**, separate from Warp's official server-provided model catalog.

**Example UX (Settings → Custom inference):**

When a provider is connected (BYOK API key or SuperGrok OAuth), show an option to add a **custom model**:

| Provider | Auth required | Example custom slug |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI | User's OpenAI API key | `gpt-6-preview` (hypothetical) |
| Anthropic / Google | User's API key | preview or account-specific slugs |
| SuperGrok / xAI OAuth | Connected subscription | `grok-composer-2.5-fast` |

Each entry would have:
- **Model slug** (sent to the provider)
- **Display name** (optional, for the picker)

Custom models would appear in the agent model picker under something like **"Custom · OpenAI"** / **"Custom · SuperGrok"**, with clear copy that they are **not part of Warp's official model catalog** and are **unsupported**.

**Important scope boundaries (non-goals for this request):**
- This is **not** a request to add specific models (e.g. Composer 2.5) to Warp's **official** xAI integration or partnership lineup.
- This is **not** a replacement for **custom endpoints** (different URL + key); it's for **extra slugs on an existing provider auth path**.
- Custom models should respect existing workspace BYO policy (same as custom endpoints / user-added keys).

**Implementation sketch (for discussion):**
- Client: inject synthetic picker entries (similar to today's `custom_llms` from custom endpoints) when user defines custom provider models.
- Request: route using existing provider auth (`openai` key, `grok_oauth_access_token`, etc.) with the user-supplied slug.
- Server: may need to accept/pass through user-declared slugs when provider auth is present (related to `warp:needs-server` on #12832).

**Precedent elsewhere:** Other tools expose this as manual/curated slugs on OAuth or BYOK (e.g. Hermes xAI OAuth extras, OpenCode provider config). Warp already supports arbitrary model names via **custom endpoints**; this closes the gap for **first-party provider auth without defining a full endpoint**.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Today, Warp's model picker is driven by the **server-provided** `feature_model_choice` catalog. That works for officially supported models (e.g. `grok-build-0.1` for SuperGrok), but users with valid provider access often have models that:

1. **Aren't listed** in Warp's catalog yet
2. **Are callable** with their existing auth (BYOK key or SuperGrok OAuth)
3. **Shouldn't require** setting up a separate custom endpoint (especially for OAuth, where pasting a token into a custom endpoint URL is brittle and undocumented)

Concrete example: #12832 - `grok-composer-2.5-fast` is available via SuperGrok/Grok Build OAuth but missing from Warp's picker. Maintainers noted it isn't on the public Grok API catalog Warp integrates against; I'm **not** asking to relitigate that - I'm asking for an **opt-in, user-declared custom slug** path so power users aren't blocked while waiting for official catalog updates.

Same pattern applies if a provider gives a user early access to a model slug Warp hasn't added yet - e.g. a stealth `gpt-6-*` preview on an OpenAI key.

**Workaround today:** Custom endpoints can approximate this for OpenAI-compatible APIs with URL + key, but that's heavy-handed and a poor fit for SuperGrok OAuth.

### Additional context

**Related issues**
- #12832 - Grok Composer 2.5 Fast missing (specific instance)
- #5867 - Integration of Grok models (broader Grok support)

**Maintainer context (from #12832):** Warp indicated Composer isn't available on the Grok API surface they support yet. This feature request explicitly accepts that and proposes a **user-initiated custom model** escape hatch instead of official catalog inclusion.

**Suggested disclaimer in UI:**
*"Custom models are not part of Warp's official catalog. Warp does not validate or support them. They may stop working without notice."*

**Open questions for maintainers**
1. Is client-only picker + payload acceptable, or is server allowlist/pass-through required before this can work end-to-end?
2. Preferred storage: settings UI vs file under `~/.warp/` (like custom model routers)?
3. Should custom provider models be disabled when team policy disables user BYO?

Happy to help refine scope or contribute a spec/PR if this direction is acceptable.

Cross-platform

4

title: OSC 22 mouse pointer shape support
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

Please support the pointer-shape escape sequence (OSC 22), which lets a TUI change the
mouse pointer (cursor) shape while it is over the terminal window:

```
    ESC ] 22 ; <shape-name> BEL        (or ST-terminated)
    ESC ] 22 ; ST                       - empty parameter: reset to default
    ESC ] 22 ; ><name> / <  ST          - push/pop shape stack (optional)
    ESC ] 22 ; ?name1,name2,... ST        - capability query, reply is a 0/1 bitmap (optional)
```

Shape names are the CSS `cursor` keyword vocabulary (`default`, `pointer`, `text`,
`ew-resize`, `grab`, `not-allowed`, ...). The protocol is specified by kitty:
https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/pointer-shapes/
Shape name reference (CSS cursor keywords): https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/cursor

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I am frustrated that my favorite terminal does not support such a useful UX functionality as Mouse pointer shape change!  Seems like a small improvement but it's so dope to see the full interactive TUI with mouse shape changes (e.g., in ghostty) - looks magical in contrast.

### Additional context

## Why this is valuable

Modern TUIs increasingly support full mouse interaction (SGR mouse tracking is
already widespread, including in Warp).  Without pointer shapes, a mouse-driven TUI
cannot communicate interactivity the way every GUI does:

- clickable rows/buttons/links → `pointer`
- draggable split/resize handles → `ew-resize` / `ns-resize`
- text inputs and selectable text → `text`
- drag state → `grab` / `grabbing`
- disabled targets → `not-allowed`

Adoption cost for applications is zero-risk by design: the spec requires unknown names and the whole sequence to be ignored gracefully, so applications can (and do) emit OSC 22 unconditionally. Terminals that add support light up existing applications with no application-side changes.

## What I tested and observed

We built an interactive probe (hover a grid cell → that shape is applied via raw
OSC 22, emitted with BOTH BEL and ST terminators; human records a per-shape verdict)
and ran it across terminals on macOS (2026-07):

| Terminal | Result |
|---|---|
| Ghostty 1.3.1 | **13 shapes render**: `default`, `pointer`, `text`, `vertical-text`, `crosshair`, `grab`, `grabbing`, `not-allowed`, `e-resize`, `w-resize`, `ew-resize`, `n-resize`, `ns-resize` (remaining names no-op - macOS NSCursor lacks e.g. `move` and diagonal-resize cursors, so this is an OS-cursor-set cap, not a protocol cap) |
| **Warp v0.2026.06** | **No effect for any of the 33 shape names; no reply to the `?` capability query** - sequences are consumed silently (good: no garbage), but no pointer ever changes |

Ghostty is the best observed behaviour so far and a good reference implementation:
it maps each OSC 22 name to the closest native OS cursor and silently ignores names
the OS cannot render. (kitty, the protocol's origin, also implements the full set
including the query form.)

## Suggested scope

Even a minimal first tier - `default`, `pointer`, `text` - covers the majority of real application use.  A second tier (`ew-resize`, `ns-resize`, `grab`, `grabbing`, `not-allowed`, `crosshair`) covers effectively all of it.  But full set support would push Warp to be effectively better than Ghostty 😉 

The push/pop stack and the `?` query form are optional but really nice extras, especially the capability query support would directly improve the UX.

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

### How important is this feature to you?

3

### Warp Internal (ignore) - linear-label:39cc6478-1249-4ee7-950b-c428edfeecd1

_No response_
