title: Windows: full process-table enumeration (with per-process CPU sampling) on every session bootstrap → DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION (0x133) on high-core-count / HVCI systems
body:
## Summary

On Windows, Warp enumerates the **entire system process table with per-process CPU cycle-time sampling** on **every terminal session bootstrap** (every tab, split pane, subshell, SSH/WSL session), with no cache and no throttle. It does this solely to check whether a process named `avp` (Kaspersky) is running.

Each per-process CPU sample makes the kernel issue `NtQueryInformationProcess(ProcessCycleTime)`, and the full-table enumeration issues `NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemProcessInformation)`. Both force the kernel to run **`KeFlushProcessWriteBuffers`**, which broadcasts a synchronous inter-processor interrupt (IPI) to **every logical core** and spin-waits for all of them. On a machine with many cores - especially with **Virtualization-Based Security / Memory Integrity (HVCI)** on, where every IPI/flush is mediated by the hypervisor - doing this across the whole process table, in bursts of session inits, keeps all cores spinning at `DISPATCH_LEVEL` long enough to trip the **DPC watchdog** and bugcheck the machine.

I root-caused this from a full kernel dump; the faulting thread was in `warp.exe`.

## Environment

- **Warp:** v0.2026.07.01.09.21.stable_01 (Windows, Stable). Reproduced across several recent auto-updated builds - not specific to one release.
- **OS:** Windows 11 24H2 (build 26100)
- **CPU:** AMD Ryzen 9 5900X - **12 cores / 24 logical processors**
- **GPU:** NVIDIA RTX 3090
- **Security:** Memory Integrity / HVCI **ON** (confirmed `SecureKernel.HalpHvciEnabled: 1` in the dump), VBS active.
- Trigger context: Warp kept open across long uptime, running an agentic CLI that spawns many short-lived child processes (heavy session/subshell churn).

## Kernel dump evidence

`BugCheck 133, {1, 1e00, ...}` - `DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION`, Arg1=1 (cumulative time at `DISPATCH_LEVEL`). `PROCESS_NAME: warp.exe`.

Faulting thread stack (Warp):

```
nt!KeBugCheckEx
nt!KeAccumulateTicks
nt!KiUpdateRunTime
nt!KeClockInterruptNotify
nt!KiIpiStallOnPacketTargetsPrcb        <- spinning on IPI to all cores
nt!KeFlushProcessWriteBuffers           <- all-core flush barrier
nt!ExpGetProcessInformation             <- SystemProcessInformation handler
nt!ExpQuerySystemInformation
nt!NtQuerySystemInformation             <- syscall issued by Warp
nt!KiSystemServiceCopyEnd               (user->kernel transition)
```

A second core was in the sibling path: `nt!KeFlushProcessWriteBuffers` ← `nt!PsQueryTotalCycleTimeProcess` ← `nt!NtQueryInformationProcess` (the per-process `ProcessCycleTime` query). `!dpcwatchdog` showed every captured core stalled in `KeFlushProcessWriteBuffers`; all pending DPCs were benign Microsoft inbox routines (no third-party driver). A `!stacks` census found exactly one thread system-wide in this path at the crash instant (a single Warp thread) - which is sufficient, because each call broadcasts to all cores; the watchdog's circular capture held 2,549 identical stacks/core in this flush path (near-continuous).

## Root cause in the source

- [`app/src/util/windows.rs`](https://github.com/warpdotdev/Warp/blob/master/app/src/util/windows.rs) - `is_kaspersky_running()` calls `refresh_all_processes()` then `processes_by_name("avp")`.
- [`app/src/system/info.rs`](https://github.com/warpdotdev/Warp/blob/master/app/src/system/info.rs) - `refresh_all_processes()` uses `refresh_processes_specifics(ProcessesToUpdate::All, true, refresh_kind())`, and `refresh_kind()` includes `.with_cpu().with_memory()` → the per-process `ProcessCycleTime` sampling on the **All** sweep.
- [`app/src/terminal/history.rs`](https://github.com/warpdotdev/Warp/blob/master/app/src/terminal/history.rs) - `init_session()` calls `is_kaspersky_running(ctx)` synchronously on every session bootstrap, with no caching.
- The boolean's only consumer is a niche fallback for reading PowerShell history in `app/src/terminal/model/session.rs` - a near-static fact recomputed per session.

Uses the `sysinfo` crate (0.37); `ProcessesToUpdate::All` + `ProcessRefreshKind::with_cpu()` is what maps to those two syscalls on Windows.

## Suggested fix

Two small, behavior-preserving changes (I have a branch ready and can open a PR once this is labeled `ready-to-implement`):

1. Give the full-table sweep a **name-only** `ProcessRefreshKind` (`ProcessRefreshKind::nothing()`), so it stops issuing per-process `ProcessCycleTime` syscalls. Names are still populated, so the Kaspersky check is unchanged. The existing 5-second single-PID self-poll keeps sampling CPU/memory (cheap - one PID).
2. **Cache** `is_kaspersky_running()` (e.g. a `OnceLock`) so the sweep runs at most once per launch instead of on every session bootstrap.

This turns "an N-process cycle-time storm on every session" into "one names-only enumeration, once per launch."

## Related

Likely also explains (or contributes to) #7771 (BSOD on Windows) and #7561 (excessive CPU/GPU while idle on Windows). Happy to provide the full `!analyze -v` / `!dpcwatchdog` / `!stacks` output.

title: SSH wrapper's remote zsh env script fails to disable rc sourcing (unset vs unsetopt)
body:
### Where

`app/assets/bundled/bootstrap/zsh_body.sh` (`warp_ssh_helper` → `zsh_env_script`), with identical copies of the same payload string in `bash_body.sh` and `fish.sh`.

### What happens

The SSH wrapper writes its env script to a temp `$ZDOTDIR/.zshenv` on the remote host, intending to start the remote zsh with minimal startup - the bootstrap body later re-sources all rc files itself with proper bracketing (`zsh_body.sh` sources `/etc/zprofile → .zprofile → /etc/zshrc → .zshrc → /etc/zlogin → .zlogin` explicitly, with timing markers).

But the env script uses `unset RCS; unset GLOBAL_RCS`, which removes shell *variables* named `RCS`/`GLOBAL_RCS`. The zsh *options* of the same name are untouched, so rc sourcing stays fully enabled:

```
% T=$(mktemp -d)
% echo 'unset RCS; unset GLOBAL_RCS' > $T/.zshenv
% ZDOTDIR=$T zsh -i -c 'echo rcs=$options[rcs] globalrcs=$options[globalrcs]'
rcs=on globalrcs=on
```

### Impact (verified against a live Ubuntu 24.04 / zsh 5.9 host over ssh)

With a marker `echo` planted in the remote `/etc/zsh/zshrc`, and the payload prefix delivered exactly the way the wrapper delivers it (written to a temp `$ZDOTDIR/.zshenv`, then an interactive zsh started against it):

```
════ current payload prefix (unset = no-op) ════
[OLD] GLOBAL-ZSHRC occurrences before handshake = 1
[OLD]   WARP_ENV_RAN
[OLD]   [GLOBAL-ZSHRC] executed 23:29:00.694   ← global rc ran pre-handshake
[OLD]   SHELL_UP

════ with unsetopt ════
[NEW] GLOBAL-ZSHRC occurrences before handshake = 0
[NEW]   WARP_ENV_RAN
[NEW]   SHELL_UP
```

Consequences on every wrapper-warpified remote zsh session:

- **Global rc files execute twice** - once bare before Warp's `InitShell` handshake, then again when the body re-sources them. (e.g. sshing into a macOS host runs `path_helper` twice, reshuffling `PATH`.)
- **Anything slow, interactive, or output-producing in global rc runs before the handshake**, where it can consume or garble the injected bootstrap - the failure family tracked in #6244.

### Expected

Remote rc sourcing is suppressed until the bootstrap body re-sources rc files itself, as the surrounding code already intends (`unsetopt ZLE` sits in the same statement - the fix is to fold `RCS GLOBAL_RCS` into it).

Related: #6244 - this is one concrete, verified failure mode in that family, not the whole issue.

Fix ready in #13407.

title: Show SSH remote metadata in the terminal footer/toolbelt
body:
## Problem

When working with multiple SSH sessions in Warp, it is not always clear enough which remote machine the current terminal input is about to affect.

Existing workarounds such as customizing the prompt, changing the tab title, or setting a tab color can help, but they are not always visible enough, can be overwritten, or may be too far away from the input area. The most important moment to confirm the remote identity is usually right before the user types and executes a command.

Because of that, it would be helpful if remote session identity could be shown close to the terminal input area.

## Proposal

Warp already has a persistent footer/toolbelt UI for Agent and CLI Agent sessions. It would be useful for regular SSH sessions to have a similar remote-session information chip.

For example, when the current tab enters an SSH session, Warp could show a persistent remote-session chip near the terminal input area:

```text
SSH · prod · 10.8.2.56
```

The chip could support displaying or configuring metadata such as:

- Real remote IP
- Environment label, such as prod / staging / dev
- SSH alias
- Resolved hostname
- Username, optionally shown and hidden by default

## Why not just the tab title?

This request is not only about changing the tab title or tab color.

The tab title is useful for distinguishing multiple sessions, but it is farther away from the input area and can be truncated when many tabs are open. The moment when the user most needs to confirm the remote identity is right before executing a command.

A footer/toolbelt chip is closer to the command input area, which makes it a better persistent reminder of which remote environment the next command will affect.

## Expected behavior

- Show the remote-session chip when an SSH session starts.
- Hide the chip when the SSH session exits.
- Make the real remote IP easy to display prominently.
- Allow the environment label to be configured, such as prod / staging / dev.
- Allow hostname and username to be shown or hidden.
- Allow users to disable this feature.
- Prioritize support for Warpified SSH sessions.
- If metadata can be inferred safely, also support regular plain SSH sessions.

## Related but not identical issues

There are already related requests, but they do not fully cover this use case:

- #2121 Shell Badge Support
- #4211 visually differentiate between SSH and local sessions on tab header
- #4668 Display the SSH server name on the tab
- #4243 Automatically use color to distinguish terminals
- #3575 Rich Metadata Status Bar

This request is specifically about showing SSH remote-session metadata, such as the real remote IP and environment label, in a bottom input-area UI similar to the Agent footer/toolbelt.

title: MCP tool results returning ImageContent blocks are silently dropped - Oz agent never receives image in vision context
body:
## Summary

When an MCP tool returns an `ImageContent` block in its tool result, Warp's relay layer drops the image entirely. The Oz agent receives no visual context - it cannot see the image at all. This affects both MCP-based tools and Warp's own native `read_files` tool when called on image/PNG files.

## Setup

I'm running Oz through a **custom inference endpoint** (Warp Settings → Custom Inference), not direct Anthropic API keys:

- **Stack:** LiteLLM gateway → ngrok tunnel → AWS Bedrock → Claude Sonnet 4.6
- **Endpoint URL:** OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions (custom endpoint configured in Warp as `litellm` / `claude-sonnet-4-6`)
- **API key:** LiteLLM gateway key

This means Warp is serializing agent requests as OpenAI Chat Completions API calls, proxied through LiteLLM to Bedrock. The image relay failure may be at Warp's serialization layer (not forwarding `ImageContent` as a `image_url` content part in Chat Completions format) or earlier in the MCP tool result conversion.

## Problem

I was trying to let the Oz agent inspect UI screenshots (e.g. `/tmp/welcome_after_login.png`) during an iterative frontend debugging session - the goal being that the agent could verify its own DOM changes visually without a human in the loop.

There are two natural paths I tried to get an image into the agent's vision context:

### Path 1 - Native `read_files` tool (Warp built-in)

The agent calls `read_files` on a PNG path. The tool returns `{}` (empty result). The agent receives no image data whatsoever. No error, no fallback, just silence.

### Path 2 - `fs-mcp` MCP server (attempted workaround)

I installed `fs-mcp` v2.1.0 as a dedicated MCP file-reading server, added it to `~/.warp/.mcp.json`, and called its `read_files` on the same PNG.

```json
// ~/.warp/.mcp.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fs-mcp": {
      "command": "/Users/gana/.local/bin/fs-mcp",
      "args": []
    }
  }
}
```

The MCP server confirmed it produced an `ImageContent` block successfully:

> _fs-mcp: 739376 bytes - passed through as MCP ImageContent block_

But the Oz agent still received nothing. When asked what it saw, it reported the tool result was empty / invisible.

### Why clipboard paste works but tools don't

Pasting a screenshot directly into the Warp input (Cmd+V from macOS clipboard) **does** work - the image reaches the agent's vision context. This is because clipboard images bypass the tool result relay entirely: they are injected as an `image` content block directly in the **user turn** of the API request.

MCP tool results containing `ImageContent` go through a different relay path. That path appears to strip or not forward `ImageContent` blocks when constructing the `tool_result` messages sent to the model provider - and in my case, when translating those to OpenAI Chat Completions format for the custom endpoint.

## Root cause hypothesis

The MCP tool result relay (likely `app/src/ai/blocklist/action_model/execute/call_mcp_tool.rs`) converts `CallToolResult` into conversation content. The conversion handles `TextContent` correctly but does not map `ImageContent` blocks into vision-compatible content (Anthropic `image` blocks or OpenAI `image_url` parts) in the `tool_result` message. Image data is silently discarded before the API request is sent.

The same gap likely exists for the native `read_files` tool on binary/image files.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint in Warp (Settings → Custom Inference) pointing to any LiteLLM/proxy gateway backed by a vision-capable model.
2. Configure `fs-mcp` in `~/.warp/.mcp.json` (see config above).
3. In an Oz agent session, call `fs-mcp`'s `read_files` on any PNG file.
4. Ask the agent: "What do you see in the image returned by the tool?"
5. Agent reports it cannot see any image / the tool result was empty.

Also reproducible with Warp's native `read_files` on any PNG - result is always `{}`.

## Expected behavior

`ImageContent` blocks returned by MCP tools should be forwarded to the model as vision-compatible content (Anthropic `image` blocks or OpenAI `image_url` parts depending on the endpoint type). The agent should be able to see images returned from tool calls, the same way clipboard-pasted images are visible.

## Actual behavior

`ImageContent` blocks are silently dropped. The agent receives an empty tool result. No error, no warning, no fallback.

## Workaround (partial)

Pasting images directly via Cmd+V from clipboard works for one-off manual use but is not viable for autonomous agent loops where the agent needs to programmatically read images from disk (e.g. screenshot verification, UI regression checks).

## Environment

- **Warp version:** v0.2026.07.01.09.21.01 (macOS stable)
- **OS:** macOS (Apple Silicon)
- **Shell:** zsh 5.9
- **Model routing:** LiteLLM gateway → ngrok → AWS Bedrock → Claude Sonnet 4.6 (custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint in Warp)
- **fs-mcp:** v2.1.0 (`/Users/gana/.local/bin/fs-mcp`)

## Related issues

This is distinct from the existing image-paste issues (#7069, #9545, #8692, #11098) which cover clipboard/drag-drop image delivery to CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex). Those are about getting images into a CLI agent's stdin. This issue is about images returned **from** MCP tool calls not reaching the Oz agent's vision context.

title: Modifier-click a Markdown link to open the local file it names (resolve from link text and URL via the file finder)
body:
### Problem

I generate and review a lot of Markdown, including Warp's own product spec (`PRODUCT.md`) and tech spec (`TECH.md`) process. These documents frequently present file references as links whose text or URL names a file/path like `crates/editor/src/render/model/mod.rs` or `mod_tests.rs`. Clicking such a link today follows its URL (which may point at GitHub, a web page, or nowhere useful) rather than opening that file locally in Warp. When reviewing a spec I want to jump straight to the local file the link refers to.

### Where this can be invoked

Anywhere Warp renders Markdown links, i.e. the surfaces that already produce clickable links:
- the Markdown Viewer (opening a `.md` doc),
- Agent Mode / AI output,
- notebooks / plans.

The common trigger is a **rendered Markdown link** - not bare text in prose.

### Proposed behavior

On a rendered Markdown link, a modifier gesture - e.g. **CMD+OPTION+click** - derives a file-name/path candidate from the link and resolves it against the current workspace using the **existing file finder**:

- The candidate comes from the link's **display text**, and when the text isn't itself a file name, from the link's **URL** (e.g. the path component or final segment of the href). The link text is often the file name, but not always - sometimes the path only appears in the URL.
- **Exactly one match** → open that file in Warp.
- **Multiple matches** → open the file finder pre-filtered to the candidates; the user picks.
- **No match** → no-op (or a subtle "no match" hint).
- Honor a `path/to/file.rs:1430` line (and optional column) suffix, in the text or URL, to land on a specific location in the opened file.

### Why scope it to links

- Authoring a file name as a link already implies it's navigable - no heuristic needed to decide which tokens are files.
- Resolution runs through the existing fuzzy finder only when the user invokes the gesture, so there's **no background index** and **no false-positive link noise**.
- The link text and URL are treated only as *sources for a file-name candidate* - Warp doesn't open the URL as a web address; it extracts a path/filename from it and looks that up locally. The URL can point anywhere (e.g. GitHub), so only its path-like portion matters.

### Alternatives considered

- Manually copying names into file search - slow and breaks review flow, and it doesn't even work when the file name isn't in the visible link text but embedded in the URL, so there's nothing useful to select and copy.
- Auto-hyperlinking bare file paths in prose (see #12421) - a different, heavier approach; scoping to existing links avoids the detection/indexing problem entirely.

### Related issues / prior art

Warp already detects and opens file paths in terminal and agent output, but a Markdown link's click follows its URL rather than opening the local file it names. This reuses the existing link onclick handler and file finder.

- #8998 - `.md` links in the agent panel should open in the Markdown Viewer
- #12038 - clicking a file reference should focus the already-open pane
- #13065 / #13280 (PRs) - making Markdown link/file clicks actionable in Agent Mode output
- #9561 - open a file at a specific line via URL scheme/CLI (the line-number half)
- #9908 - clickable-path resolution against the workspace root

title: Remove the lightened background in Agent Mode so panes respect the theme background
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

Remove the translucent lightening overlay that Agent Mode paints over the pane background, so agent conversations render with the plain terminal/theme background - exactly like a terminal pane.

Today the fullscreen agent view composites a `surface_overlay_1` fill over the theme background across the header, block list, status bar, message bar, and input footer. The proposal is a hard removal of that overlay (not a setting, not a theme property): Agent Mode should inherit the theme's background verbatim.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Yes - a few compounding problems:

1. **Dark themes are never actually dark in Agent Mode.** The overlay shifts the background lighter, so a true-black or dark theme renders washed-out gray whenever you're in an agent conversation (see #11561). Users pick their theme background deliberately; Agent Mode silently overrides it.
2. **It overloads an existing visual semantic.** Warp already uses luminance shifts to mean "inactive pane" (dim inactive panes) and "unfocused window". Using a luminance shift - in the *opposite* direction, on the *focused* pane - to also mean "agent mode" makes the signal ambiguous. Dimming maps naturally to "inactive", not to "agent".
3. **The affordance is redundant.** Agent Mode is already signaled by stronger, unambiguous cues: the agent tab icon, the "← ESC for terminal" breadcrumb, and a completely different input footer (model selector, remote-control chip, mic, cloud dispatch). A subtle whole-pane tint is the weakest signal in that set, while imposing a permanent cost on theme fidelity.

### Additional context

- Related report: #11561 (agent/conversation pane renders lighter/shifted vs. the terminal on dark themes).
- If a per-pane "you're in a conversation" cue proves necessary for edge cases (e.g. viewing a conversation while not fullscreen), a targeted affordance like a header treatment or accent border would communicate mode without taxing the entire background.
- A prototype PR removing the overlay is in progress; screenshots comparing terminal vs. agent panes before/after to follow.

Cross-platform

title: Add custom tab icon support and icon-only detection mode for Third-Party CLI Agents
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have searched Warp feature requests and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have searched Warp docs and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like

Two enhancements to the Third-Party CLI Agents detection system:

**1. Custom tab icon (SVG upload per agent pattern)**

Allow users to associate a custom SVG icon with each regex pattern in Settings → Agents → Third party CLI agents → Commands that enable the toolbar.

Currently, tab icons are hardcoded brand logos (Claude Code, Pi, Codex, etc.) managed by `CLIAgentSessionsModel`. Users running wrapper commands (e.g., `omp`, `ccs`) that are mapped to a supported agent type cannot set a distinctive icon - they get either the mapped agent's brand icon or the generic `>_` shell icon depending on detection timing.

Proposed:
- Add an "Icon" field per command pattern entry (file picker accepting `.svg` or `.png`, max 64×64)
- Fallback to the mapped agent's brand icon if no custom icon is set (preserving current behavior)
- Persist icon data in the existing Third party CLI agents config

**2. Icon-only detection mode (disable PTY state monitoring)**

Add a per-pattern toggle - e.g., "Icon only (no PTY monitoring)" - that activates the agent toolbar branding and tab icon **without** enabling the full PTY state-tracking layer (cwd detection, git branch polling, buffer reading).

When this mode is active:
- The agent toolbelt icon and tab branding appear normally
- The Rich Input editor (`Ctrl-G`) remains available
- PTY passes through raw terminal I/O unmodified - shell commands executed within the agent (e.g., Claude Code's `!ls` prefix) produce visible output as expected
- Features that depend on PTY state (vertical tab metadata with cwd/branch, agent notifications triggered by PTY events) are disabled for that pattern

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe

When Warp detects a Third-Party CLI Agent via the regex pattern `^omp(-[a-z]+)?\b` (mapped to Pi agent), it enters an enhanced PTY mode to monitor agent state. This PTY enhancement layer intercepts stdout in a way that breaks shell command output from within the agent session:

- Running `!ls` inside Claude Code (invoked via `omp`) produces **no visible output**
- Piping (`!ls -la 2>&1 | cat`) does not resolve the issue
- The `!` prefix is Claude Code's built-in shell execution feature - output should flow through the PTY normally

Removing the regex pattern from Third party CLI agents settings restores `!shell` output but loses all visual agent identification (toolbar icon, tab branding).

### How this differs from related issues

| Issue | Scope | Difference |

body:
### Pre-submit Checks

### Describe the bug

When the agent's backing model fails mid-turn (monthly AI quota exhausted), tool calls that have already executed and succeeded are reported to the agent as cancelled instead of returning their output. Because the agent cannot distinguish "my command ran but my turn died" from "my command never ran," it retries the identical command - duplicating real side effects on external systems (HTTP POSTs, DB writes, etc.).

Correlation IDs
> - request_id: f6c45c1a-18e7-4a5f-8fec-3a40a1ba0cdf
> - conversation_id: fc92f75b-9e31-4350-ac51-6fa8a0c4c296

### To reproduce

Observed behavior
> During an agent turn, a run_shell_command call ran curl -X POST to a localhost HTTP endpoint (127.0.0.1:8090). The command executed fully and the server replied {"response":"..."} with HTTP 200 - confirmed both in the command's own output (__HTTP_STATUS__:200) and in the target server's request logs. But the tool call returned {"cancelled":true} to the agent. The agent concluded the send had failed and re-ran the same command, causing the same network request (with the same non-idempotent side effect - a persisted chat message) to be delivered multiple times to the external server.

### Expected behavior

If a tool command executed and produced output, that output should be returned to the agent rather than cancelled. If the agent's backing model hits a quota/rate-limit after a command has run, the already-executed side effect should not be silently retried - at minimum the agent should be told the command completed.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

Root cause (from Warp logs)
> The backing-model failures are Warp's own monthly AI quota, surfaced in ~/Library/Logs/warp.log:
> ```
> 2026-07-10T07:51:37Z [WARN] MultiAgent request failed, retrying (attempt 1/3) - Error: QuotaLimit { user_display_message: None }
> 2026-07-10T08:24:26Z [WARN] attempts 1/3, 2/3, 3/3 - QuotaLimit
> 2026-07-10T08:24:27Z [ERROR] MultiAgent request failed after 3 retries: Request failed due to lack of AI quota.
> 2026-07-10T09:42:11-12Z  (same pattern, 3 retries → "lack of AI quota")
> ```
> The quota cycle (AIRequestQuotaInfoSetting) shows was_quota_exceeded: true for the cycle ending 2026-07-28, so the account is currently over its monthly Warp AI quota. Each failure kills the agent turn after any in-flight tool command has already run.
>
> Impact
> Breaks idempotency for any agent command with side effects. The masking is especially harmful because the agent has no signal the first attempt succeeded, so it retries autonomously - duplicating HTTP requests, messages, writes, etc. This is a correctness/safety issue, not just a UX annoyance.
>
> How to reproduce
> 1. Agent makes a tool call with a side effect (e.g. curl POST to a localhost server that persists a message).
> 2. Agent's backing model hits monthly AI quota mid-turn, after the command runs but before the turn completes.
> 3. Tool call reports cancelled; agent retries the same command; side effect is duplicated on the external server.
>
> Environment
> macOS (Apple Silicon), Warp (latest). Agent backing model: GLM 5.2 (Oz harness). Target: unrelated localhost FastAPI server.

### Describe the solution you'd like?

When using **Agent Mode** inside a **Warpified SSH session** or other **Warpified subshell** (Docker, nested shell, etc.), show a clear, persistent indicator on the **Agent Mode toolbelt / agent utility bar** that the active session is remote or nested.

Suggested UX (not prescriptive):
- A chip/badge on the Agent toolbelt such as `SSH · user@host` or `Subshell · docker`

  - Warp SSH wrapper sessions
  - Warpified `command ssh` / subshell sessions
  - Nested remote contexts where possible (documented limitations OK)

This should make it immediately obvious that agent-run commands execute on a remote/nested host rather than the local machine.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

While in Agent Mode over SSH/WSL-style nested sessions, it is easy to lose track of *where* the agent is executing. Vertical tabs can show working directory / metadata, and prompts can encode host info, but:

1. That context is easy to miss when attention is on the agent conversation and toolbelt.
2. Native agent filesystem tools are limited over SSH (fallback to shell), so misreading "local vs remote" has real impact on trust and safety of approvals.
3. Tab renames and prompt customization help, but are manual and not a first-class session-state signal on the Agent toolbelt.

I looked for an Agent toolbelt chip that indicates "SSH subshell / remote session" and did not find one in product docs or current UI.

- Closely related: #13430 - "Show SSH remote metadata in the terminal footer/toolbelt"
  - That request focuses on a persistent chip near terminal input for remote IP/host/env.
  - Discussion there notes hesitation about another footer conflicting with Agent sessions over SSH.
  - This request is complementary: put the remote/subshell signal **on the Agent Mode toolbelt itself**, where Agent Mode users already look for session controls.
- Related context/limitations: #6831 (AI/codebase features over SSH), SSH feature-support docs (native FS tools unavailable remotely; Agent falls back to terminal commands).

### Additional context

**Environment**

- Heavy use of Agent Mode for coding tasks across local WSL and remote hosts

**Why toolbelt (not only prompt/tab)**
- Prompt customization and vertical-tab metadata are useful but easy to overlook during agent turns, approvals, and multi-pane agent work.

title: Rendered SVG/image viewer panel (analogous to the Markdown viewer)
body: ### Describe the solution you'd like? Opening an `.svg` (or other image) file in Warp currently shows the raw file content - for SVG, that's raw XML text. Warp already has a rendered viewer panel for Markdown files (with a Rendered/Raw toggle), and that Markdown viewer can already display images, including SVGs, inline. Requesting: give SVGs and other common image formats (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) their own rendered image-viewer panel when opened directly, analogous to the Markdown viewer - instead of falling through to a plain-text code editor pane. Basic expectations for a first version: - Opening a `.svg`/`.png`/`.jpg`/`.gif`/`.webp` file (double-click in the file tree, `cat`/`open` in terminal, etc.) opens a rendered image pane instead of raw text/binary garbage. - Minimal chrome: fit-to-pane by default, maybe a zoom control. Doesn't need to be fancy for v1. - A Raw/Rendered toggle similar to what the Markdown viewer offers would be a nice-to-have but isn't essential for v1. ### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. I generate SVG charts/dashboards locally (dataviz output, diagrams, etc.) and open them directly in Warp to check them. Right now that just dumps the raw XML into a text pane, which is useless - I have to shell out to `open` to see the rendered image. This is also the natural companion to Markdown docs that embed images: if I follow a link to the image file itself (rather than viewing it inline in the doc), I'd expect to see it rendered too. ### Additional context **Feasibility notes (from reading the open source):** I'm not a Warp engineer, so take this as an outside read rather than an authoritative scoping, but from browsing the public repo it looks like most of the pieces already exist: - File-type → viewer dispatch already has a well-defined seam. `OpenableFileType` (code file type detection) and `FileTarget` (which viewer to route to: `MarkdownViewer`, `CodeEditor`, external editor, etc.) live in `app/src/util/openable_file_type.rs`, resolved via `resolve_file_target_with_editor_choice`. There's already an `is_supported_image_file()` helper right next to it (covers jpg/jpeg/png/gif/webp/svg) - but nothing currently routes through it; SVG today falls into the generic `Text` bucket and opens in the code editor. - The image rendering machinery is already fully built and reused elsewhere. `warpui_core::elements::Image` (backed by `ImageCache`/`ImageType` in `crates/warpui_core/src/image_cache.rs`) already rasterizes SVGs via `usvg`/`resvg` (with a bundled fallback font) as well as PNG/JPEG/WebP/animated GIF via the `image` crate, with size-aware caching, fit modes (Cover/Contain/Stretch), and animation playback. - This machinery is already proven for exactly this use case: the Markdown viewer's inline image rendering (`crates/editor/src/render/element/image.rs`, `RenderableImage`) is a ~50-line wrapper that just constructs `Image::new(asset_source, CacheOption::BySize).contain()` and lets the cache/renderer do the work. - The panel-opening mechanism looks generic, not Markdown-specific. `open_file_notebook()` (`app/src/workspace/view.rs`) - which the `FileTarget::MarkdownViewer` case calls - just builds a `FilePane` and inserts it into the active pane group via the existing `Direction`/`PanesLayout` APIs. Nothing about it appears intrinsically tied to Markdown parsing. Net read: I didn't find an architectural blocker. It looks more like a composition gap - adding an `ImageViewer` (or similar) `FileTarget` variant, wiring `is_supported_image_file()` into the dispatch logic, and building a thin viewer pane that reuses the existing `Image` element and pane-opening plumbing the same way the Markdown viewer does. Happy to be corrected if there's context I'm missing from outside the public repo. Related: #13652 (markdown raw-HTML `` support). Possibly overlaps with #9729 (image preview in the Code Editor file pane + thumbnail strip) and #12093 (image previews in the code review panel) - those are scoped to inline/thumbnail previews within other panels rather than a standalone rendered viewer for an image file opened directly, but there may be shared plumbing worth coordinating on.

title: Markdown viewer shows stale embedded local images after file content changes on disk (incl. Refresh file button)
body: ### Pre-submit Checks - [x] I have searched Warp bugs and there are no duplicates. Closest match is #12802 ("Displayed image is stale when underlying file is changed at the same path"), which was fixed by PR #12840 - but that fix is explicitly scoped to AI-block image display only. The PR description states: "non-blocklist callers (themes, **notebooks**) keep path-only caching (`content_version: None`), so their behavior is unchanged." The standalone Markdown document viewer (`FileNotebookView`, opening a `.md` file from the File Tree / Code Editor) is one of those un-fixed "notebooks" callers, and reproduces the identical bug today on current `master` (`13902088`). Also related: #9789 ("Image cache is not getting cleared", unbounded growth - different symptom, same two caches). - [x] I have searched Warp known issues page and my issue is not there. ### Describe the bug When a Markdown document is opened in the rendered Markdown viewer and it embeds a local image via `![alt](relative/dir/chart.svg)`, regenerating that image file on disk (even via an atomic temp-file-plus-rename replace, i.e. a new inode) does not update the rendered image. I tried every refresh mechanism available in the UI and all four failed: 1. Closing the document pane and reopening the file - stale image persists. 2. Toggling between Rendered and Raw view modes - stale image persists. 3. The pane header overflow menu's **"Refresh file"** action - refreshes the document's text content but not the embedded images. 4. Re-editing/re-saving the Markdown file itself (forces a text reload) - embedded images still stale. Only writing the image to a brand-new file path (and updating the Markdown reference) shows the new content, which points at a cache keyed purely by path. ### Root cause (from reading the open source) Confirmed by reading the checked-out source at `13902088` (current `master`), not just inferred from symptoms. **The cache key never changes when a Markdown-embedded image's file content changes:** - `resolve_asset_source_relative_to_directory()` in `crates/editor/src/content/edit.rs` (lines ~78-100) builds the `AssetSource::LocalFile { path, content_version: None }` for every image referenced from Markdown - both the absolute-path branch (line 87) and the relative-path branch (line 98) hardcode `content_version: None`. - `AssetSource::LocalFile` has an optional `content_version: Option` field (`crates/warpui_core/src/assets/asset_cache.rs:125-135`) that fingerprints mtime + file size specifically to solve this class of bug (doc comment: *"so a file whose contents change on disk is treated as a distinct asset and re-read, rather than served from a now-stale cache entry"*). The helper that populates it, `AssetSource::with_local_file_content_version()` (`asset_cache.rs:144-156`), is called from exactly **one** call site in the whole codebase: `app/src/ai/blocklist/block.rs:1766`, inside AI-block image resolution. The Markdown editor's `resolve_asset_source_relative_to_directory()` never calls it. - Because the cache key (`AssetHandle{ source, asset_type }`) is identical before and after the file changes, `AssetCache::load_asset()` (`asset_cache.rs:410-469`) hits `assets.contains_key(&key)` → `true` on line 419 and returns the already-loaded (stale) entry without ever re-reading the file. - A second cache layer compounds this: `ImageCache::image()` (`crates/warpui_core/src/image_cache.rs:862-966`) additionally caches the *rendered* (resized/rasterized) image, keyed by a `DefaultHasher` hash of the same `AssetSource` plus size/fit options (line 873-875) - so even if the first layer were fixed, this layer needs the same content-version-aware key to avoid serving a stale rasterization. There is an `evict_size()` method (line 836) intended to support targeted eviction, but it is marked `#[allow(dead_code)]` with the comment "Called by the debounce eviction pass added in the main changeset" / `TODO(APP-3877): remove #[allow(dead_code)] once the debounce eviction pass wires this up" - i.e. that eviction path isn't wired to any caller yet. **Why all four refresh attempts fail, specifically:** - Close/reopen and Rendered/Raw toggle: both re-render from the same `AssetSource` derived from the same path, so they hit the same cache key. - **"Refresh file"** (`FileNotebookAction::ReloadFile`, handled by `reload_file()` in `app/src/notebooks/file/mod.rs:570-583`) calls `self.open(path, session, ctx)`, which re-reads the *containing Markdown document's own bytes* from disk - but the embedded image asset sources are resolved independently via `resolve_asset_source_relative_to_directory()`, whose output is cache-key-identical to before. The button's own text/reload path works correctly; only the nested image assets are left stale, which is why it looks like a targeted bug in the button rather than a general cache problem. All four surfaces trace back to the same single defect: the Markdown image resolution path never opts into `content_version`. I'm filing this as one ticket (with "Refresh file" listed as an affected surface) rather than two, since fixing the resolver is a single, shared fix - no separate plumbing exists for the button. ### Proposed fix Mirror what PR #12840 already did for the AI-block path, applied to the Markdown editor's image resolution instead: - In `crates/editor/src/content/edit.rs`, have `resolve_asset_source_relative_to_directory()` (or its caller, off the render hot path per the existing doc comment on `with_local_file_content_version()`) call `.with_local_file_content_version()` before constructing the final `AssetSource::LocalFile`, so `content_version` is populated from mtime + file size instead of hardcoded to `None`. - This should be enough for both cache layers, since `content_version` is part of `AssetSource`, which is the key for both `AssetCache` (decoded bytes) and `ImageCache` (rendered pixels). - Given the existing PR's note that this metadata read is "off the render hot path," care should be taken about where in the Markdown parse/render pipeline the stat call happens so it isn't done per-frame - the AI-block precedent (stat once when the block resolves its image sources: creation / output completion / restore / shell-change) is a reasonable model for "stat once when the document's block list is (re)built, including on explicit Refresh file." - Separately (lower priority, already tracked in #9789/APP-3877): `ImageCache::evict_size()` is unused dead code; wiring it into an actual eviction/debounce pass would also help the unbounded-growth issue, though it's not required to fix the staleness reported here - a changed `content_version` alone makes stale entries unreachable (they'll just accumulate until the existing size-based `AssetCache` eviction or window-resize/size-change eviction reclaims them). I'd frame the specifics of *where* to trigger the stat as a judgment call for whoever picks this up - I don't have full visibility into how block-list resolution timing compares to Markdown's parse/layout pipeline, so the AI-block PR is offered as prior art, not a prescription. Related: #13652 (raw-HTML `` support - same markdown viewer surface; spec PR: #13656) and #13657 (rendered SVG/image viewer panel - filed the same day, would reuse this same image pipeline). ### To reproduce 1. Create a Markdown file that embeds a local image, e.g. `![chart](chart.svg)`, and open it in Warp's Markdown viewer (rendered mode). 2. Confirm the image renders. 3. Overwrite `chart.svg` on disk with different visual content, using an atomic temp-file + rename replace (so the file gets a new inode, ruling out any naive "same inode" caching theory). 4. Try, in turn: closing and reopening the document pane; toggling Rendered ↔ Raw; the pane header overflow menu's "Refresh file" action. 5. **Actual:** in all three cases, the original image is still displayed. 6. **Expected:** the updated image content is displayed after any of these refresh actions - most of all "Refresh file," an explicit user-triggered refresh affordance that currently silently no-ops for images while appearing to work (it does refresh the surrounding text). ### Expected behavior An explicit refresh of a Markdown document (via "Refresh file," reopening the pane, or toggling view mode) should reflect the current on-disk content of every embedded image, not just the document's own text. ### Screenshots, videos, and logs N/A - this is a source-level analysis; happy to attach a screen recording if useful for triage. ### Operating system (OS) macOS ### Operating system and version macOS 27.0 (Darwin 27.0.0) ### Shell Version zsh ### Current Warp version 0.2026.07.01.09.21.01 ### Regression No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp ### Recent working Warp date N/A ### Additional context Source read at commit `13902088` (current `master` as of 2026-07-13; the local checkout's active branch, `fbartho/gh13652-markdown-img-sizing-spec`, is that same commit plus only additive files under `specs/GH13652/`, so all cited source files are identical to `master`). ### Does this block you from using Warp daily? No ### Is this an issue only in Warp? Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

title: Support Kitty graphics protocol animation (frame transmission a=f / animation control a=a)
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

Warp already supports the Kitty graphics protocol for **static** images (transmit, display, query, delete), shipped in Launch Log 2. However, the **animation extension** of the protocol is not implemented. I'd like Warp to support animated graphics through the Kitty protocol, specifically:

- `a=f` - transmit animation frame data (including sending only the changed region / "delta" of a frame)
- `a=a` - animation control (run / stop / loop, current frame, per-frame gap)
- frame composition of stored frames

so that tools that emit animated graphics via the protocol (e.g. `kitten icat animated.gif`) animate correctly in Warp instead of showing only the first frame.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Today, any app using the Kitty animation protocol renders as a single static frame in Warp. For example, `kitten icat some.gif` shows only the first frame and never plays. This makes Warp incompatible with a documented part of the graphics protocol that other terminals (kitty, and increasingly others) support, and blocks inline previews of animated GIFs, spinners, or frame streams.

**Personal motivation:** I'm building a TUI focused on animations, and Warp is my favorite terminal. I'd love to be able to drive the Kitty animation protocol from my own TUI directly inside Warp - right now I can't, because only the first frame is displayed. Being able to rely on the animation protocol in Warp would let me build and use my animation TUI in the terminal I actually want to use every day.

### Additional context

**Root cause** (from `app/src/terminal/model/kitty.rs`): the control-data parser maps the action key `a=` only to `t` / `T` / `p` / `q` / `d`; every other value - including `a=f`, `a=a`, `a=c` - falls through to `KittyPlacementAction::Unknown`, which is then rejected as `InvalidKittyAction::UnsupportedAction`. The `KittyAction` enum also has no variant for animation frames, so frame transmission and animation control are unsupported.

**Minimal reproduction** (raw protocol, no external tools - `python3 repro.py`):

```python
import sys, base64
def rgb(w, h, c): return bytes(c) * (w * h)
def emit(ctrl, payload=b""):
    d = base64.standard_b64encode(payload).decode()
    sys.stdout.write(f"\033_G{ctrl};{d}\033\\"); sys.stdout.flush()
W = H = 30; RED = (220, 40, 40); GREEN = (40, 200, 80); BLUE = (50, 90, 230)
emit(f"a=T,f=24,s={W},v={H},i=2,c=8,r=4", rgb(W, H, RED))   # base frame (shown)
emit(f"a=f,i=2,f=24,s={W},v={H},z=500", rgb(W, H, GREEN))   # frame 2, gap 500ms
emit(f"a=f,i=2,f=24,s={W},v={H},z=500", rgb(W, H, BLUE))    # frame 3, gap 500ms
emit("a=a,i=2,s=3")                                          # run in loop
```

- In **kitty**: the image cycles red → green → blue on a loop.
- In **Warp**: it stays static on the first (red) frame - confirming `a=f` / `a=a` are dropped.

Protocol reference: https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/graphics-protocol/#animation

Related but separate gaps in the same protocol: #12058 (graphics capability negotiation on Linux) and #6210 (Unicode placeholders). This request is specifically about the animation extension.

I'm happy to implement this and take it through the spec flow if it's labeled `ready-to-spec`.

Cross-platform

5 (Can't work without it!)

title: Hoverable floods log with synthetic MouseMoved events (thousands/day)
body:
### Describe the bug

Warp's `Hoverable` handler logs and discards a continuous stream of synthetic mouse-move events:

```text
[WARN] Not handling MouseMoved event in Hoverable due to back-to-back synthetic events.
```

**1,248 occurrences in ~25 hours** of use, interleaved with normal input dispatch throughout the session - not tied to any single user action.

### To reproduce

1. Use Warp normally (TUI apps / agent sessions in panes).
2. Inspect `~/Library/Logs/warp.log` for:
   ```text
   [WARN] Not handling MouseMoved event in Hoverable due to back-to-back synthetic events.
   ```
3. Observe it recurring throughout the session (hundreds/thousands per day).

Reproduces on a **fresh boot / clean log**, in stable `v0.2026.07.08.17.54.stable_02`, and the warn is still present on current `master`.

### Expected behavior

Synthetic mouse-move events should not be generated at this volume, and the dropped-event case should not `warn!` per occurrence (it floods the log and is noisy rather than actionable).

### Root cause / additional context

`crates/warpui_core/src/elements/gui/hoverable.rs` (moved from `elements/hoverable.rs` in the recent `gui/`+`tui/` reorg; still on `master`), in `handle_mouse_moved_without_delay()`:

```rust
let was_synthetic = mem::replace(&mut self.state().last_event_is_synthetic_hover, is_synthetic);
if was_synthetic && is_synthetic {
    log::warn!("Not handling MouseMoved event in Hoverable due to back-to-back synthetic events.");
    return false;
}
```

The guard is intentional (prevents hover ↔ synthetic-move infinite loops; the code carries a `TODO: we should re-consider this approach. It can lead to missed on_hover dispatches.`). `master` adds an opt-in `MouseState::reset_interaction_state()` helper to suppress re-hover during layout, but it isn't applied by default, so the default `Hoverable` still floods. The events are already being dropped - the question is why they're synthesized at this volume on the layout/repaint path.

Suggested fix: demote the `warn!` to `debug!` (or rate-limit) to stop the log inflation, and investigate reducing synthetic-move generation during layout/repaint.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

1,248 occurrences in one ~25h rotation; interleaved with normal dispatch. Possibly related to the share-modal render loop (both suggest excess re-rendering / event synthesis under load), but the patterns differ - this is continuous, that one is bursty - so filing separately.

macOS

macOS 15.7.7 (build 24G720); Apple M3 Pro / 36 GB

zsh 5.9

v0.2026.07.08.17.54.stable_02

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No (but contributes to sluggish typing/hover and inflates the log)

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

body:

### Describe the bug

### Environment
- Warp version: v0.2026.06.24.09.19.stable_03
- OS: macOS 15 (Darwin 25.0.0)
- Shell: zsh

### Summary
The diff/preview panel caches a file's content when you enter the directory and
never re-reads it while you stay in that directory. If the file is modified on disk
by an external process (editor, formatter, code-gen, AI coding agent), the panel
keeps showing the old content. Reopening the panel for the same file does not help.

### Steps to reproduce
1. In a git repo, open a file in the diff/preview panel (e.g. a new/untracked file,
   header shows `+45 · -0`).
2. Externally edit the file on disk - insert a new line near the top
   (e.g. add `field :merchant_no, type: String` as the first field).
3. Look at the panel again, and/or close and reopen the panel for the same file.

### Expected behavior
The panel reflects the current on-disk content - the inserted line appears and the
line numbering shifts accordingly.

### Actual behavior
The panel still shows the pre-edit content. Line 8 shows the old first field
(`field :subject_name`) instead of the newly inserted `field :merchant_no`.
Reopening the panel does not refresh it.

### Workaround
Leaving the directory (`cd ..`) and re-entering it rebuilds the cache, after which
the panel shows the current content. This indicates the panel caches file content
at directory-entry time and does not re-read it while you remain in the directory.

### Impact
Anyone whose files are modified by an external process can be misled into thinking
their change didn't take effect, because the panel silently shows outdated content
with no indication it's stale.

### Suggested fix
- Add a **manual refresh button** to the diff panel that forces a re-read from disk.
- Ideally also auto-refresh via a filesystem watcher when the underlying file
  changes while the panel is open.

### To reproduce

1. In a git repo, open a file in the diff/preview panel (e.g. a new/untracked
   file - the header shows something like "+45 · -0").
2. While staying in the same directory, edit that file on disk from an external
   process (editor / formatter / code-gen / AI agent). Insert a new line near the
   top so the line numbering shifts - e.g. add `field :merchant_no, type: String`
   as the first field.
3. Look at the panel again, and also try closing and reopening the panel for the
   same file.

Result: the panel still shows the old pre-edit content (line 8 shows the old first
field `field :subject_name`, not the newly inserted `field :merchant_no`).
Reopening the panel does not refresh it.

never re-read while you stay in the directory.

title: Shared filetype → language registry (extract language identity; add LSP languageId)
body:
## Summary

Extract Warp's file → language-identity mapping into a single **shared, lightweight registry** that both the editor (tree-sitter grammar selection) and the LSP crate can consume, and add an LSP `languageId` facet to it. This is split out of the custom-language-server work (#8803, PR #11944) per review feedback that the registry should land on its own - with golden tests proving existing behavior is preserved - **before** custom-LSP dispatch depends on it.

## Motivation

Warp currently has several independent file → language mappings that don't share a source of truth (the `languages` crate's grammar map, `lsp`'s `LanguageId` enum, file icons, the agent's `ProgrammingLanguage`, notebook code-block languages, `warp_util` text/binary classification). VS Code and neovim both center on a single language *identity* (VS Code's language `id`, neovim's `filetype`) that detection feeds into and every consumer reads from. Warp already has this hub in the `languages` crate's `Language` struct, but it is (a) missing an LSP `languageId`, and (b) unreachable from `crates/lsp` - `lsp` is built for `wasm32` and must not depend on `languages` (which pulls `arborium`'s native tree-sitter parsers and `warp_editor`).

## Proposed design

- **New leaf crate `crates/language_registry`** - plain data only (no `arborium`, no `warp_editor`), so both `languages` and `lsp` (incl. its wasm target) depend *down* onto it.
- **Entry** = identity + detection inputs + per-consumer fields:
  - `id`, `extensions`, `filenames` (v1 detection inputs; `filename_patterns`/`first_line` reserved for later, resolver already shaped to accept them)
  - `language_id: Option` (LSP), `grammar: Option` (tree-sitter grammar *name*, not the parser) - independently optional
- **`resolve(path, first_line) -> Option<&LanguageEntry>`**, forward lookup; the heavy tree-sitter artifacts stay in `languages`, reached by the grammar *name*.

## v1 scope (this issue)

- Land the crate and migrate **two** consumers onto it: **tree-sitter grammar selection** (`languages::language_by_filename_parts`) and **LSP `languageId`** derivation (both built-in and custom).
- **Golden tests** proving current behavior is preserved: every existing `language_by_filename_parts` mapping and every built-in `LanguageId::lsp_language_identifier()` result is unchanged after the migration.

## Data contract (must be resolved - from PR #11944 review)

`resolve` is single-valued, so a "superset of VS Code ∪ neovim" is not well-defined where the two disagree on the same extension/filename. This issue must specify:

- **Source precedence / conflict policy** when VS Code and neovim map the same extension or filename to different language ids.
- **Pinned upstream provenance** - the exact VS Code and neovim source revisions the seed is generated from.
- **Fixture generation/update process** - how the parity fixtures are produced and refreshed, and the coverage assertion that guards against silent regression.

## Out of scope (later / other issues)

- User-extensible / settings-defined mappings (a `files.associations` analog).
- First-line/shebang and filename-glob detection (reserved inputs; inert here).
- Migrating file icons, the agent `ProgrammingLanguage` map (INT-605), notebook languages (additive fields + reverse/alias index later).
- `warp_util` text/binary classification stays separate (a content/byte concern, not language identity).

## Relationships

- Split out of #8803 / PR https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/pull/11944; the custom-LSP feature will **consume** this registry once it lands.
- Addresses the registry data-contract + sequencing review comment: https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/pull/11944#discussion_r3588806029

title: WSL bash bootstrap freezes on 'Starting bash...'; recovered handshake payload arrives corrupted (syntax error)
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have searched Warp bugs and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have searched Warp known issues page and my issue is not there

### Describe the bug

Opening a WSL (Ubuntu) pane freezes on "Starting bash..." indefinitely. Diagnosis via `warp.log` shows the shell bootstrap actually happens in two stages:

1. An `InitShell` hook succeeds immediately (via the `--rcfile <(...)` process-substitution script Warp uses to launch bash).
2. A second stage - where Warp feeds a large heredoc into the shell's stdin (as if typed) to define a `warp_bootstrapped` function, gather shell environment info (PATH, aliases, functions, builtins, etc.), and send back the `Bootstrapped` hook - never completes. The pane sits at a `>` heredoc continuation prompt (invisible to the user, since Warp's UI still shows "Starting bash...").

Pressing Enter on the frozen pane sometimes flushes the heredoc terminator and lets bash proceed, but the captured payload is then corrupted:

```
$ eval "$WARP_BOOTSTRAP_VAR"; unset WARP_BOOTSTRAP_VAR
bash: syntax error near unexpected token `then'
```

i.e. the injected bootstrap script itself arrives malformed over the pty - not a user shell config issue. `.bashrc`/`.profile` were verified to be stock Ubuntu defaults with no exec overrides, no competing prompt tool (starship/zsh/etc.), and `--rcfile` bypasses `.bashrc` during this stage anyway.

Warp log excerpt (same pattern reproduces every WSL launch, even against an already-running/warm WSL VM - a same-session PowerShell pane bootstraps instantly for comparison):

```
2026-07-17T18:30:27Z [INFO] Starting WSL shell process: "Ubuntu"
2026-07-17T18:30:27Z [INFO] Received InitShell hook
2026-07-17T18:30:34Z [WARN] Bootstrapping failed for shell "bash" on ssh false
2026-07-17T18:30:34Z [WARN] Showing bootstrap slow toast
2026-07-17T18:31:24Z [INFO] Starting direct shell process: "C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe"
2026-07-17T18:31:24Z [INFO] Received InitShell hook
2026-07-17T18:31:24Z [INFO] Received Bootstrapped hook
2026-07-17T18:31:24Z [INFO] Shell is bootstrapped with session_id SessionId(16619955081063439290)
```

Terminal capture of the frozen heredoc finally flushing (username/hostname redacted):

```
> warp_send_hook_kv_pair "path" "$PATH"
> warp_send_hook_kv_pair "cdpath" "$CDPATH"
> warp_send_hook_kv_pair_escaped "env_var_names" "$env_var_names"

> warp_send_hook_kv_pair "wsl_name" "$WSL_DISTRO_NAME"
> warp_send_hook_kv_pair "shell_path" "$BASH"
> warp_send_hook_via_kv_pairs_end
> else
> local escaped_editor="$(warp_escape_json "$EDITOR")"
> local escaped_shell_path="$(warp_escape_json "$BASH")"
> local escaped_cdpath="$(warp_escape_json "$CDPATH")"
> local escaped_json="{\"hook\": \"Bootstrapped\", \"value\": {...}}"
> warp_send_json_message "$escaped_json"
> fi
> }
> warp_bootstrapped
> fi
EOM
<user>@<hostname>:~$  stty sane
<user>@<hostname>:~$  eval "$WARP_BOOTSTRAP_VAR"; unset WARP_BOOTSTRAP_VAR
bash: syntax error near unexpected token `then'
```

### To reproduce

1. On Windows with WSL2 + Ubuntu 24.04, open a new WSL/Ubuntu pane in Warp.
2. Observe "Starting bash..." never resolves.
3. Click into the pane and press Enter - this sometimes advances past the frozen heredoc, but the subsequent `eval` throws a bash syntax error (see above), leaving shell integration in a broken/incomplete state (basic bash usable, but Warp's block tracking, CWD sync, etc. likely didn't initialize).

### Expected behavior

WSL pane should bootstrap and reach an interactive prompt with full shell integration, matching how a PowerShell pane bootstraps in the same session (instant, per the log above).

### Environment

- Warp version: v0.2026.07.15.08.55.stable_01
- Windows version: Windows 11 Pro, build 10.0.26200.887
- WSL version: 2.9.4.0
- WSL kernel version: 6.18.35.2-1
- WSLg version: 1.0.79
- Distro: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (WSL2)
- Shell: GNU bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- `/etc/wsl.conf`: `[boot] systemd=true`
- Recent environment change: uninstalled Docker Desktop for Windows, moved to Docker Engine + containerd running natively inside the WSL distro via systemd. Verified this isn't the direct mechanism - networking, DNS, WSL↔Windows interop (both directions), and PATH resolution all tested and fast/healthy - but it coincided with picking up a newer WSL platform build, which is the more likely correlated factor.

### Regression

Unknown - did not occur before a recent WSL platform update (WSL 2.9.4.0 / kernel 6.18.35.2) and a Docker Desktop → native WSL Docker migration; unclear which change (if either specifically) introduced it.

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

Yes - WSL panes are unusable without the manual "click + Enter" workaround, and even then shell integration doesn't fully initialize.

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes - confirmed WSL bash launches instantly via `wsl.exe` directly and via other terminals; the delay/corruption only occurs in Warp's bootstrap handshake.

### Additional context

Related existing issues with the same "stuck on Starting bash" / "bootstrap slow toast" symptom on WSL, previously resolved by a Warp update for other users, though the underlying cause here appears different (a corrupted stdin-injected heredoc rather than a `.bashrc`/zsh conflict):

- https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues/5937

title: Markdown viewer: platform key glyphs in <kbd> keycaps (Cmd → ⌘)
body:
## Summary

Once `<kbd>` renders as a keycap badge (#13733), a natural refinement is rendering recognized key names as their platform symbols - `<kbd>Cmd</kbd>` → ⌘, plus ⌥ ⌃ ⇧ and the enter/backspace/arrow/escape glyphs Warp's own shortcut display already maps (`Key::text()` in `ui_components/keyboard_shortcut.rs`, platform-gated). Browsers and GitHub don't substitute - this is a deliberate Warp-native touch matching how Warp renders its own shortcuts.

## Why this is its own issue

Substitution changes rendered character count ("Cmd" is 3 chars, "⌘" is 1), and the render surfaces assume rendered↔source characters map 1:1 for cursor placement, selection highlighting, and copy. Doing this correctly requires range-remapping infrastructure along the lines of what secret-masking ("password" → "•••") uses - a focused, reviewable change to offset-mapping code, not a rider on the base keycap PR. Scoping substitution to read-only surfaces only was considered and rejected (the same source would render differently across surfaces).

## Expected behavior

- Recognized key names render as their platform glyph inside keycaps at render time only; unrecognized names render literally.
- Copy/export always yields the authored text (`<kbd>Cmd</kbd>` stays "Cmd") - #13733 already lands a round-trip test pinning this invariant.
- Cursor/selection/copy offsets remain exact across substituted runs.

Related: #13733 (base keycap support), #13912 (depth-aware nested kbd), #13652 (original raw-HTML umbrella).

title: SSH bootstrap fails when the remote login shell lives outside the default PATH (Nix/home-manager): bare-name `exec -l zsh` -> "command not found: zsh", session closes
body:
### Bug description

`ssh` from Warp (with the SSH integration / Warpify active) fails to open a session on hosts where the user's login shell is installed **outside the system default `PATH`** - the canonical case being single-user Nix / home-manager setups, where zsh exists only at `~/.nix-profile/bin/zsh` and the passwd entry points at that absolute path.

Observed in a fresh Warp install (macOS, latest stable as of 2026-07-18) connecting to an Ubuntu 24.x VPS:

```text
ssh alex@tyrode.dev
zsh:58: command not found: zsh
Connection to tyrode.dev closed.
```

(The `zsh:58:` prefix is from the assembled inline bootstrap script streamed to the remote shell - line numbering is of the generated script, not of a source file.)

Plain `ssh` from any other terminal works, because sshd execs the login shell via its **absolute path** from `/etc/passwd`; no bare-name lookup is involved.

### Root cause

The zsh bootstrap ends by re-exec'ing the user shell **by bare name**:

https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/blob/26b7c9cdbd011749480be8ace9b7e8d7d3d5da8c/app/assets/bundled/bootstrap/zsh_body.sh - final `case` arm:

```sh
TMPPREFIX="'$HOME/.zshtmp-'" WARP_SSH_RCFILES="'${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}'" WARP_HONOR_PS1="'$WARP_HONOR_PS1'" ZDOTDIR="'$WARP_TMP_DIR'" exec -l zsh -g $TRACE_FLAG_IF_WARP_SHELL_DEBUG_MODE
```

At that point the environment is the non-interactive sshd default (`ENV_PATH`, e.g. `/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:...`) - the same "system default $PATH" discipline the file's own header comment prescribes via `command -p` for external binaries. If the shell binary is not in those directories, `exec -l zsh` aborts the bootstrap and the connection closes.

### Reproduction (server side)

Any Linux host where zsh is Nix-managed:

```text
$ getent passwd alex | cut -d: -f7
/home/alex/.nix-profile/bin/zsh          # absolute Nix path; sshd execs this fine

$ ls /usr/bin/zsh /bin/zsh
ls: cannot access '/usr/bin/zsh': No such file or directory
ls: cannot access '/bin/zsh': No such file or directory

$ env PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin sh -c 'command -v zsh || echo NOT_FOUND'
NOT_FOUND
```

Then `ssh` to that host from Warp with the SSH integration enabled → error above; `~/.warp*` never gets created (the failure precedes remote-server install). Homebrew-only shells on Linux hosts and other prefix-managed installs hit the same wall.

### Expected behavior

The bootstrap re-execs the shell it already targeted. Warp necessarily knows *which* shell it is bootstrapping (it selected `zsh_body.sh`); the durable fixes are either:

1. Resolve the shell to an absolute path before exec - from the login shell sshd already started (`$SHELL` / `getent passwd "$USER" | cut -d: -f7`) - and `exec -l "$resolved_shell"`; or
2. Prepend the detected shell's directory to `PATH` before the bare-name exec.

The equivalent bare-name exec in the other shell bodies presumably has the same exposure (unverified beyond zsh).

### Workaround

`sudo ln -s ~/.nix-profile/bin/zsh /usr/local/bin/zsh` on the remote host (works because `ENV_PATH` includes `/usr/local/bin`).

### Related

#5137 ("Warp fails to bootstrap when RC files change the startup shell") is adjacent - both are bootstrap assumptions about the remote shell environment - but this one requires no RC-file tricks: a stock home-manager host with `chsh` to the Nix zsh is sufficient.

### Environment

- Client: Warp latest stable (fresh install 2026-07-18), macOS
- Server: Ubuntu (kernel 6.8, x86_64), OpenSSH, login shell `/home/alex/.nix-profile/bin/zsh` (home-manager); no zsh in `/usr/bin`, `/bin`, or `/usr/local/bin`
labels: bug; triaged; repro:high; os:linux; area:shell-terminal; area:ssh; warp:auto-triage-review

title: Mouse pointer cursor is rendered at half size on GNOME Wayland HiDPI (2x) displays
body:
### What happened?

On a GNOME Wayland session with a HiDPI display (2880×1920 at scale 2.0), the mouse pointer cursor rendered while hovering over the Warp window is dramatically smaller than the system cursor - roughly half the expected size, or tiny (24 physical px) out of the box. Every other application on the same desktop shows a normally-sized cursor.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Ubuntu / GNOME on Wayland, HiDPI display with monitor scale 2.0 (e.g. 2880×1920 laptop panel).
2. Make sure `XCURSOR_SIZE` is **not** set in the session environment (GNOME does not export it by default).
3. Launch Warp and move the mouse pointer into the Warp window.

**Expected:** the pointer matches the compositor's cursor size (e.g. GNOME `cursor-size` 24 logical × 2.0 scale = 48 physical px; 48 × 2.0 = 96 for a user-enlarged cursor).

**Actual:** the pointer is rendered at 24 physical px (or, if `XCURSOR_SIZE` is set to the logical size, at exactly that many *physical* px - half of what the compositor shows).

### Root cause analysis

Warp renders the pointer cursor client-side on Wayland (winit → smithay-client-toolkit `ThemedPointer::set_cursor` legacy path). Two things combine into this bug:

1. sctk loads the Xcursor theme at `XCURSOR_SIZE × surface_scale` and calls `set_buffer_scale` accordingly ([sctk 0.19.2, `seat/pointer/mod.rs`](https://github.com/Smithay/client-toolkit/blob/v0.19.2/src/seat/pointer/mod.rs)) - but the scale of the *cursor surface* is learned from `wl_surface.enter` events, which **Mutter does not send for cursor surfaces**. The scale therefore stays at 1 forever.
2. GNOME is the one major desktop that does **not** export `XCURSOR_SIZE` into the session environment (KDE does), so the theme is loaded at the 24 px fallback.

Net result on a scale-2.0 display: a 24 px cursor buffer displayed at buffer scale 1, i.e. half (or a quarter) of the size of the compositor's own cursor.

**Empirical confirmation:** launching `XCURSOR_SIZE=96 warp-terminal` (= GNOME `cursor-size` 48 × scale 2.0 on the affected machine) renders the cursor at exactly the system size; `XCURSOR_SIZE=48` renders it at exactly half. This shows Warp treats `XCURSOR_SIZE` as physical pixels with no scale compensation.

The fully general fix (using `wp_cursor_shape_v1`, or handling cursor-surface scale differently) belongs in the `warpdotdev/winit` fork / sctk. However, Warp already works around a sibling limitation in-repo - `ensure_cursor_theme()` in `crates/warpui/src/windowing/winit/linux/cursor_theme.rs` pre-computes `XCURSOR_THEME` because winit can't - and the same pattern can fix the size: pre-compute `XCURSOR_SIZE` in physical pixels (desktop cursor size × monitor scale, both available over D-Bus on GNOME) before winit initializes its Wayland state.

I have a PR ready implementing this.

### Environment

- Warp version: v0.2026.07.15.08.55.stable_01 (also reproduces on current `master` built from source)
- OS: Ubuntu (GNOME, Wayland session)
- Display: 2880×1920 builtin panel, logical monitor scale 2.0 (`scale-monitor-framebuffer` enabled)
- GNOME `org.gnome.desktop.interface cursor-size`: 48
- `XCURSOR_SIZE` in session environment: unset
labels: bug; needs-info; triaged; repro:high; accessibility; os:linux; area:ui-framework

title: terminal::view: 5 tests fail in full-suite runs due to leaked global FeatureFlag state (AgentView never reset)
body:
## Summary

Five `terminal::view::tests` pass in isolation but fail whenever the module (or the full `warp` lib suite) runs, because other tests in `view_tests.rs` flip the process-global `FeatureFlag` state via `FeatureFlag::AgentView.set_enabled(true)` and never reset it. The five failing tests do no flag setup and implicitly rely on `AgentView` defaulting to `false`; once an earlier test leaves the global `true`, they take the wrong code branches and their assertions fail. These currently report as failures on every contributor's full-suite PR gate.

## Affected tests

All in `app/src/terminal/view_tests.rs`:

- `terminal::view::tests::test_insert`
- `terminal::view::tests::test_insert_into_input`
- `terminal::view::tests::test_viewport_iter_most_recent_at_bottom`
- `terminal::view::tests::test_reinput_blocks`
- `terminal::view::tests::test_scroll_position_doesnt_change_when_block_finished`

## Reproduction

Full suite (fails; the 5 appear among 12-14 failures depending on run):

```
cargo test -p warp --lib
```

The 5 tests pass when run together with no flag-setting test in the set:

```
cargo test -p warp --lib -- --exact \
  terminal::view::tests::test_insert \
  terminal::view::tests::test_insert_into_input \
  terminal::view::tests::test_viewport_iter_most_recent_at_bottom \
  terminal::view::tests::test_reinput_blocks \
  terminal::view::tests::test_scroll_position_doesnt_change_when_block_finished
# => test result: ok. 5 passed
```

Minimal deterministic reproduction - run a flag-setting test first, single-threaded, and the clean tests fail every time:

```
cargo test -p warp --lib -- --test-threads=1 --exact \
  terminal::view::tests::agent_view_lifecycle_updates_input_mode \
  terminal::view::tests::test_insert \
  terminal::view::tests::test_viewport_iter_most_recent_at_bottom \
  terminal::view::tests::test_scroll_position_doesnt_change_when_block_finished
# => test_insert FAILED, test_viewport_iter_most_recent_at_bottom FAILED,
#    test_scroll_position_doesnt_change_when_block_finished FAILED
```

`--test-threads=1` does not help: this is process-global state carried forward across sequential tests, not a data race.

Observed assertion failures in the full run:

- `test_insert` (view_tests.rs:2698): `left: "One", right: "None"` - a block selection that should have been cleared is retained.
- `test_insert_into_input` (view_tests.rs:2824): `Expected no selections in the blocklist but got Some(...)`.
- `test_viewport_iter_most_recent_at_bottom` (view_tests.rs:3220): `item 3` - a trailing zero-height viewport entry is missing.
- `test_reinput_blocks` (view_tests.rs:4072): `left: "pwd", right: "sudo pwd"`.
- `test_scroll_position_doesnt_change_when_block_finished` (view_tests.rs:5310): `ScrollTop(...)` vs `FollowsBottomOfMostRecentBlock`.

## Root cause

Feature-flag enabled-state is stored in a process-global array:

```rust
// crates/warp_features/src/lib.rs:918
static FLAG_STATES: [AtomicBool; cardinality::<FeatureFlag>()] =
    [const { AtomicBool::new(false) }; { cardinality::<FeatureFlag>() }];
```

`set_enabled` writes into it globally with no teardown, and its own guard documents that this is the wrong thing to do in a test:

```rust
// crates/warp_features/src/lib.rs:1038
pub fn set_enabled(self, enabled: bool) {
    if cfg!(test) && cfg!(not(feature = "integration_tests")) {
        panic!(
            "Tried to globally enable {self:?} in a test. Use FeatureFlag::{self:?}.override_enabled instead"
        );
    }
    FLAG_STATES[self as usize].store(enabled, Ordering::Relaxed);
}
```

`view_tests.rs` contains 22 `set_enabled(true)` calls (e.g. `AgentView` at lines 148, 737, 1476, 1535, 5141, 5322, 5383, 5443, 5506, 5562, 5608, 5690, 5817, 5865, 5923, 7439, 7485, 7565, 7877, 7944; `CloudMode` at 1477, 1536). None of them reset the flag afterward. Because these tests run under the `integration_tests` feature, the guard's panic is bypassed and the global write silently persists for the rest of the process.

The five failing tests read the flag and branch on it. With `AgentView` leaked `true`:

- `app/src/terminal/view.rs:19985` and `:20028` guard `clear_selected_blocks()` with `&& !FeatureFlag::AgentView.is_enabled()`. Leaked-on means the block selection is not cleared when typing in shell mode, so `test_insert` sees `"One"` selection instead of `"None"`, and `test_insert_into_input` sees a leftover `Some(...)` selection.
- `app/src/terminal/block_list_viewport.rs:2040`: `if !FeatureFlag::AgentView.is_enabled() || block_height.as_f64() > 0. { return next; }`. Leaked-on skips the trailing zero-height entry, so `test_viewport_iter_most_recent_at_bottom` panics on the missing `item 3` and `test_scroll_position_doesnt_change_when_block_finished` computes a different content height / most-recent-block and resolves the scroll position differently.
- `test_reinput_blocks` goes through `reinput_commands` → `with_non_hidden_selected_blocks` (view.rs:20954), whose filter uses the AgentView-dependent `transcript_scope`; the same non-clearing-and-scope divergence drops the `sudo` variant so the input box retains `"pwd"`.

That the same file already defensively uses `AgentView.override_enabled(false)` in places (view_tests.rs:439, 798) is direct evidence the leak is known.

## Fix direction

Replace the 22 global `set_enabled(true)` calls in `view_tests.rs` with the RAII thread-local override the module already uses in a couple of spots:

```rust
let _guard = FeatureFlag::AgentView.override_enabled(true); // reverts on drop
```

`override_enabled` (crates/warp_features/src/lib.rs:1067) writes a thread-local `FLAG_OVERRIDES` and returns an `OverrideGuard` (lib.rs:1192) that clears the override on drop, so no global write leaks across tests. This restores isolation without a per-test reset dance and matches the pattern the guard's own panic message prescribes.

## Related

Related: #13853 (warp_editor render::tests Once-poisoning - same class, different crate) and the sibling flake tickets filed alongside this one: #13973, #13974, #13975
