title: terminal secrets: redaction tests race on the shared process-global SECRETS_REGEX, failing nondeterministically in parallel runs
body:
## Summary

The secret-redaction tests each install their own regex set into a single process-global `SECRETS_REGEX` and then assert on the resulting detections. Run in parallel (or sequentially without teardown), one test overwrites another's regexes before its assertion runs, so the loser detects zero secrets instead of one and panics with `left: 0, right: 1`. Which member fails rotates run-to-run - the classic parallel-isolation signature - and all members pass in isolation. These currently report as failures on every contributor's full-suite PR gate.

## Affected tests

Primary (`app/src/terminal/model/grid/secrets_tests.rs`):

- `terminal::model::grid::grid_handler::secrets::tests::test_secret_redacted_after_byte_processing` (:34)
- `terminal::model::grid::grid_handler::secrets::tests::test_secret_redacted_after_multiple_byte_processing`
- `terminal::model::grid::grid_handler::secrets::tests::test_secret_redaction_secret_remains_after_resize` (:249)
- `terminal::model::grid::grid_handler::secrets::tests::test_secret_redaction_unobfuscated_secret_remains_after_byte_processing`
- `terminal::model::grid::grid_handler::secrets::tests::test_bytes_processed_for_secrets_after_turning_redaction` and the `_on` / `_off_then_on` / `_on_then_off` variants (:270, :301, :327, :362)

Secondary consumer of the same global, observed failing under full-suite load:

- `ai::blocklist::block::secret_redaction::tests::test_detect_secrets_no_regexes_configured`

Other modules that also write the same global (relevant to serialization scope): `app/src/ai/blocklist/block/secret_redaction_tests.rs`, `app/src/ai/blocklist/action_model/execute/grep_tests.rs`, `app/src/server/telemetry/secret_redaction.rs`.

## Reproduction

Full suite - the secrets member(s) that fail vary between runs:

```
cargo test -p warp --lib
# run A: fails test_secret_redaction_secret_remains_after_resize
# run B: fails test_secret_redacted_after_byte_processing (+ ai::blocklist ... test_detect_secrets_no_regexes_configured)
# run C: no secrets failures
```

The module self-pollutes even alone (5 pass / 5 fail):

```
cargo test -p warp --lib terminal::model::grid::grid_handler::secrets
# => test result: FAILED. 5 passed; 5 failed
```

Every named test passes in isolation:

```
cargo test -p warp --lib -- --exact terminal::model::grid::grid_handler::secrets::tests::test_secret_redacted_after_byte_processing
# => ok. 1 passed
```

`--test-threads=1` does not fully fix it - the tests still share the same global with no teardown, so ordering alone can still overwrite regexes between sequential tests.

Observed panic (identical across members):

```
thread '...::test_secret_redacted_after_byte_processing' panicked at app/src/terminal/model/grid/secrets_tests.rs:50:5:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: 0
 right: 1
```

## Root cause

There is exactly one process-global regex registry for secret detection:

```rust
// app/src/terminal/model/secrets.rs:54
pub static ref SECRETS_REGEX: Mutex<Arc<SecretsRegex>> = Mutex::new(
    Arc::new(SecretsRegex {
        regex: regex_automata::meta::Regex::new_many(&[] as &[&str])...,
        ...
    })
);
```

Every test configures its own regexes into this single global via `set_user_and_enterprise_secret_regexes` (secrets.rs:351), e.g.:

```rust
// app/src/terminal/model/grid/secrets_tests.rs:35
crate::terminal::model::secrets::set_user_and_enterprise_secret_regexes(
    [&Regex::new("ABCD").expect("...")],
    std::iter::empty(),
);
...
assert_eq!(grid_handler.secrets.len(), 1);   // :50
```

The detection path reads the same global:

```rust
// app/src/ai/blocklist/block/secret_redaction.rs:26
let secrets_regex: Arc<SecretsRegex> = { SECRETS_REGEX.lock().clone() };
```

When two secret tests run concurrently (or sequentially without reset), test B's `set_user_and_enterprise_secret_regexes(...)` replaces test A's regexes - or resets toward a set that doesn't match A's input - before A's `assert_eq!(secrets.len(), 1)` runs. A then detects 0 secrets → `left: 0, right: 1`. Because the ordering that decides the loser varies, a different member fails each run, and sometimes none do.

Note on the `_turning_redaction*` family: those tests additionally call `grid_handler.obfuscate_secrets(...)` (e.g. secrets_tests.rs:291), but obfuscation mode is per-`GridHandler` local state, not the shared global. The regex registry is the sole cross-test culprit - the "redaction toggle" in the test name should not be read as implying a redaction-mode global; there isn't one.

## Fix direction

Serialize the secret tests into one group and give the global proper per-test scoping:

- Mark the secret-redaction tests (across `grid/secrets_tests.rs`, `ai/blocklist/block/secret_redaction_tests.rs`, `ai/blocklist/action_model/execute/grep_tests.rs`, `server/telemetry/secret_redaction.rs`) with a shared `#[serial]` group so they cannot interleave on the global.
- Additionally, either save and restore `SECRETS_REGEX` around each test (snapshot the `Arc` on entry, restore on drop via an RAII guard) or add a test-scoped override analogous to the feature-flag `override_enabled` pattern, so serialization is not the only line of defense.

Serialization alone reduces flakiness but leaves the tests coupled through the global; the save/restore (or scoped override) is what actually isolates them.

## Related

Related: #13853 (warp_editor render::tests Once-poisoning - same class, different crate) and the sibling flake tickets filed alongside this one: #13972, #13974, #13975

title: Markdown viewer: hide own-line `<a id>`/`<a name>` anchor tags (currently rendered as literal text)
body: ## Problem As of #13962, a `#fragment` link can resolve and scroll to an explicit ``/`` anchor target, in addition to heading slugs. This works via a click-time text scan over the buffer (`find_matching_anchor_tag`, `app/src/notebooks/editor/model.rs`) - no content-model change was needed for *resolution* because the phase-1 inline parser only recognizes `` as a token (it requires an `href` attribute to match); a bare ``/`` tag with no `href` falls through to literal text, so its raw markup - including the id value - survives verbatim in the buffer and is scannable at click time. That same fact is why the tag is currently **visible**. GitHub and browsers render an anchor tag with no text content as nothing at all - it's metadata, not content. Warp's Markdown viewer currently renders `` as the literal string `` inline in the document. This is functionally harmless (resolution still works) but reads as a visible authoring artifact where GitHub shows nothing - worse for the exact hand-built-table-of-contents authoring pattern (#13725) that motivated the anchor feature in the first place, since users would see raw tag soup at every anchor point. ## Why it's not small Making the tag disappear from the rendered view means removing it from the block's own inline text, which means promoting it out of "ordinary paragraph text" into some new first-class concept - but nothing in the current content model has a slot for "attaches to a block, renders nothing, but must round-trip on save." Concretely: - **`BufferBlockItem`** (`crates/editor/src/content/text.rs:398` - `HorizontalRule`, `Embedded`, `Image`) is a whole-block *replacement* type: each variant occupies an entire block/line via `BlockType::Item`. It's exclusive, not additive - wrong shape for "metadata riding alongside the next block's own style." - **`BufferBlockStyle`** (`text.rs:867` - `Header`, `PlainText`, `UnorderedList`, `OrderedList`, `TaskList`, `Table`, `CodeBlock`) is the enum actually carried by every block's marker (`BufferText::BlockMarker { marker_type: BufferBlockStyle }`, `text.rs:564`). It's the natural place to *conceptually* attach "this block also has anchor ids," but every variant is destructured by named field literal (e.g. `BufferBlockStyle::Header { header_size }`), not `..`, at its construction/match sites. A `grep` for `BufferBlockStyle::Header {` alone turns up matches across a dozen files (`core.rs`, `edit.rs`, `markdown.rs` ×4, `buffer.rs`, `render/element/header.rs`, `render/model/mod.rs`, `app/src/notebooks/editor/model.rs`, plus roughly 40 individual match/construct sites in `buffer_tests.rs` alone) - and that's one variant of seven. - **`BufferText::BlockMarker`** itself is the alternative attachment point (a field alongside `marker_type`, wrapping all block kinds at once - smaller conceptually since it's one type instead of seven). But the `BlockMarker { marker_type }` shorthand pattern is used at roughly 60 call sites across `core.rs`, `buffer.rs`, `outline.rs`, `cursor.rs`, `find.rs`, `validation.rs`, and every hand-built test fixture that constructs a buffer by hand (`find_tests.rs`, `cursor_tests.rs`, `validation_tests.rs`). Every one breaks without `..` or an added field, since Rust's struct-pattern matching requires it. - **Upstream of storage**, there's no parser-side concept of an anchor-only line yet either. `markdown_parser`'s `FormattedTextLine` (one variant per line/block kind - `Heading`, `Line`, `CodeBlock`, `Table`, `UnorderedList`, ...) has no dedicated variant for "this line is a bare anchor tag, attach it to whatever follows." An own-line `` currently parses as an ordinary `FormattedTextLine::Line` (a plain paragraph). Block-attachment therefore also needs either a new `FormattedTextLine` variant plus a lowering rule in the `core.rs` edit-application loop (~`core.rs:567`+, where each `FormattedTextLine` is turned into `BufferText` pushes), or a post-parse stitching pass that recognizes an anchor-only line and merges it into the next real block before storage. Rough estimate: 70-130+ call sites touched across `core.rs`, `edit.rs`, `buffer.rs`, `markdown.rs`, `render/`, plus every hand-built test fixture. This is a genuine content-model migration, not a follow-up-sized patch - hence a ticket for design discussion, not a quick PR. ## The core constraint The Markdown viewer's buffer is editable and serializes back to Markdown on save (`BufferMarkdownParser::to_markdown`, `crates/editor/src/content/markdown.rs:60`, which walks each block's style and re-emits its prefix - `#`, `* `, `` ``` ``, etc. - before the block's text). Anything that's supposed to render as invisible metadata but isn't represented in the content model doesn't survive that round-trip: type the tag, load the document, it renders nothing (because it was never parsed into anything to render), the user saves, and the original `` text is now gone from the file, because nothing carried it forward into `to_markdown`'s output. **Any hiding mechanism must be paired with a serialization path that re-emits the hidden markup, or it's silent data loss on first edit+save** - this is the hard requirement any design here has to satisfy, not an optional nice-to-have. This is the same shape of problem raw HTML comments (``) will face if/when comment stripping is proposed (tracked separately, referenced here as #13977) - "render nothing, but don't lose it on save" is a generic content-model gap, not something specific to anchor tags. Worth solving with one shared mechanism (e.g. a general "opaque/invisible markup" block or inline concept) rather than a bespoke one-off for anchors, if the two land close together. ## Candidate approaches - **Field on `BufferText::BlockMarker`** (e.g. `anchor_ids: Vec` alongside `marker_type`). Pro: touches the block-kind-agnostic wrapper once instead of per-variant. Con: still ~60 call sites to update (most just need `..` or an empty default, but that's still a wide, low-value diff to review), and every future `BlockMarker` construction site must remember the field exists. - **Field per `BufferBlockStyle` variant.** Pro: keeps the field conceptually scoped to "this specific block's own style," possibly with different semantics per kind if that ever matters. Con: 7× the sites of the `BlockMarker` option, since each variant's construction/match sites need updating independently; no shared default via `..` unless every arm opts in. Not recommended given the multiplier cost with no clear semantic benefit over the previous option. - **Dedicated metadata "sidecar"** - a side-channel map (e.g. `CharOffset -> Vec` of anchor ids) stored on `Buffer` alongside the sum-tree content, updated on edit via the same invalidation hooks other derived state uses. Pro: zero changes to `BufferBlockStyle`/ `BlockMarker` call sites; isolates the new concept entirely. Con: reintroduces exactly the cache-invalidation-on-edit lifecycle question phase-1 of the anchors feature explicitly avoided by doing click-time live walks instead of building an index (see #13725's tech spec, "no anchor index" section) - every edit that shifts offsets would need to keep this sidecar in sync, or it drifts silently. Would need a concrete edit-hook design before this is credible. No recommendation is made here - this ticket exists specifically to get maintainer judgment on which trade-off is acceptable (or a fourth option not listed) before anyone spends the 70-130 call-site effort on the wrong one. ## Related - #13725 - original anchor-links feature request (headline issue this hiding work serves) - #13962 - anchor-links implementation PR (ships resolution with tags visible; this ticket is its explicitly deferred follow-up) - #13977 - HTML comment stripping (shares the same "invisible metadata must survive serialization" constraint; worth coordinating design if both proceed)

title: Add Turkish (tr-TR) language support to Warp's UI
body:
## Summary

Add Turkish (tr-TR) UI localization to Warp.

## Motivation

Turkey has a large and fast-growing developer community. Warp's UI is currently English-only, which is a barrier for developers who are more comfortable working in their native language. Turkish support would make Warp accessible to a significant audience across Turkey and the Turkish-speaking diaspora.

This request follows the same spirit as the existing localization asks:
- #473 (general i18n / multi-language support)
- #9002 (Chinese Simplified)
- #12697 (Spanish)

## Proposal

1. Introduce an internationalization (i18n) framework so UI strings live in localization files instead of being hardcoded.
2. Add a language selector in Settings.
3. Ship a Turkish (tr-TR) locale as one of the initial translations. The community (myself included) is happy to contribute and review the Turkish translations once the framework exists.

## Turkish-specific notes

- Turkish uses the Latin script with special characters: **ç ş ğ ü ö ı İ**. Please ensure the dotted/dotless i pair (i/İ and ı/I) and case-folding are handled correctly - this is a common source of bugs.
- Related: there is a known issue where non-English OS language settings break some keyboard shortcuts. Turkish keyboard/locale users would benefit from this being addressed alongside localization.

## Willing to help

I can contribute Turkish translations and act as a reviewer for tr-TR strings.

title: Markdown viewer: preserve scroll position when toggling Rendered/Raw views
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

When viewing a Markdown file, toggling between **Rendered** and **Raw** view modes should preserve the reading position instead of jumping back to the top of the document.

**Expected behavior:** scroll partway through a long Markdown file, toggle Rendered ⇄ Raw, and the new view opens at the equivalent position rather than at the top.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Today, toggling the view mode always resets the viewport to the top. The toggle replaces the entire pane (`FileNotebookView` ⇄ `CodeView`), and the new pane starts with a fresh scroll state, so any reading position is lost. On a long document this means re-scrolling from the top every time you switch modes to, e.g., check the raw source of a table or a link.

Because the two modes render **different documents** (rendered blocks vs. raw source lines), an exact line mapping isn't available; a proportional position (fraction of the scrollable range) is the practical target.

### Additional context

This is the scroll-preservation half of #7897, which bundles two separate asks (scroll preservation **and** find/replace in the Markdown viewer). Filing this as a focused, single-scope issue to match the repo's `Markdown viewer: ...` issue convention and to cleanly link an implementation.

PR #13967 implements this: it captures the outgoing pane's vertical scroll as a fraction of its scrollable range and re-applies it to the incoming pane after layout. The find/replace half of #7897 is intentionally out of scope here and can stay tracked on #7897 (or its own focused issue).

### Describe the bug

During an orchestration session on July 20-21, 2026, I started a task with DeepSeek v4 custom inference (BYOK) selected as my model on the orchestrator tab. Without any warning or consent, the child agents spawned during orchestration silently used Grok from my Warp plan instead, consuming approximately 7,000 credits.

I did not select Grok for this task. I did not authorize a model switch. There was no disclosure in the orchestration confirmation card that child agents would use a different model. This credit consumption happened entirely without my knowledge until after the fact.

I am requesting a full refund of the ~7,000 credits consumed during these two orchestration runs:
•  Run ID: 019f80f7-7733-79f2-b1aa-d903364e5b3f (~22:36 UTC, July 20)
•  Run ID: 019f82c2-2c94-7272-a6bf-a68fa0efa405 (~03:45 UTC, July 21)

This is a product behavior issue - the UI gave me no indication my BYOK selection would not apply to child agents, and I have log evidence confirming the Grok OAuth token was refreshed mid-session.

## Summary
When a user starts an orchestrated agent task with a BYOK or custom inference model
selected on the orchestrator tab, child agents spawned via orchestration silently
fall back to Warp's plan model (e.g. Grok) and consume Warp credits - with no
warning, no disclosure in the confirmation card, and no user consent.

## Problem
The orchestrator tab correctly shows the user's selected custom inference model
(DeepSeek v4, stored locally as a BYOK/custom inference profile). The user reasonably
expects that all agents in the orchestration run use that model. Instead, child agents
default to the Warp plan model without any notification, consuming a significant number
of credits.

There is no warning in the orchestration confirmation card that child agents will use a
different model. There is no prompt asking the user to confirm a model switch. The credit
consumption happens silently across all child agents for the entire duration of the run.

## Artifacts

title: Focus Terminal Input (Cmd+L / Ctrl+Shift+L) focuses Warp input instead of interactive PTY / CLI agent (e.g. Claude Code, alt-screen)
body:
## Problem
We need a reliable keybinding to return typing focus to the active interactive program in the terminal.

**Focus Terminal Input** (`Cmd+L` on macOS, `Ctrl+Shift+L` on Linux/Windows) correctly focuses Warp's block input when that's the right surface. But if you're in Claude Code (or another interactive shell / alt-screen program), it does **not** refocus the cursor inside the interactive program / PTY. Focus ends up on Warp chrome (or nowhere useful) instead of where the user needs to type next.

This feels solvable: the binding should restore focus to the surface that should receive keys right now.

## Expected
Pressing Focus Terminal Input should put keyboard focus on the correct typing surface:
- Warp block input when it's visible and appropriate
- Otherwise the terminal / alt-screen / PTY (including CLI-agent TUIs like Claude Code)
- If CLI-agent rich input is open, either close it and focus the agent TUI, or otherwise leave the user able to type into the interactive session

## Actual
`Cmd+L` / `Ctrl+Shift+L` focuses Warp's input editor path and does not hard-refocus the interactive shell cursor in Claude Code / similar interactive sessions.

## Repro steps
1. Start an interactive CLI agent session (e.g. Claude Code), or another interactive program (vim, sqlite3, un-warpified subshell).
2. Move focus away (click a panel, open something in the UI, select text, etc.).
3. Press **Focus Terminal Input**: `Cmd+L` (macOS) or `Ctrl+Shift+L` (Linux/Windows).
4. Observe: Warp input may take focus (or focus is not restored into the interactive program). The cursor is not reliably back inside the shell/TUI where typing should continue.

## Implementation notes (current behavior)
Today the action is effectively "focus Warp input box", not "focus wherever the user should type now":

- Default binding: `terminal:focus_input` / **Focus terminal input**
- Action path: `TerminalAction::FocusInputAndClearSelection` → `focus_input_and_clear_selections` → `focus_input_box` → focuses `self.input`
- `redetermine_global_focus` already has smarter policy for long-running / hidden-input cases (prefer terminal when input is hidden), but **Focus Input bypasses that** and always targets the Warp input view
- `is_input_box_visible` is false in common alt-screen cases (with some CLI-agent rich-input exceptions)
- CLI agents also have a separate rich-input surface (`ToggleCLIAgentRichInput` / Ctrl+G); Escape closes rich input, but there isn't a dedicated "return focus into the interactive TUI/PTY" binding that matches user expectation for Cmd+L

## Related
- Closest historical: #4202 (Focus Terminal Input with un-warpified subshells) - closed needs-info; same class of bug, not Claude/alt-screen specific
- #1775 - Cmd+L in sqlite3 CLI causes unresponsive keystrokes (interactive CLI footgun with same chord)
- #11644 - Claude Code input loses focus while typing on Linux (related surface, different trigger)
- #13480 - Ctrl+C does not restore focus to prompt (focus restoration, different trigger)

## Design question
Should **Focus Terminal Input** become a smart "focus the active typing surface" action (aligned with `redetermine_global_focus`), or should we keep the current meaning and add a separate **Focus active terminal / PTY** binding?

## Why this matters
Interactive shells and third-party CLI agents are a primary workflow. Users need one muscle-memory key to always get typing focus back into the session, the same way Cmd+L works for Warp's own input today.

title: CLI tools can't reach LAN - Warp never appears in Local Network privacy list, reboot doesn't fix (macOS 27 Golden Gate beta)
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there
- [ ] I have an issue with AI and have included the debugging ID
- [ ] I have technical issue and have included the logs

> **Related:** #12064 describes the same symptom on macOS Tahoe (26), but in that report Warp *is* present and enabled in the Local Network list and still fails. This report is a distinct variant on the macOS 27 (Golden Gate) beta where **Warp never appears in the Local Network list at all**, and a reboot does not fix it.

### Describe the bug

Any process spawned from a Warp session (`kubectl`, `ping`, `nc`, `ssh`) is blocked from *initiating* connections to LAN hosts (192.168.1.0/24), while internet connectivity works normally.

The blocker is that **Warp does not appear in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network at all**, so the permission cannot be granted, and the raw-socket CLI tools are blocked without ever triggering the Local Network permission prompt. This looks exactly like a network outage (bad Wi-Fi / VLAN / ARP), not a privacy-permission block, which made it very hard to diagnose (~1.5h lost before an A/B test isolated it).

Observed:
- `kubectl` / `ping` / `nc` / `ssh` to LAN IPs → `no route to host`; ARP entries go `(incomplete)`.
- Internet (non-LAN) traffic is unaffected.
- Identical on Wi-Fi and Ethernet (consistent with per-app TCC, not per-NIC).
- Inbound works: other LAN hosts can ping *this* Mac; only outbound from Warp children is blocked.
- Multicast/Bonjour pokes (`ping 224.0.0.251`, `dns-sd -B _services._dns-sd._udp`) did **not** cause Warp to appear in the list or fire the prompt.
- **A full Mac reboot did not fix it** - Warp still absent from the list, behavior identical afterward.

### To reproduce

1. On macOS 27 (Golden Gate) beta, run any LAN-bound command from a Warp tab, e.g. `ping 192.168.1.99` or `kubectl get nodes` against a LAN API server.
2. Observe `no route to host` / hang; ARP for the target stays `(incomplete)`.
3. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → **Local Network** - note that **Warp is not listed**, so it cannot be enabled.
4. Reboot the Mac and repeat - Warp is still absent and the behavior is unchanged.
5. Run the *exact same commands* from stock **Terminal.app** (which is present and enabled in the Local Network list) - they succeed immediately. Ghostty (also granted) works too. Only the parent terminal changed.

### Expected behavior

Either (a) Warp appears in the Local Network list so it can be granted, or (b) the first LAN access from a Warp child process triggers the standard macOS Local Network permission prompt. Instead there is no list entry, no prompt, and no recovery path.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

_Not captured - the diagnosis moved off Warp (to Terminal.app / Ghostty) to restore LAN access. Happy to gather Warp logs on request; note that reproducing requires the macOS 27 beta._

### Operating system (OS)

macOS

### Operating system and version

macOS 27.0 (Golden Gate) beta - build 26A5388g (Darwin 27.0.0)

### Shell Version

zsh 5.9

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.07.15.08.55.stable_01 (Warp Stable, bundle id `dev.warp.Warp-Stable`)

### Regression

Yes, this bug started recently or with an X Warp version

### Recent working Warp date

Worked prior to upgrading this Mac to the macOS 27 (Golden Gate) beta. Strongly suspected to be a macOS 27-beta TCC/Local-Network regression (app never registers) rather than a change in Warp itself - but Warp is the only app affected here, so flagging it so Warp can confirm/track and, if needed, escalate to Apple.

### Additional context

- Clean A/B isolates it to the parent app: identical commands fail from Warp and succeed from Terminal.app / Ghostty on the same machine and network, at the same time.
- Because Warp never appears in the Local Network list and a reboot doesn't clear it, an affected user has **no in-app path** to recover LAN access - the only workaround is to run the CLI from a different terminal that already holds the grant.
- Related report on macOS Tahoe: #12064 (there, Warp is listed and enabled but still fails - a different failure mode from this "never registers" one).

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

Yes, this issue prevents me from using Warp daily.

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

title: Async terminal find: update_dirty_matches can leave matches out of order → debug_assert! aborts (SIGABRT)
body:
## Summary
The incremental match merge in async terminal find (`BlockFindResults::update_dirty_matches`, `app/src/terminal/find/model/async_find.rs`) can produce a match list that is **not** in ascending order. In debug builds this trips the trailing `debug_assert!` and aborts the process (`SIGABRT` / "Abort trap: 6"); in release builds the assert is stripped, so the same mis-ordering silently persists and can corrupt find count / focus-traversal / highlight rendering.

## Environment
- Build: from-source `warp-oss`, `0.1.0 (20260722.050348)` (debug profile - `./script/run`)
- OS: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Apple Silicon (Mac15,8)
- Code path introduced in #9618 ("[APP-4280] Async blocklist search"); async find is now on Stable (#13515)

## Crash signature
```
Exception Type:  EXC_CRASH (SIGABRT)
Termination Reason: Namespace SIGNAL, Code 6, Abort trap: 6
Application Specific Information: abort() called

Thread 0 Crashed (main):
  core::panicking::panic_fmt
  warp::terminal::find::model::async_find::BlockFindResults::update_dirty_matches + 904
  warp::terminal::find::model::async_find::AsyncFindController::process_message
  ...::spawn_result_and_throttle_streams
  warpui_core::core::app::AppContext::relay_task_output
```
`panic_fmt` (a *formatted* panic) points at the only formatted panic in that function - the ascending-order `debug_assert!`.

## Root cause
`update_dirty_matches` picks the splice window (`replace_start` / `replace_end`) from **row** overlap between the existing matches and the dirty row range:

```rust
let replace_start = matches.iter().position(|m| m.end_row()   >= *dirty_range.start()).unwrap_or(matches.len());
let replace_end   = matches.iter().rposition(|m| m.start_row() <= *dirty_range.end()).map(|p| p + 1).unwrap_or(replace_start);
```

But `AbsoluteMatch`'s `Ord` sorts by the full **end point then start point** (row *and* column):

```rust
self.end.cmp(&other.end).then(self.start.cmp(&other.start))
```

When a block has matches sharing a row, or a match that spans rows across the dirty-range boundary, the row-based splice can insert new matches next to a retained neighbor that sorts *before* them by column - leaving the vector out of order under the real `Ord`, which the trailing assertion then rejects. (The code even documents the fragile "matches within a single grid do not overlap" assumption it relies on.)

## Reproduction (unit-level)
Existing matches (sorted): one ending on row 9, one on row 11 ending at column 2. Rescanning dirty row 10 yields a match starting on row 10 and spanning onto row 11 ending at column 4:

```
existing = [ (r9,c0)-(r9,c5), (r11,c0)-(r11,c2) ]
dirty    = 10..=10
new      = [ (r10,c0)-(r11,c4) ]   // spans the boundary row, later end column
```

The row-based splice yields `[ r9, span(end r11,c4), r11(end r11,c2) ]` → `span.end (11,4) > r11.end (11,2)` → not ascending → `debug_assert!` fires → abort.

In practice it surfaces when **Find is active on a terminal block whose content is still changing** (streaming output / scrollback churn), so `update_dirty_matches` runs repeatedly on updating dirty ranges.

## Impact
- Debug / from-source builds: hard crash (`SIGABRT`) whenever the invariant is violated.
- Release / Stable builds: no crash, but matches can be mis-ordered, affecting match count, next/previous traversal, and highlight placement.

## Suggested fix
Restore the ascending invariant after the splice (cheap `is_sorted` fast-path; re-sort only when the seam actually broke), instead of asserting it:

```rust
matches.splice(replace_range, new_matches);
if !matches.is_sorted() {
    matches.sort_unstable();
}
```

Per-block match counts are bounded and updates are throttled, so the occasional re-sort is negligible. A regression test covering the boundary-spanning case is included. A PR with the fix + test is ready.

title: Clicking away from an in-progress pane-group rename discards the edit instead of committing it (macOS inline-rename norm)
body:
### Describe the bug

When renaming a pane group in the vertical-tabs sidebar (code-side these are tab groups), the new name only takes effect on Enter. Clicking elsewhere while the rename field is open silently discards the edit. The macOS convention for inline rename (Finder, Xcode's navigator, Notes) is commit-on-blur: clicking away confirms the name; Escape is the cancel gesture.

### To reproduce

1. In the vertical-tabs sidebar, double-click a pane group's header (or choose Rename from its right-click menu)
2. Type a new name
3. Click the sidebar background instead of pressing Enter
4. The name reverts to its previous value

### Expected

Click-away commits the new name; Escape remains the way to cancel.

### Where the behavior comes from

This looks at least partly intentional, so I'm framing it as a design decision worth revisiting rather than a plain bug:

- The rename editor itself already commits on blur: `handle_tab_group_rename_editor_event` maps `EditorEvent::Blurred | Enter => finish_tab_group_rename` (`app/src/workspace/view.rs:1482-1501`). That matches the rest of the app - tab rename, pane rename, conversation rename, the host-picker slug editor, and most settings fields handle `Blurred | Enter` the same way, and the file tree commits on blur via its `View::on_blur` hook ("matches VS Code").
- But the vertical-tabs panel background dispatches `WorkspaceAction::CancelActiveRename` on click (`app/src/workspace/view/vertical_tabs.rs:1718-1720`), and that action is documented as deliberate: "Cancels any active rename ... without committing ... Dispatched when clicking on the vtab panel background while a rename editor is open" (`app/src/workspace/action.rs:189-192`). Its handler cancels all three rename kinds (`view.rs:23859-23863`); clearing the rename state makes the editor's blur-commit early-return into a no-op (`view.rs:1557-1560`).

### Why I think it's worth changing

- It's inconsistent with itself: click-away onto the sidebar background discards the edit, while click-away onto a focusable target outside the sidebar blurs the editor and commits.
- It's inconsistent with the app's own convention - everywhere else, inline editors commit on blur.
- It's contrary to the macOS norm (Finder, Xcode's navigator, Notes): click-away confirms; Escape is the cancel gesture. A silent discard also loses typed input with no signal, which is the more damaging default.

Individual tab and pane renames are affected the same way, since `CancelActiveRename` cancels all three.

### Suggested fix

If you agree the behavior should change: make the panel-background click finish the active rename instead of cancelling - or drop the `CancelActiveRename` dispatch entirely and let the editor's own `Blurred → finish` path run. No test currently covers commit-on-blur or click-away for any of the three rename flows; a regression test on the `CancelActiveRename`-vs-`finish` interaction would lock the chosen behavior in.

Related: #10580.

### Environment

- Warp: 0.2026.07.08.17.54.02 (stable)
- macOS: 27.0 (26A5388g)

title: macOS editing shortcuts (⌘+Delete, ⌘+arrows) can't be used in TUI apps - support "send text/hex" keybindings
body:
**Description**

Warp's own input editor does a great job supporting native macOS editing shortcuts: ⌘+Delete clears the line, ⌥+Delete deletes a word, ⌘+←/→ jump to line start/end. But the moment I'm inside a full-screen TUI app - Claude Code, opencode, vim, etc. - all of that muscle memory dies. Warp either consumes cmd-combos for its own actions or drops them; there's no way to forward anything useful to the app.

The frustrating part is that this is unfixable from the user side today:

- Unbinding the Warp action (e.g. `"terminal:copy": none` for ⌘C) just makes the key do nothing - it still isn't transmitted.
- `extra_meta_keys = { left_alt = true }` helps for ⌥-combos, but costs option-key character input and ⌥+←/→ word navigation in Warp's editor, and does nothing for ⌘-combos.
- Warp keybindings can only trigger built-in Warp actions - there is no "send text / send hex code" action to translate a shortcut into bytes for the running app.

**How other terminals solve this**

Zed's built-in terminal ships default macOS keybindings that translate these shortcuts into the control sequences TUIs already understand, via a generic `terminal::SendText` action:

- ⌘+Delete → `0x15` (ctrl-U, kill line)
- ⌥+Delete → `ESC DEL` (delete word)
- ⌘+← / ⌘+→ → `0x01` / `0x05` (ctrl-A / ctrl-E)
- ⌥+← / ⌥+→ → `ESC b` / `ESC f`

The result is that every readline-style prompt and TUI "just works" with Mac editing keys - no per-app configuration. iTerm2 ("Send Text with 'vim' Special Chars" / "Send Hex Code") and Alacritty offer the same capability.

**Feature request**

A `send_text` (or send-hex) action available to custom keybindings in `keybindings.yaml`, e.g.:

```yaml
"terminal:send_text('\u0015')": cmd-backspace
```

Ideally Warp would also ship the four or five macOS defaults above out of the box (when a TUI has the pty, so Warp's own editor behavior is unaffected).

This generalizes #8462 (Shift+Enter hex codes for opencode) and relates to #2528 (comprehensive keyboard handling) and #512 (option-as-alt). A single "send text on keypress" primitive would resolve the whole class.

**Environment:** Warp v0.2026.07.15.08.55 (stable), macOS 26.5.1, Apple Silicon. Reproduced with Claude Code CLI; same behavior with any readline-based prompt.

title: Projects × Tasks layout: group sessions by project, with that project's tasks as top tabs
body:
## Summary

Running several coding-agent tasks per repository is now a common workflow (git worktrees + parallel agents), but Warp's session list is a single flat/grouped list of tabs with no notion of which repository a session belongs to. With a handful of repos open at once, the tab strip becomes a mixed pile: there is no way to see "these three tasks belong to *this* project", and worktrees of the same repo look like unrelated sessions.

Tools built specifically for this workflow (e.g. Herdr) converge on a two-pane shape - **projects on the left, that project's tasks along the top** - and it maps cleanly onto what Warp already has.

## Proposal: a Projects × Tasks layout

- **Left rail = projects.** One entry per project, derived from the repository each open session is in. Selecting a project scopes the window to it.
- **Top tab bar = that project's tasks.** The existing horizontal tabs, filtered to the selected project. Tabs already show the running agent's task title and status, so each row reads as a task.
- **Worktrees unify.** All worktrees/branches of one repository appear as tasks under a single project, not as separate projects - this is the point of the feature for parallel-agent work.

## Why this needs a real model, not just a filtered render

Warp's tab machinery assumes `Workspace::tabs` is the whole world: `active_tab_index` is a raw index, next/prev walks the full vector, numeric activation indexes it directly, close-left/right use raw contiguous ranges, and drag hit-testing returns raw insertion indices. Filtering only the render would desynchronise what is displayed from what is navigated (and, for the close operations, could close tabs the user cannot see).

So the feature needs:
1. a **stable project identity** that unifies worktrees (the repo's shared git dir - `Repository::common_git_dir()` already computes this, nothing currently uses it as an identity);
2. a single **projection** (project list + tab→project map + visible raw indices) that every navigation and render path consults; and
3. the invariant that **the active tab always belongs to the selected project** - enforced at the one choke point that changes active-tab identity.

## Scope

In scope: project identity, the projection, the rail, project-scoped top tabs and navigation, and `+` creating a task inside the selected project. GUI only, behind `FeatureFlag::Projects` plus a user setting.

Out of scope for now: a distinct agent-run identity model (project → task → run with per-run evidence/attention), automatic worktree creation per task, and headless-TUI parity.

A PR implementing the above is ready.

## What happened

`cargo test -p warpui --lib` aborts on Windows with `STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION` before the suite
finishes. It is not a specific test failing - the process dies:

```
test fonts::text_layout_tests::test_layout_text_first_line_indent_medium ... ok
test fonts::text_layout_tests::test_layout_text_first_line_indent_large ... ok
test windowing::winit::fonts::layout_tests::test_fixed_width_tab_size_affects_tab_width ... ok

test windowing::winit::fonts::layout_tests::test_layout_text_first_line_indent_large ... ok

Caused by:

title: Combining marks are drawn at the pen position on winit platforms (shaper GPOS offsets are discarded)
body:
## What happens

On the winit platforms, combining marks are drawn at the pen position instead of on their base, so
they are never positioned by the font's GPOS anchors.

With a *single* mark this is usually invisible: most fonts draw mark glyphs extending left of their
origin, so a mark placed at the pen happens to land over its base. It becomes obvious as soon as two
marks stack, because both then get identical coordinates and are drawn on top of one another.

Thai is where it shows up worst - `พี่`, `ที่`, `เก้าอี้`, `ก๋วยเตี๋ยว` all lose a mark - but this
is not Thai-specific: it affects any script that relies on GPOS mark positioning, and it sits below
the terminal, so it applies to all text `warpui` lays out.

## Where

`RunBuilder::push_glyph` in `crates/warpui/src/windowing/winit/fonts/text_layout.rs` builds each
glyph's position from `LayoutGlyph::x` / `y` alone:

```rust
position_along_baseline: vec2f(glyph.x, glyph.y),
```

Those are the pen position after advance accumulation. cosmic-text keeps the shaped placement in the
separate `x_offset` / `y_offset` fields (em units, to be scaled by `font_size`) - see
`LayoutGlyph::physical` upstream - and nothing in `warpui` or `warpui_core` ever reads them.

macOS is unaffected: `platform/mac/text_layout.rs` gets final positions from CoreText.

## Reproducing it without a terminal

Shaping `b` + U+0301 COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT + U+0308 COMBINING DIAERESIS with the bundled
`RobotoFlex-Semibold.ttf` at 16px returns both marks at `x = 9.5`, which is exactly the base glyph's
advance, and `y = 0`. The shaper reported `x_offset = -0.546875` for both and `y_offset` of
`0.1577` and `0.4443` respectively - i.e. the correct stacked placement was available and discarded.

(The bundled `Roboto-Regular.ttf` cannot show this: it has no COMBINING DIAERESIS and returns zero
offsets for the acute.)

## Expected

Marks are placed using the shaper's offsets, so that stacked marks sit above one another.

## Environment

Windows 11 Pro 26120; also applies to the Linux winit path by inspection, though I have only tested
on Windows.

## Fix

PR #14322 - one-line change in `push_glyph` plus a fail-before/pass-after regression test.
labels: bug; triaged; ready-to-implement; repro:high; os:linux; os:windows; area:shell-terminal; area:ui-framework; warp:auto-triage-review

title: Crash (SIGABRT / Rust panic) in PaneGroup::shared_session_view_ids with ~30 panes; restored panes give no indication of what they were running
body:
### Description

Warp crashed (Rust panic → `abort()`) on the main thread while handling pane views, after ~41 hours of uptime with ~30+ open panes across several tabs. All terminal sessions were lost.

The panicking frame is in Warp's own pane-group / terminal-view code:

```
Thread 0 Crashed:: main  Dispatch queue: com.apple.main-thread
10  core::panicking::panic_fmt
11  <warpui_core::core::app::AppContext as warp::...::view::ViewAsRef<
       warp::pane_group::pane::view::PaneView,
       warp::pane_group::pane::terminal::view::TerminalView>>::view
12  <... as core::ops::function::impls::FnMut>::call_mut
       warp::pane_group::PaneGroup::shared_session_view_ids::{closure}
13  ...
```

`PaneGroup::shared_session_view_ids` iterating panes and resolving a `TerminalView` that no longer resolves looks like the trigger - consistent with a pane/session being torn down while the group is being enumerated.

### Environment

- Warp `v0.2026.07.22.09.01.01` (stable)
- macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Mac16,5 (Apple silicon)
- Exception: `EXC_CRASH (SIGABRT)`, "abort() called"
- Launch 2026-07-25 19:00:51 → crash 2026-07-27 11:55:28 (~41h uptime)
- 228 threads at crash time
- Layout: 4 tab groups, ~30+ panes, most running a long-lived interactive CLI agent

### Steps to reproduce

Not deterministic. Conditions in place:
1. Open many tabs, each split into multiple panes (~30+ panes total).
2. Run a long-lived interactive process in most panes.
3. Leave Warp running for a day or more, opening/closing panes over time.

### Impact

Beyond losing the window: **session restoration brings back the panes but gives no indication of what each pane was running.** After the crash there were ~30 restored panes, all showing only the working directory (identical for most), with no way to tell which process/session each one had. Reconstructing the workspace by hand is effectively impossible at that pane count.

Two things that would each materially reduce the blast radius:

- **Don't let one pane's view resolution abort the whole app** - a failed `TerminalView` lookup during `shared_session_view_ids` could degrade that pane rather than panic the process.
- **Persist and show a per-pane identity on restore** (last command / process, or a user-settable pane title distinct from the cwd). Related: #10583 (command replay on restore), #9416 (keep agent sessions alive across relaunches).

Happy to provide the full crash report privately if useful.

title: [Windows/WSL2] Minimizing the window closes idle terminal tabs ("storing data for closed tab" triggered by resize to height 0)
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have searched Warp bugs and there are no exact duplicates. Closest related report: #13358 (same environment, same `storing data for closed tab` log line, but different trigger - that report is about Git commands, not minimizing).
- [x] I have searched the Warp known issues page and my issue is not there.
- [x] I have included logs.

### Describe the bug

On Windows 11 + WSL2, minimizing the Warp window (via the native minimize button, or apparently any OS-level minimize event) causes Warp to treat the active idle terminal tab as **closed**, discarding it. When the window is restored, that tab is gone - even though the underlying WSL shell process was still alive and had done nothing wrong.

Tabs with an actively-running foreground process (e.g. an interactive CLI agent generating continuous output) seem to survive minimizing; tabs sitting idle at a plain shell prompt do not.

### To reproduce

1. On Windows 11, open Warp connected to a WSL2 distro (Ubuntu).
2. Open a plain terminal tab, just sitting at the shell prompt (no command running).
3. Click Warp's native minimize button (or otherwise trigger a Windows minimize of the Warp window).
4. Restore/reopen Warp.
5. The tab that was idle at step 2 is gone - it was not just hidden, it was discarded/archived as if it had been closed.

### Expected behavior

Minimizing the window should never discard a tab or its session state, regardless of whether a command is currently running in it.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

Log excerpt from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\warp\Warp\data\logs\warp.log`, captured right at the moment of minimizing:

```
[INFO] dispatching action for "root_view:minimize_window"
[INFO] dispatching global action for workspace:save_app
[INFO] window resized
[INFO] dispatching global action for workspace:save_app
[INFO] active window changed: None
[INFO] dispatching global action for root_view:update_quake_mode_state
[INFO] dispatching global action for workspace:save_app
[INFO] Received Preexec hook
[INFO] dispatching typed action: warp::pane_group::PaneGroupAction::HandleFocusChange
[INFO] Tried to exit the alternate screen, but it was already inactive
[INFO] Block finished with new state DoneWithExecution
[INFO] dispatching typed action: warp::pane_group::PaneGroupAction::HandleFocusChange
[INFO] storing data for closed tab
[INFO] dispatching typed action: warp::pane_group::PaneGroupAction::HandleFocusChange
[INFO] dispatching global action for workspace:save_app
[INFO] dispatching global action for workspace:save_app
[INFO] Tried to resize with size Vector2F(<25.571442, 0>). Skipping resize
[INFO] Tried to resize with size Vector2F(<25.571442, 0>). Skipping resize
[INFO] Tried to resize with size Vector2F(<25.571442, 0>). Skipping resize
```

This exact sequence was reproduced independently on two separate occasions, roughly 20 minutes apart, both starting with `root_view:minimize_window` and immediately followed by `storing data for closed tab`, then repeated `Tried to resize with size Vector2F(<25.571442, 0>). Skipping resize` events while the window stayed minimized.

**Root cause hypothesis:** minimizing on Windows sends the pane group a resize event to a degenerate size (height `0`, width `25.57`). `warp::pane_group::PaneGroupAction` appears to interpret this zero-height resize as equivalent to the pane being closed, and immediately archives it (`storing data for closed tab`) instead of just skipping/ignoring the resize like it correctly does on subsequent zero-size resize attempts.

This may be the same underlying code path referenced in #13358, whose triage explicitly asked for "the full log immediately before `storing data for closed tab` ... to identify whether ... event ... dispatched the close" - in my case that missing piece is clearly `root_view:minimize_window` → `window resized` → `storing data for closed tab`.

### Operating system (OS)

Windows

### Operating system and version

Windows 11, WSL2 (Ubuntu)

### Shell Version

bash 5.2.21(1)-release

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.07.22.09.01.stable_01

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Recent working Warp date

_No response_

### Additional context

- Ruled out as causes: Windows Power Throttling / Efficiency Mode on Warp.exe (explicitly excluded via `powercfg` and Task Manager), screen sleep (screen never turns off), and WSL `vmIdleTimeout` (would kill the whole VM, not a single tab).
- Workaround: avoid minimizing the window (switch away via Alt+Tab / another virtual desktop instead) - this fully avoids the bug, supporting the hypothesis that the resize-to-zero event specifically triggered by the minimize action is the cause.
- Related: #13358 (same `storing data for closed tab` symptom and same Windows+WSL2 environment, different trigger).

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

Yes, this issue prevents me from using Warp daily.

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

## Description

I would like to help add internationalization support and a Simplified Chinese (`zh-CN`) interface to Warp.

This proposal is related to the internationalization roadmap item in #9233.

- Add a language selector under **Settings → Appearance → Language**.

  - English
  - 简体中文 (Simplified Chinese)
- Save the selected language locally.
- English remains the default and fallback language.

Product names and technical terms that are clearer in English should remain untranslated, including:

- Warp
- Warp Drive
- Agent
- Token
- Workflow
- MCP
- API
- CLI
- Shell
- Block

- Update → 更新

- Keyboard shortcuts → 键盘快捷键

I propose using Fluent (`.ftl`) resource files because it supports variables, reusable terms, pluralization, and future languages. However, I am happy to follow the localization format preferred by the maintainers.

- The localization infrastructure

title: Show remaining Claude Code session usage in the header toolbar
body:
### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp feature requests](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Aenhancement) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev) and my feature is not there

### Describe the solution you'd like?

A small indicator in Warp's header toolbar showing how much of the current Claude Code session limit has been consumed - a percentage next to the other workspace controls, in the same place the code review and notifications items already live.

Desired behavior:

- Shows the utilization of the rolling 5-hour Claude session window as a percentage.
- Colors the percentage by severity so a glance is enough (normal → warning → critical as the limit approaches).
- On hover, shows when the session window resets, plus the weekly limit and extra-usage credits when the plan reports them.
- Clicking it refreshes usage on the spot.
- When there is no local Claude Code session, says so instead of showing a misleading number.
- Behaves like the other header toolbar items: reorderable and removable.

Crucially this should need **no additional sign-in**: Claude Code already stores an OAuth session locally (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`, and on macOS a `Claude Code-credentials` Keychain item), and that session is enough to read usage. Warp would not store any new credentials.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I'm always frustrated when Claude runs out of session budget in the middle of a task. Warp integrates Claude Code as an agent harness, but there's currently no way to see how much of the Claude session limit is left without leaving Warp - so the limit is discovered only when a run is already blocked, usually mid-task with context that then has to be rebuilt.

Knowing the remaining budget up front changes how you plan work: whether to start a large refactor now or wait for the window to reset, whether to hand something to a cheaper model, or whether to batch a few small things instead.

### Additional context

I've already implemented this and opened a PR against `master`, so this issue is mainly to give that PR the linked issue the contribution flow requires (Oz asked for one). Happy for the design to change, or to move it to a spec PR under `specs/` first if the team would rather scope it that way.

Implementation summary in the PR:

- Reads the local Claude Code OAuth session (file + macOS Keychain, preferring whichever token lives longest, since Claude Code refreshes the Keychain copy and the file can lag).
- Polls Claude's OAuth usage endpoint once a minute while a session is readable, backing off to ten minutes when there is nothing to read.
- Gated behind a new `ClaudeCodeUsageIndicator` feature flag (Dogfood), desktop only - the web build has no local Claude Code session to read.
- Unit tests cover usage-response parsing, the severity thresholds, countdown formatting, and credential parsing/expiry.

Open questions worth a maintainer's opinion:

1. Reading credentials another tool owns is a policy call as much as a technical one, even though everything stays local and nothing new is persisted. Is that acceptable, or should this wait for a first-party way to get usage?
2. Should this generalize to other harnesses (Codex, Gemini CLI) rather than being Claude-specific?

title: Paste maps numeric font-weight to a Bold boolean, dropping other CustomWeight variants
body:
The HTML clipboard paste path collapses CSS `font-weight` to a single boolean: `crates/markdown_parser/src/html_parser.rs:79-89` sets `self.bold = weight_value > 400`, and `phrasing_to_formatted_text` (`html_parser.rs:463-468`) then emits only `Some(CustomWeight::Bold)` or `None`. So pasting rich text with `font-weight: 900` (Black) or `300` (Light) lands as plain Bold or as no weight - the specific weight is lost on paste.

A bidirectional numeric `Weight ↔ CustomWeight` mapping already exists at `crates/warpui_core/src/fonts.rs:54-121`, and the full variant set (`Thin, ExtraLight, Light, Medium, Semibold, Bold, ExtraBold, Black`) is defined in `crates/markdown_parser/src/weight.rs:7-15`. Paste could map the numeric value to the nearest `CustomWeight` instead of booleanizing it.

Note: this is also the missing "front door" for #13949 - that fix makes the strip-all path clear any weight, but there's currently no user gesture that can introduce a non-Bold weight into a buffer run, so the fix has no user-visible trigger until paste (or some other ingest) preserves the weight. Out of scope for #13952.

### Describe the bug

`Tried to resize with size Vector2F(<0, 0>). Skipping resize` is emitted at INFO at roughly frame rate - peak **90 lines/second** - during normal visible operation in a stable build.

To be clear about what I am and am not claiming: I think the underlying event is **fine**. A 0×0 resize request is routine on Windows, and `Skipping resize` is a guard behaving correctly. I am reporting the **logging volume**, not the resize.

| | 16-hour log | current session |
| --- | --- | --- |
| total lines | 485,499 | 32,137 |
| this one line | **460,812 (94.9%)** | **26,648 (82.9%)** |
| peak rate | 5,416/min ≈ 90/sec | 3,272/min ≈ 55/sec |
| file size | 41.6 MB of 43.6 MB | - |

For scale, my keystrokes log at ~80/**minute**; this logs at ~90/**second**.

**Why it costs something.** Log rotation is size-based, so at ~41 MB per 16 hours the spam evicts history down to about **two days**. I hit this while investigating a GPU device-removal crash (#12132): the five lines that mattered were buried in 460,812 lines of this, and I could not tell whether earlier terminations shared the same signature because that history had already rotated away.

**Warp's own code seems to set the standard here.** `crates/warpui/src/windowing/winit/window.rs:814` gates a neighbouring surface-size diagnostic behind `debug_assertions`:

```rust
// This log exists to let us know if we can eliminate the size
// comparison and rely solely on the boolean flag... We're logging this in debug
// builds only so that we can (hopefully) understand when this occurs
// and why, but it's not something we need to log in production.
#[cfg(debug_assertions)]
if inner.surface_size != window_size && !inner.surface_requires_reconfiguration {
    log::info!("surface size changed but does not require reconfiguration!");
}
```

Same class of diagnostic, explicitly kept out of production. The zero-size resize line does not appear to be gated that way, since it floods a release build where the default filter is `Info`.

### To reproduce

**I do not have reliable steps, and I would rather say so than guess.** It is intermittent - currently not occurring at all on my machine, while earlier today it ran at 55/sec for stretches of 10+ minutes.

What I established by correlating burst minutes against local logs:

- A CLI agent running is **necessary but not sufficient** - 19 of 20 burst windows had one active, but only 122 of 716 agent-active minutes (17%) burst.
- Strong **anti-correlation with typing** - `TypedCharacters` runs 1.3/min during bursts vs 80.9/min during quiet-but-active minutes.
- **Truly idle Warp is silent** - a 2-minute probe with nothing rendering logged 0 bytes for 70 consecutive seconds, so the spam requires active rendering.

Ruled out, so nobody repeats them:

| Hypothesis | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Quake mode / hidden hotkey window | `warp.sqlite` `windows` table has one row with `quake_mode: 0`; `settings.toml` has no `[keys]` section; no quake/hotkey value in `HKCU\SOFTWARE\warp.dev\Warp` |
| Window/display geometry mismatch | Stored window 2560×1440 @(0,0) `fullscreen_state: 2` is exactly the 3840×2160 primary at 150% scaling - consistent |
| Concurrent agent sessions | Burst minutes average 1.57 concurrent sessions vs 1.78 quiet - *lower* |
| Output throughput | Burst minutes average 16.8 msgs/min vs 19.4 quiet - also *lower* |

I am filing anyway because the ask below holds regardless of the trigger.

### Expected behavior

A benign, expected condition should not be logged at frame rate at the production log level. Any of these would resolve it:

- gate it behind `debug_assertions`, matching the neighbouring diagnostic quoted above;
- log on **transition** only (once when the surface first goes degenerate, once when it recovers) rather than per frame;
- or rate-limit it.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

`%LOCALAPPDATA%\warp\Warp\data\logs\warp.log` - representative slice, unmodified:

```
2026-07-29T01:29:52Z [INFO] Tried to resize with size Vector2F(<0, 0>). Skipping resize
2026-07-29T01:30:52Z [INFO] Tried to resize with size Vector2F(<0, 0>). Skipping resize
2026-07-29T01:31:52Z [INFO] Tried to resize with size Vector2F(<0, 0>). Skipping resize
```

Busiest minutes measured across the 16-hour log:

```
2026-07-28T20:32    5,416/min  (90/sec)
2026-07-28T20:33    5,386/min  (90/sec)
2026-07-28T20:34    5,370/min  (90/sec)
2026-07-28T19:46    5,348/min  (89/sec)
2026-07-28T19:45    5,236/min  (87/sec)
```

Distribution: of 418 minutes containing the line, 220 were bursting (>100/min) and 171 were quiet (≤2/min) - so it is stretches, not a constant drip.

### Operating system (OS)

Windows

### Operating system and version

Windows 11 Pro, build 26200

### Shell Version

PowerShell 5.1 / Git Bash - shell-independent, this is renderer-side logging

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.07.22.09.01.stable_01

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Recent working Warp date

_No response_

### Additional context

**Distinct from #14328**, which reports the same log string:

| | #14328 | this report |
| --- | --- | --- |
| signature | `Vector2F(<25.571442, 0>)` - width > 0, height 0 | `Vector2F(<0, 0>)` - both zero |
| window state | minimized | visible, not minimized |
| trigger | `root_view:minimize_window` | unknown |
| consequence | idle tab discarded | log volume only |

That one is a tab-lifecycle bug that happens to log a zero-*height* resize; this is a zero-*size* resize logged at frame rate during normal visible use. Cross-referencing rather than merging, but they may share a code path.

Prior art for this bug class on Windows: #8993 (MCP server logs → 18+ GB) and #11995 (1 TB in 10 hours).

Environment, in case the mixed-DPI setup is relevant:

- Displays: `3840x2160 @240Hz` primary at 150% scaling, plus `1920x1080 @240Hz`, both `dmLogPixels=144`
- Warp renders on the **integrated** AMD adapter (`Using Dx12 IntegratedGpu (AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics) for rendering new window.`) while both monitors are driven by a **discrete** NVIDIA RTX 3090 Ti
- Usage is essentially exclusively long-running CLI agents (Claude Code, Kimi CLI)

Happy to run instrumented builds or `RUST_LOG` captures if that would help pin the trigger.

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

### Describe the bug

Warp crashed three times in five days (Jul 27, 28, 31) with an identical main-thread Rust panic and abort:

```
thread 'main' panicked at 'unable to send visible_items: Closed(..)':
/Users/runner/work/warp-internal/warp-internal/crates/warpui_core/src/elements/gui/uniform_list.rs:214
```

Backtrace (from the macOS `.ips` crash report; identical in all three crashes):

```
core::result::unwrap_failed
UniformList<warp::input_suggestions::InputSuggestions::render_items::{closure}>::layout   (uniform_list.rs:214)
Scrollable::layout
Container::layout → Stack::layout → Flex::layout
LayoutContext::layout → ... → Resizable::layout (nested, split panes) → ...
std::process::abort
```

The panic always lands on the first few keystrokes typed into Warp's native input editor ~1-2 s after ownership transitions away from a just-finished block. In the same second, `warp.log` shows several `[WARN] Failed to send Wakeup event: Closed(..)` entries - so channels tied to the finished session are already dropped while the input-suggestions `UniformList` layout still tries to send `visible_items` into one and `unwrap()`s the `SendError`.

### To reproduce

No minimal repro - hit ~3× in 5 days of heavy Claude Code use. Pattern from the logs, consistent across all three crashes:

1. Run Claude Code (CLI agent integration active, OSC 777 `warp://cli-agent` events) in a pane; split panes / multiple windows in use.
2. The claude process exits (`CommandFinished` → `Block finished with new state DoneWithExecution` → `Precmd` hook), or switch focus to another Warp window at a shell prompt.
3. Immediately type a few characters into Warp's input editor (`completions_open_while_typing = true` was set).
4. Crash on the 3rd-4th keystroke.

Crash 3 variant: copy text from a block → active window switch (`WindowId(0)` → `WindowId(2)`) → 3× `UserInsert` in the other window → panic.

### Expected behavior

A closed receiver during session teardown is an expected race; the send result should be handled (skip the frame / stop rendering the suggestions list), not unwrapped on the main thread, which aborts the whole app.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

```
2026-07-28T14:16:28Z [INFO] Received CommandFinished hook
2026-07-28T14:16:28Z [INFO] Block finished with new state DoneWithExecution
2026-07-28T14:16:28Z [INFO] Received Precmd hook

2026-07-28T14:16:29Z [INFO] dispatching typed action: warp::editor::view::EditorAction::UserInsert(UserInput { .. })   (×4, interleaved with ClearMarkedText)
2026-07-28T14:16:29Z [ERROR] thread 'main' panicked at 'unable to send visible_items: Closed(..)': .../crates/warpui_core/src/elements/gui/uniform_list.rs:214
```

title: Custom conversation/tab colors (even grayscale shades)
body:
## Feature Request

Allow users to assign custom colors to agent conversations / tabs for visual organization and quick identification.

### Current Behavior
Tabs and agent conversations in the vertical tabs panel show status badges (in progress, done, error, etc.) but there is no way for users to assign their own colors to differentiate conversations by project, topic, or priority.

### Desired Behavior
Let users pick a color (or even a grayscale shade - off-white to black) for each conversation/tab. This could be:
- A color dot next to the tab title
- A colored left border on the tab row
- A tinted background on the tab row
- The current dots are too little

Even a simple grayscale ramp (light → dark) would go a long way for organizing many concurrent agent sessions at a glance.

### Use Case
When running multiple agent conversations simultaneously (infra work, video pipeline, corporate tasks), it's hard to visually scan and find the right conversation. A user-assigned color would make this instant.

### Environment
- macOS, Apple Silicon (M2 Max)
- Warp with vertical tabs enabled

---

## Related: Subagent Model Routing Transparency

When a user selects a specific model (e.g., Qwen 3.7 Plus), internal subagents spawned by tool calls (search_warp_documentation, search_conversation_history, etc.) are dispatched by the Oz platform to different models (Kimi K3, various Qwen variants, etc.) without user input or visibility.

This creates two issues:
1. **Billing surprise** - users see credit consumption from models they didn't select
2. **No control** - there's no setting in settings.toml, the oz CLI, or the app to constrain subagent model routing to match the user's selected model or respect BYOK keys

### Desired Behavior
- Allow users to constrain subagent model routing to their selected model
- Respect BYOK keys for subagent dispatch
- Show which model handled each subagent in the conversation UI (transparency)

---

## Billing Transparency at Signup

When developers sign up for Warp's developer plans (especially with BYOK or credit-based billing), the platform should make costs transparent upfront rather than putting the onus on users to discover unexpected charges after the fact.

### The Problem
Developers working "in the zone" - deep in complex tasks, running multiple agents, spawning subagents - can easily accumulate significant credit usage without realizing it. The current model:
- Doesn't clearly communicate which operations consume credits vs. included features
- Doesn't warn users when subagent routing diverges from their selected model
- Leaves users to discover billing surprises after they've already incurred costs

### Desired Behavior
- **Clear signup disclosure**: Show exactly what consumes credits, what's included, and what costs are possible
- **Real-time spend visibility**: Show running credit consumption during sessions, not just after the fact
- **Spend alerts**: Warn users before they hit thresholds (e.g., $50, $100, $500)
- **Hard caps**: Let users set maximum spend limits that stop operations when reached
- **BYOK clarity**: Make it obvious which operations use BYOK keys vs. Warp credits

Developers shouldn't have to wrack up thousands of dollars while focused on work. The platform should make billing transparent and put guardrails in place by default.

- [x] I have [searched Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/local-agents/interacting-with-agents/conversation-forking) and this selection-based workflow is not supported

### Describe the solution you'd like?

Extend conversation forking so I can highlight text in an agent response, right-click, and choose **Fork with a question** (or similar).

The action should:

- Open the fork in a new pane by default, consistent with Warp's existing conversation-fork behavior.
- Preserve the original conversation unchanged.
- Inherit the parent conversation's context up to the selected response.
- Attach or quote the highlighted text in the new fork's input/context so I can immediately ask a follow-up about that exact excerpt.
- Let me edit the prefilled input before sending.
- Work while a clarification/question prompt is pending, so I can ask a side question about an option or its wording without first answering or disrupting the original flow.

This would complement the existing fork entry points documented in [Conversation Forking](https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/local-agents/interacting-with-agents/conversation-forking) - the Command Palette action, the AI block footer fork button, `/fork`, `/fork-and-compact`, `/fork-from`, and right-click **Fork conversation from here** - rather than replace them. ChatGPT's desktop app has a similar branching workflow.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Sometimes an agent response contains a detail I want to investigate, but asking about it in the current conversation bloats or derails the context for the main task. The same problem occurs during a structured question flow: I may need clarification about the question itself before I can confidently answer it.

Today I can fork the broader conversation, or fork from a specific agent response block, but every documented entry point forks at message granularity. None of them carry a highlighted excerpt into the new thread. Copying the text, manually creating a fork, and pasting it is unnecessary friction and makes the relationship between the side question and the source output less clear.

### Additional context

- Related prior issue: https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues/7887 covered the broader conversation-forking request.
- This issue re-files https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues/14610, which the reporter closed; it is specifically about initiating a fork from highlighted response text and seeding the new thread with that selection.
- Existing behavior for reference: https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/local-agents/interacting-with-agents/conversation-forking (including the **Settings > Features > Open forked conversation layout** default of Split Pane).

Suggested interaction:

1. Highlight text in an agent response.
2. Right-click and select **Fork with a question**.
3. Warp opens a side pane containing a fork of the conversation.
4. The selected excerpt is attached to or prefilled in the input.
5. Ask follow-up questions in the fork while the parent conversation remains exactly where it was.

Cross-platform
